full_output.paper_title: The fitness cost of antibiotic resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae: insight from the field.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mefA/E and ermB as the primary mechanisms of azithromycin resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae and estimated their relative fitness costs.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic analysis of resistance profiles and mathematical modeling of transmission dynamics.

full_output.paper_title: Cell walls of Saccharomyces cerevisiae differentially modulated innate immunity and glucose metabolism during late systemic inflammation.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effects of MOS and VIRG on innate immunity and glucose metabolism during late systemic inflammation in a Salmonella LPS-induced chicken model. MOS was found to modulate innate immune responses and metabolic pathways differently compared to VIRG, with MOS showing potential to terminate inflammation earlier and reduce glucose mobilization.
full_output.methodology: Microarray analysis was used to investigate the effects of MOS and VIRG on gene expression in a Salmonella LPS-induced systemic inflammation chicken model.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular analysis of imipenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolated from US service members wounded in Iraq, 2003-2008.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaOXA-23 and blaOXA-51 as the primary genes responsible for imipenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from US service members. Additionally, ISAba1 was implicated in the overexpression of OXA-51, contributing to resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, plasmid transformation, PFGE, and MLST were used to characterize resistance mechanisms and genetic relationships among isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of sterilized human fecal extract on the sensitivity of Escherichia coli ATCC 25922 to enrofloxacin.

gyrA.notes: No mutations in the QRDR region of gyrA were found in E. coli ATCC 25922.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that sterilized human fecal extract increased the growth of E. coli ATCC 25922 in the presence of enrofloxacin, suggesting that the extract may contain factors that enhance bacterial resistance to the antibiotic. No mutations in the QRDR region of gyrA were detected.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR amplification and sequencing analysis to detect mutations in the QRDR region of gyrA, and growth kinetics assays to assess the effect of sterilized fecal extract on E. coli ATCC 25922.

full_output.paper_title: Global regulation of gene expression by OxyR in an important human opportunistic pathogen.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies OxyR as a global regulator of gene expression in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, highlighting its role in oxidative stress response and other cellular processes.
full_output.methodology: ChIP-chip, EMSA, qRT-PCR, and Western blot analysis were used to investigate OxyR's regulatory targets and mechanisms.

full_output.key_findings: The study focused on improving the drug loading and antibacterial activity of minocycline-loaded PLGA nanoparticles using a solid/oil/water ion pairing method. The results showed that the nanoparticles had enhanced drug entrapment efficiency and exhibited higher antibacterial activity compared to free minocycline.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the preparation of PLGA nanoparticles using various methods, including emulsification, nanoprecipitation, and ion pairing. The nanoparticles were characterized for size, morphology, drug loading, and antibacterial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative genomics and drug resistance of a geographic variant of ST239 methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus emerged in Russia.

ccrC1.mechanism: confers resistance to chloramphenicol and rifampicin

tetM.mechanism: confers resistance to tetracycline and minocycline

rpoB.mechanism: mutant forms confer resistance to rifampicin

grlA.mechanism: mutant forms confer resistance to levofloxacin

gyrA.mechanism: mutant forms confer resistance to levofloxacin

rpoB.notes: Mutation in rpoB gene leads to rifampicin resistance.

grlA.notes: Mutation in grlA gene leads to levofloxacin resistance.

gyrA.notes: Mutation in gyrA gene leads to levofloxacin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes a Russian variant of ST239 methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) with unique genomic features and drug resistance mechanisms, including mutations in rpoB, grlA, and gyrA genes leading to resistance against rifampicin and levofloxacin, as well as the presence of the tetM gene for tetracycline resistance and the ccrC1 gene for chloramphenicol and rifampicin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, mutational analysis, and conjugative transfer experiments were conducted to characterize the drug resistance mechanisms in the Russian variant of ST239 MRSA.
full_output.sample_size: 13 MRSA strains from outpatients and 18 MRSA strains from inpatients

full_output.paper_title: RNA-seq based transcriptional map of bovine respiratory disease pathogen "Histophilus somni 2336".
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a comprehensive transcriptome map of H. somni 2336, identifying 94 sRNAs, 38 novel protein-coding genes, and correcting gene annotations. It highlights the utility of RNA-Seq in discovering non-coding RNAs and improving genome annotation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized RNA-Seq to analyze the transcriptome of H. somni 2336, leading to the identification of novel sRNAs and protein-coding genes, as well as corrections to existing genome annotations.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanisms of acquired crizotinib resistance in ALK-rearranged lung Cancers.

ALK.notes: These mutations were identified in crizotinib-resistant patients and confirmed through sequencing and cell line experiments.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several ALK mutations (L1196M, G1202R, S1206Y, and 1151Tins) that confer resistance to crizotinib in ALK-rearranged lung cancers. These mutations were validated through sequencing and cell line experiments.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of ALK TK domain, cell line experiments, and FISH analysis.

full_output.paper_title: A systematic review of gyrase mutations associated with fluoroquinolone-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis and a proposed gyrase numbering system.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in gyrA codons 90, 91, and 94 are commonly associated with fluoroquinolone resistance.

gyrB.notes: Mutations in gyrB codons 461, 470, 499, 500, 504, and 538 are associated with fluoroquinolone resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various mutations in the gyrA and gyrB genes of Mycobacterium tuberculosis that are associated with fluoroquinolone resistance, highlighting the importance of these mutations in molecular detection of resistance.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review of studies reporting mutations in DNA gyrase genes in clinical M. tuberculosis isolates, with biochemical validation of resistance-conferring mutations.

full_output.paper_title: IncP-1ε Plasmids are Important Vectors of Antibiotic Resistance Genes in Agricultural Systems: Diversification Driven by Class 1 Integron Gene Cassettes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies IncP-1ε plasmids as significant vectors for antibiotic resistance genes in agricultural systems, highlighting the role of class 1 integron gene cassettes in their diversification. Key resistance genes such as sul1, aadA, aadB, dfrA1b, and catB were characterized.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PCR, hybridization, Southern blotting, and sequencing to characterize IncP-1ε plasmids and their resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Novel bacterial metabolite merochlorin A demonstrates in vitro activity against multi-drug resistant methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies merochlorin A as a novel compound with in vitro activity against multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, including MRSA and VRE, without cross-resistance to current antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The compound was isolated from a marine actinomycete, and its activity was tested using broth microdilution and agar dilution methods against various bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: A new model for raf kinase inhibitory protein induced chemotherapeutic resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that RKIP depletion leads to increased NRF2 activation, which is associated with chemotherapeutic resistance in cancer cells. This occurs through the stabilization of KEAP1 and subsequent upregulation of antioxidant and detoxification genes.
full_output.methodology: The study used Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and gene expression analyses to investigate the role of RKIP in chemotherapeutic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of a mosaic locus in the genome of 'Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus'.

CLIBASIA_05650.notes: The insertion in CLIBASIA_05650 leads to a 24-amino-acid repeat unit, creating an in-frame mutation.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a mosaic locus in the genome of 'Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus' associated with citrus Huanglongbing (HLB), revealing significant genetic diversity among strains from different geographic regions. Insertion/deletion events at the CLIBASIA_05650 locus contribute to the observed DNA mosaicism.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, DNA sequencing, and bioinformatics analysis were used to investigate genetic variation in 'Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus' strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports high levels of drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) in North India, with particular emphasis on multidrug-resistant (MDR) TB cases. It identifies resistance to first-line anti-TB drugs such as rifampicin, isoniazid, streptomycin, and ethambutol.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted drug-susceptibility testing (DST) using the proportion method on Lowenstein-Jensen medium for MTB isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis: Mechanisms and Targets
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the characterization of several adenylating enzymes involved in antimicrobial resistance in M. tuberculosis, including BirA, FadD, and others, highlighting their roles in lipid metabolism and potential as drug targets.
full_output.methodology: The study involves biochemical characterization, kinetic analysis, and structural studies of adenylating enzymes in M. tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: The genome and proteome of a Campylobacter coli bacteriophage vB_CcoM-IBB_35 reveal unusual features.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the genome and proteome of the Campylobacter coli bacteriophage vB_CcoM-IBB_35, identifying unique features such as genes involved in nucleotide metabolism, replication, morphogenesis, and lysis, including a lysozyme associated with the tail and genes encoding for tail fibers and a lytic cassette.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, proteomic analysis via SDS-PAGE and mass spectrometry, and bioinformatics tools for annotation and comparison with other phages.

full_output.paper_title: Expression of Escherichia coli virulence usher protein attenuates wild-type Salmonella.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that overexpression of the E. coli CFA/I fimbriae, particularly the usher gene CfaC, can attenuate wild-type Salmonella, making it less virulent and capable of conferring protection against subsequent infections.
full_output.methodology: The study used recombinant Salmonella strains with modified cfa/I operons, along with in vitro macrophage infection assays and in vivo mouse models to evaluate the effects of CFA/I fimbriae overexpression on Salmonella virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Food as a source for quorum sensing inhibitors: iberin from horseradish revealed as a quorum sensing inhibitor of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies iberin, a quorum sensing inhibitor (QSI) from horseradish, which specifically targets the QS networks in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, leading to downregulation of QS-controlled genes and reduced rhamnolipid production.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of bioassay-guided fractionation, LC-DAD-MS, NMR spectroscopy, and transcriptomic analysis to identify and characterize iberin as a QSI.

full_output.paper_title: Reduced aeration affects the expression of the NorB efflux pump of Staphylococcus aureus by posttranslational modification of MgrA.
full_output.key_findings: Reduced aeration increases the expression of the NorB efflux pump in Staphylococcus aureus, leading to increased resistance to moxifloxacin and sparfloxacin.
full_output.methodology: MIC assays, real-time RT-PCR, Western blotting, and mass spectrometry.

full_output.paper_title: Polyadenylation helps regulate functional tRNA levels in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pcnB as a gene involved in the polyadenylation of tRNA and 5S rRNA precursors, which affects their stability and maturation in Escherichia coli.
full_output.methodology: Northern blot analysis, poly(A) sizing assay, Western blot analysis, and genetic manipulation of E. coli strains.

full_output.paper_title: SpyA is a membrane-bound ADP-ribosyltransferase of Streptococcus pyogenes which modifies a streptococcal peptide, SpyB.
full_output.key_findings: SpyA is a membrane-bound ADP-ribosyltransferase that modifies SpyB, a small peptide, through ADP-ribosylation. SpyB is localized to the streptococcal membrane and is a substrate for SpyA.
full_output.methodology: Expression, localization, and functional assays of SpyA and SpyB in Streptococcus pyogenes.

full_output.paper_title: Role of mixed ion channel effects in the cardiovascular safety assessment of the novel anti-MRSA fluoroquinolone JNJ-Q2
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the cardiovascular safety of JNJ-Q2, a novel fluoroquinolone with anti-MRSA activity, focusing on its effects on ion channels and QT interval prolongation. It highlights the importance of mixed ion channel effects in mitigating QT prolongation and torsades de pointes risk.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro and in vivo models including hERG assays, sodium and calcium channel recordings, and ECG monitoring in guinea pigs and dogs, along with a clinical thorough QT study in humans.

full_output.paper_title: Novel functions for glycosyltransferases Jhp0562 and GalT in Lewis antigen synthesis and variation in Helicobacter pylori.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies jhp0562 and galT as essential genes for Lewis antigen synthesis in Helicobacter pylori, demonstrating their roles in both type 1 and type 2 pathways through mutagenesis and complementation experiments.
full_output.methodology: Mutagenesis, complementation analysis, PCR, and ELISA were used to validate the roles of jhp0562 and galT in Lewis antigen synthesis.

full_output.paper_title: Hyperinduction of host beta interferon by a Listeria monocytogenes strain naturally overexpressing the multidrug efflux pump MdrT.

full_output.paper_title: Charge distribution and imperfect amphipathicity affect pore formation by antimicrobial peptides.
full_output.key_findings: Mutations in antimicrobial peptides alter pore formation mechanisms, highlighting the importance of charged residues and helical structure in determining pore type.
full_output.methodology: Molecular dynamics simulations were used to analyze the impact of mutations on pore formation by antimicrobial peptides.

full_output.paper_title: Cloning and characterization of two glutathione S-transferases from pyrethroid-resistant Culex pipiens.
full_output.key_findings: Two glutathione S-transferase genes, CpGSTd1 and CpGSTd2, were cloned and characterized from pyrethroid-resistant Culex pipiens. They belong to the Delta class of GSTs and exhibit distinct biochemical properties, although they do not appear to play a major role in permethrin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Molecular cloning, bacterial expression, and biochemical characterization of the recombinant GSTs.

full_output.paper_title: Association of the emerging carbapenemase NDM-1 with a bleomycin resistance protein in Enterobacteriaceae and Acinetobacter baumannii.

ble MBL.validation_method: expression in E. coli and MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel bleomycin resistance protein, BRP MBL, associated with the carbapenemase NDM-1 in Enterobacteriaceae and Acinetobacter baumannii, which confers resistance to bleomycin and zeocin.
full_output.methodology: Expression of the ble MBL gene in E. coli and determination of MICs for bleomycin and zeocin.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical and Microbiologic Characteristics of Cephalosporin-Resistant Escherichia coli at Three Centers in the United States.

blaCTX-M-15.mechanism: hydrolysis of cephalosporins and other beta-lactam antibiotics

blaCMY-2.mechanism: hydrolysis of cephalosporins and other beta-lactam antibiotics

blaKPC.mechanism: hydrolysis of carbapenems and other beta-lactam antibiotics

full_output.key_findings: The study identified CTX-M-15 as the most common ESBL in cephalosporin-resistant E. coli, followed by CMY-2, SHV, TEM, and KPC beta-lactamases. These genes confer resistance to various beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to identify beta-lactamase genes in cephalosporin-resistant E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Nosocomial outbreak of Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella oxytoca in Austria.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports a clonal outbreak of KPC-producing Klebsiella oxytoca in Austria, highlighting the emergence of carbapenem resistance in this species.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective observational study, PCR, rep-PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various penA alleles associated with reduced penicillin susceptibility in Neisseria meningitidis isolates in Belgium from 2000 to 2010.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, sequencing of the penA gene, and statistical analysis.

full_output.paper_title: MurAA is required for intrinsic cephalosporin resistance of Enterococcus faecalis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies murAA as a crucial gene for intrinsic cephalosporin resistance in Enterococcus faecalis, showing that its deletion increases susceptibility to cephalosporins and that its catalytic activity is necessary but not sufficient for resistance.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, gene deletion, complementation, and enzymatic assays were used to investigate the role of murAA in cephalosporin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: An antibiotic that inhibits a late step in wall teichoic acid biosynthesis induces the cell wall stress stimulon in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: Targocil, an inhibitor of the late step in wall teichoic acid (WTA) biosynthesis, induces the cell wall stress stimulon in Staphylococcus aureus, causing morphological abnormalities and reducing the expression of virulence genes.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptional profiling and transmission electron microscopy were used to analyze the effects of targocil on S. aureus.

aac(6')-Ie/aph(2'')-Ia.validation_method: structural analysis via small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS)

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the structure of the bifunctional antibiotic resistance enzyme aac(6')-Ie/aph(2'')-Ia, revealing a rigid solution structure that may enhance enzymatic properties and resistance to aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: Small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) analysis to determine the solution structure of the enzyme.

full_output.paper_title: Alterations of OprD in carbapenem-intermediate and -susceptible strains of Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from patients with bacteremia in a Spanish multicenter study.

oprD.notes: Mutations in oprD were associated with reduced expression of the porin and increased carbapenem MICs.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the oprD gene, which encodes the outer membrane porin OprD, leading to reduced expression and increased carbapenem resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains.
full_output.methodology: The study used sequencing analysis, outer membrane protein analysis, and real-time PCR to investigate oprD mutations and their effects on carbapenem susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Deciphering the magainin resistance process of Escherichia coli strains in light of the cytosolic proteome.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies differentially expressed proteins in magainin-resistant Escherichia coli strains, highlighting metabolic adaptations including energy metabolism, nitrogen metabolism, stress response, and amino acid metabolism.
full_output.methodology: Comparative proteomic analysis using two-dimensional electrophoresis and mass spectrometry to identify differentially expressed proteins in magainin-resistant and susceptible E. coli strains.

full_output.paper_title: Involvement of the AcrAB-TolC efflux pump in the resistance, fitness, and virulence of Enterobacter cloacae.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the AcrAB-TolC efflux pump plays a critical role in the resistance, fitness, and virulence of Enterobacter cloacae. Deletion of acrA or tolC leads to increased susceptibility to multiple antibiotics, reduced fitness, and decreased virulence in a mouse model.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic knockout techniques, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and competition experiments in vitro and in vivo to evaluate the role of the AcrAB-TolC efflux pump.

full_output.paper_title: Small plasmids harboring qnrB19: a model for plasmid evolution mediated by site-specific recombination at oriT and Xer sites.

qnrB19.mechanism: protects type II DNA topoisomerases from quinolone action
qnrB19.validation_method: plasmid sequencing and comparison with other qnrB19-harboring plasmids

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies small plasmids harboring the qnrB19 gene, which confers quinolone resistance. These plasmids exhibit a conserved genetic environment and are involved in plasmid evolution through site-specific recombination at oriT and Xer sites.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid sequencing, PCR, and bioinformatic analysis were used to characterize the genetic environment of qnrB19 and its role in plasmid evolution.

full_output.paper_title: Novel variants of AbaR resistance islands with a common backbone in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates of European clone II.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies novel variants of AbaR resistance islands in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates of European clone II, including genes such as strA, strB, tetB, aacA4, catB8, aadA1, blaOXA-23, and blaOXA-72, which confer resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the resistance genes and structures of AbaR islands.

full_output.paper_title: Contrasting epidemic histories reveal pathogen-mediated balancing selection on class II MHC diversity in a wild songbird.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that house finches with intermediate to high multi-locus class II MHC diversity exhibited greater resistance to Mycoplasma gallisepticum (MG) infection, indicating pathogen-mediated balancing selection on MHC diversity.
full_output.methodology: The study used experimental infection challenges, SSCP analysis, and molecular sequence analyses to investigate MHC diversity and its association with resistance to MG.

full_output.paper_title: Spread of epidemic MRSA-ST5-IV clone encoding PVL as a major cause of community onset staphylococcal infections in Argentinean children.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the ST5-IV-PVL+ clone as a major cause of community-onset staphylococcal infections in Argentinean children, highlighting the spread of this epidemic MRSA clone.
full_output.methodology: Molecular typing, PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Crosstalk between virulence loci: regulation of Salmonella enterica pathogenicity island 1 (SPI-1) by products of the std fimbrial operon.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the stdE and stdF genes as part of the std fimbrial operon, which are involved in Dam-dependent control of Salmonella SPI-1. Deletion of stdE or stdF suppresses SPI-1 repression in a Dam- background, while constitutive expression of StdE and StdF represses SPI-1. These findings explain the invasion defect of Salmonella Dam- mutants and demonstrate that StdEF-mediated repression of SPI-1 prevents invasion in inappropriate environments.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screening, plasmid library construction, β-galactosidase assays, Western blotting, and invasion assays in HeLa cells and mice.

full_output.paper_title: Novel AlkB dioxygenases--alternative models for in silico and in vivo studies.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes novel AlkB homologs from cyanobacteria and Arabidopsis thaliana, demonstrating their roles in repairing alkylation lesions in DNA and RNA. Several cyanobacterial AlkB homologs were shown to complement the E. coli alkB mutant, enhancing phage survival after treatment with alkylating agents.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics analysis, plasmid construction, phage survival assays, and subcellular localization studies were conducted to characterize the AlkB homologs.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmid-cured Chlamydia caviae activates TLR2-dependent signaling and retains virulence in the guinea pig model of genital tract infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that plasmid-deficient C. caviae strain CC13 retains TLR2-dependent signaling and virulence in the guinea pig model, indicating that the plasmid is not essential for these functions.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, RT-PCR, and in vitro and in vivo infection models to analyze the effects of plasmid deficiency in C. caviae.

full_output.paper_title: Site-specific integration of foreign DNA into minimal bacterial and human target sequences mediated by a conjugative relaxase.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the site-specific integration capabilities of the TrwC relaxase, demonstrating its ability to mediate integration into bacterial and human target sequences, highlighting its potential for genomic engineering applications.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic assays, plasmid construction, and molecular biology techniques including PCR, restriction analysis, and transformation to investigate TrwC-mediated integration.

full_output.paper_title: The structural basis for substrate versatility of chloramphenicol acetyltransferase CATI.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the structure and function of chloramphenicol acetyltransferase CATI, demonstrating its ability to inactivate chloramphenicol and bind fusidic acid, providing insights into its substrate versatility.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis using X-ray crystallography and enzymatic activity assays.

full_output.paper_title: Natural competence is a major mechanism for horizontal DNA transfer in the oral pathogen Porphyromonas gingivalis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies comF as a critical gene for natural competence in Porphyromonas gingivalis, enabling DNA uptake and transformation.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, DNA transfer assays, and mutant analysis were used to investigate DNA exchange mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Extraintestinal Pathogenic Escherichia coli: A Combination of Virulence with Antibiotic Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the emergence of multidrug-resistant extraintestinal pathogenic E. coli (ExPEC) strains, particularly those producing newer beta-lactamases such as CTX-M, CMY, and NDM, which confer resistance to various beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Literature review and analysis of clinical data on antibiotic resistance in E. coli.
full_output.sample_size: various clinical isolates from different regions

full_output.paper_title: The ζ toxin induces a set of protective responses and dormancy.
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the ζ toxin and its effects on Bacillus subtilis, including the induction of dormancy and permeability to propidium iodide (PI). It also examines the role of the ε 2 antitoxin in reversing these effects.
full_output.methodology: The study uses genetic manipulation, transcriptome analysis, and biochemical assays to investigate the effects of the ζ toxin and ε 2 antitoxin on B. subtilis.

full_output.paper_title: The increased expression of integrin α6 (ITGA6) enhances drug resistance in EVI1(high) leukemia.
full_output.key_findings: Increased expression of ITGA6 and ITGB4 in EVI1 high leukemia cells enhances cell adhesion to laminin complexes, contributing to drug resistance. Downregulation of these genes restores chemo-sensitivity.
full_output.methodology: Gene expression analysis, cell adhesion assays, siRNA knockdown, and flow cytometry.

full_output.paper_title: A bile-inducible membrane protein mediates bifidobacterial bile resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Bbr_0838 as a bile-inducible membrane protein that plays a crucial role in bile tolerance in Bifidobacterium breve UCC2003. Insertional inactivation of Bbr_0838 reduces bile tolerance, and complementation restores the wild-type phenotype.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, complementation, and transcriptomic analysis were used to assess the role of Bbr_0838 in bile tolerance.

full_output.paper_title: The effect of Clostridium perfringens type C strain CN3685 and its isogenic beta toxin null mutant in goats.

mutations_found.nucleotide_change: insertion of a targeted group II intron
mutations_found.validated_by: characterization studies confirmed that this insertional event had inactivated CPB production
characterization studies confirmed that this insertional event had inactivated CPB production

cpb.notes: The cpb gene was modified in the mutant strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrated that the beta toxin (CPB) of Clostridium perfringens type C is essential for inducing disease in goats. The CPB null mutant failed to cause clinical signs, while the reversed mutant showed partial virulence.
full_output.methodology: Construction and testing of isogenic CPB null and reversed mutants in a goat model.

full_output.paper_title: Injection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Exo toxins into host cells can be modulated by host factors at the level of translocon assembly and/or activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the use of ExoS-Bla and ExoY-Bla fusion proteins as reporters for monitoring the translocation efficiency of Pseudomonas aeruginosa type III secretion system (T3SS) in various cell lines.
full_output.methodology: Flow cytometry and fluorescence microscopy were used to assess the translocation efficiency of ExoS-Bla and ExoY-Bla fusion proteins in different cell lines.

full_output.paper_title: Patient's origin and lifestyle associated with CTX-M-producing Escherichia coli: a case-control-control study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified factors associated with CTX-M-producing E. coli infections, including patient's origin outside Europe, chronic infections, and antibiotic treatment.
full_output.methodology: The study used a case-control-control design to analyze factors associated with CTX-M-producing E. coli infections in hospitalized patients.
full_output.sample_size: 152 cases with two controls for each case (304)

eds1.encodes: a negative regulator of SA signaling
eds1.notes: mutant shows increased susceptibility to Xcc

eds5.encodes: a component of the SA signaling pathway
eds5.notes: mutant shows increased susceptibility to Xcc

pad4.encodes: a component of the SA signaling pathway
pad4.notes: mutant shows increased susceptibility to Xcc

sid2.encodes: a key enzyme in SA biosynthesis
sid2.notes: mutant shows increased susceptibility to Xcc

npr1.encodes: a central regulator of SA signaling
npr1.notes: mutant shows increased susceptibility to Xcc

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the role of SA signaling pathway genes in non-host resistance against Xcc in Arabidopsis, highlighting the importance of EDS1, EDS5, PAD4, and NPR1 in mediating resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genetic and molecular analysis of Arabidopsis mutants to assess their susceptibility to Xcc.

full_output.paper_title: First evaluation of an improved assay for molecular genetic detection of tuberculosis as well as rifampin and isoniazid resistances.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the MTBDRplus 2.0 assay for detecting Mycobacterium tuberculosis and mutations conferring resistance to rifampin (RMP) and isoniazid (INH). Key mutations identified include S531L in rpoB for RMP resistance and S315T in katG, along with C15T and A16G in inhA for INH resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used the MTBDRplus 2.0 assay to detect MTBC and analyze resistance mutations in clinical specimens, comparing results with culture and DST.

full_output.paper_title: Determinants of murein hydrolase targeting to cross-wall of Staphylococcus aureus peptidoglycan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the roles of LysM domains in the targeting of murein hydrolases LytN and Sle1 to the cross-wall of Staphylococcus aureus peptidoglycan. It shows that LysM domains bind to the repeating disaccharide β-N-acetylmuramic acid-(1→4)-β-N-acetylglucosamine of peptidoglycan, and that wall teichoic acid modification prevents this binding. The research highlights the importance of LysM domains for the correct localization and function of these hydrolases in cell wall splitting and separation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic manipulation, fluorescence cytometry, microscopy, and biochemical assays to investigate the role of LysM domains in the targeting of murein hydrolases to the cross-wall of Staphylococcus aureus peptidoglycan.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the H58 haplotype as the dominant S. Typhi population in Kolkata, associated with multidrug resistance (MDR) and quinolone resistance. H58-G showed high levels of nalidixic acid resistance and reduced susceptibility to ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: SNP haplotyping and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze S. Typhi isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Salmonella Enteritidis strains from poultry exhibit differential responses to acid stress, oxidative stress, and survival in the egg albumen.

rpoS.notes: Mutations in rpoS gene affecting stress response

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of the SOS response of Vibrio and other bacteria with multiple chromosomes.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the SOS regulon in the Vibrionaceae family, identifying several genes regulated by LexA, including novel genes such as unfA (VP1264) and unfB (VP1428), which may be involved in pathogenicity and antibiotic resistance. It also highlights the role of the SOS response in the dissemination of antibiotic resistance and pathogenicity in Vibrio species.
full_output.methodology: The study combines in silico and in vitro techniques, including comparative genomics analysis and electrophoresis mobility shift assays (EMSA), to investigate the SOS regulon in Vibrionaceae and other bacterial groups with multiple chromosomes.

full_output.paper_title: Listeria monocytogenes Shows Temperature-Dependent and -Independent Responses to Salt Stress, Including Responses That Induce Cross-Protection against Other Stresses.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the mrpABCDEFG operon as a key player in Listeria monocytogenes' adaptation to salt stress, demonstrating its importance in resisting osmotic stress at both 7°C and 37°C.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis and deletion mutant studies were used to investigate gene expression and functional roles in salt stress adaptation.

full_output.paper_title: Commercially distributed meat as a potential vehicle for community-acquired methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) strains in commercially distributed meat and human diarrheal stool samples, suggesting that meat could be a potential source of community-acquired MRSA.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed meat and stool samples for MRSA using culture, PCR, and molecular typing techniques.
full_output.sample_size: 197 meat samples and 1,287 diarrheal stool samples

full_output.paper_title: In-feed antibiotic effects on the swine intestinal microbiome.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that in-feed antibiotics increased the abundance and diversity of antibiotic resistance genes in the swine gut microbiome, including resistance to antibiotics not administered, and increased the abundance of E. coli, a potential human pathogen.
full_output.methodology: Phylotype, metagenomic, and qPCR approaches were used to assess the impact of antibiotics on the swine microbiome.

full_output.paper_title: Assembly and Channel Opening of Outer Membrane Protein in Tripartite Drug Efflux Pumps of Gram-negative Bacteria
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the structural and functional analysis of the outer membrane protein OprM and its interaction with the membrane fusion protein MexA in the tripartite drug efflux pump of Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The research elucidates the assembly and channel opening mechanism of the MexAB-OprM pump, highlighting the critical role of the α-hairpin domain of MexA in binding to OprM.
full_output.methodology: Structural biology techniques including X-ray crystallography and electron microscopy were employed to analyze the interactions between MexA and OprM.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence strategies of the dominant USA300 lineage of community-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CA-MRSA).
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the virulence strategies of the USA300 lineage of community-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CA-MRSA), highlighting the role of specific genes such as sec, seq, lukS-PV, lukF-PV, hla, and hld in its pathogenicity.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature and analyzes the genetic and virulence characteristics of the USA300 lineage of CA-MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: IcsA autotransporter passenger promotes increased fusion protein expression on the cell surface.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the IcsA autotransporter passenger domain enhances the surface expression of fusion proteins, including TEM-1 beta-lactamase (Bla), leading to increased ampicillin resistance in E. coli K-12 UT5600.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic engineering, SDS-PAGE, Western blotting, and ampicillin susceptibility testing to analyze the expression and functionality of IcsA and IcsA β fusion proteins.

full_output.paper_title: Risk factors for vancomycin-resistant enterococci colonisation in critically ill patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies vanC as a gene responsible for low-level vancomycin resistance in Enterococcus gallinarum and Enterococcus casseliflavus, highlighting its role in hospital settings.
full_output.methodology: Active surveillance cultures and susceptibility testing were conducted to identify vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) and analyze risk factors for colonization.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of modifications in microbial, native tRNA that suppress immunostimulatory activity.

G m 18.validation_method: experimental validation through molecular surgery and modulation of tRNA

G m 34.validation_method: experimental validation through molecular surgery and modulation of tRNA

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies G m 18 and G m 34 as critical 2'-O-methyl modifications in tRNA that suppress immunostimulatory activity by modulating TLR7 recognition.
full_output.methodology: Experimental validation through molecular surgery, tRNA modification analysis, and immunostimulatory assays.

full_output.paper_title: Helicobacter pylori CagA triggers expression of the bactericidal lectin REG3γ via gastric STAT3 activation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies REG3γ as a transcriptional target of the H. pylori cytotoxin CagA, highlighting its role in gastric immunity and the involvement of IL-11 and STAT3 signaling in its regulation.
full_output.methodology: The study uses in vitro cell models, quantitative PCR, and immunoblotting to investigate the role of CagA in regulating REG3γ expression.

full_output.paper_title: Integrating Conjugative Elements as Vectors of Antibiotic, Mercury, and Quaternary Ammonium Compound Resistance in Marine Aquaculture Environments
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SXT/R391-like integrating conjugative elements (ICEs) carrying antibiotic, mercury, and quaternary ammonium compound (QAC) resistance genes in marine aquaculture environments. Novel resistance determinants, including rifampin resistance (arr) and QAC resistance (qacL), were discovered and functionally validated.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, conjugation experiments, and resistance profiling were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes in the ICEs.

full_output.paper_title: Efflux pumps of Mycobacterium tuberculosis play a significant role in antituberculosis activity of potential drug candidates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified four efflux pumps in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Rv1218c, Rv1258c, Rv0849, and Rv3065) that play significant roles in mediating the efflux of various chemical classes and antibiotics. Inhibitors of these pumps, such as verapamil and PAβN, increased the susceptibility of M. tuberculosis to different compounds.
full_output.methodology: The study generated knockout mutants of four efflux pumps and tested their susceptibility to various compounds using MIC and bactericidality assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that ajoene, a compound derived from garlic, can inhibit quorum sensing (QS) in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, leading to reduced virulence and improved antibiotic efficacy. Ajoene was shown to downregulate QS-controlled genes, including rhlA, and reduce rhamnolipid production, which is associated with PMN lysis.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized bioassays, transcriptome analysis, and in vivo experiments to investigate the effects of ajoene on QS and virulence in P. aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Cotrimoxazole Prophylaxis Specifically Selects for Cotrimoxazole Resistance in Streptococcus mutans and Streptococcus sobrinus with Varied Polymorphisms in the Target Genes folA and folP.
full_output.key_findings: Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis selects for cotrimoxazole resistance in Streptococcus mutans and Streptococcus sobrinus, with varied polymorphisms in the folP gene contributing to resistance.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of folA and folP genes, cloning, and functional analysis in E. coli.

full_output.key_findings: The study focused on the population dynamics of uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) during urinary tract infection (UTI) using isogenic tagged clones. It revealed that UPEC lineages exhibit metapopulation behavior, with dynamic shifts in abundance and distribution across organs. The research highlighted the impact of host environment factors on bacterial population structure and identified barriers to bacterial ascension and dissemination.
full_output.methodology: The study used Tn7 transposon tagging to create isogenic UPEC clones, followed by quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) to track tag abundance in mouse organs during UTI. Principal component analysis (PCA) and nonmetric multidimensional scaling (nMDS) were employed to analyze population dynamics.

full_output.paper_title: Type III secretion and effectors shape the survival and growth pattern of Pseudomonas syringae on leaf surfaces.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the roles of the T3SS, HopAA1, and HopZ3 in the epiphytic survival and growth of Pseudomonas syringae on plant surfaces, highlighting their host-specific functions.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized quantitative microscopy, leaf wash assays, and genetic manipulation to analyze the impact of T3SS and effectors on bacterial survival and growth.

full_output.paper_title: Discrete cyclic di-GMP-dependent control of bacterial predation versus axenic growth in Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes five GGDEF domain proteins (DgcA, DgcB, DgcC, DgcD, and CdgA) in Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus, highlighting their roles in regulating c-di-GMP signaling pathways that control predatory and axenic growth. DgcA is involved in gliding motility, DgcB in prey invasion, DgcC in the transition to axenic growth, and CdgA functions as a c-di-GMP receptor critical for rapid prey entry.
full_output.methodology: Genetic deletion analysis, biochemical characterization, and fluorescent protein localization were used to study the functions of GGDEF domain proteins in Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic pathway in acquisition and loss of vancomycin resistance in a methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) strain of clonal type USA300.

yvqF.evidence_note: The paper states that the mutation in yvqF (Y220C) caused over-expression of the vraS transcript, leading to increased vancomycin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in yvqF and vraS as critical for vancomycin resistance in a VISA strain of MRSA USA300, with yvqF acting as a negative regulator of the vraSR operon.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, complementation experiments, qRT-PCR, and MIC testing.

full_output.paper_title: A bacterial acetyltransferase destroys plant microtubule networks and blocks secretion.
full_output.key_findings: HopZ1a is an acetyltransferase that binds to tubulin and microtubules, leading to microtubule network destruction and suppression of plant defense mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Protein binding assays, acetylation assays, microtubule co-sedimentation, in planta growth assays, and confocal microscopy.

full_output.paper_title: First initial community-acquired meningitis due to extended-spectrum beta-lactamase producing Escherichia coli complicated with multiple aortic mycotic aneurysms.
full_output.key_findings: The case report describes an extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli causing community-acquired meningitis complicated with multiple aortic mycotic aneurysms, highlighting the resistance profile of the isolate.
full_output.methodology: Clinical case report with microbiological analysis including MIC testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that 90% of turkey flocks were positive for MRSA, with spa types t011, t002, t1456, t034, and t2330 identified. MRSA was also detected in 37.3% of people working on turkey farms. The predominant spa type was t011, and resistance to various antibiotics was observed, including tetracycline, oxacillin, erythromycin, and clindamycin.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed swab samples from turkeys, dust, and humans using molecular techniques such as PCR, spa-typing, SCC mec-typing, and MLST to identify MRSA and determine resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Effects of doxycycline on gene expression in Wolbachia and Brugia malayi adult female worms in vivo.
full_output.key_findings: Doxycycline treatment led to significant down-regulation of Wolbachia genes involved in protein synthesis, DNA replication, and energy metabolism, while some genes related to energy metabolism and nucleic acid repair were up-regulated.
full_output.methodology: Microarray analysis and qRT-PCR were used to analyze gene expression changes in Wolbachia and Brugia malayi after doxycycline treatment.

full_output.paper_title: Microcolonies in fluoroquinolone agar proportion susceptibility testing of Mycobacterium tuberculosis: an indicator of drug resistance.

gyrA.notes: Only one isolate had this mutation.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies microcolonies as an indicator of fluoroquinolone resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, with confirmation of the Ala90Val mutation in the QRDR of gyrA in two ofloxacin-resistant isolates.
full_output.methodology: Agar proportion susceptibility testing, PCR, sequencing of the quinolone resistance-determining region (QRDR) of gyrA and gyrB.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of gene mutations associated with isoniazid, rifampicin and ethambutol resistance among Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the katG gene (Ser315Thr1) and inhA gene (C15T) associated with isoniazid resistance, mutations in the rpoB gene (Ser531Leu, His526Asp) linked to rifampicin resistance, and mutations in the embB gene (Met306Ile, Met306Val) related to ethambutol resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Ethiopia.
full_output.methodology: GenoType MTBDRplus and MTBDRsl assays, BacT/ALERT 3D system drug susceptibility testing.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized biochemical assays, mutagenesis, and mathematical modeling to investigate the mechanisms governing activation surges in two-component systems.

expression of mutant PSMB5 in hTERT-RPE1 cells

full_output.methodology: Transcriptome sequencing of drug-resistant clones and bioinformatics analysis to identify mutations in drug targets.

full_output.paper_title: Assessing the contributions of the LiaS histidine kinase to the innate resistance of Listeria monocytogenes to nisin, cephalosporins, and disinfectants.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LiaS as a key histidine kinase involved in the innate resistance of Listeria monocytogenes to nisin, cephalosporins, and disinfectants. Deletion of liaS leads to increased nisin resistance and decreased cephalosporin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used gene deletion mutants, antimicrobial sensitivity assays, and RT-PCR to analyze the role of LiaS in antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, enumeration, serotypes, and antimicrobial resistance phenotypes of salmonella enterica isolates from carcasses at two large United States pork processing plants.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple Salmonella enterica serotypes, including Typhimurium, Derby, and Anatum, with high prevalence on pork carcasses. Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Salmonella was found on 3.2% of final carcasses, highlighting the need for improved interventions to reduce AMR in pork processing.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed Salmonella isolates from pork carcasses using antimicrobial susceptibility testing and serotyping to assess resistance profiles and prevalence.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypes, exotoxin gene content, and antimicrobial resistance of Staphylococcus aureus strains recovered from foods and food handlers.

ermC.mechanism: confers resistance to erythromycin and clindamycin

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes in S. aureus strains from foods and food handlers, including blaZ, mupA, ermC, msrB, msrA, aacA, aphD, aadD, and tetK, which confer resistance to beta-lactams, mupirocin, erythromycin, clindamycin, aminoglycosides, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, MIC testing, and molecular typing techniques were used to identify AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the TEM-1 beta-lactamase gene and the aadA1 aminoglycoside adenyltransferase gene in Escherichia coli O55:H7 strain RM12579, which confer resistance to ampicillin and streptomycin, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and experimental validation of antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Novel, highly specific N-demethylases enable bacteria to live on caffeine and related purine alkaloids.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes the ndmA, ndmB, and ndmD genes in Pseudomonas putida CBB5, which encode N1- and N3-specific methylxanthine demethylases and a reductase involved in caffeine metabolism.
full_output.methodology: Cloning, heterologous expression, and biochemical characterization of the ndm genes in E. coli.

rmtC.validation_method: MALDI mass spectrometry and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies RmtC as an aminoglycoside resistance methyltransferase that methylates G1405 in 16S rRNA, leading to high-level resistance against various aminoglycosides. It also shows that RmtC does not impose a significant fitness cost on E. coli.
full_output.methodology: Generation of mutant strains, MALDI mass spectrometry, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Crystal structures of KPC-2 β-lactamase in complex with 3-nitrophenyl boronic acid and the penam sulfone PSR-3-226.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes KPC-2 β-lactamase and identifies 3-NPBA and PSR-3-226 as inhibitors that form acyl-enzyme complexes with KPC-2, providing structural insights for inhibitor design.
full_output.methodology: X-ray crystallography and enzyme inhibition assays were used to analyze the interaction of KPC-2 with 3-NPBA and PSR-3-226.

full_output.paper_title: Computational analysis of pathogen-borne metallo β-lactamases reveals discriminating structural features between B1 types.

blaNDM-1.genetic_context: plasmid-borne
blaNDM-1.evidence_note: The paper states that NDM-1 is capable of hydrolyzing a broad range of antibiotics and confers resistance to all but a small handful of β-lactam antimicrobials.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies structural features of the NDM-1 metallo-beta-lactamase, highlighting a unique linker region that distinguishes it from other B1 MBLs and contributes to its broad substrate specificity and resistance profile.
full_output.methodology: Structural and sequence analysis of B1 MBLs, including NDM-1, using computational methods and structural alignment techniques.

full_output.paper_title: LytA, major autolysin of Streptococcus pneumoniae, requires access to nascent peptidoglycan.

lytA.validation_method: Mutant construction and complementation, immunoblot analysis, growth kinetics

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the localization and function of LytA, a major autolysin in Streptococcus pneumoniae, showing that it primarily resides in the cytoplasm and is released during stationary phase or cell wall synthesis inhibition, suggesting a regulatory mechanism involving peptidoglycan modifications.
full_output.methodology: The study uses biochemical and molecular biological approaches including immunoblotting, growth kinetics, and mutagenesis to analyze LytA's localization and function.

full_output.paper_title: Neisseria gonorrhoeae virulence factor NG1686 is a bifunctional M23B family metallopeptidase that influences resistance to hydrogen peroxide and colony morphology.

ng1686.validation_method: mutant analysis and enzymatic activity assays

full_output.key_findings: NG1686 is a bifunctional M23B family zinc metallopeptidase with endopeptidase and carboxypeptidase activities that influences resistance to hydrogen peroxide and colony morphology in Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
full_output.methodology: Mutant analysis, enzymatic activity assays, zymogram analysis, and HPLC/MS-based characterization of reaction products.

full_output.paper_title: Copper in microbial pathogenesis: meddling with the metal.
full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews the role of copper in microbial pathogenesis, focusing on copper resistance mechanisms in various bacteria, including the Cue system in Salmonella and E. coli, the CsoR system in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and other Cu resistance pathways in Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Listeria monocytogenes.
full_output.methodology: The paper summarizes experimental studies on copper resistance mechanisms in bacteria, including genetic analyses, mutant studies, and functional characterizations of copper-related genes.

full_output.paper_title: Heterogeneity in Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms includes expression of ribosome hibernation factors in the antibiotic-tolerant subpopulation and hypoxia-induced stress response in the metabolically active population.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the roles of rmf and PA4463 in ribosome hibernation, contributing to antibiotic tolerance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms.
full_output.methodology: Microarray analysis, laser capture microdissection, qRT-PCR, and mutant analysis were used to investigate gene expression and functionality in Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Novel colicin Fy of Yersinia frederiksenii inhibits pathogenic Yersinia strains via YiuR-mediated reception, TonB import, and cell membrane pore formation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel colicin, F Y, produced by Yersinia frederiksenii, which inhibits pathogenic Yersinia strains. The colicin F Y activity gene (cfyA) and immunity gene (cfyI) were characterized, along with the YiuR receptor and TonB import system necessary for its function.
full_output.methodology: The study involved cloning, sequencing, and susceptibility testing of colicin F Y, as well as transposon mutagenesis and complementation experiments to identify the receptor and import system.

full_output.paper_title: Passage of Campylobacter jejuni through the chicken reservoir or mice promotes phase variation in contingency genes Cj0045 and Cj0170 that strongly associates with colonization and disease in a mouse model.
full_output.key_findings: Phase variation in contingency genes Cj0045 and Cj0170 strongly correlates with enhanced colonization and disease in a mouse model. The 10G allele of Cj0170 and the 9G allele of Cj0045 are associated with successful colonization.
full_output.methodology: Fragment analysis, PCR, and colonization experiments in a mouse model.

full_output.paper_title: Transcriptome mapping of pAR060302, a blaCMY-2-positive broad-host-range IncA/C plasmid.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the transcriptome of pAR060302, a blaCMY-2-positive IncA/C plasmid, highlighting the transcription of resistance genes such as blaCMY-2, aadA, aacA, and floR, which confer resistance to extended-spectrum cephalosporins, aminoglycosides, and phenicols, respectively.
full_output.methodology: RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) was used to map the transcriptome of pAR060302 under various antibiotic treatments.

full_output.paper_title: Versatile transformation system that is applicable to both multiple transgene expression and gene targeting for Thraustochytrids.
full_output.key_findings: A versatile transformation system for thraustochytrids was established, enabling multiple transgene expression and gene targeting. The neomycin resistance gene (neo_r) was successfully integrated into the chromosomal DNA of various thraustochytrid genera, providing a selectable marker for transformation.
full_output.methodology: Transformation of thraustochytrids using electroporation and particle bombardment, followed by genomic PCR and Southern blot analysis to confirm integration of the neo_r gene.

full_output.paper_title: Induction of holomycin production and complex metabolic changes by the argR mutation in Streptomyces clavuligerus NP1.
full_output.key_findings: The argR mutation in Streptomyces clavuligerus NP1 leads to overproduction of holomycin and affects the expression of various genes involved in metabolic pathways, including those related to holomycin biosynthesis.
full_output.methodology: Comparative proteomic analysis and gene disruption experiments were conducted to investigate the effects of the argR mutation on metabolic processes and holomycin production.

full_output.paper_title: Safety assessment of Bifidobacterium longum JDM301 based on complete genome sequences.

BLJ_0923.mechanism: confers resistance to bacitracin via ABC transporter
BLJ_0923.role_in_paper: identified as a bacitracin resistance gene
BLJ_0923.genetic_context: located in the genome of Bifidobacterium longum JDM301
BLJ_0923.evidence_note: The gene BLJ_0923 is listed in Table 1 as a putative bacitracin resistance gene encoding an ABC transporter-related protein.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes in Bifidobacterium longum JDM301, including those conferring resistance to bacitracin, vancomycin, chloramphenicol, thiostrepton, penicillin, kasugamycin, tetracycline, carbomycin, sulfonamide, tetracenomycin C, trimethoprim, and macrolides. Some of these genes require experimental validation.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and analysis, along with antibiotic susceptibility testing using E-test.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LecRK-V.5 as a key regulator of stomatal immunity in Arabidopsis, showing that its absence enhances resistance to Pst DC3000 by maintaining stomatal closure, whereas its overexpression increases susceptibility by promoting stomatal reopening.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis, stomatal aperture measurements, and transgenic approaches were used to investigate the role of LecRK-V.5 in stomatal immunity.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmid-Mediated Quinolone Resistance; Interactions between Human, Animal, and Environmental Ecologies.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance (PMQR) mechanisms, including Qnr proteins, the aminoglycoside acetyltransferase AAC(6′)-Ib-cr, and the efflux pumps QepA and OqxAB. These genes contribute to low-level resistance to quinolones and fluoroquinolones, and their presence in various bacterial species highlights the role of environmental and animal reservoirs in the dissemination of PMQR.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed clinical isolates, plasmid-mediated resistance, and characterized the mechanisms of resistance through experimental validation.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of Benzimidazole Resistance in Haemonchus contortus Using Comparative PCR-RFLP Methods.

beta_tubulin.notes: No resistant alleles were detected in the studied samples.

full_output.key_findings: The study found no evidence of benzimidazole resistance in Haemonchus contortus in Iran, as all samples were homozygous for the susceptible allele at codon 200 of the beta tubulin isotype 1 gene.
full_output.methodology: PCR-RFLP and sequencing of the beta tubulin gene to detect mutations associated with benzimidazole resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Toward new therapeutics for skin and soft tissue infections: propargyl-linked antifolates are potent inhibitors of MRSA and Streptococcus pyogenes.

dhfr.notes: Point mutation at the active site of DHFR, specifically Phe98Tyr, was identified in MRSA mutants resistant to compound 24.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a point mutation (Phe98Tyr) in the dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) gene of MRSA that confers resistance to trimethoprim. The research also highlights the development of propargyl-linked antifolates with potent antibacterial activity against MRSA and Streptococcus pyogenes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized enzyme inhibition assays, crystallography, and direct colony PCR to identify and characterize the DHFR mutation and assess the antibacterial activity of the compounds.

full_output.paper_title: RNA interference of NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase results in reduced insecticide resistance in the bed bug, Cimex lectularius.

ClCPR.validation_method: dsRNA knockdown leading to increased susceptibility to deltamethrin

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ClCPR as a gene involved in P450-mediated metabolic detoxification, which contributes to deltamethrin resistance in bed bugs. Silencing ClCPR increased susceptibility to deltamethrin in resistant populations.
full_output.methodology: Cloning, RNAi, qRT-PCR, and bioassays were used to analyze ClCPR's role in deltamethrin resistance.
full_output.sample_size: Three bed bug colonies: LA-1 (susceptible), CIN-1 (resistant), and NY-1 (resistant).

full_output.paper_title: Global effects of catecholamines on Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae gene expression.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several genes regulated by epinephrine and norepinephrine in Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae, including virulence factors like apxIA, biofilm formation genes like pgaB, and adhesion-related genes like APL_0443. Regulatory genes such as ygiY and narQ were also found to be differentially expressed.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptional profiling using microarrays and qRT-PCR to analyze gene expression changes in response to catecholamines.

full_output.paper_title: High temperature in combination with UV irradiation enhances horizontal transfer of stx2 gene from E. coli O157:H7 to non-pathogenic E. coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that high temperature combined with UV irradiation enhances the activation of lambdoid prophages carrying the stx2 gene in E. coli O157:H7, facilitating horizontal gene transfer to non-pathogenic E. coli, thereby generating new Shiga toxin-producing E. coli (STEC).
full_output.methodology: Phage induction, PCR, ELISA, and in situ colony hybridization were used to analyze stx2 gene transfer.

full_output.paper_title: Use of a molecular diagnostic test in AFB smear positive tuberculosis suspects greatly reduces time to detection of multidrug resistant tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the Genotype MTBDR plus assay for rapid detection of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) and identified key mutations in katG, inhA, and rpoB genes associated with isoniazid and rifampicin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The Genotype MTBDR plus assay was used to detect genetic mutations in M. tuberculosis isolates from sputum samples, identifying resistance to isoniazid and rifampicin.

full_output.paper_title: Enzymatic quorum quenching increases antibiotic susceptibility of multidrug resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that enzymatic quorum quenching using lactonase (aiiA) enhances the susceptibility of multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa to antibiotics by disrupting biofilms and reducing virulence factor production.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized biofilm assays, lactonase activity assays, and antibiotic susceptibility testing to evaluate the effects of quorum quenching on Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.sample_size: Eight urinary tract infection (UTI) and ten sepsis isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance profile and presence of class I integrongs among Salmonella enterica serovars isolated from human clinical specimens in Tehran, Iran.

sul1.validation_method: PCR detection of class I integrons

intI.validation_method: PCR detection of class I integrons

full_output.key_findings: The study detected class I integrons in 88.3% of multidrug-resistant Salmonella isolates, with sul1 being a component of these integrons. High levels of multidrug resistance were observed, particularly to ampicillin, chloramphenicol, kanamycin, nalidixic acid, streptomycin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and tetracyclines.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing by disk diffusion and MIC, PCR for class I integrons.

full_output.paper_title: Functional metagenomics reveals previously unrecognized diversity of antibiotic resistance genes in gulls.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified numerous antibiotic resistance (AR) genes in gulls, including both known and previously undescribed ones. It highlights the significant diversity of AR genes in gulls, emphasizing their potential role in spreading resistance genes between human and environmental habitats.
full_output.methodology: Functional metagenomics was used to analyze the diversity of AR genes in gull feces, involving DNA extraction, cloning, and screening for resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.sample_size: Four gulls from Appledore Island, Maine, and two gulls from Rochester, New Hampshire.

full_output.paper_title: Evidence for conserved function of γ-glutamyltranspeptidase in Helicobacter genus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two γ-glutamyltranspeptidase (γGT) paralogues, bgh1 and bgh2, in Helicobacter bilis. While bgh2 encodes a functional γGT, bgh1 lacks enzymatic activity due to impaired maturation and does not confer resistance.
full_output.methodology: Functional complementation, mutagenesis, and biochemical characterization of recombinant proteins.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus capitis with reduced vancomycin susceptibility causes late-onset sepsis in intensive care neonates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a clonal population of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus capitis (MRSC) with reduced vancomycin susceptibility causing late-onset sepsis in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs).
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of blood cultures, pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE), and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Multiple mutations in heterogeneous miltefosine-resistant Leishmania major population as determined by whole genome sequencing.

PK.validation_method: transfection of a wild-type gene restored susceptibility

full_output.paper_title: Regulation of Cu(I)/Ag(I) efflux genes in Escherichia coli by the sensor kinase CusS.

cusS.mechanism: activates the cusCFBA efflux system in response to Cu(I)/Ag(I)
cusS.validation_method: gene disruption and complementation experiments showing increased sensitivity to Cu(I)/Ag(I) in ΔcusS mutants

full_output.paper_title: Assigning a function to a conserved archaeal metallo-β-lactamase from Haloferax volcanii.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the function of the HVO_2763 gene in Haloferax volcanii, demonstrating that it does not possess RNA processing activity or other enzymatic activities typical of metallo-β-lactamases. Instead, the deletion of HVO_2763 leads to decreased expression of transport-related genes, suggesting a potential role in membrane transport processes.
full_output.methodology: In vitro activity tests, transcriptome analysis, and gene deletion experiments were conducted to characterize the function of HVO_2763.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of the deletion of the six mce operons in Mycobacterium smegmatis.

mce4.notes: The mce4 operon is involved in cholesterol transport in M. smegmatis.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the mce4 operon is involved in cholesterol transport in M. smegmatis, and its deletion impairs cholesterol uptake.
full_output.methodology: Construction of mce mutants, cholesterol uptake experiments, and biofilm formation analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Loss of outer membrane protein C in Escherichia coli contributes to both antibiotic resistance and escaping antibody-dependent bactericidal activity.

ompC.mechanism: loss of OmpC reduces susceptibility to carbapenems and 4th-generation cephalosporins
ompC.role_in_paper: The study demonstrates that loss of OmpC contributes to both antibiotic resistance and escaping antibody-dependent bactericidal activity.
ompC.validation_method: Mutant construction and antimicrobial susceptibility testing
ompC.genetic_context: The ompC deletion mutant showed significantly decreased susceptibility to carbapenems and cefepime.
ompC.evidence_note: The paper shows that the loss of OmpC leads to resistance to carbapenems and cefepime.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the loss of OmpC in E. coli leads to increased resistance to carbapenems and 4th-generation cephalosporins, as well as resistance to serum bactericidal activity mediated by the classical complement pathway.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic manipulation to create an ompC deletion mutant and complemented strain, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing and bactericidal assays.

full_output.paper_title: Altered murine tissue colonization by Borrelia burgdorferi following targeted deletion of linear plasmid 17-carried genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that deletion of genes bbd16 to bbd25 in Borrelia burgdorferi leads to impaired tissue colonization, particularly in the bladder, and altered expression of OspC, which is regulated by bbd18.
full_output.methodology: Targeted deletion of genes on linear plasmid lp17 in B. burgdorferi, followed by in vitro and in vivo analysis of growth and tissue colonization.

full_output.paper_title: Selective FLT3 inhibition of FLT3-ITD+ acute myeloid leukaemia resulting in secondary D835Y mutation: a model for emerging clinical resistance patterns.

mutations_found.validated_by: in vitro and in vivo resistance testing

FLT3.notes: The D835Y mutation was selected during long-term exposure to MLN518 and conferred resistance to multiple FLT3 inhibitors.
FLT3.evidence_note: The D835Y mutation was selected during long-term exposure to MLN518 and conferred resistance to multiple FLT3 inhibitors.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a secondary D835Y mutation in FLT3-ITD+ AML cells that confers resistance to FLT3 inhibitors such as AC220, Sorafenib, and MLN518. The dual FLT3-Aurora kinase inhibitor CCT137690 overcomes this resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro and in vivo models to characterize the resistance mechanisms and evaluate the efficacy of CCT137690 against FLT3-ITD+ AML cells with the D835Y mutation.

full_output.paper_title: Phytosphingosine-1-phosphate is a signaling molecule involved in miconazole resistance in sessile Candida albicans cells.

LCB4.mechanism: involved in the phosphorylation of dihydrosphingosine and phytosphingosine
LCB4.validation_method: experimental validation through gene deletion and complementation studies

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LCB4 as a gene involved in miconazole resistance in sessile Candida albicans cells, showing that its deletion increases susceptibility to miconazole. Phytosphingosine-1-phosphate (PHS-1-P) was found to enhance miconazole resistance by possibly acting as a signaling molecule that affects efflux pump activity.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion and complementation studies, gene expression analysis, and susceptibility testing of biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of extended-spectrum-β-lactamase-producing and plasmid-mediated AmpC β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli isolated from stray dogs in South Korea.

blaCTX-M-24.genetic_context: IS Ecp1 upstream of the bla genes

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) genes, including bla CTX-M-14, bla CTX-M-24, bla CTX-M-3, bla CTX-M-55, bla CTX-M-27, and bla CTX-M-65, as well as plasmid-mediated AmpC beta-lactamase gene bla CMY-2 and bla DHA-1 in Escherichia coli isolates from stray dogs in South Korea.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, sequencing, and conjugation experiments to identify and characterize the AMR genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiological analysis of Escherichia coli sequence type ST131 (O25:H4) and blaCTX-M-15 among extended-spectrum-β-lactamase-producing E. coli from the United States, 2000 to 2009.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaCTX-M-15 as a prevalent extended-spectrum beta-lactamase gene in US E. coli isolates, particularly in sequence type ST131, which is associated with increased resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics and enhanced virulence.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR-based detection, phylogenetic grouping, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to analyze E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: New mutations in the mycobacterial ATP synthase: new insights into the binding of the diarylquinoline TMC207 to the ATP synthase C-ring structure.

atpE.notes: Mutations in the atpE gene encoding the c subunit of the ATP synthase were identified in TMC207-resistant mycobacterial mutants.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the atpE gene, which encodes the c subunit of the ATP synthase, that confer resistance to TMC207 in various mycobacterial species.
full_output.methodology: The study used MIC testing, complementation assays, and structural modeling to analyze the impact of mutations in the atpE gene on TMC207 resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the microbiological profiles of odontogenic infections and found that moxifloxacin (MXF) exhibited high in vitro activity against a variety of oral pathogens, with 98% of isolates being susceptible. Clindamycin (CLI) showed lower susceptibility rates, particularly against Neisseria spp. and certain streptococcal groups.
full_output.methodology: The study involved culturing bacterial isolates from patients with odontogenic infections and determining their susceptibility to various antibiotics using Etest methodology.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of Proteus mirabilis harboring blaKPC-2 and qnrD in a Chinese Hospital.

gyrB.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that the E466D mutation in gyrB contributes to quinolone resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emergence of Proteus mirabilis isolates harboring blaKPC-2 and qnrD, highlighting the role of chromosomal mutations in quinolone resistance and plasmid-mediated carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PFGE, conjugation experiments, and Southern blot analysis.
