full_output.paper_title: Structure-Based Homology Searches and Identification of Type III Toxin-Antitoxin Loci

toxIN.validation_method: functional analysis of toxin and antitoxin plasmids

cptIN.validation_method: functional analysis of toxin and antitoxin plasmids

tenpIN.validation_method: functional analysis of toxin and antitoxin plasmids

full_output.key_findings: Three novel Type III toxin-antitoxin families (toxIN, cptIN, and tenpIN) were identified and characterized, showing bacteriophage resistance capabilities.
full_output.methodology: Structure-based homology searches, functional analysis of cloned toxin and antitoxin plasmids, and phylogenetic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Microbial flora and food borne pathogens on minced meat and their susceptibility to antimicrobial agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance in Staphylococcus aureus isolates, with 90% being methicillin-resistant (MRSA) and showing resistance to multiple antibiotics including oxacillin, ampicillin, erythromycin, and amoxicillin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that Staphylococcus aureus isolates from indoor air in operating rooms and surgical wards showed 100% resistance to methicillin and 82.8% resistance to ampicillin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method on Mueller-Hinton agar.

full_output.paper_title: The toxin/immunity network of Burkholderia pseudomallei contact-dependent growth inhibition (CDI) systems.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes several CdiA-CT/CdiI toxin/immunity pairs in Burkholderia pseudomallei, demonstrating their tRNase activity and ability to inhibit cell growth. These systems are functional in bacterial competition and require specific interactions between CdiA-CT and CdiI for toxicity and immunity.
full_output.methodology: Expression in E. coli, tRNA cleavage assays, co-expression experiments, and growth inhibition assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, and Mycoplasma genitalium samples from Guinea-Bissau, highlighting high resistance levels to traditional gonorrhea antimicrobials but susceptibility to extended-spectrum cephalosporins, spectinomycin, and azithromycin. It identifies diverse NG-MAST sequence types and genovar distributions.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, NG-MAST typing, ompA and mgpB gene sequencing, and phylogenetic analysis.
full_output.sample_size: 31 N gonorrhoeae isolates, 60 C trachomatis samples, 30 M genitalium samples

full_output.paper_title: Characterization and determination of holin protein of Streptococcus suis bacteriophage SMP in heterologous host.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes the holin protein HolSMP from the Streptococcus suis bacteriophage SMP, demonstrating its function in triggering lysis of host cells when expressed in E. coli.
full_output.methodology: Functional analysis of HolSMP in E. coli, including expression, toxicity assays, and complementation tests.

full_output.paper_title: The importance of the trans-enamine intermediate as a β-lactamase inhibition strategy probed in inhibitor-resistant SHV β-lactamase variants.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the S130G and M69V mutations in the SHV β-lactamase, showing how these mutations affect the ability of the inhibitor SA2-13 to form a stable trans-enamine intermediate, leading to reduced susceptibility to β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Crystallography, biochemical assays, and site-directed mutagenesis were used to analyze the structural and functional impact of the S130G and M69V mutations on the SHV β-lactamase.

full_output.paper_title: The Threshold Length of the PolyQ Tract Above Which Chimeras Aggregate Into Amyloid-Like Fibrils Depends on the Structural Integrity of BlaP
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the aggregation behavior of BlaP chimeras with varying lengths of polyglutamine (polyQ) tracts, identifying a threshold length (above 55 glutamines) for amyloid-like fibril formation that depends on the structural integrity of BlaP.
full_output.methodology: The study used biochemical and biophysical methods including size-exclusion chromatography, circular dichroism spectroscopy, and transmission electron microscopy to analyze the structural and aggregation properties of BlaP chimeras with polyQ tracts of different lengths.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of OxyR as a negative transcriptional regulator that represses catalase production in Corynebacterium diphtheriae.

oxyR.validation_method: gel mobility shift assays, complementation tests, transcriptional analysis

full_output.key_findings: OxyR acts as a negative regulator of the cat gene in Corynebacterium diphtheriae and Corynebacterium glutamicum, reducing catalase production and increasing sensitivity to H2O2.
full_output.methodology: Generation of in-frame deletion mutants, catalase activity assays, and molecular biology techniques.

full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on improving the success rate of Melt-MAMA assays for SNP genotyping in bacterial pathogens, highlighting the effectiveness of specific design strategies and optimization techniques.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the performance of 185 Melt-MAMAs across eight bacterial pathogens, examining the effects of genome size, %GC content, and primer ratios on assay success.
full_output.sample_size: 185 SNPs from eight bacterial pathogen species

full_output.paper_title: GlmS and NagB regulate amino sugar metabolism in opposing directions and affect Streptococcus mutans virulence.
full_output.key_findings: GlmS and NagB regulate amino sugar metabolism in Streptococcus mutans, with GlmS promoting and NagB inhibiting virulence factors and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: Gene knockout, complementation, and expression analysis using PCR, immunoblotting, and quantitative PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Structures of Helicobacter pylori shikimate kinase reveal a selective inhibitor-induced-fit mechanism.

R57.notes: R57 is critical for catalytic activity.

R116.notes: R116 is critical for catalytic activity.

R132.notes: R132 is critical for catalytic activity.
R132.evidence_note: The paper describes the role of R132 in catalytic activity and its importance in shikimate binding, but does not indicate that mutations in R132 confer resistance to antibiotics.

D33.notes: D33 is critical for catalytic activity.

F48.notes: F48 is critical for catalytic activity.
F48.evidence_note: The paper describes the role of F48 in catalytic activity and its effect on enzyme function.

M10.evidence_note: The paper describes the mutation M10A in Helicobacter pylori shikimate kinase and reports that this mutation retained 38% relative activity.

E114.evidence_note: The paper mentions that E114A retained 82% relative activity, indicating that the mutation does not completely abolish function.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies critical residues in Helicobacter pylori shikimate kinase (HpSK) involved in catalytic activity and inhibitor binding, highlighting the importance of R57, R116, R132, D33, F48, M10, and E114 in enzyme function.
full_output.methodology: Site-directed mutagenesis, isothermal titration calorimetry, and X-ray crystallography were used to analyze the structure and function of HpSK and its mutants.

full_output.paper_title: RpoS regulates a novel type of plasmid DNA transfer in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: RpoS regulates plasmid transformation in E. coli, and the K173E mutation in RpoS reduces plasmid transformation efficiency.
full_output.methodology: Transformation frequency analysis, RT-PCR, and genetic manipulation of rpoS.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of an antimicrobial L-amino acid oxidase and peptide derivatives from Bothropoides mattogrosensis pitviper venom.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel L-amino acid oxidase (Bm LAO) from Bothrops mattogrosensis venom with antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive and -negative bacteria. Synthetic peptide fragments (Bm LAO-f1, Bm LAO-f2, Bm LAO-f3) also exhibit antimicrobial activity, suggesting potential for antibiotic development.
full_output.methodology: Isolation and characterization of Bm LAO, synthesis of peptide fragments, and evaluation of antimicrobial activity against various bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of velvet complex on transcriptome and penicillin G production in glucose-limited chemostat cultures of a β-lactam high-producing Penicillium chrysogenum strain.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the impact of the velvet complex on penicillin G production in glucose-limited chemostat cultures of a β-lactam high-producing Penicillium chrysogenum strain. It shows that deletions of PcvelA and PclaeA have a moderate effect on penicillin production under these conditions, suggesting that the role of the velvet complex in penicillin biosynthesis is context-dependent.
full_output.methodology: The study used gene deletion mutants, transcriptome analysis, and quantitative PCR to examine the effects of the velvet complex on penicillin G production in P. chrysogenum.

full_output.paper_title: Antistaphylococcal activity of bacteriophage derived chimeric protein P128.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the development and in vitro evaluation of P128, a chimeric protein derived from bacteriophage K and lysostaphin, showing potent bactericidal activity against diverse staphylococcal species, including methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) and methicillin-sensitive S. aureus (MSSA).
full_output.methodology: The study utilized broth microdilution, time-kill assays, and hydrogel formulations to assess the antibacterial activity of P128 against a panel of S. aureus strains.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of genes expressed in cultures of E. coli lysogens carrying the Shiga toxin-encoding prophage Φ24B.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 26 phage genes expressed in E. coli lysogen culture, including genes encoding hypothetical proteins and structural components. Some genes showed expression patterns linked to the lytic cycle, while others were expressed in stable lysogens. The research highlights the complexity of gene expression in lysogenic phages and provides insights into the functional roles of previously uncharacterized genes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized CMAT, 2D-PAGE, and qPCR to identify and analyze gene expression in E. coli lysogens carrying the Shiga toxin-encoding prophage Φ24B.

full_output.paper_title: Mutagenesis-mediated virus extinction: virus-dependent effect of viral load on sensitivity to lethal defection.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the effect of viral load and mutagenesis on the extinction of RNA viruses, focusing on LCMV, VSV, FMDV, and EMCV. It highlights the role of mutagenic agents like FU in altering viral replication and the importance of MOI in determining the effectiveness of mutagenesis.
full_output.methodology: The study used experimental virology techniques, including viral replication assays, mutation frequency analysis, and computational modeling to understand the mechanisms of lethal mutagenesis.

full_output.paper_title: Formulation of a mmaA4 gene deletion mutant of Mycobacterium bovis BCG in cationic liposomes significantly enhances protection against tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the mmaA4 gene deletion mutant of Mycobacterium bovis BCG and evaluates its protective efficacy against tuberculosis when formulated in DDA/TDB adjuvant.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a mouse aerosol Mycobacterium tuberculosis challenge model to investigate the protective efficacy of the mmaA4 gene deletion mutant of Mycobacterium bovis BCG.

full_output.paper_title: Diversity of Melissococcus plutonius from honeybee larvae in Japan and experimental reproduction of European foulbrood with cultured atypical isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified atypical Melissococcus plutonius isolates that maintain virulence even after repeated subculture in laboratory media, contrasting with typical isolates that lose virulence rapidly. These atypical isolates were shown to cause European foulbrood in honeybee larvae.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic characterization, DNA-DNA hybridization, PFGE analysis, and experimental infection of honeybee larvae.

full_output.paper_title: Turbidostat culture of Saccharomyces cerevisiae W303-1A under selective pressure elicited by ethanol selects for mutations in SSD1 and UTH1.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: The UTH1 D224Y allele was the only one consistently co-segregated with the ethanol tolerance phenotype.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in SSD1 and UTH1 that contribute to ethanol tolerance in Saccharomyces cerevisiae W303-1A. Specifically, mutations in SSD1, such as the replacement of the stop codon with an amino acid, and a point mutation in UTH1 (D224Y) were found to enhance ethanol tolerance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, genetic crosses, and spot assays were used to analyze mutations and their impact on ethanol tolerance.

full_output.paper_title: Gene cluster analysis for the biosynthesis of elgicins, novel lantibiotics produced by Paenibacillus elgii B69.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a novel lantibiotic-like gene cluster in Paenibacillus elgii B69, leading to the isolation of four new lantibiotics named elgicins AI, AII, B, and C with broad inhibitory spectra against various bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, bioinformatics, and purification techniques were used to characterize the gene cluster and elgicins.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that dogs can carry methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius (MRSP) for over a year, and systemic antimicrobial treatment with agents to which MRSP is resistant was associated with prolonged carriage.
full_output.methodology: PCR, susceptibility testing, and longitudinal sampling of dogs.

full_output.paper_title: Database screening and in vivo efficacy of antimicrobial peptides against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus USA300.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies six antimicrobial peptides with potent activity against MRSA USA300, including DASamP1, which shows specificity for S. aureus and effectiveness in suppressing biofilm formation in vivo.
full_output.methodology: In vitro and in vivo testing of antimicrobial peptides against MRSA USA300.

full_output.paper_title: New sequence types and multidrug resistance among pathogenic Escherichia coli isolates from coastal marine sediments.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes in E. coli isolates from coastal marine sediments, including blaTEM, tetA, aadA1, dfrA1, and sul2, which confer resistance to various antibiotics such as ampicillin, tetracycline, streptomycin, trimethoprim, and sulfamethoxazole.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to detect AMR genes and determine resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance in Escherichia coli isolates from raccoons (Procyon lotor) in Southern Ontario, Canada.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of antimicrobial resistance genes such as bla CMY-2, tet(A), and tet(B) in Escherichia coli isolates from raccoons in Southern Ontario, Canada. These genes confer resistance to ceftiofur and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of antimicrobial resistance genes and susceptibility testing of E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Listeria monocytogenes grown at 7° C shows reduced acid survival and an altered transcriptional response to acid shock compared to L. monocytogenes grown at 37° C.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that L. monocytogenes grown at 7°C showed reduced acid survival and altered transcriptional responses to acid shock compared to those grown at 37°C. Key findings include the induction of bacteriophage-like operons in stationary-phase cells at 7°C and differences in gene expression related to stress response and acid resistance.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis using microarrays and survival assays in artificial gastric fluid and acidified BHI.

full_output.paper_title: Type I signal peptidase and protein secretion in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 46 proteins whose secretion in Staphylococcus aureus depends on SPase activity, highlighting the role of SPase in the secretion of virulence factors and other proteins. Additionally, it reveals that certain transmembrane proteins, like LtaS and OatA, are processed by SPase despite lacking typical signal peptides.
full_output.methodology: The study uses MudPIT mass spectrometry to analyze the secretome of a SPase mutant strain of S. aureus in the presence of arylomycin A-C 16, combined with qRT-PCR to assess gene expression changes.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the relationship between SOS response and vesiculation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa under ciprofloxacin treatment. It shows that SOS activation increases OMV production and cytotoxicity, while the LexA noncleavable strain (lexAN) exhibits reduced vesiculation and cytotoxicity, indicating SOS involvement in these processes.
full_output.methodology: The study used OMV isolation, microscopic analysis, lipid quantification, proteomic analysis, and cytotoxicity assays to investigate the effects of ciprofloxacin on P. aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: MoVAC8 and MoTSC13 Are Not Required for Nuclear Degeneration during Appressorium Development in Magnaporthe oryzae
full_output.key_findings: The study identified MoVAC8 and MoTSC13 as genes involved in vacuolar and ER functions, but they are not required for nuclear degeneration during appressorium development in Magnaporthe oryzae. MoVAC8 is involved in the caffeine response, while MoTSC13 is essential for full virulence and cell wall integrity.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic manipulation, fluorescence microscopy, and complementation experiments to analyze the functions of MoVAC8 and MoTSC13 in Magnaporthe oryzae.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic basis of rifampicin resistance in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus suggests clonal expansion in hospitals in Cape Town, South Africa.

rpoB.notes: novel

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of selective menaquinone biosynthesis inhibitors against Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified novel MenA inhibitors that show significant activity against non-replicating Mycobacterium tuberculosis without affecting other Gram-positive bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and evaluation of MenA inhibitors using enzymatic and bacterial growth assays.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular fingerprinting of Staphylococcus aureus isolated from patients with osteomyelitis in Argentina and clonal distribution of the cap5(8) genes and of other selected virulence genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the molecular fingerprinting of S. aureus isolates from osteomyelitis patients in Argentina, highlighting the clonal distribution of cap5(8) genes and other virulence genes such as lukS-PV, lukF-PV, seg, and sei. It also found associations between cap5 genes and methicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Molecular typing, PCR amplification, and statistical analysis were used to evaluate the clonality and virulence gene distribution in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolated in Nepal.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the rpoB gene associated with rifampin resistance and mutations in the katG gene and inhA promoter region linked to isoniazid resistance in multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Nepal.
full_output.methodology: DNA sequencing of the rpoB, katG, and inhA promoter regions to detect resistance-associated mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Class A carbapenemase FPH-1 from Francisella philomiragia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies FPH-1, a novel class A carbapenemase from Francisella philomiragia, which confers high-level resistance to penicillins, cephalothin, aztreonam, ceftazidime, and carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, protein expression, enzyme kinetics, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: NDM-1-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae resistant to colistin in a French community patient without history of foreign travel.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the identification of NDM-1-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae strains resistant to colistin in a French community patient without a history of foreign travel, highlighting the emergence of multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the NDM-1-producing strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the multidrug transporter AcrB, focusing on its structural mechanisms involved in drug transport, including the identification of access and deep binding pockets and the role of a switch-loop in facilitating drug movement.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis using X-ray crystallography and biochemical assays.

full_output.paper_title: Structure-activity relationships, ligand efficiency, and lipophilic efficiency profiles of benzophenone-type inhibitors of the multidrug transporter P-glycoprotein.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes benzophenone derivatives as inhibitors of the multidrug transporter P-glycoprotein, focusing on their structure-activity relationships, ligand efficiency, and lipophilic efficiency.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and biological activity assessment of benzophenone analogues using daunorubicin efflux protocols.

full_output.paper_title: Clostridium difficile genotypes other than ribotype 078 that are prevalent among human, animal and environmental isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various Clostridium difficile PCR ribotypes prevalent in humans, animals, and the environment, highlighting differences in antibiotic resistance profiles between human and animal isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR ribotyping, PFGE, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize C. difficile isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that Clostridium difficile was isolated from 18 of 539 animals at feedlot arrival and from 18 of 335 cattle at mid-feeding period, with all isolates being ribotype 078, a toxinotype V strain with genes encoding toxins A, B, and CDT. All strains were classified as NAP7 by PFGE and had a 39 base pair deletion and upstream truncating mutation on the tcdC gene.
full_output.methodology: Selective culture for C. difficile, ribotyping, pulsed-field gel electrophoresis, and molecular analysis including PCR and sequencing of the tcdC gene.
full_output.sample_size: 539 cattle at arrival and 335 cattle at mid-feeding period

full_output.paper_title: Genetically divergent methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and sec-dependent mastitis of dairy goats in Taiwan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the sec gene as a significant virulence factor in S. aureus isolates associated with mastitis in goats, highlighting its role in the pathogenesis of mastitis.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PCR-RFLP analysis, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and PFGE analysis to characterize S. aureus isolates and identify the sec gene.

full_output.paper_title: Nodularin, a cyanobacterial toxin, is synthesized in planta by symbiotic Nostoc sp.
full_output.key_findings: This study demonstrates the synthesis of nodularin and [L-Har 2] nodularin in a non-Nodularia species and the production of cyanobacterial hepatotoxin by a symbiont in planta.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, HPLC HESI-MS/MS, PP2A inhibition assay

full_output.paper_title: Virulence potential and genomic mapping of the worldwide clone Escherichia coli ST131.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the ST131 clone, despite being part of the B2 phylogenetic group, exhibited lower virulence compared to other non-ST131 group B2 strains in both C. elegans and zebrafish embryo models. The ST131 strains lacked certain classical virulence factors and showed reduced pathogenic potential.
full_output.methodology: The study used C. elegans and zebrafish embryo models to assess the virulence of ST131 strains and compared them with non-ST131 strains. Optical mapping was employed to analyze genome organization.
full_output.sample_size: Nine E. coli strains including three ST131 strains

full_output.paper_title: Involvement of multiple distinct Bordetella receptor proteins in the utilization of iron liberated from transferrin by host catecholamine stress hormones.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies BfrA, BfrD, and BfrE as novel TonB-dependent outer membrane receptors involved in catecholamine utilization by Bordetella bronchiseptica, demonstrating their role in iron acquisition from transferrin and lactoferrin.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis, mutation studies, and complementation experiments were conducted to characterize the role of these receptors in iron acquisition.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis of ureidomuraymycidine derivatives for structure-activity relationship studies of muraymycins.
full_output.key_findings: The paper describes the synthesis of ureidomuraymycidine derivatives for structure-activity relationship studies of muraymycins, focusing on the development of a stereoselective synthesis of (2S,3S)-muraymycidine derivatives. The study involves the synthesis and characterization of various intermediates and final products, but does not identify any AMR genes or mutations.
full_output.methodology: The paper details a synthetic approach involving the preparation of various compounds through multiple steps, including the use of Strecker reactions, lactone-opening reactions, and other organic transformations.

full_output.paper_title: The CXXC motifs in the metal binding domains are required for ATP7B to mediate resistance to cisplatin.

full_output.paper_title: Acidic pH induced STM1485 gene is essential for intracellular replication of Salmonella.
full_output.key_findings: The STM1485 gene is essential for intracellular replication of Salmonella by facilitating SPI-2 translocon formation and preventing phagosome-lysosome fusion.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, complementation, protein expression, and intracellular survival assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the performance of a chromogenic medium (chromID CARBA) for detecting carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae (CPE) in rectal swabs. It identifies 92 CPE strains, including 56 KPC-positive Klebsiella pneumoniae, 29 VIM-positive K. pneumoniae, and 7 KPC-positive Enterobacter aerogenes strains.
full_output.methodology: The study compares the performance of chromID CARBA with other culture-based screening methods for CPE detection using rectal swab specimens and confirms results through phenotypic and molecular assays.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of first- and second-line drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis clinical isolates by pyrosequencing.

rpoB.notes: Mutations in rpoB are associated with rifampin resistance.

katG.notes: Mutations in katG are associated with isoniazid resistance.

embB.notes: Mutations in embB are associated with ethambutol resistance.

rrs.notes: Mutations in rrs are associated with resistance to aminoglycosides.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in gyrA are associated with fluoroquinolone resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a pyrosequencing method for detecting mutations associated with resistance to first- and second-line drugs in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including rifampin, isoniazid, ethambutol, amikacin, kanamycin, capreomycin, and ofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Pyrosequencing was used to detect mutations in specific genes associated with drug resistance in M. tuberculosis clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: SCCmec Type IX Element in Methicillin Resistant Staphylococcus aureus spa Type t337 (CC9) Isolated from Pigs and Pork in Thailand.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes in MRSA isolates from pigs and pork in Thailand, including blaZ, aac-aphD, vga(A), tetM, tet_efflux, ermB, aadD, cat, and fex(A). These genes confer resistance to various antibiotics such as penicillin, gentamicin, tiamulin, tetracycline, erythromycin, chloramphenicol, and florfenicol.
full_output.methodology: Microarray analysis, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PFGE, spa typing, SCCmec typing, and MLST.

full_output.paper_title: Monoclonal antibodies to meningococcal factor H binding protein with overlapping epitopes and discordant functional activity.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies specific amino acid residues in fHbp that are crucial for the binding of anti-fHbp mAbs JAR 1 and mAb502, highlighting the importance of inhibiting factor H binding for bactericidal activity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized ELISA, flow cytometry, and site-directed mutagenesis to analyze the binding characteristics of anti-fHbp mAbs and their impact on factor H binding and bactericidal activity.

full_output.paper_title: Diversity of integron- and culture-associated antibiotic resistance genes in freshwater floc.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a diverse array of antibiotic resistance genes in freshwater floc, including aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes, beta-lactamases, chloramphenicol resistance genes, and tetracycline resistance genes. The presence of these genes highlights the significance of floc as a reservoir for antibiotic resistance in aquatic environments.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR amplification, microarray-based detection, and sequencing to identify antibiotic resistance genes in floc samples from various freshwater systems.

full_output.paper_title: Stringent response regulation of biofilm formation in Vibrio cholerae.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the stringent response, mediated by (p)ppGpp, plays a critical role in biofilm formation in Vibrio cholerae. Mutants lacking (p)ppGpp synthases (relA, spoT, relV) exhibit reduced biofilm formation, and the stringent response regulates the expression of vpsR and vpsT, which are essential for biofilm development.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic mutants, promoter fusions, β-galactosidase assays, and qRT-PCR to investigate the role of the stringent response in biofilm formation.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of the Group A Streptococcus Mga virulence regulator reveals a role for the C-terminal region in oligomerization and transcriptional activation.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the Group A Streptococcus Mga virulence regulator, revealing that the C-terminal region is critical for oligomerization and transcriptional activation. The research highlights the importance of the C-terminal 139 amino acids in Mga's in vivo activity, demonstrating that while DNA binding is necessary, it is not sufficient for full Mga function. Additionally, the study shows that the C-terminal region facilitates oligomerization, which correlates with transcriptional activation.
full_output.methodology: The study involved purification and biochemical characterization of Mga, including DNA binding assays, gel filtration, analytical ultracentrifugation, and co-immunoprecipitation experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Drug susceptibility of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Beijing genotype and association with MDR TB.

rpoB.notes: Mutations in rpoB were identified in rifampin-resistant mutants.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that Beijing genotype Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains have higher mutation frequencies for rifampin compared to East-African/Indian (EAI) genotype strains, with specific rpoB mutations (H526D, H526Y, S531L) associated with rifampin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used a liquid culturing system and agar proportion method to determine drug susceptibility and mutation frequencies, along with molecular assays to identify rpoB mutations.
full_output.sample_size: 10 strains (5 Beijing and 5 EAI genotype strains)

full_output.paper_title: The Bacillus subtilis cannibalism toxin SDP collapses the proton motive force and induces autolysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SdpI as a membrane protein that confers resistance to the SDP cannibalism toxin in Bacillus subtilis. SDP collapses the proton motive force (PMF) and induces autolysis in Gram-positive bacteria, but not in Gram-negative species due to their outer membrane barrier.
full_output.methodology: Fluorescence microscopy, viable cell counts, and PMF assays were used to investigate the mechanism of SDP action and resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli serotype O78:H(-) in family, Finland, 2009.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a sorbitol-fermenting STEC O78:H- strain carrying stx1c and hlyA genes that caused bacteremia and HUS in a neonate and was found in asymptomatic family members.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, PFGE, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Summary of ceftaroline activity against pathogens in the United States, 2010: report from the Assessing Worldwide Antimicrobial Resistance Evaluation (AWARE) surveillance program.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the in vitro activity of ceftaroline against various pathogens, highlighting its effectiveness against staphylococci, streptococci, and certain Gram-negative bacteria, with particular emphasis on its potency against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and penicillin-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized susceptibility testing via broth microdilution methods as per CLSI guidelines, analyzing a large number of clinical isolates from different regions of the United States.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of mutation and genetic background on drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and characterization of cytotoxic, aggregative Citrobacter freundii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a cytotoxic and aggregative strain of Citrobacter freundii (CF74) with unique genomic features, including a type VI secretion system (T6SS) and fimbriae islands, which may contribute to its pathogenic potential.

full_output.paper_title: Fusion of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigen 85A to an oligomerization domain enhances its immunogenicity in both mice and non-human primates.

full_output.methodology: DNA and MVA vaccines were used to assess the immunogenicity of Ag85A fused with IMX313 in mice and rhesus macaques.

full_output.paper_title: Exploiting adaptive laboratory evolution of Streptomyces clavuligerus for antibiotic discovery and overproduction.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that adaptive laboratory evolution of Streptomyces clavuligerus against MRSA N315 led to the emergence of a strain capable of constitutive production of holomycin. The evolved strain, clavu7, exhibited a loss of the pSCL4 plasmid and several SNPs in genes related to secondary metabolite biosynthesis.
full_output.methodology: Adaptive laboratory evolution was conducted by serially passing S. clavuligerus against MRSA N315 on agar plates, followed by genome re-sequencing and chemical analysis to identify mutations and bioactive compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Genome sequence and transcriptome analysis of the radioresistant bacterium Deinococcus gobiensis: insights into the extreme environmental adaptations.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes involved in DNA repair and UV resistance in Deinococcus gobiensis, including ddrA, ddrB, phrB, recB, and polB, which are induced upon UV irradiation.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and transcriptome analysis using RNA-Seq.

full_output.paper_title: Role of the N-terminus in determining metal-specific responses in the E. coli Ni- and Co-responsive metalloregulator, RcnR.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and diversity of multiresistant Corynebacterium striatum clinical isolates by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry and by a multigene sequencing approach.

full_output.paper_title: Fitness of Escherichia coli strains carrying expressed and partially silent IncN and IncP1 plasmids.

full_output.paper_title: Mediator acts upstream of the transcriptional activator Gal4.

full_output.methodology: Genetic screens, Western blot analysis, and real-time PCR were used to investigate the role of ubiquitin-mediated protein degradation in the regulation of the GAL genes.

full_output.paper_title: The Nucleotide Context Around Nonsense Mutations Influences Aminoglycoside-Induced Readthrough

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of genetic mutations associated with Mycobacterium tuberculosis resistance to amikacin, kanamycin and capreomycin: a systematic review.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and characterization of microcin S, a new antibacterial peptide produced by probiotic Escherichia coli G3/10.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of novel Mt-Guab2 inhibitor series active against M. tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative omics-driven genome annotation refinement: application across Yersiniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 96 unannotated or erroneous protein coding regions across three Yersinia strains, highlighting the importance of integrating omics data for genome annotation refinement.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of chromosomal genes in Yersinia pestis that influence type III secretion and delivery of Yops into target cells.

full_output.paper_title: CRISPR/cas loci of type II Propionibacterium acnes confer immunity against acquisition of mobile elements present in type I P. acnes.

full_output.paper_title: The flagellar regulator fliT represses Salmonella pathogenicity island 1 through flhDC and fliZ.

full_output.paper_title: Involvement of iron in biofilm formation by Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that PGG, an iron chelator, inhibits biofilm formation by S. aureus SA113 by depleting iron, leading to the expression of iron-regulated genes such as isdA and isdB. Adding iron restores biofilm formation, highlighting the importance of iron in biofilm development.

full_output.paper_title: Peptidolipins B-F, antibacterial lipopeptides from an ascidian-derived Nocardia sp.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that antimony-resistant Leishmania donovani up-regulates host IL-10, leading to overexpression of multidrug-resistant protein 1 (MDR1), which contributes to antimony resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized gene expression analysis, efflux assays, and genetic manipulations to investigate the role of MDR1 in antimony resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical implications of pneumococcal serotypes: invasive disease potential, clinical presentations, and antibiotic resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the clinical implications of pneumococcal serotypes, focusing on their invasive disease potential, clinical presentations, and antibiotic resistance. It highlights the multidrug-resistant nature of serotypes 19A and 6C/6D, emphasizing their prevalence and resistance profiles in different regions.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature and surveillance data to analyze the relationships between pneumococcal serotypes and their clinical and resistome characteristics.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility of stenotrophomonas maltophilia isolates from Korea, and the activity of antimicrobial combinations against the isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study determined the antimicrobial susceptibility of 206 clinical Stenotrophomonas maltophilia isolates from Korea and evaluated the in vitro activity of antimicrobial combinations. High susceptibility rates were observed for trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (96%) and minocycline (99%), while levofloxacin showed a 64% susceptibility rate. All tested antimicrobial combinations exhibited synergy against many isolates, with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole plus ticarcillin-clavulanate showing the most significant synergistic effect.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the CLSI agar dilution method, and in vitro activity of antimicrobial combinations was tested using the checkerboard method.

full_output.paper_title: A secretory protein of necrotrophic fungus Sclerotinia sclerotiorum that suppresses host resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SSITL, a secretory protein from the necrotrophic fungus Sclerotinia sclerotiorum, which suppresses host resistance mechanisms. SSITL is similar to integrin-like proteins and is highly expressed during early infection stages. Silencing SSITL leads to reduced virulence and altered hyphal growth and sclerotial development.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular cloning, RNA interference, northern blot analysis, real-time RT-PCR, and immunolocalization techniques to investigate the function and expression of SSITL in S. sclerotiorum.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a low prevalence of multidrug-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates in West Africa, with only one multidrug-resistant isolate detected, belonging to the PMEN clone ST 63. Resistance was highest for tetracycline (48%), followed by chloramphenicol and penicillin (5% each). No resistance was observed for erythromycin, cefotaxime, and ampicillin.
full_output.methodology: Multilocus sequence typing (MLST) and antibiotic susceptibility testing were conducted on 73 S. pneumoniae isolates from West Africa.

full_output.paper_title: Transcriptome of Dickeya dadantii infecting Acyrthosiphon pisum reveals a strong defense against antimicrobial peptides.

full_output.methodology: Transcriptome analysis using CDS pangenomic microarrays and mutant survival tests.

full_output.paper_title: Structural characterization of de novo designed L5K5W model peptide isomers with potent antimicrobial and varied hemolytic activities.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a series of de novo designed L5K5W model peptides with potent antimicrobial activity against various bacterial strains, including multidrug-resistant ones, and varying hemolytic activities against human erythrocytes.
full_output.methodology: The peptides were designed to be amphipathic and helical, with structural validation via CD, fluorescence, and NMR spectroscopy. Antimicrobial activity was assessed using MIC values, and hemolytic activity was evaluated against human red blood cells.

full_output.paper_title: A genetic approach to the development of new therapeutic phages to fight pseudomonas aeruginosa in wound infections.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses challenges and considerations in phage therapy for Pseudomonas aeruginosa, focusing on non-canonical phage-bacterium interactions, pseudolysogeny, and pseudovirulence. It highlights the risks of horizontal gene transfer and the need for careful phage selection and management.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature and experimental studies on phage-bacterium interactions, focusing on mechanisms of phage resistance and the implications for phage therapy.

full_output.paper_title: Convergence and divergence in the evolution of the APOBEC3G-Vif interaction reveal ancient origins of simian immunodeficiency viruses.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in APOBEC3G (A3G) that confer resistance to Vif-mediated antagonism, highlighting the evolutionary arms race between lentiviruses and their hosts.
full_output.methodology: The study uses co-expression of A3G variants with Vif-deficient HIV-1 and measures infectivity to assess resistance to Vif-mediated antagonism.
full_output.sample_size: various primate species including De Brazza's monkey, Wolf's guenon, mustached guenon, rhesus macaque, and human.

full_output.paper_title: Correlation of Minimum Inhibitory Concentration Breakpoints and Methicillin Resistance Gene Carriage in Clinical Isolates of Staphylococcus epidermidis.

mecA.validation_method: PCR detection of mecA gene carriage and correlation with methicillin resistance phenotype

full_output.key_findings: The study found that the mecA gene is correlated with methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus epidermidis isolates, with a better correlation observed at a lower MIC breakpoint of 0.5 µg/ml.
full_output.methodology: Disc diffusion, broth microdilution, and PCR were used to assess methicillin resistance and detect the mecA gene.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular basis of antibiotic multiresistance transfer in Staphylococcus aureus.

nes.mechanism: initiates and terminates plasmid transfer by creating a transient single-strand DNA break and covalent protein-DNA intermediate
nes.validation_method: structural and functional analysis including crystallography, DNA binding studies, and conjugation assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the nes gene encoding a relaxase enzyme essential for conjugative plasmid transfer in Staphylococcus aureus, which facilitates the spread of multidrug resistance, including resistance to vancomycin, gentamicin, and mupirocin.
full_output.methodology: Structural and functional analysis including crystallography, DNA binding studies, and conjugation assays.

full_output.paper_title: Household risk factors for colonization with multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that multidrug-resistant MRSA isolates are prevalent among hospitalized patients, with resistance to multiple antibiotics such as erythromycin, ciprofloxacin, clindamycin, amikacin, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, gentamicin, tetracycline, quinupristin/dalfopristin, and chloramphenicol. Recent hospitalization was a significant risk factor for multidrug resistance, while animal contact, especially with household pets, showed potential as an emerging risk factor.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted a prospective analysis of MRSA isolates from hospitalized patients, assessing antimicrobial susceptibility and evaluating risk factors for multidrug resistance through interviews and microbiological testing.

full_output.paper_title: The capsular polysaccharide and lipopolysaccharide structures of two carbapenem resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae outbreak isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the KPC-1 gene as responsible for carbapenem resistance in two outbreak isolates of Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: PCR and molecular characterization of the KPC-1 gene in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of MicA interactions suggests a potential novel means of gene regulation by small non-coding RNAs.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes MicA, a small non-coding RNA, and its interactions with target mRNAs, particularly ompA. It identifies a stabilized form of MicA (MicA stab) that enhances binding affinity to ompA and reveals insights into the structural dynamics of MicA and its regulation by Hfq and Mg2+.
full_output.methodology: Biochemical and biophysical studies including EMSA, thermal melting, size-exclusion chromatography, AUC, SAXS, and CD spectroscopy were used to analyze MicA structure and interactions.

full_output.paper_title: NrdH-redoxin of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Corynebacterium glutamicum dimerizes at high protein concentration and exclusively receives electrons from thioredoxin reductase.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes NrdH-redoxin from Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Corynebacterium glutamicum, showing that it is reduced by thioredoxin reductase and not by mycothiol. It also reveals that NrdH-redoxin forms non-swapped dimers at high concentrations and has a thioredoxin-like structural fold.
full_output.methodology: Structural biology techniques, including X-ray crystallography, small-angle X-ray scattering, and biochemical assays, were used to analyze NrdH-redoxin's structure and function.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of T6SS-dependent effector and immunity proteins by Tn-seq in Vibrio cholerae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three T6SS immunity genes (tsiV1, tsiV2, tsiV3) and their corresponding effectors (tseL, vasX, vgrG3) in Vibrio cholerae, demonstrating their roles in T6SS-dependent killing and immunity.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis combined with deep sequencing (Tn-seq) was used to identify T6SS immunity and effector proteins.

full_output.paper_title: NDM-1, the ultimate promiscuous enzyme: substrate recognition and catalytic mechanism.
full_output.key_findings: NDM-1 is a metallo-beta-lactamase that hydrolyzes and inactivates nearly all known beta-lactam-based antibiotics, demonstrating broad substrate recognition and catalytic versatility.
full_output.methodology: Structural biology, X-ray crystallography, molecular dynamics simulations, and biochemical assays.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a small-molecule inhibitor of bacterial AraC family activators.

full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening, in vivo and in vitro DNA binding assays, and dose-response experiments.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaOXA-51-like genes as conserved in Acinetobacter baumannii and a beta-lactamase gene (ABAYE2456) that is acquired in the Acb complex.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and functional analysis of the type VI secretion system in Acinetobacter.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes the type VI secretion system (T6SS) in Acinetobacter species, particularly highlighting the role of Hcp and TssM in T6SS functionality. The T6SS was found to be active in several Acinetobacter species, but its role in virulence and antibacterial activity was not confirmed.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial activities of methanol extracts from ten Cameroonian vegetables against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, showing significant inhibitory effects with MIC values ranging from 128 to 1024 μg/ml.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus containing mecC in Swedish dairy cows.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the first occurrence of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) harboring the mecC gene in Swedish dairy cows, highlighting the emergence of a novel mecA homologue in animal-associated MRSA strains.
full_output.methodology: PCR, susceptibility testing, and molecular typing techniques including spa-typing, MLST, and PFGE.

full_output.key_findings: The study focused on the development of a DNA vaccine expressing the Ag85A-HA2 fusion protein to protect against influenza A virus and Staphylococcus aureus. The vaccine induced Th1-type immune responses and provided protection against both pathogens.
full_output.methodology: The study involved constructing a DNA vaccine, evaluating its expression in mammalian cells, and assessing its protective efficacy in mice against influenza A virus and S. aureus through various immunological and pathological analyses.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular and structural basis of inner core lipopolysaccharide alterations in Escherichia coli: incorporation of glucuronic acid and phosphoethanolamine in the heptose region.

full_output.methodology: Mutational analysis, structural examination, mass spectrometry, and NMR spectroscopy were used to validate the roles of waaH and eptC in LPS modifications.

full_output.paper_title: A technology for developing synbodies with antibacterial activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the development of synbodies, which are protein affinity agents designed to target specific bacteria. The synbodies were created by combining a binding peptide with a lytic peptide, resulting in a compound with enhanced antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus. The synbody demonstrated effectiveness in inhibiting bacterial growth and protecting human cells from S. aureus-induced cell death without significant toxicity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a peptide microarray screening approach to identify binding and lytic peptides. These peptides were then combined to create synbodies, which were tested for antibacterial activity using in vitro growth inhibition assays and cytotoxicity tests.

full_output.key_findings: The study found a significant reduction in cefepime-resistant and ESBL-producing gram-negative organisms after implementing an antibiotic rotation strategy in febrile neutropenic patients.
full_output.methodology: The study involved a prospective trial of antibiotic rotation in febrile neutropenic patients, analyzing the effects on antimicrobial resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-resistant gram-negative bacteria colonization of healthy US military personnel in the US and Afghanistan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline resistance genes tet(A) and tet(B) in multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli isolates from both US and Afghanistan-based military personnel.
full_output.methodology: Molecular testing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify tetracycline resistance genes and evaluate resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Rac and Rab GTPases dual effector Nischarin regulates vesicle maturation to facilitate survival of intracellular bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: Nischarin, a novel dual effector of Rac and Rab GTPases, facilitates the maturation of Salmonella-containing vacuoles (SCVs) by interacting with Rab14 and Rab9, promoting acidification and supporting intracellular survival of Salmonella.
full_output.methodology: Yeast two-hybrid screens, GST bead-binding assays, immunofluorescence, FRAP, and siRNA knockdown experiments were used to analyze Nischarin's interactions and functional role in vesicle maturation and Salmonella survival.

full_output.paper_title: Ertapenem disk performance to predict Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase produced by Gram-negative bacilli isolated in a São Paulo city public hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the performance of ertapenem disks to predict the presence of Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase (KPC) in Gram-negative bacilli. It found that ertapenem disk resistance was not a reliable predictor of KPC production, as only 36% of resistant strains had the blaKPC gene.
full_output.methodology: Disk diffusion and PCR were used to detect resistance and the presence of the blaKPC gene.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a phenylalanine clamp (F64/F68) in AiiA that enhances substrate specificity for longer AHLs. Mutations in this region (F107W and F64C/F68C) alter substrate binding and catalytic efficiency, demonstrating the importance of this hydrophobic region in substrate recognition.
full_output.methodology: Crystallography, site-directed mutagenesis, and steady-state kinetics were used to analyze AiiA variants.

full_output.paper_title: Assessing the resistance and bioremediation ability of selected bacterial and protozoan species to heavy metals in metal-rich industrial wastewater.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several heavy metal resistance genes in bacterial and protozoan isolates, including copC, chrB, cnrA3, and nccA, which confer resistance to copper, chromium, cobalt, nickel, and cadmium.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and gel electrophoresis to detect metal resistance genes in microbial isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Electric Current Alone Killed S. epidermidis Biofilms
full_output.key_findings: Electric current effectively killed S. epidermidis and P. aeruginosa biofilms, with the effect being dose-dependent and influenced by chloride availability. Free chlorine generation was identified as a major factor in the antibacterial effect of electric current.
full_output.methodology: Experimental analysis of biofilm reduction under various current levels and electrolyte conditions, including chlorine concentration measurements and statistical modeling.

full_output.paper_title: Incidence and risk factors for extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis in Delhi region.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 18 XDR-TB isolates (3.7%) among 483 MDR-TB isolates, highlighting the association of XDR-TB with family history of TB, socioeconomic status, comorbidities, and previous intake of second-line injectable drugs.
full_output.methodology: Drug susceptibility testing (DST) using MGIT 960 system for RIF, INH, OFX, AMK, CAP, KAN, and LVF.

full_output.paper_title: Suppression of hepcidin expression and iron overload mediate Salmonella susceptibility in ankyrin 1 ENU-induced mutant.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a nonsense mutation in the Ank1 gene as the cause of increased Salmonella susceptibility in Ity16 mutant mice, highlighting the role of ankryin 1 in maintaining erythrocyte structure and preventing iron overload, which facilitates Salmonella proliferation.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screening, immunoblotting, and bacterial load analysis in mouse models.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteriophage-encoded lytic enzymes control growth of contaminating Lactobacillus found in fuel ethanol fermentations.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies four phage endolysins (LysA, LysA2, LysgaY, and lambdaSa2 endolysin) that exhibit strong lytic activity against Lactobacillus species, demonstrating their potential as antimicrobials to control bacterial contamination in fuel ethanol fermentations.
full_output.methodology: The study involves the purification and characterization of phage endolysins using turbidity reduction assays and zymogram analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Ureaplasma serovars & their antimicrobial susceptibility in patients of infertility & genital tract infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Ureaplasma serovars 3/14, 1, and 6 as prevalent in patients with genital tract infections and infertile women. Most Ureaplasma isolates were susceptible to doxycycline and josamycin, while resistance to ofloxacin and azithromycin was observed.
full_output.methodology: PCR-based serotyping and microbroth dilution method for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of line probe assay with liquid culture for rapid detection of multi-drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

rpoB.notes: Mutations in rpoB gene confer resistance to rifampicin.

inhA.notes: Mutations in inhA gene confer resistance to isoniazid.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the Genotype MTBDR plus assay for detecting rifampicin and isoniazid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, identifying specific mutations in rpoB, katG, and inhA genes that confer resistance.
full_output.methodology: The Genotype MTBDR plus assay was used to detect mutations in rpoB, katG, and inhA genes, with results compared to the MGIT 960 system.

full_output.paper_title: Reversal of MRP7 (ABCC10)-mediated multidrug resistance by tariquidar.

MRP7.validation_method: expression in HEK293 cells, resistance to MRP7 substrates

full_output.key_findings: Tariquidar reverses MRP7-mediated multidrug resistance by inhibiting MRP7 protein expression and function, increasing the sensitivity of MRP7-expressing cells to anticancer drugs such as paclitaxel, docetaxel, vincristine, vinblastine, and vinorelbine.
full_output.methodology: Expression of MRP7 in HEK293 cells, MTT assay, immunoblotting, [3H]-paclitaxel accumulation and efflux studies, flow cytometry.

full_output.paper_title: Decontamination of mycoplasma-contaminated Orientia tsutsugamushi strains by repeating passages through cell cultures with antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that repeated passages of mycoplasma-contaminated Orientia tsutsugamushi strains through cell cultures with lincomycin effectively eliminate mycoplasmas without affecting the growth of O. tsutsugamushi.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR-based methods and immunofluorescence staining to monitor mycoplasma contamination and O. tsutsugamushi growth during antibiotic treatment.

full_output.paper_title: Phosphorylation of HopQ1, a type III effector from Pseudomonas syringae, creates a binding site for host 14-3-3 proteins.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that phosphorylation of HopQ1 at Ser-51 creates a binding site for host 14-3-3 proteins, which influences its subcellular localization and stability.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized mass spectrometry, FRET analysis, and biochemical assays to investigate the interaction between HopQ1 and 14-3-3 proteins.

full_output.paper_title: Phosphate limitation induces the intergeneric inhibition of Pseudomonas aeruginosa by Serratia marcescens isolated from paper machines.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies an endonuclease bacteriocin produced by Serratia marcescens WW4 that inhibits Pseudomonas aeruginosa WW5 under phosphate-limiting conditions.
full_output.methodology: Random transposon mutagenesis and mutant analysis to identify the inhibitory gene.

full_output.paper_title: A hospital-based matched case-control study to identify clinical outcome and risk factors associated with carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M-2 and bla GES-1 as the main resistance mechanisms in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, along with alterations in ompK35 and ompK36 genes contributing to reduced carbapenem susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, and SDS-PAGE were used to analyze beta-lactamase genes and outer membrane protein alterations.

full_output.paper_title: Diverse and abundant antibiotic resistance genes in Chinese swine farms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a wide variety of antibiotic resistance genes in Chinese swine farms, highlighting the extensive and diverse nature of the antibiotic resistance reservoir in these environments.
full_output.methodology: The study used high-capacity quantitative PCR to analyze the abundance and diversity of antibiotic resistance genes in manure, compost, and soil samples from swine farms.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies auranofin as an effective treatment against metronidazole-resistant Giardia lamblia, demonstrating its activity against diverse isolates and overcoming metronidazole resistance.
full_output.methodology: Screening of a chemical library of approved drugs and bioactive compounds for antigiardial activity, followed by in vitro and in vivo testing.

full_output.paper_title: Bis-(3′-5′)-Cyclic Dimeric GMP Regulates Antimicrobial Peptide Resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that low intracellular levels of c-di-GMP enhance resistance to colistin in Pseudomonas aeruginosa by inducing the expression of pmrB and arnB, which are involved in lipid A modification.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized proteomics analysis, fluorescence-based reporter assays, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to investigate the role of c-di-GMP in antimicrobial peptide resistance.

full_output.methodology: Modified serum bactericidal assay, colony immunoblotting, Western blot, whole-cell ELISA, and FACS analysis were used to assess the impact of porA phase variation on immune escape.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the mechanism of tetracycline resistance mediated by the ribosomal protection protein Tet(O), highlighting the critical role of three loops in domain IV of Tet(O) in disrupting tetracycline binding to the ribosome.
full_output.methodology: Cryo-EM, mutational analysis, and MIC measurements were used to investigate the structural and functional aspects of Tet(O)-mediated tetracycline resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Honeybees and tetracycline resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the presence of diverse tetracycline resistance genes in the honeybee gut, indicating the impact of long-term tetracycline use in beekeeping on the development of resistance in non-pathogenic gut flora.
full_output.methodology: Analysis of honeybee gut flora and comparison with resistance patterns in other ecosystems.

full_output.paper_title: Evidence for an ABC-type riboflavin transporter system in pathogenic spirochetes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies an ABC-type riboflavin transporter system in pathogenic spirochetes, including Treponema pallidum, which is essential for acquiring riboflavin, an essential nutrient for the organism's survival.
full_output.methodology: Structural and functional characterization of recombinant proteins, UV-visible spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, thin-layer chromatography, RT-PCR, and X-ray crystallography.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Adenylosuccinate Synthetase and Lyase in Leishmania donovani
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the L. donovani ASL gene, demonstrating its functionality through complementation of E. coli asl deficiency and kinetic analysis.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial complementation, protein purification, and kinetic analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the evolutionary dynamics of β-lactamases, highlighting their role as a model for understanding the mechanisms of antibiotic resistance. It emphasizes the ancient origins of antibiotic resistance genes and their diversification through horizontal gene transfer and environmental pressures.
full_output.methodology: The paper uses phylogenetic analysis and comparative genomics to study the evolution of β-lactamase families.

full_output.paper_title: Litopenaeus vannamei sterile-alpha and armadillo motif containing protein (LvSARM) is involved in regulation of Penaeidins and antilipopolysaccharide factors.
full_output.key_findings: LvSARM was identified as a negative regulator of the Toll pathway in shrimp, modulating the expression of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) such as Penaeidins and antilipopolysaccharide factors (ALFs).
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, qPCR, luciferase reporter assays, and RNAi experiments were used to characterize LvSARM's role in immune regulation.

full_output.paper_title: Fermentation of Propionibacterium acnes, a commensal bacterium in the human skin microbiome, as skin probiotics against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: Propionibacterium acnes fermentation reduces the growth of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) by producing short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), including propionic acid, which lowers the intracellular pH of S. aureus and suppresses its growth.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro and in vivo experiments, including overlay assays, NMR analysis, and mouse skin infection models, to evaluate the antimicrobial effects of P. acnes fermentation products against MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Community-wide plasmid gene mobilization and selection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a variety of antibiotic and heavy metal resistance genes in plasmid metagenomes from activated sludge systems, highlighting the role of plasmids in the mobilization and selection of resistance traits in microbial communities.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis of plasmid DNA from activated sludge samples, followed by sequencing, assembly, and functional annotation.

full_output.paper_title: Acquisition of drug resistance and dependence by prions.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that prions can acquire resistance and dependence to the drug swainsonine through propagation in specific PK1 cell sublines, highlighting conformational changes in the prion protein as the underlying mechanism.

full_output.paper_title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa PA1006, which plays a role in molybdenum homeostasis, is required for nitrate utilization, biofilm formation, and virulence.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PA1006 as a critical gene for nitrate utilization, biofilm formation, and virulence in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Deletion of PA1006 leads to impaired anaerobic growth, reduced virulence, and defective biofilm maturation.
full_output.methodology: The study uses genetic deletion mutants, complementation experiments, and various microbiological assays to investigate the role of PA1006 in P. aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Sensitive detection of pre-existing BCR-ABL kinase domain mutations in CD34+ cells of newly diagnosed chronic-phase chronic myeloid leukemia patients is associated with imatinib resistance: implications in the post-imatinib era.

full_output.methodology: The study used ASO-PCR and DNA sequencing to detect BCR-ABL mutations in CD34+ cells from 100 chronic-phase CML patients.

full_output.methodology: Phage display library screening, ELISA, fluorometry, antimicrobial activity assays, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to characterize the peptide EC5.

full_output.methodology: SLIC cloning, PCR linearization, and transformation into E. coli cells.

full_output.paper_title: Disruption of the serine/threonine protein kinase H affects phthiocerol dimycocerosates synthesis in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.methodology: The study used radiolabelling, TLC, MS, and immunostaining to analyze lipid profiles and protein expression in wild-type, ΔpknH, and complemented strains of M. tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Injured Libyan combatant patients: both vectors and victims of multiresistance bacteria?
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the spread of multidrug-resistant bacteria, including carbapenemase-producing K. pneumoniae (OXA-48, CTX-M-15, DHA-1), A. baumannii (OXA-23, NDM-1), and MRSA, among injured Libyan patients transferred to various countries.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular cloning of a novel bioH gene from an environmental metagenome encoding a carboxylesterase with exceptional tolerance to organic solvents.
full_output.key_findings: A novel bioH gene, bioHx, was cloned and characterized from an environmental metagenome. The BioHx protein exhibited carboxylesterase activity and exceptional resistance to organic solvents.
full_output.methodology: Functional metagenomic approach, gene cloning, expression in E. coli, and biochemical characterization.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of genes involved in serum tolerance in the clinical strain Cronobacter sakazakii ES5.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified genes involved in serum tolerance in Cronobacter sakazakii ES5, including ESA_04103 and ybaJ, through transposon mutagenesis and functional analysis.

full_output.paper_title: The impact of aminoglycosides on the dynamics of translation elongation.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the mechanisms of action of three aminoglycosides (apramycin, paromomycin, and gentamicin) on translation elongation, focusing on their effects on ribosomal dynamics and tRNA interactions.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized single-molecule fluorescence measurements, structural analyses, and biochemical techniques to examine the effects of aminoglycosides on ribosomal function.

full_output.paper_title: YihE kinase is a central regulator of programmed cell death in bacteria.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies YihE as a central regulator of programmed cell death in bacteria, showing that its absence increases stress-mediated lethality and that it protects E. coli from various stressors by antagonizing the MazEF toxin-antitoxin system.

full_output.paper_title: Phylogenetic and molecular analysis of food-borne shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli.

Loss-of-function mutations in tarO, tarA, and tarG confer resistance to these inhibitors, highlighting their importance in WTA biosynthesis and antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Chemical screening, whole genome sequencing, mutagenesis, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and validate WTAI targets and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Clonal multidrug-resistant Corynebacterium striatum within a nosocomial environment, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study documents a nosocomial outbreak of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Corynebacterium striatum in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, highlighting the prevalence of MDR strains and their association with severe clinical outcomes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized 16S rRNA and rpoB gene sequencing for identification, PFGE for clonal analysis, and disk diffusion for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Shigella in Brazilian children with acute diarrhoea: prevalence, antimicrobial resistance and virulence genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of Shigella infection in Brazilian children, with a shift from S. flexneri to S. sonnei. High rates of trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole resistance were observed, and various virulence genes (ipaH, iuc, sen, ial, sat, set1A) were detected in Shigella isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of virulence genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing via disk diffusion.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmid-based controls to detect rpoB mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis by quantitative polymerase chain reaction-high-resolution melting.

rpoB.mechanism: mutation in rifampicin resistance-determining region

rpoB.notes: C531T mutation in the rifampicin resistance-determining region of rpoB

full_output.key_findings: The study developed plasmid-based controls for detecting rpoB mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis using qPCR-HRM, identifying C526T and C531T mutations in the rifampicin resistance-determining region.
full_output.methodology: qPCR-HRM analysis and DNA sequencing were used to detect rpoB mutations in M. tuberculosis strains.

full_output.paper_title: Outbreak of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae: two-year epidemiologic follow-up in a tertiary hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes a carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) outbreak, identifying the blaKPC gene as a key factor in carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Polymerase chain reaction assays and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis were used to detect the blaKPC gene and characterize the outbreak.

full_output.paper_title: Magnetic separation and antibiotics selection enable enrichment of cells with ZFN/TALEN-induced mutations.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes two novel reporter systems for enriching cells with nuclease-induced mutations using magnetic separation and hygromycin selection. The hygromycin resistance gene was used as a selectable marker to identify cells with mutations.
full_output.methodology: Construction of reporter vectors, transfection of cells, magnetic separation, hygromycin selection, T7E1 assay, and sequencing analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic inducibility of the mexXY multidrug efflux operon of Pseudomonas aeruginosa: involvement of the MexZ anti-repressor ArmZ.
