full_output.paper_title: Discovery and Characterization of Chemical Compounds That Inhibit the Function of Aspartyl-tRNA Synthetase from Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two chemical compounds, BT02A02 and BT02C05, that inhibit the function of aspartyl-tRNA synthetase (AspRS) from Pseudomonas aeruginosa. These compounds showed broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against various bacterial strains, including efflux pump mutants and hypersensitive strains of P. aeruginosa, but did not affect wild-type strains. The mechanism of action of the compounds was found to be non-competitive with ATP or aspartic acid.
full_output.methodology: The study involved cloning and characterizing the AspRS gene from P. aeruginosa, followed by high-throughput screening of chemical compounds using scintillation proximity assay (SPA) technology to identify inhibitors of AspRS activity.

full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) strains (56.2%) in Kabul, Afghanistan, with most strains being multidrug-resistant. All strains were susceptible to vancomycin, and the most effective antibiotics were vancomycin, rifampicin, imipenem, clindamycin, amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, cefazolin, gentamicin, and doxycycline.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility profiles were determined by the disc diffusion method using standard CLSI protocols.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of Oxacillin and Cefoxitin Disk Diffusion and MIC Breakpoints Established by the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute for Detection of mecA-Mediated Oxacillin Resistance in Staphylococcus schleiferi.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates oxacillin and cefoxitin disk diffusion and MIC breakpoints for detecting mecA-mediated oxacillin resistance in Staphylococcus schleiferi, demonstrating that oxacillin testing using S. pseudintermedius breakpoints reliably identifies mecA-positive isolates, whereas cefoxitin testing performs poorly.

full_output.paper_title: Multi-antibiotic resistant extended-spectrum beta-lactamase producing bacteria pose a challenge to the effective treatment of wound and skin infections.

These bacteria exhibit multidrug resistance, particularly to beta-lactam antibiotics, with resistance rates exceeding 50% for certain antibiotics.

full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and ERIC-PCR were used to detect MBL-encoding genes and assess genetic relatedness.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring quinolone resistance-determining region in Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates from across India.

gyrA.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that a S91F substitution in the gyrA gene was demonstrated in all ciprofloxacin non-susceptible isolates and that this substitution may be used as a marker for ciprofloxacin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the gyrA and parC genes of Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates from India, with a S91F substitution in gyrA being prevalent in all ciprofloxacin non-susceptible isolates. Additionally, various mutations in parC, including G85D, S87N, E91G, and E91K, were observed, contributing to ciprofloxacin resistance.
full_output.methodology: DNA sequence analysis of gyrA and parC genes combined with minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) determination using E-test.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Antibacterial Evaluation of a Series of 11,12-Cyclic Carbonate Azithromycin-3-O-descladinosyl-3-O-carbamoyl Glycosyl Derivatives.
full_output.key_findings: The study synthesized and evaluated a series of 11,12-cyclic carbonate azithromycin-3-O-descladinosyl-3-O-carbamoyl glycosyl derivatives, demonstrating improved antibacterial activity against various bacterial strains compared to the parent compound azithromycin.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis and in vitro antibacterial evaluation using MIC assays.

full_output.paper_title: Bloodstream infections at a tertiary level paediatric hospital in South Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the prevalence of bloodstream infections (BSI) in children at a South African hospital, noting the dominance of gram-negative bacteria such as Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae. It reports on the antimicrobial resistance profiles, including extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing organisms, and emphasizes the importance of monitoring resistance trends.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of blood culture data and antimicrobial susceptibility testing results from a pediatric hospital in South Africa.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative analysis of the Burkholderia cenocepacia K56-2 essential genome reveals cell envelope functions that are uniquely required for survival in species of the genus Burkholderia.

wq49_rs30025.validation_method: transposon insertion analysis and sequence homology

wq49_rs29130.validation_method: transposon insertion analysis and sequence homology

wq49_rs05300.validation_method: transposon insertion analysis and sequence homology

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 508 essential genes in Burkholderia cenocepacia K56-2, highlighting cell envelope functions that are uniquely essential for survival in Burkholderia species. It also finds 158 essential genes conserved across four Burkholderia strains, including those involved in cell wall/membrane/envelope biogenesis, lipid IV A biosynthesis, peptidoglycan biosynthesis, and 4-amino-4-deoxy-arabinose biosynthesis.
full_output.methodology: High-density transposon mutagenesis and Tn-seq circle method were used to identify essential genes, followed by bioinformatic analysis and comparison with other Burkholderia genomes.

full_output.paper_title: Novel large-scale chromosomal transfer in Bacteroides fragilis contributes to its pan-genome and rapid environmental adaptation.
full_output.key_findings: Large-scale chromosomal transfer in B. fragilis leads to the replacement of polysaccharide biosynthesis loci and introduces new restriction-modification systems, enhancing genomic diversity and environmental adaptation.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing, PCR analysis, and comparative genome analysis were used to characterize the transferred chromosomal segments and their impact on B. fragilis.

full_output.paper_title: Population structure of Escherichia coli O26 : H11 with recent and repeated stx2 acquisition in multiple lineages.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the mcr-1 gene, a plasmid-encoded colistin resistance gene, in two closely related ST21C1 strains isolated from bovines in Japan, highlighting the accumulation of antimicrobial resistance genes in the ST21C1 lineage.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis of O26: H11 strains to identify antimicrobial resistance genes and their distribution.

full_output.paper_title: Transcriptional Profiling of Saccharomyces cerevisiae Reveals the Impact of Variation of a Single Transcription Factor on Differential Gene Expression in 4NQO, Fermentable, and Nonfermentable Carbon Sources.

SNQ2.validation_method: overexpression in yeast and growth assays

Yrr1.notes: The I775E mutation in Yrr1 enhances 4NQO resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SNQ2 as a multidrug transporter that contributes to 4NQO resistance in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, with its overexpression sufficient to overcome 4NQO sensitivity.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq and ChIP-seq analyses combined with overexpression experiments and growth assays.

full_output.paper_title: Aminoglycoside interactions and impacts on the eukaryotic ribosome.

paromomycin.validation_method: X-ray crystallography and single-molecule FRET analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the binding sites of various aminoglycosides, including G418, paromomycin, gentamicin, and TC007, on the eukaryotic 80S ribosome, revealing their interactions and effects on ribosomal function and translation.
full_output.methodology: X-ray crystallography, single-molecule FRET analysis, and biochemical experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of D-Ala:D-Ala ligase through a phosphorylated form of the antibiotic D-cycloserine.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies DCSP, a phosphorylated form of D-cycloserine, as a novel chemical entity that inhibits D-Ala:D-Ala ligase (DdlB) by mimicking the D-alanyl phosphate intermediate, revealing a unique mechanism of antibiotic action.
full_output.methodology: Structural, chemical, and mechanistic studies including X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, and kinetic assays.

full_output.paper_title: Integrated Genomic and Proteomic Analyses of High-level Chloramphenicol Resistance in Campylobacter jejuni.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies cje1167 and cje1432 as genes contributing to high-level chloramphenicol resistance in Campylobacter jejuni, with cje1167 being a radical SAM enzyme and cje1432 a 16 S rRNA dimethyltransferase. Multiple mutations in cje1821 (cmeB) were also found to contribute to resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, gene knockout, complementation, and proteomic analysis were used to identify and validate AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Colistin-Resistant Escherichia coli Isolated from Diseased Pigs in France.

mgrB.notes: Detected in 1 CSTR isolate
mgrB.evidence_note: The mgrB gene was sequenced in the 79 CSTR isolates and in the 11 mcr-1 -positive or -negative CSTS isolates. Two mutations V8A (one mcr-1 negative isolate) and Q33R (three mcr-1 -positive isolates) were detected only in CSTR isolates.

phoP.evidence_note: The paper states that mutations in PhoP, specifically V108M and A182P, were detected in CSTR isolates.

pmrB.notes: Detected in 1 mcr-1-negative isolate

MgrB.encodes: transmembrane protein involved in regulation of PhoQ
MgrB.evidence_note: Mutations in MgrB were detected in colistin-resistant E. coli isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mcr-1 gene as a major contributor to colistin resistance in Escherichia coli isolates from diseased pigs in France, along with various mutations in genes involved in the regulation of colistin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Influence of Stress and Antibiotic Resistance on Cell-Length Distribution in Mycobacterium tuberculosis Clinical Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that multidrug-resistant (MDR) Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains exhibited increased cell length heterogeneity compared to sensitive strains in infected macrophages and during growth under rifampicin (RIF) treatment. Additionally, host stress factors such as oxidative stress and iron deficiency were associated with increased cell-length distribution in M. tuberculosis strains.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed M. tuberculosis cell-length distribution in sputum, macrophage infections, and liquid cultures using Ziehl-Neelsen staining and image analysis. Drug susceptibility tests were performed using the BACTEC MGIT 960 SIRE Kit.

full_output.paper_title: CTX-M-15-Producing E. coli Isolates from Food Products in Germany Are Mainly Associated with an IncF-Type Plasmid and Belong to Two Predominant Clonal E. coli Lineages.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla CTX-M-15-positive E. coli isolates from food products in Germany, primarily associated with IncF-type plasmids and belonging to two predominant clonal lineages, ST167 and ST410. These isolates carry various resistance genes including aac(6')-Ib-cr, aadA5, bla OXA-1, catB3, mph(A), sul1, tet(B), and dfrA17.
full_output.methodology: PCR, Sanger sequencing, whole genome sequencing, and molecular typing techniques such as PFGE and MLST were used to characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Increased Expression of a MicroRNA Correlates with Anthelmintic Resistance in Parasitic Nematodes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies hco-miR-9551 as a microRNA significantly upregulated in ivermectin-resistant strains of Haemonchus contortus and Teladorsagia circumcincta, suggesting its involvement in anthelmintic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Microarray and qRT-PCR analysis were used to assess miRNA expression in resistant and susceptible nematode strains.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple strains and backcross generations analyzed.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance of Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae: Epidemiology, Hypervirulence-Associated Determinants, and Resistance Mechanisms.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the emergence of carbapenem-resistant hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (hvKP) strains, particularly those harboring the blaKPC-2 and blaSHV-11 genes, which confer resistance to carbapenems and beta-lactams, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Analysis of clinical isolates and molecular characterization of resistance genes.
full_output.sample_size: Various clinical isolates from different regions

full_output.paper_title: Serotype prevalence and antibiotic susceptibility patterns of pneumococcal isolates in Zunyi city, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the most prevalent pneumococcal serotypes in Zunyi city, China, and assessed their antibiotic susceptibility. It found that serotypes 19F, 6A/6B, 19A, 23F, and 15B/15C were the most common, with high resistance rates to erythromycin, tetracycline, and trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole. Penicillin remained largely effective, with low resistance rates.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of pneumococcal isolates using VITEK2 and E-tests for antimicrobial susceptibility, and multiplex PCR for serotyping.

full_output.paper_title: AcAxl2 and AcMst1 regulate arthrospore development and stress resistance in the cephalosporin C producer Acremonium chrysogenum.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies AcAxl2 and AcMst1 as key regulators of arthrospore development and stress resistance in Acremonium chrysogenum, demonstrating that AcAxl2 accelerates and AcMst1 delays arthrospore formation, highlighting their roles in stress response mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Functional characterization of gene deletions and overexpression strains, microscopic analysis, and stress assays were employed to investigate the roles of AcAxl2 and AcMst1 in arthrospore development and stress resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Structural and immunological analysis of the Leptospira LigB protein reveals a novel vaccine candidate
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the LigB protein as a critical surface antigen of Leptospira and demonstrates that chimeric LigB Ig-like domains can elicit protective immunity against leptospiral infection.
full_output.methodology: The research combined structural biology techniques, including SAXS and NMR, with immunological assays to analyze the LigB protein and evaluate the efficacy of chimeric LigB constructs as vaccine candidates.

full_output.paper_title: Dual Regulation of the Small RNA MicC and the Quiescent Porin OmpN in Response to Antibiotic Stress in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the small RNA MicC and the quiescent porin OmpN are co-regulated in response to antibiotic stress, particularly β-lactam antibiotics. It also highlights the role of σ E and H-NS in regulating MicC and OmpN expression.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized lacZ transcriptional fusions, β-galactosidase assays, Western blot analysis, and mutagenesis to investigate the regulation of MicC and OmpN in response to antibiotic stress.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified arsenic resistance genes arsB and arsC in E. coli strains from Bangladeshi children with high arsenic exposure, which were not present in the European cohort.
full_output.methodology: 16S rRNA gene sequencing, whole metagenome shotgun sequencing, qPCR, and bioinformatic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antibiotic resistance of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in water samples in central Italy and molecular characterization of oprD in imipenem resistant isolates.

oprD.validation_method: DNA sequencing and analysis of oprD gene

oprD.notes: Mutations in oprD lead to loss of porin function and imipenem resistance.
oprD.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that mutations in oprD, including deletions and insertions, lead to loss of porin function and imipenem resistance.

full_output.key_findings: Imipenem resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates was associated with inactivating mutations in the oprD gene, leading to loss of the OprD porin and reduced susceptibility to imipenem.
full_output.methodology: DNA sequencing of the oprD gene and analysis of mutations in imipenem-resistant isolates.

full_output.paper_title: LipL21 lipoprotein binding to peptidoglycan enables Leptospira interrogans to escape NOD1 and NOD2 recognition.
full_output.key_findings: LipL21, a conserved outer membrane lipoprotein of pathogenic Leptospira interrogans, binds to peptidoglycan and prevents its degradation into muropeptides, thereby enabling the bacteria to escape recognition by NOD1 and NOD2 receptors.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, PCR, Western blot, HPLC, mass spectrometry, and reporter assays in HEK293T cells.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple strains of Leptospira interrogans and L. biflexa, including mutants and complemented strains.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Investigation of a Putative Endoscope-Associated Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacter cloacae Outbreak Reveals a Wide Diversity of Circulating Strains and Resistance Mutations.

full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing of 42 CREC isolates and 38 contemporaneous carbapenem-sensitive isolates, along with genomic analysis to identify resistance mechanisms.
full_output.sample_size: 42 CREC isolates and 38 contemporaneous carbapenem-sensitive isolates

full_output.paper_title: Quizartinib (AC220) reverses ABCG2-mediated multidrug resistance: In vitro and in vivo studies.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized a melting curve assay with a microarray to detect mutations in M. tuberculosis strains.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations in the PA Protein of Avian H5N1 Influenza Viruses Affect Polymerase Activity and Mouse Virulence.

full_output.paper_title: A Comprehensive Assessment of the Genetic Determinants in Salmonella Typhimurium for Resistance to Hydrogen Peroxide Using Proteogenomics.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes involved in Salmonella Typhimurium's resistance to hydrogen peroxide, including aromatic amino acid biosynthesis genes (aroB, aroK), putative iron transporter genes (ybbK, ybbL, ybbM), DNA repair genes (recA, recG, xthA, uvrA, uvrC, uvrD, polA), Fe-S cluster biogenesis genes (iscA, hscB, hscA, sufS, sufC), DNA adenine methylase genes (dam, damX), and others (rpoS, pgm, tonB).

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Fusobacterium varium Fv113-g1 isolated from a patient with ulcerative colitis based on complete genome sequence and transcriptome analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of metallo-β-lactamases-encoding genes among clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in a tertiary care hospital, Kathmandu, Nepal.

full_output.paper_title: PsrA controls the synthesis of the Pseudomonas aeruginosa quinolone signal via repression of the FadE homolog, PA0506.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that PsrA represses PA0506, a FadE homolog, which is crucial for the fatty acid β-oxidation pathway. This repression allows the accumulation of octanoyl-CoA, a precursor for PQS synthesis. Deletion of psrA leads to increased PA0506 expression, reducing PQS production.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic mutants, qRT-PCR, and biochemical assays to investigate the role of PsrA and PA0506 in PQS production.

full_output.paper_title: Cleavage of osmosensitive transcriptional factor NFAT5 by Coxsackieviral protease 2A promotes viral replication.

mutations_found.validated_by: site-directed mutagenesis and Western blot analysis

NFAT5.notes: The G503A mutation prevents cleavage by CVB3 protease 2A.
NFAT5.evidence_note: The mutation was validated through site-directed mutagenesis and Western blot analysis.

full_output.key_findings: NFAT5 is cleaved by CVB3 protease 2A at G503, and the cleavage product p70-NFAT5 acts as a dominant negative fragment, reducing NFAT5 activity and promoting CVB3 replication.
full_output.methodology: Western blot analysis, site-directed mutagenesis, and luciferase assays.

full_output.paper_title: A Novel Nonantibiotic, lgt-Based Selection System for Stable Maintenance of Expression Vectors in Escherichia coli and Vibrio cholerae.

lgt.mechanism: essential for the biosynthesis of bacterial lipoprotein
lgt.role_in_paper: core component of the selection system

full_output.key_findings: The study describes a novel nonantibiotic selection system using the lgt gene for stable maintenance of expression vectors in E. coli and V. cholerae. Deletion of lgt is lethal, and its complementation with the V. cholerae lgt gene allows for plasmid maintenance without antibiotic selection.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, complementation, plasmid construction, and expression analysis in E. coli and V. cholerae.

full_output.paper_title: Immune stealth-driven O2 serotype prevalence and potential for therapeutic antibodies against multidrug resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies human monoclonal antibodies targeting O-antigens of K. pneumoniae, which show protective effects against multidrug-resistant strains, especially in combination with antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation and characterization of monoclonal antibodies against K. pneumoniae O1 and O2 LPS, assessment of their opsonophagocytic killing activity, and evaluation of their protective effects in murine infection models.

full_output.paper_title: Surveillance of antibiotic resistance among common Clostridium difficile ribotypes in Hong Kong.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized the antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of common Clostridium difficile ribotypes in Hong Kong, revealing high resistance to cephalosporins, fluoroquinolones, and other antibiotics, with ribotypes 017 and 002 showing significant multi-drug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using the agar dilution method, and PCR ribotyping was employed to identify prevalent ribotypes.

full_output.paper_title: Biotrophy-necrotrophy switch in pathogen evoke differential response in resistant and susceptible sesame involving multiple signaling pathways at different phases.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that the resistant sesame variety Nirmala exhibits delayed disease progression and enhanced defense mechanisms against the fungal pathogen Macrophomina phaseolina, including reduced ROS accumulation, upregulated ROS signaling genes, and improved antioxidant enzyme activities. Additionally, the resistant variety showed greater accumulation of secondary metabolites and upregulated secondary metabolite-related genes after the biotrophy-to-necrotrophy switch (BNS).
full_output.methodology: The study utilized microscopic analysis, q-PCR, and biochemical assays to examine the defense responses in resistant and susceptible sesame varieties during different infection phases of M. phaseolina.

full_output.paper_title: Phylogeny and antimicrobial resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates from Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

tetM.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The study characterized 116 Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates from Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, highlighting high resistance rates to penicillin, tetracycline, ciprofloxacin, and azithromycin. Key resistance mechanisms included chromosomal mutations in ponA, porB, rpsJ, gyrA, parC, and rrl, as well as plasmid-mediated resistance via blaTEM-1 and tetM. Promoter and coding region mutations in mtrR were also linked to azithromycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, agar dilution MIC testing, and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify resistance mechanisms and genetic variations.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular evaluation of colistin-resistant gene expression changes in Acinetobacter baumannii with real-time polymerase chain reaction.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pmrA and pmrB genes as critical for colistin resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii, showing that increased expression of pmrA is strongly correlated with resistance.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR and gene expression analysis were used to evaluate the role of pmrA and pmrB in colistin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin resistance and selective genetic determinants of Staphylococcus aureus isolates with bovine mastitis milk origin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a low prevalence of methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) isolates among bovine mastitis milk samples, with only 1.3% being methicillin-resistant. The spa, fnb, and ebpS genes were the most prevalent virulence factors.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and phenotypic testing for methicillin resistance and virulence genes.

full_output.paper_title: Cysteine and histidine residues are involved in Escherichia coli Tn21 MerE methylmercury transport.

merE.mechanism: metal-binding amino acid residues involved in mercury transport
merE.validation_method: site-directed mutagenesis and mercury uptake assays

mutations_found.position_in_molecule: periplasmic face between first and second transmembrane domains
periplasmic face between first and second transmembrane domains

merE.notes: Mutations in merE resulted in reduced mercury uptake.
merE.evidence_note: The paper describes the construction of merE variants and their effects on mercury uptake, supporting the role of merE in mercury transport.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the critical role of cysteine and histidine residues in the MerE protein for methylmercury and Hg(II) transport in E. coli.
full_output.methodology: Site-directed mutagenesis and mercury uptake assays were used to investigate the role of specific amino acid residues in MerE.

full_output.paper_title: Self-Conjugation of the Enteropathogenic Escherichia coli Adherence Factor Plasmid of Four Typical EPEC Isolates.

kanamycin resistance cassette.mechanism: insertion of a kanamycin resistance cassette into the pEAF plasmid

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the pEAF plasmids from four tEPEC strains are self-conjugative, capable of transferring to various E. coli strains, including a laboratory strain, with transfer frequencies ranging from 10^-6 to 10^-9. Additionally, aEPEC strains can receive the pEAF plasmid.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, conjugation experiments, and plasmid profiling were used to analyze the conjugative transfer ability of the pEAF plasmids.
full_output.sample_size: Four tEPEC strains and two aEPEC strains.

full_output.paper_title: What matters in chronic Burkholderia cenocepacia infection in cystic fibrosis: Insights from comparative genomics.

katG.encodes: hydrogen peroxide-detoxifying enzyme with hybrid catalase/peroxidase activity

yedY.encodes: methionine-sulfoxide reductase which repairs periplasmic proteins

cusS.encodes: sensory kinase that senses periplasmic copper

BCAL0155.encodes: cation diffusion facilitator family of divalent metal efflux transporter

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in genes involved in oxidative stress protection, such as katG, yedY, moeA1, cusS, and BCAL0155, which are associated with reduced resistance to hydrogen peroxide in Burkholderia cenocepacia ST32 during chronic infection.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, in vitro susceptibility testing, and deep population sequencing were used to analyze mutations and their effects on hydrogen peroxide resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Riemerella anatipestifer M949_0459 gene is responsible for the bacterial resistance to tigecycline.

M949_0459.mechanism: confers resistance to tigecycline via enzymatic inactivation
M949_0459.validation_method: overexpression in E. coli BL21 and MIC analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the M949_0459 gene in Riemerella anatipestifer as responsible for tigecycline resistance. Overexpression of this gene in E. coli BL21 conferred tigecycline resistance, demonstrating its role in enzymatic inactivation of the antibiotic.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, MIC assays, qRT-PCR, and gene overexpression in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: The rumen microbiome as a reservoir of antimicrobial resistance and pathogenicity genes is directly affected by diet in beef cattle.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that diet significantly affects the abundance and diversity of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes in the rumen microbiome of beef cattle, with concentrate diets enriching AMR genes such as those for macrolide, beta-lactam, chloramphenicol, aminoglycoside, and streptomycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis of rumen samples from beef cattle under different dietary regimes.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility of Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates in Vientiane, Lao PDR.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high resistance rates to penicillin (89.9%), tetracycline (99.4%), and ciprofloxacin (84.8%) among Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates in Vientiane, Laos, while all isolates remained susceptible to ceftriaxone and spectinomycin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility was determined using the disk diffusion method for 158 isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Insights into Colistin-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae from a Tunisian Teaching Hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the mgrB gene as a primary mechanism of colistin resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from a Tunisian hospital.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and complementation assays were used to investigate colistin resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Topical Antibiotic Use Coselects for the Carriage of Mobile Genetic Elements Conferring Resistance to Unrelated Antimicrobials in Staphylococcus aureus.

mupA.genetic_context: colocated downstream of the qacA gene on a resistance cassette on pNZAK1
mupA.evidence_note: The mupA gene (mediating high-level mupirocin resistance) was colocated downstream of the qacA gene on a resistance cassette on pNZAK1.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies fusC, mupA, and qacA as genes responsible for resistance to fusidic acid, mupirocin, and biocides, respectively, in Staphylococcus aureus. These genes are located on mobile genetic elements and contribute to multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and experimental assays were used to analyze the resistance mechanisms in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.sample_size: 118 ST1 S. aureus isolates from New Zealand and 61 international ST1 isolates

full_output.paper_title: Cystatins 9 and C as a Novel Immunotherapy Treatment That Protects against Multidrug-Resistant New Delhi Metallo-Beta-Lactamase-1-Producing Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that recombinant cystatin 9 (rCST9) and cystatin C (rCSTC) have antimicrobial activity against NDM-1-producing K. pneumoniae, reducing bacterial viability and improving survival in a murine model of pneumonia.
full_output.methodology: In vivo mouse model of NDM-1 K. pneumoniae infection, evaluation of survival, cytokine levels, bacterial load, and lung histology.

full_output.paper_title: cas9 Enhances Bacterial Virulence by Repressing the regR Transcriptional Regulator in Streptococcus agalactiae.

regR.validation_method: transcriptomic analysis and hyaluronidase activity assay

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies regR as a transcriptional regulator that represses hyaluronidase activity in Streptococcus agalactiae, and shows that cas9 is required for the degradation of regR mRNA, leading to increased hyaluronidase activity and enhanced virulence.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis, qRT-PCR, hyaluronidase activity assay, and bacterial infection models.

full_output.paper_title: Structure and activity of ChiX: a peptidoglycan hydrolase required for chitinase secretion by Serratia marcescens.
full_output.key_findings: ChiX is a Zn2+-dependent l-Ala d-Glu endopeptidase that plays a crucial role in the secretion of chitinolytic machinery in Serratia marcescens. A D120A mutation in ChiX leads to loss of enzymatic activity and inability to rescue the secretion defect in a chiX mutant strain.
full_output.methodology: Structural and biochemical characterization, site-directed mutagenesis, peptidoglycan hydrolysis assays, and complementation of mutant phenotypes.

full_output.paper_title: Multiple substitutions lead to increased loop flexibility and expanded specificity in Acinetobacter baumannii carbapenemase OXA-239.
Structural and functional insights into the role of BamD and BamE within the β-barrel assembly machinery in Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that BamD is essential for the viability of Neisseria gonorrhoeae, while BamE is not. BamE is surface-exposed under native conditions, but in its absence, BamD becomes surface-exposed, leading to increased antibiotic susceptibility and altered membrane vesicle composition.
full_output.methodology: The study employed mutagenesis, knockout studies, and structural analyses to investigate the roles of BamD and BamE in N. gonorrhoeae.

full_output.paper_title: A novel Tn1696-like composite transposon (Tn6404) harboring bla (IMP-4) in a Klebsiella pneumoniae isolate carrying a rare ESBL gene bla (SFO-1).

blaIMP-4.evidence_note: blaIMP-4 is carried by a novel In804-like integron (intlI-blaIMP-4-Kl.pn.I3-qacG2-aacA4-catB3∆) associated with a novel Tn1696-like transposon (designed Tn6404) flanked by IS5075.

blaSFO-1.evidence_note: blaSFO-1 was identified in the plasmid pKP1814-1 and is associated with an IS/Tn-independent genetic context.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel Tn1696-like transposon (Tn6404) harboring the carbapenemase gene blaIMP-4 and the rare ESBL gene blaSFO-1 in a multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolate. Both genes were experimentally validated for their resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, cloning, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Serotype and virulence genes of Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from mink and its pathogenesis in mice and mink.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various virulence genes in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from mink, including wabG, ureA, rmpA, aerobactin, uge, IucB, and ybtA, which are associated with the pathogenicity of the bacteria in mice and mink.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect serotypes and virulence genes in K. pneumoniae isolates, followed by animal experiments to assess pathogenicity.

full_output.key_findings: Collismycin C from Streptomyces sp. MC025 was identified as a potent antibiofilm agent that inhibits biofilm formation by both methicillin-sensitive and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus by chelating iron ions.
full_output.methodology: Bioactivity-guided isolation, NMR spectroscopy, and biofilm formation assays were used to characterize the antibiofilm activity of compounds isolated from Streptomyces sp. MC025.

full_output.paper_title: Novel Effective Small-Molecule Antibacterials against Enterococcus Strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the discovery of novel indolyl benzocarbazole compounds with potent antibacterial activity against Enterococcus species, including vancomycin-resistant strains. Substitution patterns on the indole ring significantly influenced the antibacterial efficacy.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of indolyl benzocarbazoles and evaluation of their antibacterial activity using MIC assays against various Enterococcus strains.

full_output.key_findings: Elizabethkingia miricola was identified as an opportunistic oral pathogen in a patient with common variable immunodeficiency, showing resistance to multiple antibiotics except ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.
full_output.methodology: Microbial culture, MALDI-TOF MS identification, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of OXA-204 carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae reveals possible endoscopy-associated transmission, France, 2012 to 2014.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the blaOXA-204 gene as a carbapenemase responsible for resistance in Enterobacteriaceae, highlighting its association with an IncA/C plasmid and potential for endoscopy-associated transmission.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, susceptibility testing, MLST, and rep-PCR analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Diversification of Type VI Secretion System Toxins Reveals Ancient Antagonism among Bee Gut Microbes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Rhs toxins in S. alvi that have antibacterial activity and are upregulated in vivo. These toxins are associated with T6SS-1 and are functionally validated through cloning and expression in E. coli.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, RNA-Seq, transposon mutagenesis, and cloning in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Importance of Core Genome Functions for an Extreme Antibiotic Resistance Trait.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies core genome functions that play a crucial role in high-level tobramycin resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii, highlighting the significance of phospholipid biosynthesis, phosphate regulation, and envelope homeostasis. It also reveals that even in the presence of aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes, core functions remain vital for resistance.
full_output.methodology: Transposon sequencing (Tn-seq) and mutant MIC testing were used to identify genes and mutations involved in tobramycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Disabling a Type I-E CRISPR-Cas Nuclease with a Bacteriophage-Encoded Anti-CRISPR Protein.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the anti-CRISPR protein AcrE1, which inhibits the type I-E CRISPR-Cas system in Pseudomonas aeruginosa by binding to and inactivating the Cas3 nuclease.
full_output.methodology: X-ray crystallography, copurification experiments, and transcriptional repression assays.

full_output.paper_title: Persister Phenotypes as an 'Inside Job' of Φ80
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights that prophage induction and contamination significantly impact persister cell assays, leading to misleading results. It identifies that the presence of cryptic prophages and phi80 phage infections can alter persister survival measurements, challenging previous conclusions about the role of TA modules in persister formation.
full_output.methodology: The study used bacterial culture experiments, PCR, and genomic sequencing to investigate the effects of prophages on persister cell assays.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of Cytosolic Shigella flexneri via a C-Terminal Triple-Arginine Motif of GBP1 Inhibits Actin-Based Motility.

GBP1.mechanism: recruits to cytosolic bacteria via a C-terminal triple-arginine motif
GBP1.validation_method: colocalization studies with mCherry-GBP1 fusion proteins

GBP2.mechanism: recruited to cytosolic bacteria in a GBP1-dependent manner
GBP2.validation_method: colocalization studies with mCherry-GBP2 fusion proteins

full_output.key_findings: GBP1 recognizes cytosolic Gram-negative bacteria via a C-terminal triple-arginine motif, leading to bacterial clustering and inhibition of actin-based motility. GBP1's triple-arginine motif is crucial for its targeting to S. flexneri and B. thailandensis.
full_output.methodology: Colocalization studies using mCherry-GBP fusion proteins, mutagenesis, and bacterial infection assays.

full_output.paper_title: Lipoteichoic acid deficiency permits normal growth but impairs virulence of Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TacL as a lipoteichoic acid ligase necessary for LTA synthesis in Streptococcus pneumoniae, demonstrating that LTA is critical for virulence but not for normal growth.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, biochemical analysis, and molecular techniques were used to investigate the role of TacL in LTA synthesis and its impact on pneumococcal virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Balancing mcr-1 expression and bacterial survival is a delicate equilibrium between essential cellular defence mechanisms.

mcr-1.validation_method: overexpression in E. coli and measurement of growth, viability, and membrane integrity

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the mcr-1 gene, which encodes a lipid A modifying enzyme that confers resistance to colistin. Overexpression of mcr-1 leads to reduced bacterial growth, viability, and membrane integrity in E. coli.
full_output.methodology: Overexpression of mcr-1 in E. coli, growth curve analysis, qRT-PCR, TEM, and LIVE/DEAD staining.

full_output.paper_title: Revisiting unexploited antibiotics in search of new antibacterial drug candidates: the case of γ-actinorhodin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies γ-actinorhodin (γ-ACT) as a potent antibacterial compound with activity against Gram-positive pathogens, including methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) and vancomycin-intermediate S. aureus (VISA). It exhibits low resistance potential and a unique mode of action involving collapse of the proton motive force and generation of reactive oxygen species.
full_output.methodology: The study characterizes the antibacterial activity of γ-ACT through in vitro susceptibility testing, time-kill experiments, and mode of action studies using S. aureus strains and related mutants.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the efficacy of a phage cocktail for treating bovine Staphylococcus aureus mastitis in a mouse model, showing significant reduction in bacterial counts and improvement in pathology.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro and in vivo experiments to assess the effectiveness of a phage cocktail against S. aureus N305, including bacterial load quantification and histopathological analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Insertional inactivation of oprD in carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains isolated from burn patients in Tehran, Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies IS Ppu 21 insertion in the oprD gene as a novel mechanism of carbapenem resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from burn patients in Tehran, Iran.
full_output.methodology: PCR, real-time RT-PCR, SDS-PAGE, and RAPD-PCR were used to analyze gene expression, resistance mechanisms, and genetic relationships.

full_output.paper_title: Aminoglycoside resistance profile and structural architecture of the aminoglycoside acetyltransferase AAC(6')-Im.

aac(6')-Im.validation_method: expression in E. coli JM83 and MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The aminoglycoside acetyltransferase AAC(6')-Im confers resistance to 4,6-disubstituted aminoglycosides, with higher MICs compared to AAC(6')-Ie. It does not confer resistance to the atypical aminoglycoside fortimicin.
full_output.methodology: Expression in E. coli JM83, MIC testing, protein purification, crystallization, and structural analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic adaptation of microbial populations present in high-intensity catfish production systems with therapeutic oxytetracycline treatment.

ABC_efflux.validation_method: metagenomic analysis and selective sweep analysis

RND_efflux.validation_method: metagenomic analysis and selective sweep analysis

tet_MFS_efflux.encodes: Tetracycline resistance major facilitator superfamily efflux pump
tet_MFS_efflux.validation_method: metagenomic analysis and selective sweep analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study identified 21 antibiotic resistance (AR) genes under selection in microbial populations from high-intensity catfish production systems, primarily involving efflux pumps such as ABC, RND, and MFS families, along with beta-lactamases. These genes were linked to environmental selection pressures from oxytetracycline treatment.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing, selective sweep analysis, and comparative genomics were used to analyze microbial populations and their resistance mechanisms.
full_output.sample_size: Water and sediment samples from catfish production systems and control watersheds

full_output.paper_title: Illumina short-read and MinION long-read WGS to characterize the molecular epidemiology of an NDM-1 Serratia marcescens outbreak in Romania.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the molecular epidemiology of an NDM-1 Serratia marcescens outbreak in Romania, identifying blaNDM-1 as the primary resistance gene responsible for carbapenem resistance in the outbreak strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing using Illumina and MinION platforms, along with PCR and bioinformatics analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Zoonotic Transfer of Clostridium difficile Harboring Antimicrobial Resistance between Farm Animals and Humans.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of various antimicrobial resistance genes, including cdeA and ermB, in Clostridium difficile RT078 strains isolated from both humans and animals, suggesting a shared resistome and potential zoonotic transmission of these strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and comparative genomic analysis of 247 C. difficile RT078 strains from multiple countries.

full_output.paper_title: Recovery of Bordetella bronchiseptica sequence type 82 and B. pseudohinzii from urban rats in Terengganu, Malaysia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a novel B. bronchiseptica ST82 and B. pseudohinzii from wild rats in Malaysia, highlighting their antimicrobial resistance profiles and phylogenetic relationships.
full_output.methodology: 16S rDNA sequencing, MLST, nrdA typing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Treatment with Cefotaxime Affects Expression of Conjugation Associated Proteins and Conjugation Transfer Frequency of an IncI1 Plasmid in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: Cefotaxime treatment up-regulates conjugation-associated proteins and increases conjugation transfer frequency of an IncI1 plasmid carrying bla CTX-M-1 in Escherichia coli.
full_output.methodology: Proteome analysis, RT-qPCR, and conjugation experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteriocinogenic potential and virulence traits of Enterococcus faecium and E. faecalis isolated from human milk.
full_output.key_findings: E. faecalis TA102 exhibited vancomycin resistance through the presence of the vanA gene, along with virulence factors cylA and esp. E. faecium TA0033 lacked virulence and resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: PCR, phenotypic analysis, and agar well diffusion assay.

EhPgp5.mechanism: transcriptional activation by heat shock element (HSE) in response to emetine stress
EhPgp5.validation_method: transfection assays, CAT activity measurements, gel-shift assays, UV-crosslinking, western blotting

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a heat shock element (HSE) in the promoter region of the EhPgp5 gene that regulates its transcriptional activation in response to emetine stress. The HSE is essential for EhPgp5 gene expression, and its interaction with nuclear proteins suggests a role in multidrug resistance mechanisms in Entamoeba histolytica.
full_output.methodology: Transfection assays, CAT activity measurements, gel-shift assays, UV-crosslinking, and western blotting were used to analyze the functional role of the HSE in EhPgp5 gene regulation.

full_output.paper_title: Angular Phenozaxine Ethers as Potent Multi-microbial Targets Inhibitors: Design, Synthesis, and Molecular Docking Studies.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on designing, synthesizing, and evaluating the molecular docking of angular phenoxazine ether derivatives as potential inhibitors of microbial targets, including glucosamine-6-phosphate synthase, AmpC beta-lactamase, and Lanosterol-14alpha-demethylase. The compounds showed strong drug-likeness and favorable binding affinities to these targets, indicating their potential as antimicrobial agents.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of phenoxazine ether derivatives using palladium-catalyzed coupling reactions, followed by in-silico evaluations of drug-likeness and molecular docking studies to assess binding affinities to target proteins.

full_output.paper_title: Fusion proteins towards fungi and bacteria in plant protection.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed fusion proteins combining Blad, an antifungal protein, with SP10-5 and Sub5, antibacterial peptides, resulting in enhanced antimicrobial activity against various plant pathogens.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the design, expression, and evaluation of fusion proteins for antimicrobial activity against plant pathogens.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies l-cyclopropylalanine as a novel compound that inhibits the biosynthesis of l-leucine by targeting alpha-isopropylmalate synthase (alpha-IPMS), representing a new antibiotic mechanism.
full_output.methodology: The study isolates l-cyclopropylalanine from Amanita virgineoides and evaluates its inhibitory effects on fungal and bacterial growth, along with biochemical analysis of its target enzyme alpha-IPMS.

full_output.paper_title: Time trend analysis (2009-2016) of antimicrobial susceptibility in Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolated in Italy following the introduction of the combined antimicrobial therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the antimicrobial susceptibility trends of Neisseria gonorrhoeae in Italy from 2009 to 2016, focusing on azithromycin, cefixime, and ceftriaxone. It found a decrease in cefixime resistance and an increase in azithromycin resistance over time, highlighting the importance of monitoring resistance patterns to guide treatment strategies.
full_output.methodology: The study used a network of sexually transmitted disease clinics and laboratories to collect and analyze Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates. Antimicrobial susceptibility was tested using gradient diffusion methods, and statistical analyses were performed to evaluate resistance trends and associations with patient characteristics.

full_output.key_findings: The study presents a platform for rapid development of antimicrobials using synbodies, which are bivalent peptides capable of binding and neutralizing pathogens. The research focuses on the design and application of a 100-peptide microarray to identify peptides that can bind various pathogens, leading to the creation of synbodies with antiviral and antibacterial activities.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a 10,000-peptide microarray to screen for pathogen-binding peptides, followed by the development of a 100-peptide microarray. Synbodies were created by combining selected peptides and tested for their ability to inhibit viral and bacterial growth.

full_output.paper_title: Interaction of Antibiotics with Innate Host Defense Factors against Salmonella enterica Serotype Newport.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the activity of antibiotics against Salmonella enterica serotype Newport, highlighting the synergistic effects of ceftriaxone (CRO) and ciprofloxacin (CIP) in both conventional and physiological media, as well as their synergy with the cathelicidin LL-37. It also shows that sub-MIC concentrations of CRO can sensitize Salmonella to innate immune-mediated killing.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, checkerboard assays, time-kill assays, and neutrophil and whole-blood killing assays were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of the Mechanisms of Daptomycin Resistance among Gram-Positive Bacterial Pathogens by Multidimensional Lipidomics.

mutations_found.validated_by: HILIC-IM-MS lipid profiling and whole-genome sequencing

pgsA.notes: Mutation in pgsA was found in daptomycin-resistant S. aureus and C. striatum.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies designed host defense peptides (dHDPs) with broad-spectrum bactericidal activity against Gram-positive and -negative bacteria, including drug-resistant strains like MRSA and P. aeruginosa. full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the bactericidal activity of dHDPs using MIC and MBEC assays, time-kill assays, and in vivo murine models of bacterial keratitis.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility and molecular epidemiology of clinical Enterobacter cloacae bloodstream isolates in Shanghai, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Enterobacter cloacae bloodstream isolates, including ESBLs (SHV-12, CTX-M-15, CTX-M-65), carbapenemases (IMP-26, NDM-1), plasmid-mediated AmpC beta-lactamases (ACT-20, ACT-3, DHA-1), and TEM-1. These genes were associated with resistance to various antibiotics, highlighting the need for continued surveillance.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect AMR genes, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using disk diffusion.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical and microbiological characteristics of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium bloodstream infection in Central Taiwan.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the vanA gene as the prevalent genotype among vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VRE fae) isolates, which confers resistance to vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: PCR-based genotyping and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and characterization of HepP: a virulence-related Pseudomonas aeruginosa heparinase.

hepP.mechanism: confers resistance to host defenses via degradation of heparin and heparan sulfate
hepP.validation_method: functional characterization of recombinant HepP showing heparinase activity

zbdP.mechanism: may contribute to virulence through unknown pathway

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes hepP, a gene encoding a potential heparinase in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and shows its role in virulence and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, expression, purification, and activity assays were performed to characterize HepP.

full_output.paper_title: Detection and identification of antimicrobial-resistant Salmonella in raw beef at Wolaita Sodo municipal abattoir, Southern Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 12.5% of raw beef samples were contaminated with Salmonella, and most isolates exhibited multidrug resistance. High resistance rates were observed to tetracycline, nitrofurantoin, streptomycin, and chloramphenicol.
full_output.methodology: The study involved microbiological isolation and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of Salmonella isolates from raw beef samples using disk diffusion methods.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome sequencing reveals transmission of gonococcal antibiotic resistance among men who have sex with men: an observational study.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the transmission of antibiotic-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains between men who have sex with men, highlighting the role of specific genes and mutations in conferring resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and comparative genomic analysis were used to investigate the transmission of antibiotic resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic dissection of cyclic pyranopterin monophosphate biosynthesis in plant mitochondria.

ATM3.notes: causes a substitution in the sixth transmembrane helix

CNX2.notes: causes a substitution in the N-terminus
CNX2.evidence_note: The paper describes a mutation in CNX2 (G263>A) that causes a substitution of arginine 88 with glutamine (R88Q) in the N-terminus of the protein. This mutation was identified through sequencing and enzyme activity assays. The paper also mentions that the mutation was found in Arabidopsis thaliana.

full_output.paper_title: Increasing the permeability of Escherichia coli using MAC13243.
full_output.key_findings: MAC13243 increases the permeability of the outer membrane of Escherichia coli, making it more susceptible to large-scaffold antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening, NPN uptake assays, susceptibility testing, and CRISPRi experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Culture and Next-generation sequencing-based drug susceptibility testing unveil high levels of drug-resistant-TB in Djibouti: results from the first national survey.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) in Djibouti, with 4.7% of new and 30.8% of previously treated cases. Mutations in the rrs, tlyA, and pncA genes were associated with resistance to aminoglycosides, capreomycin, and pyrazinamide, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome and targeted next-generation sequencing were used to identify drug resistance mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial activity of ceramide and ceramide analogs against pathogenic Neisseria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that sphingosine, short-chain C6-ceramide, and omega-azido-C6-ceramide exhibit significant antibacterial activity against Neisseria meningitidis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae, demonstrating potent bactericidal effects.
full_output.methodology: Broth microdilution assays, time-killing studies, flow cytometry, and super-resolution imaging techniques were employed to evaluate the antibacterial activity and mechanisms of ceramide and ceramide analogs.

full_output.paper_title: Leukotriene B(4) is essential for lung host defence and alpha-defensin-1 production during Achromobacter xylosoxidans infection.
full_output.key_findings: LTB4 induces alpha-defensin-1 expression, which is critical for clearing A. xylosoxidans by disrupting its cell wall.
full_output.methodology: Mouse infection models, qRT-PCR, ELISA, and bacterial killing assays.

full_output.paper_title: Intrinsic Immunity Shapes Viral Resistance of Stem Cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies IFITM1, IFITM2, IFITM3, and p21/CDKN1A as intrinsic antiviral genes in stem cells that confer resistance to multiple viruses, including dengue, yellow fever, zika, and West Nile viruses.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, shRNA-mediated knockdown, viral infection assays, and RNA-Seq transcriptome analyses.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Activity of Neomycin, Streptomycin, Paromomycin and Apramycin against Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacteriaceae Clinical Strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that apramycin showed high in vitro activity against carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) strains, with 95.5% of the strains being susceptible. The aac(3)-IVa gene was identified as the resistance determinant for apramycin in the resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study determined the in vitro susceptibility of four aminoglycosides against CRE clinical strains using broth microdilution and identified resistance genes through whole genome sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Clonal Diversity, Virulence Potential and Antimicrobial Resistance of Escherichia coli Causing Community Acquired Urinary Tract Infection in Switzerland.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified plasmid-mediated resistance genes aac(6')-Ib-cr, bla CTX-M-14, bla CTX-M-15, and mph(A) in Escherichia coli isolates causing community-acquired urinary tract infections in Switzerland.
full_output.methodology: Multilocus sequence typing, virulence factor determination, and phenotypic and genotypic antimicrobial resistance testing were performed on 44 non-duplicate UPEC isolates.

full_output.paper_title: XAP5 CIRCADIAN TIMEKEEPER Positively Regulates RESISTANCE TO POWDERY MILDEW8.1-Mediated Immunity in Arabidopsis.

mutations_found.protein_change: truncated XCT lacking the C-terminal 79 amino acid residues

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel allele of XCT (xct-5) that impairs RPW8.1-mediated immunity against powdery mildew and bacterial pathogens. XCT positively regulates RPW8.1 expression and immunity.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screening, mutant analysis, transgenic overexpression, qRT-PCR, and complementation tests.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Conserved ABC Importers Necessary for Intracellular Survival of Legionella pneumophila in Multiple Hosts.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies lpg0730 and lpg0122 as conserved ABC importer complex components crucial for the intracellular survival of Legionella pneumophila in multiple host cells, including amoebae and macrophages. Disruption of these genes leads to impaired intracellular survival, and their functionality is conserved in other bacterial pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide transposon mutagenesis, transposon insertion site validation, complementation studies, and intracellular survival assays in various host cell types.

full_output.paper_title: Cis-acting DNA elements flanking the variable major protein expression site of Borrelia hermsii are required for murine persistence.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the upstream homology sequence (UHS) and downstream homology sequence (DHS) of the vmp Ex locus are crucial for antigenic switching and persistence of Borrelia hermsii in immunocompetent mice.
full_output.methodology: Targeted deletion and in cis complementation techniques were used to generate mutants and analyze their ability to relapse in mice.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Evaluation of (S)-Amino Acid-Derived Thiazole Analogues as P-gp Modulators
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several (S)-amino acid-derived thiazole analogues that modulate P-gp activity, with compound 53 showing strong ATPase inhibition and potential as a P-gp inhibitor. Structural modifications at the C-terminus and N-terminus of the thiazole scaffold significantly affect P-gp interaction.
full_output.methodology: The paper describes the synthesis of thiazole analogues and evaluates their effects on P-gp ATPase activity, binding affinity, and multidrug resistance reversal using biochemical assays and molecular modeling.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic analysis reveals different mechanisms of fusidic acid resistance in Staphylococcus aureus from Danish atopic dermatitis patients.

fusC.encodes: protein that blocks the binding of fusidic acid to EF-G

fusA.notes: mutations in fusA and fusE were identified in resistant isolates
fusA.evidence_note: Mutations in fusA and fusE were identified in fusidic acid-resistant S. aureus isolates through whole-genome sequencing.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies fusC gene carriage and fusA mutations as the primary mechanisms of fusidic acid resistance in Staphylococcus aureus from Danish atopic dermatitis patients.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and PCR were used to identify resistance genes and mutations in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of the impact of rpoB mutations on the in vitro and in vivo competitive fitness of Clostridium difficile and susceptibility to fidaxomicin.

rpoB.notes: Mutations in rpoB were shown to confer reduced susceptibility to fidaxomicin.

full_output.paper_title: HCV p7 amino-terminal alterations impair NS2, NS5A and E2 interactions required for envelopment of infectious particles

full_output.methodology: Site-directed mutagenesis, Western blot, infectivity assays, confocal microscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Update of incidence and antimicrobial susceptibility trends of Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from Chinese intra-abdominal infection patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports a decreasing trend in ESBL-screen positive Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from Chinese intra-abdominal infections between 2012 and 2014. It highlights the effectiveness of carbapenems against these isolates.
full_output.methodology: Susceptibility testing of 5160 GNB isolates using CLSI broth microdilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanisms of bacterial membrane permeabilization by crotalicidin (Ctn) and its fragment Ctn(15-34), antimicrobial peptides from rattlesnake venom.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the antimicrobial mechanisms of crotalicidin (Ctn) and its fragment Ctn(15-34), demonstrating their bactericidal activity through membrane permeabilization and disruption.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized time-kill assays, flow cytometry, surface plasmon resonance, and atomic force microscopy to investigate the mechanisms of action of Ctn and Ctn(15-34).

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of a Rhodococcus jostii RHA1 γ-butyrolactone(-like) signalling molecule and its main biosynthesis gene gblA.

gblA.validation_method: deletion and overexpression experiments with reporter assay

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies gblA as the main biosynthesis gene for a gamma-butyrolactone(-like) signaling molecule in Rhodococcus jostii RHA1. Deletion of gblA abolishes RJB synthesis, while overexpression increases it. The RJB molecule binds to the ScbR receptor protein of Streptomyces coelicolor, suggesting potential for interspecies communication.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, overexpression, reporter assays, and LC-MS analysis were used to characterize the role of gblA in gamma-butyrolactone biosynthesis.

full_output.paper_title: Computational and biological profile of boronic acids for the detection of bacterial serine- and metallo-β-lactamases.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes a set of boronic acid derivatives that inhibit clinically relevant β-lactamases, including AmpC, ESBLs, KPC-2, NDM-1, and VIM-2, demonstrating their potential as diagnostic tools for detecting β-lactamase production in clinical isolates.
full_output.methodology: Covalent molecular modeling, synthetic chemistry, enzyme kinetics, and antibacterial susceptibility testing were used to evaluate the inhibitory activity of boronic acid derivatives against β-lactamases.

full_output.paper_title: Effective Antimicrobial Activity of Plectasin-Derived Antimicrobial Peptides against Staphylococcus aureus Infection in Mammary Glands.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that plectasin-derived antimicrobial peptides NZ2114 and MP1102 exhibit strong antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus in both in vitro and in vivo settings, suggesting their potential as therapeutic agents for treating S. aureus-induced mastitis.
full_output.methodology: The study assessed the antimicrobial activity of NZ2114 and MP1102 against S. aureus in milk, cultured mammary epithelial cells, and a mouse model of mastitis.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Bacteria That Cause Bovine Respiratory Disease Complex in Alberta, Canada.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high levels of antimicrobial resistance among bovine respiratory disease pathogens, particularly resistance to macrolides, tetracyclines, and aminoglycosides. Multidrug resistance was prevalent, with significant variation between feedlots.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of Resistance Mutations in Salmonella enterica Serovar Typhi Against Fluoroquinolones.

full_output.paper_title: Severe infections emerge from commensal bacteria by adaptive evolution.

full_output.paper_title: High Conservation of Tetanus and Botulinum Neurotoxins Cleavage Sites on Human SNARE Proteins Suggests That These Pathogens Exerted Little or No Evolutionary Pressure on Humans.

full_output.paper_title: Study of mcr-1 Gene-Mediated Colistin Resistance in Enterobacteriaceae Isolated from Humans and Animals in Different Countries.

full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, plasmid typing, conjugation experiments, and analysis of genetic environments.

full_output.paper_title: Amikacin: Uses, Resistance, and Prospects for Inhibition.

full_output.methodology: The study discusses the role of the aac(6′)-Ib gene in amikacin resistance and describes its characterization through cloning and MIC testing.

full_output.paper_title: Synergy between Ursolic and Oleanolic Acids from Vitellaria paradoxa Leaf Extract and β-Lactams against Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus: In Vitro and In Vivo Activity and Underlying Mechanisms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ursolic acid (UA) and oleanolic acid (OA) as compounds that enhance the efficacy of β-lactam antibiotics against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) through mechanisms involving disruption of peptidoglycan synthesis and inhibition of β-lactamase activity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized HPLC-MS for compound identification, MIC determination, time-kill assays, fluorescence microscopy, and a murine infection model to evaluate the antimicrobial activity and mechanisms of action of UA and OA in combination with β-lactams.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of antimicrobial compounds targeting bacterial type FAD synthetases.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified compounds that inhibit the FMNAT activity of bacterial FAD synthetases, highlighting their potential as antimicrobial agents.

full_output.paper_title: COMPLETE LIGHT-TRIGGERED ELIMINATION OF LYSOSOMES IN 5-FU RESISTANT PANCREATIC CANCER CELLS
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies CD105 as a potential drug target for enhancing the efficacy of photochemical internalization (PCI)-based therapies in 5-FU resistant pancreatic cancer cells. Overexpression of CD105 in 5-FU resistant cells allows for targeted delivery of CD105-saporin, leading to significant cytotoxic effects.
full_output.methodology: The study uses MTS assays, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and fluorescence microscopy to evaluate the effects of CD105-saporin and other treatments on cell viability and gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Nasal colonization and antimicrobial susceptibility pattern of Staphylococcus aureus among pre-school children in Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that none of the Staphylococcus aureus isolates were methicillin-resistant (MRSA). The isolates showed resistance to β-lactam drugs, while being sensitive to several other antibiotics including Gentamycin, Erythromycin, Clindamycin, Chloramphenicol, Doxycycline, Tetracycline, Kanamycin, and Augmentin.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting nasal swabs from pre-school children, identifying S. aureus isolates, and performing antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Deciphering Multifactorial Resistance Phenotypes in Acinetobacter baumannii by Genomics and Targeted Label-free Proteomics.

full_output.methodology: Genomic and proteomic analysis combining whole genome sequencing, RT-qPCR, and targeted label-free proteomics using SRM.

full_output.paper_title: A Specialized Peptidoglycan Synthase Promotes Salmonella Cell Division inside Host Cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PBP3 SAL, a specialized peptidoglycan synthase in Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium that promotes cell division specifically in acidic environments. It is active at low pH and is not present in nonpathogenic bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, expression in E. coli mutants, beta-lactam binding assays, and cell division assays.

full_output.paper_title: Computational antimicrobial peptide design and evaluation against multidrug-resistant clinical isolates of bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents the design and evaluation of antimicrobial peptides (NN2_0018 and NN2_0050) against multidrug-resistant clinical isolates, demonstrating their effectiveness against carbapenem-resistant and methicillin-resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized a long short-term memory (LSTM) language model to design antimicrobial peptides, followed by synthesis and experimental evaluation of their antimicrobial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison between Listeria sensu stricto and Listeria sensu lato strains identifies novel determinants involved in infection.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-Genome Analysis of Recurrent Staphylococcus aureus t571/ST398 Infection in Farmer, Iowa, USA.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports recurrent Staphylococcus aureus t571/ST398 infection in a farmer, highlighting the development of borderline oxacillin resistance through a mutation in a penicillin-binding protein rather than acquisition of the mecA gene.

full_output.paper_title: Inferring genetic interactions from comparative fitness data.
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on higher-order epistasis in genetic systems, including the TEM-family of β-lactamase, which contributes to antibiotic resistance. It demonstrates that higher-order interactions can be inferred from rank orders and partial fitness orders without needing exact fitness values.
full_output.methodology: The research uses rank orders and partial fitness orders to analyze epistatic interactions in genetic systems, including the TEM-family of β-lactamase.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance Profiling, Analysis of Virulence Aspects and Molecular Genotyping of Staphylococcus aureus Isolated in Sicily, Italy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mecA gene, which confers methicillin resistance, in four S. aureus isolates. It also found high levels of penicillin G and tetracycline resistance, along with various toxin genes.
full_output.methodology: PFGE, MLST, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and multiplex PCR were used to analyze S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Calli Essential Oils Synergize with Lawsone against Multidrug Resistant Pathogens.

full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activities of lawsone and Calli oil were tested using disc diffusion and microdilution assays. The synergy between the two compounds was assessed, and liposome formulations were used to evaluate stability and toxicity.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that 88% of Staphylococcus aureus isolates were resistant to one or more antibiotics, with high resistance rates to benzylpenicillin (71.9%), erythromycin (34.3%), and fusidic acid (22.9%). Methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) accounted for 21% of isolates, with high resistance to erythromycin (60.2%), fusidic acid (45.7%), clindamycin (38.9%), and tetracycline (35.5%).

full_output.key_findings: The study characterized the presence of tcdB, tcdA, cdtA, and cdtB genes in Clostridium difficile isolates, along with a putative negative regulatory gene tcdC carrying an 18-bp deletion. full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobials for the treatment of drug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii pneumonia in critically ill patients: a systemic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: This study compared various antimicrobial strategies for treating drug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii pneumonia and identified sulbactam monotherapy, high-dose sulbactam, fosfomycin plus colistin, inhaled colistin plus colistin, and high-dose tigecycline as more effective than colistin monotherapy.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis of 23 studies evaluating antimicrobial treatments for drug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii pneumonia.

full_output.paper_title: Nitric Oxide-Mediated Induction of Dispersal in Pseudomonas aeruginosa Biofilms Is Inhibited by Flavohemoglobin Production and Is Enhanced by Imidazole.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies fhp as a gene encoding a flavohemoglobin that scavenges NO, thereby impairing biofilm dispersal. Mutant analysis confirmed that fhp is crucial for this process.
full_output.methodology: Mutant analysis, complementation, qRT-PCR, and biofilm dispersal assays were used to validate the role of fhp in NO scavenging and biofilm dispersal.

full_output.methodology: The study uses transformation, in vitro mutant selection, liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) proteomics, and whole-genome sequencing to analyze mechanisms of fluoroquinolone resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: Successive Emergence of Ceftazidime-Avibactam Resistance through Distinct Genomic Adaptations in blaKPC-2-Harboring Klebsiella pneumoniae Sequence Type 307 Isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Reversal of Azole Resistance in Candida albicans by Sulfa Antibacterial Drugs.

full_output.paper_title: The Toll pathway underlies host sexual dimorphism in resistance to both Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria in mated Drosophila.

full_output.paper_title: Expression characteristics of the plasmid-borne mcr-1 colistin resistance gene.

full_output.methodology: PCR, RT-qPCR, and statistical analysis of gene expression and resistance correlations.

It highlights the role of beta-lactamases such as blaADC, blaOXA, blaVIM, blaKPC, and blaNDM in carbapenem resistance, as well as other resistance mechanisms like efflux pumps and intrinsic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature and summarizes the clinical impact and resistance mechanisms of non-fermenting Gram-negative bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology of invasive group B streptococcal disease in infants from urban area of South China, 2011-2014.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that all 68 GBS isolates were susceptible to penicillin, ceftriaxone, vancomycin, and linezolid, but 57.4% were resistant to erythromycin and 51.5% to clindamycin. High resistance to tetracycline (95.6%) and multi-drug resistance to tetracycline, lincosamides, and macrolides (33.8%) were observed.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using AST-GP67 or manual Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion.

full_output.paper_title: Multi-clonal evolution of multi-drug-resistant/extensively drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis in a high-prevalence setting of Papua New Guinea for over three decades.
