full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, SNP analysis, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations.
full_output.sample_size: 198 S. Typhi and 66 S. Paratyphi A isolates

full_output.paper_title: MoYvh1 subverts rice defense through functions of ribosomal protein MoMrt4 in Magnaporthe oryzae.
full_output.key_findings: MoYvh1 and MoMrt4 are involved in the regulation of ROS scavenging and virulence in Magnaporthe oryzae. Mutations in MoMrt4 (G69D and G69E) can rescue the defects in growth and virulence caused by the deletion of MoYvh1.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, fluorescence microscopy, Western blotting, and pathogenicity assays were used to characterize the functions of MoYvh1 and MoMrt4.

full_output.paper_title: The kinetics of TEM1 antibiotic degrading enzymes that are displayed on Ure2 protein nanofibrils in a flow reactor.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the TEM1 beta-lactamase, demonstrating its ability to hydrolyze ampicillin when displayed on Ure2 protein nanofibrils, maintaining 80% of the catalytic turnover rate compared to the soluble enzyme.
full_output.methodology: Protein expression, purification, co-fibrillation, and kinetic analysis of ampicillin hydrolysis using a flow reactor.

full_output.paper_title: Nasal carriage, risk factors and antimicrobial susceptibility pattern of methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus among healthcare workers in Adigrat and Wukro hospitals, Tigraw, Northern Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 5.8% of healthcare workers were colonized with MRSA, with higher prevalence among nurses and those working in surgical wards. Resistance to penicillin, ampicillin, erythromycin, tetracycline, and ciprofloxacin was high, while chloramphenicol and clindamycin showed lower resistance.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method on Mueller-Hinton agar.

full_output.paper_title: d-Alanyl-d-Alanine Ligase as a Broad-Host-Range Counterselection Marker in Vancomycin-Resistant Lactic Acid Bacteria.

Plasmid expression in L. plantarum and MIC testing

ddl.notes: Mutations in Ddl lead to decreased vancomycin resistance by altering peptidoglycan structure.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the Ddl dipeptide ligase can be used as a counterselection marker in vancomycin-resistant lactic acid bacteria. Mutations in Ddl, such as F258Y and F260Y, increase vancomycin sensitivity by modifying peptidoglycan structure.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid expression, MIC testing, PCR, and phylogenetic analysis were used to validate the role of Ddl and its mutations in vancomycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Three Substrains of the Cyanobacterium Anabaena sp. Strain PCC 7120 Display Divergence in Genomic Sequences and hetC Function.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Activity of Ceftazidime-Avibactam against Isolates from Patients in a Phase 3 Clinical Trial for Treatment of Complicated Intra-abdominal Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of ceftazidime-avibactam against clinical isolates from patients with complicated intra-abdominal infections, demonstrating high activity against Enterobacteriaceae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, including ceftazidime-nonsusceptible isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 1,440 clinical isolates using broth microdilution to determine susceptibility to ceftazidime-avibactam and other antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Retained Activity of an O25b-Specific Monoclonal Antibody against an Mcr-1-Producing Escherichia coli Sequence Type 131 Strain.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the mcr-1 gene, which confers colistin resistance, does not affect the activity of the monoclonal antibody ASN-4 against Escherichia coli ST131-H30 strains.
full_output.methodology: Cloning of mcr-1 into E. coli, colistin MIC testing, and assessment of monoclonal antibody activity.

full_output.paper_title: Pathogenic Nocardia cyriacigeorgica and Nocardia nova Evolve To Resist Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole by both Expected and Unexpected Pathways.

dhfr.mechanism: mutations in the dhfr gene confer resistance to trimethoprim by decreasing the affinity of trimethoprim for the enzyme while maintaining sufficient enzyme activity
dhfr.genetic_context: mutations in the dhfr gene were identified in resistant isolates, and these mutations were shown to decrease the affinity of trimethoprim for the enzyme while maintaining sufficient enzyme activity

The paper describes mutations in the dihydrofolate reductase (dhfr) gene of Nocardia cyriacigeorgica and Nocardia nova that confer resistance to trimethoprim.

full_output.paper_title: Identifying and exploiting genes that potentiate the evolution of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the ampR gene regulates the expression of the ampC β-lactamase gene, which is crucial for the evolution of ceftazidime resistance in Pseudomonas species. Mutations in peptidoglycan biosynthesis genes (ampD, mpl, dacB) enhance resistance by increasing ampC expression, and blocking this pathway with avibactam can prevent resistance development.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing, MIC determination, experimental evolution, and competition experiments were used to analyze resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution of high-level resistance during low-level antibiotic exposure.

trkH.validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and reconstruction of mutants

trkH.evidence_note: The paper states that trkH mutations reduce streptomycin uptake.

full_output.key_findings: High-level streptomycin resistance in Salmonella enterica evolved through combinations of five mutations: gidB, trkH, nuoG, cyoB, and znuA, along with the aadA gene. These mutations collectively enhance resistance through altered ribosomal targets, reduced drug uptake, and enzymatic modification.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, mutant reconstruction, and transcript level analysis were used to validate resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: A novel in vitro metric predicts in vivo efficacy of inhaled silver-based antimicrobials in a murine Pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumonia model.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces a novel in vitro metric called the 'Drug Efficacy Metric' (DEM) that predicts the in vivo efficacy of silver-based antimicrobials against Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The DEM, calculated as the ratio of in vitro LD50 to MBC, showed strong correlation with in vivo survival outcomes in a murine pneumonia model.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro cytotoxicity assays, antimicrobial activity tests, and in vivo survival experiments in a murine Pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumonia model to evaluate the efficacy of silver-based antimicrobials.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance in clinical isolates of Enterobacteriaceae strains in Hamadan, West of Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study detected the presence of qnrB, qnrS, and aac(6′)-Ib-cr genes in fluoroquinolone-resistant Enterobacteriaceae isolates, highlighting their role in plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR assay and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to detect and characterize AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: Acinetobacter spp. as nosocomial pathogens: Epidemiology and resistance features.

adeABC.validation_method: experimental characterization of efflux pump activity

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the epidemiology and resistance features of Acinetobacter spp., focusing on multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains. It highlights the role of beta-lactamases, efflux pumps, and outer membrane proteins in conferring resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature and provides a comprehensive analysis of resistance mechanisms in Acinetobacter spp.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, identification of virulence factors, O-serogroups and antibiotic resistance properties of Shiga-toxin producing Escherichia coli strains isolated from raw milk and traditional dairy products.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified aac(3)-IV, CITM, and tetA as the most prevalent antibiotic resistance genes in STEC strains isolated from raw milk and traditional dairy products, with high resistance rates against gentamicin, ampicillin, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR and disk diffusion methods were used to identify virulence factors, O-serogroups, and antibiotic resistance genes in STEC strains.

full_output.paper_title: Genome-scale metabolic modeling of responses to polymyxins in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a comprehensive genome-scale metabolic model (i PAO1) for Pseudomonas aeruginosa, focusing on metabolic responses to polymyxin treatment. It highlights the role of lipid A modifications in altering outer membrane properties but does not identify specific AMR genes or mutations with experimental validation.
full_output.methodology: Genome-scale metabolic modeling combined with transcriptomics and flux balance analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Characterization of Nonclonal mcr-1-Positive Multidrug-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae from Clinical Samples in Thailand.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mcr-1 as the primary mediator of colistin resistance in two nonclonal multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, QS17-0029 and QS17-0161, which also carry multiple other resistance genes including bla NDM-1, bla OXA-232, bla CTX-M-15, and others.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, conjugation experiments, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the resistance genes and mechanisms in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and transcriptomic alterations in Leishmania donovani lines experimentally resistant to antileishmanial drugs.

D-LDH.validation_method: over-expression in Leishmania promastigotes and amastigotes followed by drug susceptibility testing

BCAT.validation_method: over-expression in Leishmania promastigotes and amastigotes followed by drug susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LinJ.36.2510 (SMT) as associated with AmB resistance and the tandem D-LDH-BCAT amplification as linked to PMM resistance in Leishmania donovani.
full_output.methodology: Transfection experiments and RNA-Seq analysis were used to validate the roles of SMT, D-LDH, and BCAT in drug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Haploid genetic screens identify genetic vulnerabilities to microtubule-targeting agents.

FBXW7.evidence_note: The paper states that inactivation of FBXW7 sensitizes HAP1 cells to vinorelbine, vincristine, vinblastine, and vindesine.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ABCB1 as a gene whose loss increases sensitivity to docetaxel and vinorelbine, highlighting its role in drug efflux and resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide loss-of-function screens in human haploid HAP1 cells, knockout clones, and sensitivity testing.

full_output.paper_title: Targeting species specific amino acid residues: Design, synthesis and biological evaluation of 6-substituted pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidines as dihydrofolate reductase inhibitors and potential anti-opportunistic infection agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on designing and synthesizing 6-substituted pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidines as dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) inhibitors for treating Pneumocystis jirovecii infections. Compounds 4 and 12 showed improved potency and selectivity for P. jirovecii DHFR over human DHFR.
full_output.methodology: The research involved computational design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel DHFR inhibitors, with a focus on optimizing selectivity and potency through structural modifications.

full_output.paper_title: Clinically Relevant Plasmid-Host Interactions Indicate that Transcriptional and Not Genomic Modifications Ameliorate Fitness Costs of Klebsiella pneumoniae Carbapenemase-Carrying Plasmids.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that pKpQIL-UK and pKpQIL-D2 plasmids affect gene expression in K. pneumoniae without causing genomic mutations. These plasmids influence resistance to carbapenems and other antibiotics through the expression of genes like blaKPC and blaTEM, as well as efflux pumps such as acrAB and oqxB.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and RNA sequencing were used to analyze gene expression and mutations in K. pneumoniae strains carrying pKpQIL-UK and pKpQIL-D2 plasmids.

full_output.paper_title: Extensive Gene Amplification as a Mechanism for Piperacillin-Tazobactam Resistance in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaTEM-1 gene amplification as a mechanism for piperacillin-tazobactam resistance in E. coli 907355, showing that increased gene dosage leads to higher Bla TEM-1 protein levels and resistance.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic analyses, including Western immunoblotting, qPCR, and whole-genome sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of circulating Mycobacterium tuberculosis-specific DNA by droplet digital PCR for vaccine evaluation in challenged monkeys and TB diagnosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that ddPCR is more sensitive than qPCR for detecting Mycobacterium tuberculosis-specific DNA in blood samples, enabling earlier detection of infection and improved vaccine evaluation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) and quantitative PCR (qPCR) to quantify M. tb-specific DNA in blood samples from vaccinated and infected rhesus monkeys, as well as from TB patients and healthy donors.

full_output.paper_title: Erythromycin leads to differential protein expression through differences in electrostatic and dispersion interactions with nascent proteins.

ermCL.notes: Mutations in the C-terminal residues of ErmCL increase its interaction with erythromycin, leading to ribosome stalling.

hns.notes: Mutations in the N-terminal and C-terminal residues of H-NS affect its interaction with erythromycin, enabling it to bypass the drug.

full_output.key_findings: Erythromycin interacts differently with the C-terminal residues of ErmCL and H-NS, leading to ribosome stalling for ErmCL and bypass for H-NS. These interactions involve electrostatic and dispersion forces.
full_output.methodology: Steered molecular dynamics simulations were used to analyze the interactions between erythromycin and the peptides ErmCL and H-NS during protein synthesis.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genotypic characterization of carbapenem resistance mechanisms in Klebsiella pneumoniae from blood culture specimens: A study from North India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified CTX-M group 1 ESBL and NDM-type MBL as the major contributors to carbapenem resistance in K. pneumoniae isolates from North India.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic methods including disc diffusion, E-test, and multiplex PCR were used to characterize resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization and antimicrobial susceptibility profile of New Delhi metallo-beta-lactamase-1-producing Escherichia coli among hospitalized patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of the blaNDM-1 gene in 7.2% of E. coli isolates, indicating carbapenem resistance. These isolates exhibited high resistance to multiple antibiotics, including carbapenems, aminoglycosides, and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: PCR and phenotypic testing for carbapenemase production.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence determinant and extended spectrum beta-lactamase production in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from a tertiary care hospital, South India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaSHV, blaCTX-M-1, and blaCTX-M-15 as the primary extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) genes in K. pneumoniae isolates, highlighting their association with resistance to third-generation cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: PCR and gel electrophoresis for detection of ESBL genes in K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Inorganic Polyphosphate, Exopolyphosphatase, and Pho84-Like Transporters May Be Involved in Copper Resistance in Metallosphaera sedula DSM 5348(T).
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ppx as a gene encoding a functional exopolyphosphatase (PPX) in Metallosphaera sedula DSM 5348(T), which plays a role in copper resistance by hydrolyzing polyphosphate. Mutations in critical residues (E111A, E113A) abolish PPX activity, confirming their importance in catalysis.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, protein purification, enzymatic activity assays, site-directed mutagenesis, qRT-PCR, and electron microscopy were used to characterize the role of ppx in copper resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and molecular characterization of Klebsiella spp. isolates causing community-acquired infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the CTX-M-15 beta-lactamase gene in ESBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, which conferred resistance to ceftazidime and cefotaxime.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize AMR genes and resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Francisella tularensis D-Ala D-Ala Carboxypeptidase DacD Is Involved in Intracellular Replication and It Is Necessary for Bacterial Cell Wall Integrity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies DacD as a critical factor for intracellular replication and cell wall integrity in Francisella tularensis, demonstrating that its absence leads to increased sensitivity to stress and membrane defects.
full_output.methodology: Generation of a dacD mutant strain through insertional mutagenesis, functional complementation, and assessment of intracellular replication, stress sensitivity, and membrane integrity.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of E. coli inhibition by plain and polymer-coated silver nanoparticles.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial efficacy of polymer-coated silver nanoparticles (AgPVP, Ag 10% + Polymer) and plain silver nanoparticles (AgNP) against E. coli, showing that polymer coatings did not reduce antibacterial activity despite lower silver ion concentrations.
full_output.methodology: The study used atomic force microscopy, minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) assays, bacterial growth curve assays, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and qRT-PCR to evaluate nanoparticle effects on E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Synergism of Antimicrobial Frog Peptides Couples to Membrane Intrinsic Curvature Strain.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the synergistic activity of antimicrobial frog peptides magainin 2 (MG2) and PGLa, focusing on their interaction with lipid membranes and the role of intrinsic curvature in enhancing their antimicrobial effects.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized lipid vesicle leakage assays, Monte Carlo simulations, and microbial growth inhibition tests to analyze the synergistic effects of MG2 and PGLa.

full_output.paper_title: Bortezomib prevents cytarabine resistance in MCL, which is characterized by down-regulation of dCK and up-regulation of SPIB resulting in high NF-κB activity.

dCK.validation_method: protein expression analysis and functional assays

SPIB.validation_method: gene expression analysis and functional assays

full_output.key_findings: Down-regulation of dCK and up-regulation of SPIB contribute to cytarabine resistance in MCL, with dCK being critical for resistance development. Bortezomib prevents resistance by maintaining dCK levels.
full_output.methodology: Gene expression analysis, protein expression analysis, and functional assays in MCL cell lines.

full_output.paper_title: Elucidation of the anti-hyperammonemic mechanism of Lactobacillus amylovorus JBD401 by comparative genomic analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Lactobacillus amylovorus JBD401 as a strain capable of reducing blood ammonia levels through the assimilation of ammonia into amino acids and polyamines. The genome of JBD401 contains genes for carbamate kinase (CK) and ornithine carbamoyltransferase (OTC), which are involved in ammonia assimilation.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, BLAST analysis, and in vitro screening of probiotic strains for ammonia removal.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance among clinically relevant bacterial isolates in Accra: a retrospective study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high resistance rates among bacterial isolates in Accra, particularly against tetracycline, ampicillin, cotrimoxazole, and cephalosporins, while showing lower resistance to amoxiclav and aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of culture and sensitivity test results from six laboratories in Accra, Ghana.

full_output.paper_title: Targeting protein biotinylation enhances tuberculosis chemotherapy.

rv3406.validation_method: overexpression in Mtb and resistance assay

full_output.key_findings: The study identified Rv3406 as a gene that, when overexpressed, confers resistance to Bio-AMS in Mycobacterium tuberculosis by enzymatically degrading the compound.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic manipulation, overexpression of Rv3406, and resistance assays to determine the role of Rv3406 in Bio-AMS resistance.

full_output.paper_title: A wheat caffeic acid 3-O-methyltransferase TaCOMT-3D positively contributes to both resistance to sharp eyespot disease and stem mechanical strength.
full_output.key_findings: TaCOMT-3D enhances resistance to sharp eyespot disease and increases stem mechanical strength in wheat by promoting lignin accumulation, particularly syringyl monolignol.
full_output.methodology: Transgenic overexpression, gene silencing, qRT-PCR, and lignin content analysis.

full_output.paper_title: CsrA and its regulators control the time-point of ColicinE2 release in Escherichia coli.

second CsrA binding site in the SD sequence of cel

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the global carbon storage regulator CsrA controls the delay between ColicinE2 production and release by binding to the Shine-Dalgarno sequence of the cel gene. Mutations in the CsrA binding site affect the delay time, demonstrating the critical role of CsrA in regulating ColicinE2 expression.
full_output.methodology: Site-directed mutagenesis, fluorescence microscopy, gel shift analysis, and theoretical modeling were used to investigate the role of CsrA and its binding sites in ColicinE2 expression dynamics.

full_output.paper_title: Acid-regulated gene expression of Helicobacter pylori: Insight into acid protection and gastric colonization.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes involved in acid acclimation and antioxidant response in H. pylori, highlighting the importance of urease, carbonic anhydrase, and antioxidant enzymes in adapting to gastric acidity.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq, qPCR, and Western blot analysis were used to examine gene expression in H. pylori under varying pH conditions.

full_output.paper_title: Comprehensive identification of Vibrio vulnificus genes required for growth in human serum.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified VV0357 and VV0358 as genes necessary for capsule formation, HS-resistance, and virulence in mice. These genes are involved in capsule biosynthesis and are required for growth in human serum but not in heat-inactivated serum.
full_output.methodology: Transposon insertion sequencing (TIS) was used to identify genes required for V. vulnificus growth in human serum.

full_output.paper_title: Matrix metalloproteinase inhibitors enhance the efficacy of frontline drugs against Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: MMP inhibitors enhance the efficacy of frontline TB drugs INH and RIF by stabilizing blood vessels and improving drug delivery in the infected lung tissue.
full_output.methodology: Experiments involving MMP inhibitors, bacterial burden assessment, histology, and drug delivery analysis in Mtb-infected mice.

full_output.paper_title: Practical spectrophotometric assay for the dapE-encoded N-succinyl-L,L-diaminopimelic acid desuccinylase, a potential antibiotic target.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes a new enzymatic assay for the bacterial enzyme DapE, which is involved in the lysine biosynthetic pathway and essential for bacterial survival. The assay uses N6-methyl-L,L-SDAP as a substrate and detects the enzymatic product using ninhydrin. The study also identifies several inhibitors of DapE, including captopril, 3-mercaptobenzoic acid, phenylboronic acid, and 2-thiopheneboronic acid, with varying inhibitory potencies.
full_output.methodology: The study involves the development of a spectrophotometric assay for DapE, synthesis of substrate analogs, molecular modeling, and determination of enzyme inhibition constants (IC50).

full_output.paper_title: Differentially expressed microRNAs associated with changes of transcript levels in detoxification pathways and DDT-resistance in the Drosophila melanogaster strain 91-R.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies differentially expressed microRNAs (miRNAs) in the DDT-resistant Drosophila melanogaster strain 91-R compared to the susceptible strain 91-C, highlighting their potential role in regulating detoxification pathways and DDT resistance.
full_output.methodology: Small RNA sequencing and RT-qPCR were used to analyze miRNA expression and validate target gene interactions.

full_output.paper_title: The magnitude of antibiotic resistance to Helicobacter pylori in Africa and identified mutations which confer resistance to antibiotics: systematic review and meta-analysis.

H. pylori.notes: Mutation in 23S rRNA gene leading to ribosome modification and resistance to macrolides

full_output.key_findings: High levels of antibiotic resistance in H. pylori in Africa, particularly to metronidazole, clarithromycin, and amoxicillin. Key mutations identified include A2143G, A2142G, A2147G, A2146C for clarithromycin resistance, D87I and D91N for quinolone resistance, and RdxA for metronidazole resistance.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on H. pylori antibiotic resistance in Africa.

full_output.paper_title: Draft Genome Sequence of Multidrug-Resistant Escherichia coli NIVEDI-P44, Isolated from a Chicken Fecal Sample in Northeast India.
full_output.key_findings: The multidrug-resistant E. coli strain NIVEDI-P44 was found to harbor multiple antibiotic resistance genes including blaDHA-1, mph(A), strA, strB, dfrA14, sul-2, tet(A), and qnrS1, indicating resistance to various antibiotics such as beta-lactams, macrolides, streptomycin, trimethoprim, sulfonamides, tetracycline, and quinolones.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify the resistance genes in the E. coli strain NIVEDI-P44.

full_output.paper_title: Optically-controlled bacterial metabolite for cancer therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel approach called photo-controlled bacterial metabolite therapy (PMT) using carbon nitride (C3N4) combined with Escherichia coli carrying nitric oxide (NO) generation enzymes. This system enables the production of NO under light irradiation, demonstrating effective anti-cancer properties by inducing apoptosis in cancer cells.
full_output.methodology: The study employed a combination of biochemical assays, fluorescence imaging, and in vivo experiments to investigate the NO generation capabilities of the CCN@E. coli system and its anti-cancer effects.
full_output.sample_size: n=5 for in vivo fluorescence imaging, n=3 for ex vivo fluorescence imaging, n=6 for in vivo anti-cancer effect

full_output.paper_title: Progressive cationic functionalization of chlorin derivatives for antimicrobial photodynamic inactivation and related vancomycin conjugates.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the synthesis and antimicrobial photodynamic inactivation (aPDI) testing of chlorin derivatives with varying numbers of cationic charges, highlighting their effectiveness against Gram-positive bacteria, with Zn-Phe-N5+ showing the highest activity.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of chlorin derivatives with cationic charges, aPDI testing against bacterial and fungal strains, and analysis of photophysical properties.

full_output.paper_title: Exogenous fatty acids alter phospholipid composition, membrane permeability, capacity for biofilm formation, and antimicrobial peptide susceptibility in Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: Exogenous polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) alter phospholipid composition, membrane permeability, and antimicrobial peptide susceptibility in Klebsiella pneumoniae. Specifically, PUFAs reduced the MICs of polymyxin B and colistin, indicating increased susceptibility to these antimicrobial peptides.
full_output.methodology: The study used thin-layer chromatography, UPLC/ESI-MS, crystal violet and ethidium bromide uptake assays, antimicrobial peptide susceptibility assays, and biofilm formation assays to investigate the effects of exogenous PUFAs on K. pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Antibacterial Activity of New Thiazolidine-2,4-dione-Based Chlorophenylthiosemicarbazone Hybrids.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and antibacterial activity of new thiazolidine-2,4-dione-based chlorophenylthiosemicarbazone hybrids. Some compounds showed good to limited antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria, with compound 38 being the most active. The study also highlights the complexity of structure-activity relationships (SARs) and the need for further investigation into the molecular mechanisms of antibacterial activity.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized and tested for antibacterial activity using broth dilution and agar dilution methods. MIC values were determined, and the bactericidal or bacteriostatic nature of the compounds was assessed.

full_output.paper_title: Colonization With Levofloxacin-resistant Extended-spectrum β-Lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae and Risk of Bacteremia in Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-14, bla CTX-M-27, and bla TEM-1 as genes conferring resistance to various beta-lactam antibiotics in ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae isolated from hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients.
full_output.methodology: Molecular beacon probes in a real-time PCR assay were used to detect beta-lactamase genes in ceftriaxone-resistant Enterobacteriaceae.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Novel Neisseria gonorrhoeae Lineages Harboring Resistance Plasmids in Coastal Kenya.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies novel Neisseria gonorrhoeae lineages in coastal Kenya with high prevalence of plasmid-mediated resistance. Key findings include the identification of pTetM and p bla TEM plasmids, along with chromosomal mutations in gyrA, penA, ponA, mtrR, and porB contributing to resistance against tetracycline, penicillin, and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, cgMLST analysis, and MIC testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Adenosine signaling modulates immune responses and carbohydrate metabolism during bacterial infection in Drosophila

adoR.notes: The adoR mutation leads to reduced resistance to bacterial infections.

adgf-a.evidence_note: The paper describes a null mutation in the adgf-a gene and its effects on resistance to bacterial infections.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the roles of adenosine signaling and ADGF-A in modulating immune responses and carbohydrate metabolism during bacterial infections in Drosophila. Mutations in adoR and adgf-a lead to reduced resistance to bacterial infections.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, survival analysis, pathogen load measurement, and gene expression analysis were used to investigate the roles of adenosine signaling and ADGF-A in immune responses and carbohydrate metabolism.

full_output.paper_title: VIM-Klebsiella oxytoca outbreak in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit. This time it wasn't the drain.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes a VIM-Klebsiella oxytoca outbreak in a NICU, identifying blaVIM as the carbapenemase gene responsible for resistance. The source of the outbreak was other patients rather than environmental reservoirs.
full_output.methodology: PCR and molecular typing were used to confirm carbapenemase genes, while epidemiological surveillance tracked the outbreak.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular analysis of immune evasion cluster (IEC) genes and intercellular adhesion gene cluster (ICA) among methicillin-resistant and methicillin-sensitive isolates of Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of the mecA gene in 44% of S. aureus isolates, indicating methicillin resistance, and the icaD gene in 84% of isolates, suggesting a role in biofilm formation. However, no significant association was found between icaD gene presence and biofilm production.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of mecA and icaD genes, disk diffusion for antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and biofilm formation assays.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative analysis of Klebsiella pneumoniae strains isolated in 2012-2016 that differ by antibiotic resistance genes and virulence genes profiles.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: loss of hypermucoviscosity and reduced virulence

It also characterized the hypervirulent K. pneumoniae strain KPB2580-14, which carries bla CTX-M-15 and bla OXA-48 genes on pCTX-M-15-like and pOXA-48-like plasmids.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and MIC testing were used to identify and characterize AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypical resistance correlation networks for 10 non-typhoidal Salmonella subpopulations in an active antimicrobial surveillance programme.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed phenotypic resistance correlation networks in 10 non-typhoidal Salmonella subpopulations, highlighting collaterally resistant patterns and the impact of antimicrobial usage on resistance development.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized network-based approaches and linear models to analyze antimicrobial resistance patterns in Salmonella isolates from the NARMS program.

full_output.paper_title: Effects of the 1- N -(4-Amino-2 S -hydroxybutyryl) and 6'- N -(2-Hydroxyethyl) Substituents on Ribosomal Selectivity, Cochleotoxicity, and Antibacterial Activity in the Sisomicin Class of Aminoglycoside Antibiotics.

These modifications affect the ability of the antibiotics to overcome resistance mediated by these enzymes.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial screening and analysis of resistance mechanisms in bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic combination efficacy (ACE) networks for a Pseudomonas aeruginosa model.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates antibiotic combination efficacy (ACE) networks in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, highlighting the impact of synergistic and antagonistic drug interactions on bacterial adaptation and population extinction.
full_output.methodology: The research involved extensive experimental evolution experiments with Pseudomonas aeruginosa, assessing drug interactions and their effects on bacterial adaptation and survival.

full_output.paper_title: Histone acetyltransferase TGF-1 regulates Trichoderma atroviride secondary metabolism and mycoparasitism.

tgs-1.notes: Overexpression of tgs-1 affects antimicrobial compound production

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the role of TGF-1, a histone acetyltransferase, in regulating mycoparasitism and secondary metabolism in Trichoderma atroviride. It characterizes the expression of mycoparasitism-related genes (ech-42, prb-1) and secondary metabolism-related genes (pbs-1, tps-1) under different conditions.
full_output.methodology: Expression analysis via RT-qPCR, dual culture assays, and antimicrobial activity testing.

full_output.paper_title: The SecA2 pathway of Mycobacterium tuberculosis exports effectors that work in concert to arrest phagosome and autophagosome maturation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SapM and PknG as effectors exported by the SecA2 pathway of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which contribute to phagosome and autophagosome maturation arrest.
full_output.methodology: Immunoblot analysis, phosphatase activity assay, and immunofluorescence microscopy were used to investigate the role of SapM and PknG in phagosome and autophagosome maturation.

full_output.paper_title: Activities of Combinations of Antistaphylococcal Antibiotics with Fusidic Acid against Staphylococcal Biofilms in In Vitro Static and Dynamic Models.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the activity of fusidic acid in combination with other antistaphylococcal antibiotics against staphylococcal biofilms in both static and dynamic models, highlighting the synergistic effects of fusidic acid with daptomycin or linezolid.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro static and dynamic biofilm models to assess the activity of fusidic acid and its combinations with other antibiotics against staphylococcal biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: First Penicillin-Binding Protein Occupancy Patterns of β-Lactams and β-Lactamase Inhibitors in Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: This study presents the first PBP binding data for K. pneumoniae using 13 chemically diverse and clinically relevant β-lactams and β-lactamase inhibitors. The study characterizes the binding affinities (IC50) of these compounds to different penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) in K. pneumoniae strains ATCC 43816 and ATCC 13883.
full_output.methodology: PBP binding assays using Bocillin FL as a fluorogenic probe, SDS-PAGE, and mass spectrometry analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Determination of MIC Distribution and Mechanisms of Decreased Susceptibility to Bedaquiline among Clinical Isolates of Mycobacterium abscessus.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the repressor gene mab_4384, leading to overexpression of the efflux pump gene mmpS5/mmpL5, which contributes to decreased bedaquiline susceptibility in Mycobacterium abscessus clinical isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, qRT-PCR analysis, and broth microdilution susceptibility testing were used to determine the mechanisms of decreased bedaquiline susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of High-Level Colistin Resistance in an Acinetobacter baumannii Clinical Isolate Mediated by Inactivation of the Global Regulator H-NS.

hns.validation_method: Genome sequencing, transcriptomic analysis, and MIC assays were used to validate the role of hns in colistin resistance.

full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, transcriptomic analysis, and complementation experiments were used to investigate the role of hns in colistin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the role of alanine dehydrogenase (Ald) in Mycobacterium smegmatis and investigates the effects of gene deletions on bacterial growth and susceptibility to Q203, a potential antitubercular compound.

full_output.paper_title: C/EBPβ enhances platinum resistance of ovarian cancer cells by reprogramming H3K79 methylation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies C/EBPβ as a key regulator of platinum resistance in ovarian cancer through its role in reprogramming H3K79 methylation, which affects the expression of cisplatin-resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, Western blotting, and in vivo tumor models to investigate the role of C/EBPβ in platinum resistance.

full_output.paper_title: The LetA/S two-component system regulates transcriptomic changes that are essential for the culturability of Legionella pneumophila in water.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the LetA/S two-component system as critical for the culturability of Legionella pneumophila in water, highlighting its role in regulating transcriptomic changes necessary for survival under nutrient-poor conditions.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized CFU counts, microscopic analysis, and transcriptomic analysis via DNA microarrays to investigate the role of the LetA/S system in L. pneumophila survival in water.

full_output.paper_title: An effector from the Huanglongbing-associated pathogen targets citrus proteases.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SDE1, an effector from 'Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus', as a novel virulence factor that interacts with and inhibits citrus papain-like cysteine proteases (PLCPs), thereby suppressing plant defense mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Yeast-two-hybrid screening, in vitro pull-down assays, activity-based protein profiling, and transgenic plant experiments.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple citrus varieties and transgenic lines.

full_output.paper_title: Parallel evolution of vgsc mutations at domains IS6, IIS6 and IIIS6 in pyrethroid resistant Aedes aegypti from Mexico.

vgsc.notes: The mutation V410L in the voltage-gated sodium channel (vgsc) is associated with pyrethroid resistance in Aedes aegypti.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the V410L mutation in the voltage-gated sodium channel (vgsc) of pyrethroid-resistant Aedes aegypti from Mexico, which contributes to knockdown resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genotyping and phenotype-genotype association study using PCR, sequencing, and insecticide bioassays.

full_output.paper_title: A Comparison of the Antibacterial and Antifungal Activities of Thiosulfinate Analogues of Allicin.
full_output.key_findings: The study compares the antimicrobial activities of various thiosulfinate analogues of allicin, highlighting their effectiveness against bacteria and fungi, with particular emphasis on their modes of action related to glutathione metabolism.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro antimicrobial assays, including MIC, MBC, and MFC determinations, as well as chemogenetic screens with yeast mutants to evaluate the effects of thiosulfinate analogues.

full_output.paper_title: Shared strategies for β-lactam catabolism in the soil microbiome.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a β-lactam catabolic pathway involving β-lactamases, amidases (put1 and put2), and the phenylacetic acid catabolon (paa) in four soil isolates. The pathway enables the breakdown of penicillin into phenylacetic acid, which is then processed through central metabolism.
full_output.methodology: Genomic and transcriptomic analyses, gene knockout experiments, and enzymatic assays were conducted to characterize the catabolic pathway.

full_output.methodology: The study involved molecular characterization, plasmid analysis, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Quorum Sensing Extracellular Death Peptides Enhance the Endoribonucleolytic Activities of Mycobacterium tuberculosis MazF Toxins.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that extracellular death factors (EDFs) from E. coli and P. aeruginosa enhance the endoribonucleolytic activities of M. tuberculosis MazF toxins (MazF-mt3 and MazF-mt6) and overcome the inhibitory effects of their respective antitoxins (MazE-mt3 and MazE-mt6).

full_output.paper_title: UNG-1 and APN-1 are the major enzymes to efficiently repair 5-hydroxymethyluracil DNA lesions in C. elegans.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies UNG-1 and APN-1 as critical enzymes in the base-excision repair pathway for processing 5-hydroxymethyluracil (5-hmU) lesions in C. elegans. Mutants lacking these genes show increased sensitivity to 5-hmU, demonstrating their essential role in DNA repair.
full_output.methodology: Mutant analysis, RNAi, and enzymatic assays were used to evaluate the role of UNG-1 and APN-1 in repairing 5-hmU lesions.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Surveillance Reveals Diversity of Multidrug-Resistant Organism Colonization and Infection: A Prospective Cohort Study in Liver Transplant Recipients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mcr-1 and blaKPC genes as responsible for polymyxin and carbapenem resistance, respectively, in multidrug-resistant organisms colonizing liver transplant recipients.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and genomic analysis were used to identify and characterize AMR genes in multidrug-resistant organisms.

full_output.paper_title: MetaCompare: a computational pipeline for prioritizing environmental resistome risk.
full_output.key_findings: The paper introduces MetaCompare, a computational pipeline for assessing and prioritizing environmental resistome risk based on metagenomic data. It evaluates the potential for antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) to be associated with mobile genetic elements (MGEs) and mobilize to pathogens.
full_output.methodology: The paper uses metagenomic sequencing data and computational analysis to identify and quantify ARGs, MGEs, and pathogen-like sequences in environmental samples.
full_output.sample_size: Three data sets representing distinct environments

full_output.paper_title: Daptomycin selects for genetic and phenotypic adaptations leading to antibiotic tolerance in MRSA.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies eight novel mutations in S. aureus that contribute to daptomycin tolerance, with some mutations causing heterotolerance. These mutations do not significantly affect daptomycin MICs but enhance survival during treatment.
full_output.methodology: Genomic regions were analyzed for mutations after prolonged daptomycin exposure. Mutations were introduced into S. aureus J01 and MICs were determined by microbroth dilution. Kill curve analyses assessed daptomycin killing and tolerance.

full_output.paper_title: Sulfamethoxazole - Trimethoprim represses csgD but maintains virulence genes at 30°C in a clinical Escherichia coli O157:H7 isolate.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that SMX-TM affects the transcriptome of E. coli O157:H7, leading to changes in the expression of virulence genes such as stx1, stx2, ler, grlA, grlR, pchA, pchB, pchC, recA, and lexA. These genes are involved in the regulation of virulence and the SOS response.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis using RNA-Seq and qRT-PCR to evaluate gene expression changes in response to SMX-TM exposure.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of MVATG18598 therapeutic efficacy in a post-exposure mouse model
full_output.key_findings: MVATG18598 vaccine reduces Mycobacterium tuberculosis regrowth and enhances immune responses in post-exposure mouse models.
full_output.methodology: Mouse vaccination and bacterial load assessment

full_output.paper_title: RIOK-1 Is a Suppressor of the p38 MAPK Innate Immune Pathway in Caenorhabditis elegans.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies RIOK-1 as a novel suppressor of the p38 MAPK innate immune pathway in C. elegans, demonstrating that its suppression confers resistance to Aeromonas dhakensis infection.
full_output.methodology: RNAi screening, qRT-PCR, Western blot analysis, and life span assays were used to investigate the role of RIOK-1 in the p38 MAPK pathway and its impact on resistance to A. dhakensis infection.

full_output.paper_title: A Novel PhoP/PhoQ Regulation Pathway Modulates the Survival of Extraintestinal Pathogenic Escherichia coli in Macrophages.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies hlyF, mig-14p, and ompTp as key virulence factors in ExPEC that contribute to resistance against cationic antimicrobial peptides and intracellular survival in macrophages.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptional analysis, functional assays, and Western blotting were used to characterize the roles of hlyF, mig-14p, and ompTp in ExPEC.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of antimicrobial resistance-associated proteins by titanium dioxide-facilitated intact bacteria mass spectrometry.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the successful detection of antimicrobial resistance-associated proteins using TiO2-facilitated MALDI-TOF MS without sample pre-treatment. Specific resistance proteins such as blaTEM-1, aacC1, cat, and ampC were identified in various bacterial strains.
full_output.methodology: TiO2-modified target plates were used for MALDI-TOF MS analysis of intact bacteria to detect resistance-associated proteins.

full_output.paper_title: Quantifying the Evolutionary Conservation of Genes Encoding Multidrug Efflux Pumps in the ESKAPE Pathogens To Identify Antimicrobial Drug Targets.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes encoding multidrug efflux pumps in ESKAPE pathogens that are under stabilizing selection, highlighting potential targets for efflux pump inhibitors. It reveals that certain efflux pump genes, such as msrC in E. faecium and acrAB-tolC in E. coli, show high conservation and could serve as stable drug targets.
full_output.methodology: In silico analysis of efflux pump genes using dN/dS ratios, phylogenetic comparisons, and selection models to determine evolutionary conservation and potential as drug targets.

full_output.paper_title: Susceptibility patterns and the role of extracellular DNA in Staphylococcus epidermidis biofilm resistance to physico-chemical stress exposure.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that S. epidermidis biofilms were less susceptible to physico-chemical stress induced by disinfectants compared to planktonic cells. Additionally, biofilms released more extracellular DNA (eDNA) in response to certain stressors, suggesting a role for eDNA in biofilm resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the susceptibility of S. epidermidis biofilms and planktonic cells to various physico-chemical stresses, including heat, NaCl, NaOCl, and H2O2, through colony-forming unit (CFU) enumeration and eDNA quantification.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of phenotypic variation and genome aberrations observed among Phytophthora ramorum isolates from diverse hosts.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes chromosomal aberrations, including copy neutral loss of heterozygosity (cnLOH) and aneuploidy, in Phytophthora ramorum isolates from non-oak hosts, highlighting host-induced phenotypic diversification (HIPD) and its potential as a model for studying genome plasticity in plant pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Genome analyses, copy number variation (CNV) detection, and phenotypic profiling of P. ramorum isolates from diverse hosts.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteremia and meningitis caused by OXA-23-producing Acinetobacter baumannii - molecular characterization and susceptibility testing for alternative antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Improved Subtyping of Staphylococcus aureus Clonal Complex 8 Strains Based on Whole-Genome Phylogenetic Analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Structural and Functional Analysis of TM0415 and Its Homologs

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of 3-methylbenzo[d]thiazol-methylquinolinium derivatives as novel antimicrobial agents. full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic-Resistant Pathogenic Escherichia Coli Isolated from Rooftop Rainwater-Harvesting Tanks in the Eastern Cape, South Africa.

full_output.paper_title: Development of a melting-curve based multiplex real-time PCR assay for simultaneous detection of Streptococcus agalactiae and genes encoding resistance to macrolides and lincosamides.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a multiplex real-time PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of Streptococcus agalactiae and genes encoding resistance to macrolides and lincosamides, specifically targeting the cfb, erm(A), erm(B), and mef(A/E) genes.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex real-time PCR assay with melting curve analysis for detection of GBS and resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Clonal diversity and genetic profiling of antibiotic resistance among multidrug/carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from a tertiary care hospital in Saudi Arabia.

blaNDM-1.genetic_context: ISAba125 and ble MBL flanking this gene

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of OXA-48 and NDM-1 carbapenemase genes, along with CTX-M-15 and CTX-M-14 extended-spectrum beta-lactamases, in multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from Saudi Arabia.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, sequencing, and plasmid typing to characterize resistance genes and clonality in 71 multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Delamanid for rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis: a retrospective study from South Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness and safety of delamanid (Dlm) in treating rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (RR-TB) in a programmatic setting in South Africa. It found that Dlm was associated with favorable early treatment responses and acceptable safety profiles, with rare occurrences of cardiotoxicity.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing data from patients treated with Dlm-containing regimens for RR-TB.

full_output.key_findings: The study presents a barcoded E. coli library for tracking and comparing evolving lineages during adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) experiments. It shows that multiplexed phenotyping using barcodes correlates with traditional methods and identifies cross-resistance between doxycycline (DOX) and cefepime (FEP) evolved lineages.
full_output.methodology: Adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) with barcoded E. coli strains, IC90 determination, growth rate measurements, and multiplexed phenotyping using barcode frequency analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Development of a generic β-lactamase screening system for improved signal peptides for periplasmic targeting of recombinant proteins in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a β-lactamase screening system to optimize signal peptides for periplasmic targeting of recombinant proteins in E. coli. The TEM-1 β-lactamase (bla) was used as a reporter for periplasmic localization, and various signal peptides were evaluated for their effectiveness in enhancing periplasmic translocation of the scFv 13R4 antibody fragment.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized error-prone PCR and chemical synthesis to generate signal peptide libraries, which were screened for β-lactamase activity. The activity of the β-lactamase was measured using nitrocefin and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) assays.

full_output.paper_title: Anti-biofilm and Anti-Virulence Efficacy of Celastrol Against Stenotrophomonas maltophilia.
full_output.key_findings: Celastrol inhibited biofilm formation and virulence factors in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia by down-regulating the expression of genes such as smeYZ, fsnR, bfmA, and bfmK.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic analyses, including crystal violet biofilm assay, XTT reduction assay, confocal laser scanning microscopy, swimming motility assay, protease activity assay, and qRT-PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery and Optimization of Indolyl-Containing 4-Hydroxy-2-Pyridone Type II DNA Topoisomerase Inhibitors Active against Multidrug Resistant Gram-negative Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports on the discovery and optimization of 4-hydroxy-2-pyridone compounds targeting type II DNA topoisomerases in multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, showing improved activity against fluoroquinolone-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Synthetic chemistry and in vitro antibacterial activity testing against Gram-negative strains.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Aminoglycoside-Modifying Enzymes in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae Producing Extended Spectrum β-Lactamases Collected in Two Multicenter Studies in Spain.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified aac(6')-Ib, aac(3)-IIa, and aph(3')-Ia as the most prevalent aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae producing extended spectrum β-lactamases in Spain. These genes were associated with resistance to various aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: PCR and MIC testing were used to detect aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes and assess antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Group B streptococci vaginal colonization and drug susceptibility pattern among pregnant women attending in selected public antenatal care centers in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high rates of Group B Streptococcus (GBS) colonization among pregnant women in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, with notable resistance to several antibiotics including tetracycline, penicillin, ampicillin, clindamycin, and vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of multidrug-resistant Providencia rettgeri isolates co-producing NDM-1 carbapenemase and PER-1 extended-spectrum β-lactamase causing a first outbreak in Korea.

blaPER-1.evidence_note: The paper states that all isolates harbored the bla NDM-1 carbapenemase and the bla PER-1 type extended-spectrum β-lactamases genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first outbreak of multidrug-resistant Providencia rettgeri isolates co-producing NDM-1 carbapenemase and PER-1 extended-spectrum beta-lactamase in Korea.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and PFGE analysis were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes and genetic relatedness of the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Susceptibility of Methicillin-Resistant and -Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus Isolates of Various Clonal Lineages from Germany to Eight Biocides.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes associated with biocide and heavy metal resistance in Staphylococcus aureus isolates, including mepA, lmrS, norA, sepA, qacA, qacB, qacG, qacJ, smr, mco, copA, and czrC. These genes were found to contribute to increased MIC values for various biocides and heavy metals.
full_output.methodology: PCR and MIC testing were used to identify and validate AMR genes in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Effects of Ceftiofur and Chlortetracycline on the Resistomes of Feedlot Cattle.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that tetracycline resistance genes, particularly tet(Q) and tet(40), were significantly enriched in cattle fed chlortetracycline. β-lactam resistance genes such as bla_CFX-A6 and bla_ACI-1 were also identified, but no significant changes were observed in their relative abundances. Aminoglycoside resistance genes showed an increase despite no aminoglycoside administration.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing of fecal samples from feedlot cattle to analyze resistance gene profiles before and after antimicrobial treatment.

full_output.paper_title: Structural and functional determination of homologs of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis N-acetylglucosamine-6-phosphate deacetylase (NagA).
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the structural and functional properties of NagA enzymes from Mycobacterium smegmatis (MSNagA) and Mycobacterium marinum (MMNagA), highlighting their role in deacetylating GlcNAc6P and their structural similarities to other NagA enzymes.
full_output.methodology: X-ray crystallography, site-directed mutagenesis, and biochemical assays were used to analyze the structure and function of MSNagA and MMNagA.

full_output.paper_title: Propyl-5-hydroxy-3-methyl-1-phenyl-1H-pyrazole-4-carbodithioate (HMPC): a new bacteriostatic agent against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

mgrA.notes: Mutations in mgrA were associated with HMPC resistance.

fmtC.notes: Mutations in fmtC were associated with HMPC resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the transcriptional regulator mgrA and the phosphatidylglycerol lysyltransferase fmtC as contributing to HMPC resistance in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing of HMPC-resistant mutants and promoter-lux array screening were used to identify resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Prediction and characterization of a novel hemocyanin-derived antimicrobial peptide from shrimp Litopenaeus vannamei.
full_output.key_findings: The study predicts and characterizes a novel hemocyanin-derived antimicrobial peptide, L1, which exhibits strong antibacterial activity against both Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria. Structural analysis reveals that L1 possesses α-helical and β-turn conformations, which are crucial for its antimicrobial activity.
full_output.methodology: The study uses bioinformatics tools to predict antimicrobial peptides from the large subunit of Litopenaeus vannamei hemocyanin, followed by experimental validation through synthesis, MIC testing, CD spectroscopy, NMR analysis, and SEM imaging.

full_output.paper_title: The widespread use of topical antimicrobials enriches for resistance in Staphylococcus aureus isolated from patients with atopic dermatitis.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that Staphylococcus aureus isolates from patients with atopic dermatitis (AD) show higher prevalence of fusidic acid resistance compared to nasal carriers, with resistance mediated by mutations in the fusA gene and the presence of fusB and fusC genes. Additionally, qac genes associated with antiseptic resistance were more common in AD isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and in silico characterization of S. aureus isolates from AD patients and nasal carriers.

full_output.paper_title: Ugly bugs in healthy guts! Carriage of multidrug-resistant and ESBL-producing commensal Enterobacteriaceae in the intestine of healthy Nepalese adults.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla-TEM, bla-CTX-M, and bla-SHV as the primary ESBL genes in multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae isolated from healthy Nepalese adults, highlighting the significance of these genes in conferring resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and phenotypic confirmation were used to identify ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae and characterize their resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Ambulance vehicles as a source of multidrug-resistant infections: a multicenter study in Assiut City, Egypt.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that ambulance vehicles in Assiut City, Egypt, were heavily contaminated with multidrug-resistant bacteria, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Gram-negative bacteria such as Klebsiella spp. and Escherichia coli.
full_output.methodology: The study involved swabbing 16 sampling points in 25 ambulance vehicles and analyzing the bacterial isolates for antimicrobial resistance using standard microbiological techniques and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Evidence for Environmental Dissemination of Antibiotic Resistance Mediated by Wild Birds.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mcr-1 gene, which confers colistin resistance, in colistin-resistant E. coli isolates from the Jin River water and egret feces, indicating the environmental dissemination of this gene via wild birds.
full_output.methodology: PCR survey, sequencing, and qPCR to detect and characterize antibiotic resistance genes.
full_output.sample_size: 95 E. coli isolates from river water, 94 from egret feces, 81 from park soil, and 91 from campus soil

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Clinically Isolated Metallo-beta-lactamase-producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Coding Genes, and Possible Risk Factors in Iran.

blaVIM.evidence_note: The paper states that bla VIM and bla IMP were predominant MBLs among P. aeruginosa strains, and that they confer resistance to imipenem and meropenem.

blaIMP.evidence_note: The paper states that bla VIM and bla IMP were predominant MBLs among P. aeruginosa strains, and that they confer resistance to imipenem and meropenem.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaVIM and blaIMP as the predominant metallo-beta-lactamase genes in carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates in Iran, with no reports of blaNDM1 or blaSPM1.
full_output.methodology: Meta-analysis of studies on MBL-producing P. aeruginosa isolates in Iran.

full_output.paper_title: The prevalence of quinolone resistance genes of A, B, S in Escherichia coli strains isolated from three major hospitals in Tehran, Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of quinolone resistance genes qnrB and qnrS in Escherichia coli strains isolated from patients with urinary tract infections in Tehran, Iran. The frequency of qnrB was 25% and qnrS was 36%.
full_output.methodology: PCR and gel electrophoresis were used to detect qnr genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Activation of Host IRE1α-Dependent Signaling Axis Contributes the Intracellular Parasitism of Brucella melitensis.

IRE1α.notes: IRE1α activation contributes to Bm16M intracellular parasitism
