full_output.methodology: The study utilized a combination of in vitro experiments, including growth assays, morphological analysis, and phenotypic assessments, along with in vivo toxicity studies in zebrafish and mouse models to evaluate the effects of Q22 on BCC bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Genome analyses of bla(NDM-4) carrying ST 315 Escherichia coli isolate from sewage water of one of the Indian hospitals.

bla(NDM-4).genetic_context: bla NDM-4 , b bla CTX-M-15 , c bla TEM1b , d Class I integron carrying: dfrA12, aad, qacEδ1 and sul1 , e aac(3)-Ile, f sul2 , strA , strB , tetR (A) and tetA
bla(NDM-4).evidence_note: The paper describes the presence of bla(NDM-4) in an E. coli isolate and its role in carbapenem resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first detection of bla(NDM-4) carrying ST 315 Escherichia coli in India, highlighting the presence of a multidrug-resistant plasmid with various resistance markers.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, annotation, and analysis of the E. coli isolate AK-1.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluating the Frequency of aac(6')-IIa, ant(2")-I, intl1, and intl2 Genes in Aminoglycosides Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Isolates Obtained from Hospitalized Patients in Yazd, Iran.

aac(6')-IIa.validation_method: PCR and correlation with antibiotic resistance

ant(2\")-Ia.validation_method: PCR and correlation with antibiotic resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study found high frequencies of aac(6')-IIa, ant(2")-Ia, and intl1 genes in aminoglycoside-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from Yazd, Iran, indicating their potential role in antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to analyze the presence of resistance genes and their correlation with resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic Activity of Colistin/Fosfomycin Combination against Carbapenemase-Producing Klebsiella pneumoniae in an In Vitro Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic Model.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the synergistic activity of colistin/fosfomycin combination against carbapenemase-producing K. pneumoniae, highlighting the effectiveness of the combination in reducing bacterial load and preventing the emergence of colistin-resistant subpopulations in susceptible isolates.
full_output.methodology: In vitro pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model to assess the antibacterial effects of colistin and fosfomycin against K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Polymer-augmented liposomes enhancing antibiotic delivery against intracellular infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel drug delivery system called polymer-augmented liposomes (PALs) that enhances the intracellular delivery of streptomycin, an aminoglycoside antibiotic, to combat intracellular infections. PALs are designed to improve the cytosolic delivery of antibiotics by incorporating a multifunctional diblock copolymer that enables targeted delivery, pH-responsive drug release, and endosomal release activity.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and characterization of a multifunctional diblock copolymer, the preparation of polymer-augmented liposomes (PALs), and evaluation of their performance in delivering streptomycin to intracellular bacteria using in vitro models.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of most common human pathogenic Campylobacter spp. in dogs and cats in Styria, Austria.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a low prevalence of Campylobacter spp. in dogs and cats in Styria, Austria, with C. jejuni being the most common species. High resistance rates were observed for several antibiotics in C. jejuni isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study used microbiological culture, real-time PCR, and antibiotic susceptibility testing to analyze Campylobacter spp. in fecal samples from dogs and cats.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes the design and evaluation of bi-shRNA constructs targeting KRAS mutations (G12D, G12V, G12C, G12R) for effective and specific knockdown in cancer cells, showing reduced tumor growth in vivo.
full_output.methodology: Reporter vectors, RFLP analysis, in vitro cell growth assays, and in vivo xenograft models were used to evaluate the effectiveness of bi-shRNA constructs targeting KRAS mutations.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence of MRSA and multi-resistant gram-negative bacteria in refugees admitted to the hospital-But no hint of transmission.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of MRSA and MDR-GNB in refugee patients, but no transmission of these organisms to other patients was observed.
full_output.methodology: Screening for MDRO, WGS, and epidemiological analysis.

full_output.paper_title: A repetitive mutation and selection system for bacterial evolution to increase the specific affinity to pancreatic cancer cells.

mutations_found.nucleotide_position: 3 nucleotides before the transcription start of fimB gene
mutations_found.position_in_molecule: 3 nucleotides before the transcription start of fimB gene

ycdR.encodes: predicted enzyme associated with biofilm formation

icd.notes: These are silent mutations in the icd gene.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in fimB and fimE genes in E. coli that increased type I pili expression, enhancing adhesion to pancreatic cancer cells. Additionally, mutations in ycdR and uvrX in B. subtilis were found to influence biofilm formation and UV damage repair, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing, genomic PCR, and adhesion assays were used to identify and validate mutations affecting bacterial adhesion to cancer cells.

full_output.paper_title: Dissection of the antimicrobial and hemolytic activity of Cap18: Generation of Cap18 derivatives with enhanced specificity.

Cap18.notes: Mutations in Cap18 result in loss of antimicrobial activity.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified specific amino acid substitutions in Cap18 that significantly affect its antimicrobial activity against various bacterial pathogens. Mutations at positions I13, L17, and I24 resulted in a complete loss of antimicrobial activity against all tested bacterial species.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a positional scanning library of Cap18 derivatives to screen for antimicrobial activity against several bacterial strains, including Yersinia ruckeri, Aeromonas salmonicida, and Salmonella Typhimurium, through MIC testing.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and Antibiogram Assessment of Staphylococcus aureus in Beef at Municipal Abattoir and Butcher Shops in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that all 133 Staphylococcus aureus isolates were resistant to bacitracin, neomycin, and methicillin. Additionally, 95% of the isolates were resistant to tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method on Mueller Hinton agar plates.

full_output.paper_title: A novel PBP3 substitution in Haemophilus influenzae confers reduced aminopenicillin susceptibility.

ftsI.notes: The wild-type ftsI gene was susceptible to aminopenicillins.

full_output.key_findings: A novel PBP3 substitution, Y528H, was identified in Haemophilus influenzae, which reduces aminopenicillin susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Site-directed mutagenesis and broth microdilution were used to validate the impact of the Y528H substitution on aminopenicillin susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Risk factors for carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae bloodstream infection and predictors of mortality in Chinese paediatric patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified NDM-1, IMP-4, and KPC-2 as the primary carbapenemases associated with carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae (CRKP) bloodstream infections in pediatric patients. Hematologic malignancies and previous cephalosporin administration were significant risk factors for CRKP BSI, and isolation of CRKP was an independent predictor of mortality.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective case-control study analyzing clinical data, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and PCR for carbapenemase genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a low prevalence of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) in both armed force and civilian patients at AFRTH, with all MDR-TB cases being previously treated. Risk factors for MDR-TB included category of attendants, HIV infection, and TB contact history.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study involving drug susceptibility testing and statistical analysis of patient data.

full_output.paper_title: Deltamethrin resistance in the salmon louse, Lepeophtheirus salmonis (Krøyer): Maternal inheritance and reduced apoptosis.

COX1.mechanism: Non-synonymous SNP causing amino acid change

COX3.mechanism: Non-synonymous SNP causing amino acid change

ND1.mechanism: Non-synonymous SNP causing amino acid change

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mitochondrial gene SNPs, including non-synonymous changes in COX1, COX3, ND1, and ND5, associated with deltamethrin resistance in Lepeophtheirus salmonis, suggesting a maternal inheritance mechanism.
full_output.methodology: RNAseq, TaqMan assay, and bioassays were used to analyze mitochondrial gene SNPs and their correlation with deltamethrin resistance.
full_output.sample_size: Various strains and generations analyzed, including F2 progeny from crosses between sensitive and resistant strains.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative genomic analysis of a naturally competent Elizabethkingia anophelis isolated from an eye infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study isolate of Elizabethkingia anophelis exhibits resistance to multiple antibiotics, including penicillins, cephalosporins, monobactam, carbapenems, aminoglycosides, and trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole. It possesses several beta-lactamase genes (bla GOB, blab, bla CME), vancomycin resistance gene VanW, and genes associated with heavy metal and arsenic resistance. Additionally, it contains multidrug efflux pumps contributing to its broad-spectrum resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and PCR confirmation of natural transformation.

full_output.paper_title: Clay-induced DNA breaks as a path for genetic diversity, antibiotic resistance, and asbestos carcinogenesis.

recA.encodes: RecA protein involved in DNA repair and recombination

mutations_found.effect_on_function: The inactivation of the recA gene suppresses the mutagenic effect of sepiolite.
mutations_found.origin: The inactivation of the recA gene suppresses the mutagenic effect of sepiolite.

recA.notes: Inactivation of recA gene suppresses the mutagenic effect of sepiolite.

full_output.key_findings: Sepiolite and asbestos fibers induce DNA double-strand breaks in E. coli through mechanical friction, leading to increased mutant frequency. The recA gene is essential for the mutagenic effect of sepiolite.
full_output.methodology: Mutant frequency measurements, plasmid integrity analysis, and scanning electron microscopy were used to assess DNA damage and mutagenesis.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of serogroup 19 Streptococcus pneumoniae in the Czech Republic in the post-vaccine era.

tetM.validation_method: PCR amplification of the 1862-bp fragment from positions 21 to 1882 of the published sequence of the tetM gene

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of the ermB and tetM genes in serogroup 19 Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates, which conferred resistance to erythromycin and tetracycline, respectively. Additionally, mutations in penicillin-binding protein (PBP) genes were associated with penicillin resistance in 19F isolates.
full_output.methodology: MLST analysis, WGS, PCR amplification, and MIC testing were used to characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro synergistic effect of amlodipine and imipenem on the expression of the AdeABC efflux pump in multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of efflux pump genes adeB, adeE, adeJ, abeM, and abeS in multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates and demonstrates that amlodipine enhances the antimicrobial activity of imipenem by inhibiting the AdeABC efflux pump.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification, sequencing, and gene silencing experiments were conducted to analyze efflux pump gene expression and antimicrobial susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: The co-existence of NS5A and NS5B resistance-associated substitutions is associated with virologic failure in Hepatitis C Virus genotype 1 patients treated with sofosbuvir and ledipasvir.

NS5A.notes: Mutations in NS5A were associated with virologic failure.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified that co-existing NS5A and NS5B resistance-associated substitutions (RASs) were linked to virologic failure in patients with Hepatitis C Virus genotype 1 treated with sofosbuvir and ledipasvir.
full_output.methodology: The study used direct sequencing to analyze the prevalence of NS5A and NS5B RASs in patients treated with sofosbuvir and ledipasvir.

full_output.paper_title: Facilely accessible quinoline derivatives as potent antibacterial agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the development of quinoline derivatives with potent antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant Gram-positive bacteria, including C. difficile. Compound 6 showed strong activity with a MIC of 1.0 μg/mL against C. difficile, comparable to vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of quinoline compounds, determination of MICs against bacterial strains, and in vivo evaluation in a mouse model of C. difficile infection.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation of Toxigenic Clostridium difficile from Animal Manure and Composts Being Used as Biological Soil Amendments.

ermB.notes: The ermB gene was detected in 4 out of 58 C. difficile isolates, which showed resistance to clindamycin.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that 53.45% of C. difficile isolates exhibited reduced susceptibility to clindamycin, and the ermB gene was identified in 4 of these isolates, indicating a mechanism of clindamycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR for gene detection, agar dilution method for antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and capillary gel electrophoresis-based PCR-ribotyping for strain characterization.

full_output.paper_title: A protein that controls the onset of a Salmonella virulence program.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies CigR and MgtC as key players in controlling the onset of a Salmonella virulence program. CigR acts as an anti-virulence factor by inhibiting MgtC, which is involved in virulence mechanisms such as ATP synthesis inhibition and PhoP stabilization.
full_output.methodology: Co-immunoprecipitation, western blot analysis, and bacterial growth experiments were used to validate the interactions and roles of CigR and MgtC.

full_output.paper_title: Specific binding between Bacillus thuringiensis Cry9Aa and Vip3Aa toxins synergizes their toxicity against Asiatic rice borer (Chilo suppressalis).
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies specific binding regions between Cry9Aa and Vip3Aa toxins that are critical for their synergistic toxicity against Asiatic rice borer. Mutations in these regions significantly reduce the synergistic effect.
full_output.methodology: Expression and purification of toxins, binding assays, site-directed mutagenesis, and bioassays.

full_output.paper_title: Porcine Circovirus Type 2 Suppresses IL-12p40 Induction via Capsid/gC1qR-Mediated MicroRNAs and Signalings.
full_output.key_findings: PCV2 infection suppresses IL-12p40 expression and Th1 immune response, increasing susceptibility to PRRSV and H. parasuis infections. PCV2 Cap plays a predominant role in suppressing IL-12p40, and miR-23a and miR-29b are key mediators of this suppression.
full_output.methodology: Experimental investigation of PCV2's impact on IL-12p40 expression and Th1 immune response using PAMs, siRNA knockdown, and miRNA mimics/inhibitors.
full_output.sample_size: 30 piglets in first experiment, 70 in second

full_output.key_findings: The study highlights that competitive inter-species interactions in multispecies brewery biofilms lead to increased antimicrobial tolerance, particularly through reduced competition allowing certain species to thrive. It also shows that the presence of competing species can directly enhance the inherent tolerance of others, affecting the effectiveness of antimicrobials like sulfathiazole.
full_output.methodology: The research involved constructing defined multispecies biofilm models from brewery isolates, assessing inter-species interactions, and evaluating antimicrobial tolerance using sulfathiazole.

full_output.paper_title: Risk factors and molecular features of sequence type (ST) 131 extended-Spectrum-β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli in community-onset female genital tract infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies CTX-M-15, CTX-M-55, and CTX-M-27 as the primary ESBLs in ST131 E. coli isolates causing community-onset female genital tract infections, highlighting their association with multidrug resistance and specific risk factors.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, PFGE, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize ESBL-producing E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Association of virulence gene expression with colistin-resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii: analysis of genotype, antimicrobial susceptibility, and biofilm formation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that reduced expression of recA, along with increased in vivo expression of lpsB, dnaK, and blsA, are associated with colistin resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR, qRT-PCR, and animal infection model.

full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that MazF, an endoribonuclease, cleaves a wide range of cellular mRNAs and rRNA precursors, leading to the inhibition of both translation and ribosome biogenesis. It shows that MazF does not produce a large pool of leaderless mRNAs or specialized ribosomes, but instead disrupts rRNA maturation and ribosome biogenesis.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized paired-end RNA-Seq, qRT-PCR, ribosome profiling, and Northern blotting to analyze the effects of MazF on E. coli transcripts and ribosomes.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative Genomics Analysis of Plasmid pPV989-94 from a Clinical Isolate of Pantoea vagans PV989.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes within the R4' fragment of plasmid pPV989-94, including those involved in glycometabolism, resistance, and DNA repair. These genes contribute to the adaptability of Pantoea vagans PV989 in diverse environments.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and comparative genomics analysis were used to identify and characterize the genes in the R4' fragment of plasmid pPV989-94.

full_output.paper_title: Cloning and Expression of the Organophosphate Pesticide-Degrading α-β Hydrolase Gene in Plasmid pMK-07 to Confer Cross-Resistance to Antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the alpha-beta hydrolase gene from Bacillus sp. MK-07, which confers cross-resistance to several antibiotics through nonspecific cleavage, suggesting a link between pesticide degradation and antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Cloning and expression of the alpha-beta hydrolase gene in E. coli, followed by biochemical and computational analysis of its antibiotic degradation capabilities.

full_output.paper_title: Drug-resistance patterns of Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains and associated risk factors among multi drug-resistant tuberculosis suspected patients from Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains, particularly resistance to isoniazid, streptomycin, rifampicin, ethambutol, and pyrazinamide. The prevalence of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) was 39.4%, with significant associations between MDR-TB and risk factors such as TB/HIV co-infection, cigarette smoking, alcohol consumption, hospital admission, and health facility visits.
full_output.methodology: The study used sputum samples analyzed through Ziehl-Neelsen staining, GeneXpert MTB/RIF assay, and culture methods (Lowenstein-Jensen and MGIT). Drug susceptibility testing was performed using the Bactec MGIT 960 method.

full_output.paper_title: Association of bacterial genotypes and epidemiological features with treatment failure in hemodialysis patients with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that CA genotypes (SCC mec type IV or V) were associated with better clinical outcomes in hemodialysis patients with MRSA bacteremia compared to HA genotypes (SCC mec type I, II, or III).
full_output.methodology: Retrospective review and molecular analysis of clinical isolates from 106 HD patients with MRSA bacteremia.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical and bacteriological features and prognosis of ascitic fluid infection in Chinese patients with cirrhosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter spp. and Klebsiella spp. were associated with higher 30-day mortality in patients with ascitic fluid infection. Additionally, resistance to third-generation cephalosporins (TGC) and carbapenems was linked to reduced survival probabilities.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of bacteriological and clinical data from patients with spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP) and bacterascites (BA) at a Chinese hospital.

full_output.paper_title: Screening for fecal presence of colistin-resistant Escherichia coli and mcr-1 and mcr-2 genes in camel-calves in southern Tunisia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found no presence of colistin resistance or mcr-1 and mcr-2 genes in E. coli isolates from camel-calves in southern Tunisia, although one E. cloacae isolate was found to be colistin-resistant without carrying mcr-1 or mcr-2 genes.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection and MIC testing for colistin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that 96% of potable water samples from peri-urban communities in Karachi, Pakistan, were microbiologically unsafe, with 29.2% of fecal indicator organisms producing extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs).
full_output.methodology: Microbiological quality assessment and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of water samples from peri-urban households.

full_output.paper_title: CpxR/CpxA Controls scsABCD Transcription To Counteract Copper and Oxidative Stress in Salmonella enterica Serovar Typhimurium.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the scsABCD operon as a copper-activated system regulated by the CpxR/CpxA two-component system, which plays a role in counteracting copper and oxidative stress in Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium.
full_output.methodology: The study used transcriptomic analysis, promoter reporter assays, mutagenesis, and copper sensitivity assays to investigate the role of the scsABCD operon in stress response.

full_output.paper_title: Combined Drug Resistance Mutations Substantially Enhance Enzyme Production in Paenibacillus agaridevorans.
full_output.key_findings: Drug resistance mutations in rsmG, rpsL, and rpoB significantly enhance CITase production in Paenibacillus agaridevorans.
full_output.methodology: Screening for drug-resistant mutants, gene sequencing, and enzyme activity assays.

full_output.paper_title: ABC transporter content diversity in Streptococcus pneumoniae impacts competence regulation and bacteriocin production.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that ABC transporters ComAB and BlpAB in Streptococcus pneumoniae are involved in the secretion of bacteriocins and pheromones, and that BlpAB can also secrete CSP, leading to com activation. BlpAB(+) strains have a competitive advantage over BlpAB(-) strains during nasopharyngeal colonization.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a dual luciferase reporter system, peptide-processing assays, and bioluminescence assays to analyze the roles of ComAB and BlpAB in pneumocin secretion and competence regulation.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Activity of Plazomicin against Gram-Negative and Gram-Positive Isolates Collected from U.S. Hospitals and Comparative Activities of Aminoglycosides against Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacteriaceae and Isolates Carrying Carbapenemase Genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of plazomicin against a wide range of clinical isolates, including carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) and isolates carrying carbapenemase genes. Plazomicin showed high activity against most Enterobacteriaceae, including CRE, with MIC 50 and MIC 90 values of 0.5/2 μg/ml and 0.25/1 μg/ml, respectively. It was effective against isolates resistant to other aminoglycosides like gentamicin and tobramycin.
full_output.methodology: The study used the CLSI reference broth microdilution method to test the antimicrobial activity of plazomicin and comparator agents against 4,825 clinical isolates collected from U.S. hospitals.

full_output.paper_title: Diversity of Carbapenemase-Producing Escherichia coli Isolates in France in 2012-2013.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various carbapenemase-producing Escherichia coli isolates in France, including OXA-48-like, NDM, VIM, and KPC carbapenemases. These isolates exhibited resistance to carbapenems, with OXA-48-like being the most prevalent.
full_output.methodology: The study involved PCR and sequencing to detect carbapenemase-encoding genes, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Few Conserved Amino Acids in the Small Multidrug Resistance Transporter EmrE Influence Drug Polyselectivity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several conserved amino acid residues in the small multidrug resistance transporter EmrE that influence drug polyselectivity, particularly in relation to quaternary cation compounds (QCCs). Key residues included E14 (E14D and E14A), A10C, F44C, L47C, and W63A, which affected resistance to various QCCs.
full_output.methodology: Site-directed mutagenesis and agar spot dilution plating were used to assess the impact of specific EmrE mutations on resistance to quaternary cation compounds.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro and Intracellular Activity of Imipenem Combined with Rifabutin and Avibactam against Mycobacterium abscessus.

blaMAb.validation_method: comparison of CIP104536 and a β-lactamase-deficient derivative

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Bla MAb as a β-lactamase that confers resistance to imipenem in Mycobacterium abscessus. Inhibition of Bla MAb by avibactam enhances the efficacy of imipenem.
full_output.methodology: Comparison of wild-type and β-lactamase-deficient derivatives of M. abscessus to assess the impact of Bla MAb on antibiotic activity.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the Bactericidal Activity of Plazomicin and Comparators against Multidrug-Resistant Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.key_findings: Plazomicin shows potent bactericidal activity against multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae, including those with aminoglycoside and beta-lactam resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) and time-kill assays were performed to evaluate the bactericidal activity of plazomicin and comparators against MDR Enterobacteriaceae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial resistance in Brucella melitensis from a Norwegian perspective.

full_output.paper_title: Combination Therapy Strategies Against Multiple-Resistant Streptococcus Suis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes in multidrug-resistant Streptococcus suis isolates, including tetM, lnuB, erm(B), tetO, tetL, and aph3′, which confer resistance to tetracycline, clindamycin, erythromycin, and aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to identify AMR genes in S. suis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Polyphyletic Nature of Salmonella enterica Serotype Derby and Lineage-Specific Host-Association Revealed by Genome-Wide Analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified AMR genes aadA2, sul1, and tetA in Salmonella enterica serovar Derby strains, with a multidrug-resistant profile STR-SSS-TET in certain lineages.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, MLST, SNP analysis, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of Colistin and Its Combination With Rifampin in Vitro and in Experimental Models of Infection Caused by Carbapenemase-Producing Clinical Isolates of Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the efficacy of colistin and rifampin combination against carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae (CP-Kp) isolates. While colistin showed variable in vitro activity, the combination with rifampin demonstrated synergistic effects and prevented the development of colistin-resistant mutants. However, the combination had limited efficacy in treating severe peritoneal sepsis, except against the KPC-3 strain.
full_output.methodology: The study used time-kill curves, in vivo murine models of peritoneal sepsis and pneumonia, and MIC testing to evaluate the efficacy of colistin and rifampin against CP-Kp isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of Phloeophagus Beetles as a Source of Pseudomonas Strains That Produce Potentially New Bioactive Substances and Description of Pseudomonas bohemica sp. nov.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Pseudomonas bohemica sp. nov. as a new species capable of producing antimicrobial substances. The genome analysis revealed various gene clusters potentially involved in the production of bioactive compounds, including colicin V, siderophores, and other secondary metabolites.
full_output.methodology: The study involved bacterial isolation from bark beetles, 16S rRNA sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, genome sequencing, and bioactivity screening against various microbial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution and Genetic Characteristics of SXT/R391 Integrative Conjugative Elements in Shewanella spp. From China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the SXT/R391 integrative conjugative element ICE Sup CHN110003 in Shewanella upenei strains, which carries antibiotic resistance genes floR, strA, strB, and sul2, conferring resistance to chloramphenicol, streptomycin, and sulfamethoxazole.
full_output.methodology: PCR screening, genome sequencing, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and conjugation assays were used to characterize the SXT/R391 elements and their resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation, Functional Characterization and Transmissibility of p3PS10, a Multidrug Resistance Plasmid of the Fish Pathogen Piscirickettsia salmonis.

tetA(t31).encodes: tetracycline efflux pump, major facilitator superfamily (MFS) transporter
tetA(t31).evidence_note: The plasmid p3PS10, which harbors multidrug resistance genes for tetracyclines [tet(31)], was shown to confer resistance to oxytetracycline.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes the multidrug resistance plasmid p3PS10 in Piscirickettsia salmonis, which carries genes conferring resistance to chloramphenicol (cat2), tetracyclines (tetA(t31)), aminoglycosides (aadA1, sat1), and sulfonamides (sul2).
full_output.methodology: Functional characterization through cloning, MIC assays, and mating experiments.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple P. salmonis isolates from Chilean aquacultures

full_output.paper_title: Glucocorticoids Impair Phagocytosis and Inflammatory Response Against Crohn's Disease-Associated Adherent-Invasive Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that glucocorticoids impair phagocytosis and induce anti-inflammatory polarization in macrophages infected with Crohn's disease-associated adherent-invasive Escherichia coli (AIEC), potentially contributing to the survival of AIEC in infected CD patients.
full_output.methodology: The study used microarray analysis, quantitative PCR, amikacin protection assay, and flow cytometry to evaluate the effects of glucocorticoids on macrophage function and gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Commensal Bacteria-Dependent CD8αβ(+) T Cells in the Intestinal Epithelium Produce Antimicrobial Peptides.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that commensal bacteria regulate the number of CD8αβ+ IELs in the intestinal epithelium and that these cells produce antimicrobial peptides, such as α-defensins, which exhibit antimicrobial activity against bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Flow cytometry, microarray analysis, qPCR, and antimicrobial activity assays were used to analyze the role of commensal bacteria in regulating CD8αβ+ IELs and their antimicrobial properties.
full_output.sample_size: Varied depending on the experiment, with n=4-6 mice per group in some experiments.

full_output.paper_title: The occurrence and frequency of genomic mutations that mediate Isoniazid and Rifampicin resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from untreated pulmonary Tuberculosis cases in urban Blantyre, Malawi.

katG.mechanism: confers resistance to Isoniazid (INH)

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a low frequency of genomic mutations in the katG gene that confer resistance to Isoniazid (INH) among Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from untreated pulmonary TB cases in urban Blantyre, Malawi. Specifically, all katG mutations detected were the S315T1 point mutation, which is associated with high INH resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used the GenoType MTBDRplus Ver 2.0 assay to detect genomic mutations in the katG, inhA promoter, and rpoB genes in 141 MTB clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: In-Group" Communication in Marine Vibrio: A Review of N-Acyl Homoserine Lactones-Driven Quorum Sensing.
full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the characteristics, detection methods, and regulatory mechanisms of N-Acyl Homoserine Lactones (AHLs) in marine Vibrio species, highlighting their role in quorum sensing and pathogenicity.
full_output.methodology: Review of existing literature on AHLs in marine Vibrio, focusing on their structural characteristics, detection techniques, and regulatory pathways.

full_output.paper_title: The Aspergillus flavus Phosphatase CDC14 Regulates Development, Aflatoxin Biosynthesis and Pathogenicity.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: increased sensitivity to osmotic and cell wall integrity stresses

AflCDC14.notes: AflCDC14 is a phosphatase involved in various cellular processes, and its deletion leads to several phenotypic changes.
AflCDC14.evidence_note: The paper describes the deletion of AflCDC14 and its effects on various cellular processes, but does not provide evidence that this gene confers resistance to antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies AflCDC14 as a phosphatase involved in regulating development, aflatoxin biosynthesis, and pathogenicity in Aspergillus flavus. Its deletion leads to growth defects, abnormal conidium morphology, defective septum, and increased aflatoxin production.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion and complementation strategies, PCR, RT-PCR, Southern blot analysis, and phenotypic assays were used to study the role of AflCDC14.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and Validation of an Antivirulence Agent Targeting HlyU-Regulated Virulence in Vibrio vulnificus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies fursultiamine hydrochloride (FTH) as an antivirulence agent that inhibits HlyU-regulated virulence factors in Vibrio vulnificus without inducing antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used an inhibitor-screening reporter platform, qRT-PCR, and hemolysis assays to validate the antivirulence effects of FTH.

full_output.paper_title: Live Attenuated Tularemia Vaccines for Protection Against Respiratory Challenge With Virulent F. tularensis subsp. tularensis.
full_output.key_findings: The paper characterizes several live attenuated Francisella tularensis vaccine candidates, including mutants with deletions in genes such as purMCD, sodB Ft, emrA1, dsbA, clpB, capB, wzy, wbtA, FTL_0057, FTL_0325, FTL_0552, FTL_0291, and FTL_0304, which show varying degrees of attenuation and protective efficacy against respiratory challenge with virulent F. tularensis subsp. tularensis.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized experimental validation through growth assays, challenge experiments, and analysis of immune responses in murine and other animal models.

full_output.paper_title: Group A Streptococcus M1T1 Intracellular Infection of Primary Tonsil Epithelial Cells Dampens Levels of Secreted IL-8 Through the Action of SpyCEP.

spycep.validation_method: western blot analysis, ELISA, and mutagenesis

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SpyCEP, a serine protease from Group A Streptococcus M1T1, as a key factor in degrading IL-8, thus dampening the host's inflammatory response during infection.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq, ELISA, western blot, and mutagenesis were used to analyze gene expression and functional characterization of SpyCEP.

full_output.paper_title: Evidence of link between quorum sensing and sugar metabolism in Escherichia coli revealed via cocrystal structures of LsrK and HPr.
Group B Streptococcus Biofilm Regulatory Protein A Contributes to Bacterial Physiology and Innate Immune Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies BrpA as a LytR-CpsA-Psr enzyme that plays a crucial role in Group B Streptococcus (GBS) cell wall integrity, biofilm formation, and resistance to innate immune components. BrpA deficiency leads to increased susceptibility to neutrophil and blood killing, reduced biofilm formation, and impaired vaginal colonization.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized targeted mutagenesis, RNA sequencing, and various in vitro and in vivo assays to investigate the role of BrpA in GBS physiology and virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Beta-defensin derived cationic antimicrobial peptides with potent killing activity against gram negative and gram positive bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the development of short linear cationic antimicrobial peptides (CAMPs) derived from avian β-defensins (AvBDs) with potent antimicrobial activity against multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa and methicillin-resistant S. pseudintermedius. These peptides demonstrate strong antimicrobial activity, resistance to physiological salt concentrations, and protease resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the design, synthesis, and evaluation of novel CAMPs for antimicrobial activity, salt resistance, protease resistance, and cytotoxicity using in vitro assays.

full_output.paper_title: Structural mechanism of AadA, a dual-specificity aminoglycoside adenylyltransferase from Salmonella enterica.

mutations_found.validated_by: in vitro activity assays and structural analysis

full_output.paper_title: A rapid culture system uninfluenced by an inoculum effect increases reliability and convenience for drug susceptibility testing of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The DAC system was developed to improve the reliability and convenience of drug susceptibility testing (DST) for Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) by eliminating the inoculum effect. The system demonstrated consistent MIC values across varying inoculum sizes and showed high agreement with the L-J method for DST results.
full_output.methodology: The DAC system was validated using 254 clinical MTB strains, comparing DST results with the L-J method and analyzing discrepancies through DNA sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Terrein is an inhibitor of quorum sensing and c-di-GMP in Pseudomonas aeruginosa: a connection between quorum sensing and c-di-GMP.
full_output.key_findings: Terrein inhibits quorum sensing (QS) and c-di-GMP signaling in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, reducing virulence factor production and biofilm formation without affecting cell viability.
full_output.methodology: Bioassay-guided fractionation, QS competition assays, and c-di-GMP level measurements were used to evaluate terrein's effects.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug resistant pathogens respond differently to the presence of co-pathogen, commensal, probiotic and host cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes and their expression changes in response to co-culturing with other bacteria and host cells, highlighting the dynamic nature of AMR gene regulation in multidrug-resistant organisms.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, RNA-Seq, and qPCR were used to analyze AMR gene expression in multidrug-resistant organisms under various co-culture conditions.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial peptide-loaded liquid crystalline precursor bioadhesive system for the prevention of dental caries.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of the D1-23 peptide fragment, a part of human beta-defensin-3, against Streptococcus mutans biofilm. The D1-23 peptide showed significant antimicrobial activity, reducing biofilm formation effectively.
full_output.methodology: Microdilution broth method for determining MIC and MBC, biofilm assays, and cytotoxicity tests.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of amikacin against various Gram-negative bacteria, including E. coli, K. pneumoniae, P. aeruginosa, and A. baumannii, highlighting varying susceptibility rates and the challenges posed by multidrug-resistant isolates.
full_output.methodology: Minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) were determined using agar dilution methods according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of multidrug-resistant Gram-negative pathogens isolated from febrile neutropenic cancer patients with bloodstream infections in Egypt and new synergistic antibiotic combinations.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes including ESBLs (ctx-m, shv, tem), aac(6')-Ib, aac(6')-Ib-cr, and PMQR genes (qnrS, qnrB, qnrA) in MDR Gram-negative bacteria isolated from febrile neutropenic cancer patients in Egypt. These genes conferred resistance to multiple antibiotics, highlighting the need for new empirical antibiotic strategies.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to detect and characterize AMR genes in MDR Gram-negative isolates.

full_output.paper_title: First description of a cefixime- and ciprofloxacin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolate with mutations in key antimicrobial susceptibility-determining genes from the country of Georgia.

full_output.methodology: Prospective evaluation of patients treated with resistance-guided therapy for M. genitalium infections, including PCR-based resistance assays and Sanger sequencing for mutation detection.

Additionally, the Pdr1 transcription factor and its gain-of-function mutant Pdr1 L280F are shown to influence both antifungal resistance and adherence.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, mutational analysis, heterologous expression in S. cerevisiae, and adherence assays were used to characterize the functions of adhesins and regulatory elements.

full_output.paper_title: Metatranscriptome Analysis of the Vaginal Microbiota Reveals Potential Mechanisms for Protection against Metronidazole in Bacterial Vaginosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies CRISPR-associated (Cas) genes in Gardnerella vaginalis that are highly upregulated in nonresponding patients to metronidazole treatment, suggesting a potential mechanism for protection against metronidazole through DNA repair.
full_output.methodology: Metatranscriptome analysis of vaginal microbiota from patients with bacterial vaginosis before and after metronidazole treatment.

full_output.paper_title: Metallo-β-lactamase-mediated resistance among clinical carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates in northern Iran: A potential threat to clinical therapeutics.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaIMP, blaVIM, and blaNDM genes as major contributors to carbapenem resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates in northern Iran.

full_output.paper_title: The tigecycline evaluation and surveillance trial; assessment of the activity of tigecycline and other selected antibiotics against gram-positive and gram-negative pathogens from France collected between 2004 and 2016.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of tigecycline and other antibiotics against various Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens in France from 2004 to 2016. It found that tigecycline remained effective against many isolates, with high susceptibility rates for several bacterial species, including Enterococcus, Staphylococcus aureus, and Streptococcus pneumoniae. However, increasing resistance to certain antibiotics was noted, particularly among Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed antimicrobial susceptibility data from 26,486 isolates collected over 12 years, using broth microdilution methods and EUCAST breakpoints to determine susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Functional insights into the Streptococcus pneumoniae HicBA toxin-antitoxin system based on a structural study.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the HicBA toxin-antitoxin system in Streptococcus pneumoniae, revealing the structural and functional details of HicA as a ribonuclease and HicB as an antitoxin that binds to promoter DNA.

full_output.paper_title: QQS orphan gene and its interactor NF-YC4 reduce susceptibility to pathogens and pests.

full_output.paper_title: 3-methylcrotonyl Coenzyme A (CoA) carboxylase complex is involved in the Xanthomonas citri subsp. citri lifestyle during citrus infection.

full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics analysis, in vitro reconstitution, enzymatic activity assays, and mutant strain characterization.

full_output.methodology: qRT-PCR, whole genome sequencing, and cytochrome C binding assays were used to analyze gene expression and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Interplay of a non-conjugative integrative element and a conjugative plasmid in the spread of antibiotic resistance via suicidal plasmid transfer from an aquaculture Vibrio isolate.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the plasmid pSEA1 and the integrative element Tn 6283, which carry various antibiotic resistance genes including tet(M), mef(C), mph(G), sul2, catII, and bla, facilitating the spread of antibiotic resistance in aquatic environments.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, PCR amplification, and Southern hybridization were used to analyze the resistance genes and their integration patterns.

full_output.paper_title: A cell-based infection assay identifies efflux pump modulators that reduce bacterial intracellular load.
full_output.key_findings: Three efflux pump modulators (EPM30, EPM35, and EPM43) were identified that inhibit bacterial efflux pumps, reduce intracellular bacterial load, and enhance the activity of antimicrobial peptides and antibiotics in macrophages and epithelial cells.
full_output.methodology: High-content screening platform (SAFIRE) and biochemical assays were used to identify and characterize EPMs targeting efflux pumps in Salmonella.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes the successful expression and purification of recombinant LtxA and LtxC in E. coli, highlighting the importance of post-translational acylation for LtxA's biological activity.
full_output.methodology: Expression of ltxA and ltxC in E. coli, purification via Ni-NTA chromatography, and functional assays including cytotoxicity and CD spectroscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of fluoroquinolone and/or cephalosporin resistance in Shigella sonnei isolates from yaks.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified fluoroquinolone and cephalosporin resistance mechanisms in Shigella sonnei isolates from yaks, including mutations in gyrA and parC, and the presence of aac(6')-Ib-cr, qnrS, qnrB, blaTEM-1, blaOXA-1, blaCTX-M-14, and blaCTX-M-79 genes.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance genes and mutations in Shigella sonnei isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified coagulase-negative staphylococci (CNS) as the primary pathogens in periprosthetic joint infections (PJIs), with S. epidermidis being the most prevalent and resistant species. Resistance to methicillin, ofloxacin, and rifampicin was widespread, while no resistance was observed to linezolid or daptomycin.

full_output.key_findings: Selenium was found to inhibit UPEC biofilm formation on urinary catheters by reducing EPS production and the expression of biofilm-associated genes such as fimA, fimH, sfaS, focA, and papG. full_output.paper_title: Pyrimidine synthesis inhibition enhances cutaneous defenses against antibiotic resistant bacteria through activation of NOD2 signaling.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteriological profile and antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of urine culture isolates from patients in Ndjamena, Chad.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of antimicrobial resistance among urine culture isolates, particularly Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae. Resistance to aminoglycosides was primarily mediated by AAC(3)-I and AAC(6')-I enzymes, while quinolone resistance was linked to mutations in gyrA and parC genes.

full_output.paper_title: Whole genome sequence revealed the fine transmission map of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumonia isolates within a nosocomial outbreak.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of blaKPC-2, blaSHV-1, and blaCTX-M-15 genes in all 26 CRKP isolates, which conferred resistance to multiple beta-lactam antibiotics. The isolates belonged to sequence type ST11 and exhibited a clonal outbreak pattern.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, PCR, and sequencing were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes in the CRKP isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance to Agents Used for Staphylococcus aureus Decolonization: Is There a Reason for Concern?
full_output.key_findings: The review discusses the emergence of resistance to chlorhexidine gluconate (CHG) and mupirocin in Staphylococcus aureus, highlighting the role of efflux pumps (qacA/B) in CHG resistance and target modification (mupA) in mupirocin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Review of existing literature and studies on antimicrobial resistance in S. aureus related to decolonization agents.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes AcLys, a prophage-encoded endolysin from Acinetobacter baumannii AB 5075, which exhibits antimicrobial activity against Gram-negative bacteria. The protein's C-terminal α-helix is suggested to aid in membrane penetration, although its activity is limited by rapid inactivation.
full_output.methodology: The study involved cloning, expression, purification, and biochemical characterization of AcLys, along with structural analysis via X-ray crystallography.

full_output.paper_title: A Marine Isolate of Bacillus pumilus Secretes a Pumilacidin Active against Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a marine isolate of Bacillus pumilus, SF214, which secretes two antimicrobial molecules: a small molecule (<3 kDa) active against Staphylococcus aureus and a larger molecule (>10 kDa) active against Listeria monocytogenes. The small molecule is a mixture of lipopeptides resembling pumilacidins, which are nonribosomally synthesized biosurfactants.

full_output.paper_title: CRISPR-FRT targets shared sites in a knock-out collection for off-the-shelf genome editing.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the use of CRISPR-FRT for targeted genome editing in E. coli, allowing for the introduction of specific mutations in genes such as basR, basS, and acrR, which confer resistance to colistin and ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR-FRT was used to introduce specific mutations in E. coli genes, followed by MIC testing to assess resistance phenotypes.

full_output.paper_title: Expression of the Shrimp wap gene in Drosophila elicits defense responses and protease inhibitory activity.
full_output.key_findings: The wap gene from Chinese white shrimp, when expressed in Drosophila, conferred antibacterial activity against various bacteria, including MRSA, and protease inhibitory activity. The WAP protein extract showed broad-spectrum antimicrobial effects and was more effective than ampicillin in some cases.
full_output.methodology: Transgenic Drosophila construction, qRT-PCR, antimicrobial and protease activity assays, and in vivo models.

full_output.paper_title: The lytic transglycosylase MltB connects membrane homeostasis and in vivo fitness of Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mltB as a critical fitness factor in Acinetobacter baumannii, essential for in vivo fitness, stress resistance, and cell envelope homeostasis.
full_output.methodology: Transposon-directed insertion site sequencing (TraDIS) and neutropenic murine model of bacteremia were used to identify and validate the role of mltB in A. baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Expression and regulation of the Pseudomonas aeruginosa hibernation promoting factor.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the hpf gene as having its own promoter (P hpf ) within the rpoN gene, demonstrating independent expression of hpf from the rpoN promoter. It also shows that hpf is expressed at low levels via transcriptional read-through from the rpoN promoter. Additionally, the research reveals that the 5' untranslated region (UTR) and the 5' end of the hpf coding region regulate hpf expression through mRNA folding, with specific hairpin loop structures influencing the amount of HPF produced.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized reporter fusions, 5'-RACE, RT-qPCR, and immunoblotting to analyze hpf expression and regulation.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of Bacterial Gene Transcription with an RpoN-Based Stapled Peptide.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the design and synthesis of stapled σ54 peptides that inhibit the transcription of σ54-dependent genes in bacteria by blocking the interaction between σ54 and its target DNA promoter.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized peptide synthesis, fluorescence polarization binding assays, gel shift assays, DNase digestion assays, flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, RT-qPCR, and RNA-Seq to investigate the effects of stapled σ54 peptides on bacterial gene transcription.

full_output.paper_title: CpxR negatively regulates the production of xenocoumacin 1, a dihydroisocoumarin derivative produced by Xenorhabdus nematophila.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization and clonal dynamics of nosocomial blaOXA-23 producing XDR Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes blaOXA-23, carO, adeB, aacA4, and aac(6')Ib-cr as key AMR genes in XDR Acinetobacter baumannii strains, highlighting their roles in carbapenem, tigecycline, and aminoglycoside resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, qPCR, MLST, and whole genome sequencing were used to identify and characterize AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: New Class of Adjuvants Enables Lower Dosing of Colistin Against Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a new class of adjuvants that enhance the potency of colistin against Acinetobacter baumannii, enabling a significant reduction in the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of colistin. These adjuvants show effectiveness in both in vitro and in vivo models, including a Galleria mellonella infection model.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and evaluation of urea-containing 2-aminoimidazole-based adjuvants, assessing their ability to potentiate colistin activity through MIC determination and in vivo experiments using a Galleria mellonella model.

full_output.paper_title: Cobalt Complex with Thiazole-Based Ligand as New Pseudomonas aeruginosa Quorum Quencher, Biofilm Inhibitor and Virulence Attenuator.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports a cobalt coordination complex (Co(HL)2) that inhibits the Pseudomonas aeruginosa LasI/LasR quorum sensing (QS) system, biofilm formation, and virulence factors. The compound interferes with the production and detection of the autoinducer 3-oxo-C12-HSL, demonstrating potential as a QS inhibitor and biofilm disruptor.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular docking, QS inhibition screening, biofilm prevention assays, and virulence factor analysis to evaluate the effects of Co(HL)2 on P. aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the Antimicrobial Activity and Cytotoxicity of Different Components of Natural Origin Present in Essential Oils.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antimicrobial activity of essential oil components such as carvacrol, cinnamaldehyde, and thymol against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, highlighting their bactericidal mechanism through membrane disruption.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution, SEM, flow cytometry, and confocal microscopy to assess the antimicrobial activity and mechanisms of essential oil components.

full_output.paper_title: Risk Factors for Gastrointestinal Colonization and Acquisition of Carbapenem-Resistant Gram-Negative Bacteria among Patients in Intensive Care Units in Thailand.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified carbapenemase genes bla OXA-23, bla OXA-24, bla OXA-51, bla OXA-58, bla NDM, and bla IMP in carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, highlighting their role in resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect carbapenemase genes in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Chloramphenicol Resistance Requires an Inner Membrane Permease
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ABUW_0982 as a novel chloramphenicol resistance gene in Acinetobacter baumannii strain Ab5075, demonstrating that its disruption leads to increased susceptibility to chloramphenicol.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, complementation, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to validate the role of ABUW_0982 in chloramphenicol resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Clonal Background, Resistance Gene Profile, and Porin Gene Mutations Modulate In Vitro Susceptibility to Imipenem-Relebactam in Diverse Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the addition of relebactam (REL) reduced imipenem (IMI) minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) to the susceptible range for 88% of clinical carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) isolates, highlighting the effectiveness of IMI-REL against CRE, especially those harboring bla KPC.
full_output.methodology: Broth microdilution testing and whole-genome sequencing were used to evaluate the susceptibility of CRE isolates to IMI and IMI-REL and to identify resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Biochemical and Structural Basis of Triclosan Resistance in a Novel Enoyl-Acyl Carrier Protein Reductase.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies FabL2, a novel enoyl-acyl carrier protein reductase (ENR) from a metagenome, which exhibits triclosan resistance. The resistance is attributed to an extrapolated loop in the protein structure that prevents triclosan from accessing the active site.
full_output.methodology: The study involved purification and biochemical analysis of the FabL2 protein, as well as structural modeling and molecular dynamics simulations to understand the mechanism of triclosan resistance.

full_output.paper_title: cis- and trans-Acting Factors Influence Expression of the norM-Encoded Efflux Pump of Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Levels of Gonococcal Susceptibility to Substrate Antimicrobials.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies norM as a gene encoding an efflux pump that contributes to resistance against ciprofloxacin, solithromycin, berberine, and ethidium bromide in Neisseria gonorrhoeae. The expression of norM is regulated by cis- and trans-acting factors, including a poly(T) tract in the promoter and a TetR-like regulator.
full_output.methodology: Mutant construction, MIC testing, qRT-PCR, and promoter analysis were used to investigate the role of norM in antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of a Cefazolin Inoculum Effect Associated with blaZ Gene Types among Methicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus Isolates from Four Major Medical Centers in Chicago.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the blaZ gene, encoding a beta-lactamase, was associated with a cefazolin inoculum effect (CInE) in methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) isolates. The prevalence of a pronounced CInE was low, and the blaZ gene types A, B, C, and D were identified, with type C being the most prevalent.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR and sequencing to analyze the blaZ gene in MSSA isolates and determined cefazolin MICs using broth microdilution.

full_output.paper_title: Deinococcus radiodurans HD-Pnk, a Nucleic Acid End-Healing Enzyme, Abets Resistance to Killing by Ionizing Radiation and Mitomycin C.
full_output.key_findings: Deinococcus radiodurans HD-Pnk is a bifunctional end-healing enzyme that contributes to resistance against ionizing radiation and mitomycin C. Mutations in HD-Pnk significantly increase sensitivity to these stressors.
full_output.methodology: Biochemical purification, gene knockout, and complementation experiments were conducted to analyze HD-Pnk's role in DNA repair and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcus aureus targets the purine salvage pathway to kill phagocytes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SLC29A1, ADK, and DCK as critical genes involved in deoxyadenosine (dAdo)-mediated macrophage cell death. Mutations in these genes confer resistance to dAdo intoxication by disrupting the purine salvage pathway.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR-Cas9 knockout screens, sequencing, and biochemical assays were used to identify and validate the role of SLC29A1, ADK, and DCK in dAdo-mediated macrophage cell death.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring the role of unnatural amino acids in antimicrobial peptides.
full_output.key_findings: The study explores the role of unnatural amino acids in enhancing the stability and antimicrobial activity of synthetic peptides, demonstrating their effectiveness against various bacterial strains.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the design, synthesis, and evaluation of three nine-residue antimicrobial peptides with unnatural amino acids, assessing their antimicrobial activity and stability in serum.

full_output.methodology: Structural biology techniques, functional studies, and genetic analyses were employed to characterize the role of MacB, MacA, and TolC in antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Immunomodulation of Host Chitinase 3-Like 1 During a Mammary Pathogenic Escherichia coli Infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the role of chitinase 3-like 1 (CHI3L1) in the innate immune response during Escherichia coli infection of the mammary gland. It shows that CHI3L1 is expressed in infected mammary tissue and is involved in regulating immune cell infiltration and cytokine production.
full_output.methodology: The study used a murine intramammary infection model, Western blotting, RT-qPCR, and histological analysis to examine CHI3L1 expression and its effects on immune responses during E. coli infection.

full_output.paper_title: Indolyl Azaspiroketal Mannich Bases Are Potent Antimycobacterial Agents with Selective Membrane Permeabilizing Effects and in Vivo Activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several indolyl azaspiroketal Mannich bases, including 1, 10-16, as potent antimycobacterial agents with submicromolar activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv and Mycobacterium bovis BCG. These compounds show selective membrane permeabilizing effects and in vivo activity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized turbidity measurements, membrane permeability assays, and in vivo experiments in a mouse model of tuberculosis to evaluate the antimycobacterial activity of the synthesized compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Reassessing the Role of Type II Toxin-Antitoxin Systems in Formation of Escherichia coli Type II Persister Cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that deletion of 10 type II TA systems does not affect persistence to antibiotics in E. coli, contradicting previous assumptions about their role in persister cell formation.
full_output.methodology: The study used independently constructed strains, fluorescent reporters, and microfluidic experiments to assess the role of TA systems in persistence.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Insight into Symbiosis-Induced Insect Color Change by a Facultative Bacterial Endosymbiont, "Candidatus Rickettsiella viridis".

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology of Staphylococcus aureus in neonates on admission to a Chinese neonatal intensive care unit.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the molecular epidemiology of Staphylococcus aureus in neonates admitted to a Chinese neonatal intensive care unit, highlighting the prevalence of methicillin-susceptible (MSSA) and methicillin-resistant (MRSA) strains, with specific clones such as ST188 and ST59 being predominant. The sasX gene was not detected in any isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study involved molecular typing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and cytotoxicity assays of S. aureus isolates from neonates.

full_output.paper_title: RHS-elements function as type II toxin-antitoxin modules that regulate intra-macrophage replication of Salmonella Typhimurium.
full_output.key_findings: RHS elements function as type II toxin-antitoxin modules that regulate Salmonella Typhimurium proliferation within macrophages. The Rhs-CT main and Rhs-CT orphan toxins are expressed intracellularly and repress bacterial growth, while their corresponding antitoxins, RhsI main and RhsI orphan, neutralize the toxic effects.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative real-time PCR, transcriptional fusion assays, toxicity assays, co-immunoprecipitation, Western blot, and macrophage infection experiments.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the efficacy of β-lactam antibiotics, including Ampicillin, Augmentin, Unasyn, and Tazocin, in treating Bacillus anthracis meningitis in a rabbit model. It found that Ampicillin and Augmentin were highly effective, while Tazocin was ineffective. The study also highlighted the importance of optimizing antibiotic dosages and BBB penetration for successful treatment.
full_output.methodology: The study used a rabbit central nervous system infection model to evaluate the efficacy of various β-lactam antibiotics against Bacillus anthracis. It involved administering different antibiotic doses and assessing survival rates and time to death.

full_output.paper_title: Species and drug susceptibility profiles of staphylococci isolated from healthy children in Eastern Uganda.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes including mecA, vanA, vanB, aac(6')-Ie-aph(2'')-Ia, ant(4')-Ia, and aph(3')-IIIa in staphylococci isolated from healthy children in Eastern Uganda. These genes were associated with resistance to methicillin, vancomycin, and aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and assess resistance profiles in staphylococci isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial activity of Ib-M peptides against Escherichia coli O157: H7.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of Ib-M peptides against Escherichia coli O157: H7, demonstrating that Ib-M1 and Ib-M2 exhibited the highest inhibitory effects, with minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) ranging from 1.6 to 12.5 μM. All peptides showed bactericidal activity, with Ib-M4 being the least effective.
full_output.methodology: The study used microdilution methods to determine MIC and MBC, along with time-kill kinetics and cytotoxicity assays to evaluate the antimicrobial efficacy and safety of Ib-M peptides against E. coli O157: H7.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the triclosan resistance gene fabI and the chlorhexidine resistance gene qacA on the pC02 plasmid in Staphylococcus aureus, demonstrating that subinhibitory concentrations of antiseptics can reduce the fitness cost of carrying this plasmid.
full_output.methodology: Macrobroth and microbroth dilution assays were used to measure antimicrobial susceptibility, and competitive fitness assays were performed to evaluate the impact of pC02 on bacterial growth.

full_output.paper_title: Extended-Spectrum β-lactamase-Producing Enterobacteriaceae Shedding in Farm Horses Versus Hospitalized Horses: Prevalence and Risk Factors.

full_output.paper_title: A comparative genomic analysis between methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus strains of hospital acquired and community infections in Yunnan province of China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified three major MRSA clones in Yunnan province, China: ST239-t030, ST59-t437, and ST6-t701. ST239-t030 was primarily associated with hospital-acquired infections, while ST59-t437 and ST6-t701 were linked to community-acquired infections. The study also highlighted differences in antibiotic resistance profiles among these clones.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing and comparative genomic analysis of 60 MRSA isolates from patients and food sources in Yunnan province, China.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular diversity and profile analysis of virulence-associated genes in some Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several virulence genes in multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, including AcrAB, tolC, OmpK35, entB, irP-1, and others, highlighting their potential roles in virulence and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Whole Genome Sequencing of Escherichia coli From Store-Bought Produce.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antimicrobial resistance genes in tetracycline-resistant E. coli strains from store-bought produce, highlighting the prevalence of multidrug resistance and the role of plasmids and integrons in the spread of resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Should we leave the paper currency? A microbiological examination.

full_output.paper_title: Dominant resistance and negative epistasis can limit the co-selection of de novo resistance mutations and antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Cannabidiol is an effective helper compound in combination with bacitracin to kill Gram-positive bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: CBD potentiates the effect of bacitracin against Gram-positive bacteria, reducing MIC values and demonstrating synergistic effects. The combination affects cell division and autolysis, with down-regulation of ezrA and up-regulation of lytM and lytN.
full_output.methodology: MIC determination, growth experiments, time-kill assays, TEM, fluorescence microscopy, qPCR, and autolysis assays.

full_output.paper_title: Microbial and Viral Communities and Their Antibiotic Resistance Genes Throughout a Hospital Wastewater Treatment System.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 264 unique antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in a hospital wastewater treatment system, including genes conferring resistance to critically important antibiotics such as carbapenems, cephalosporins, and fluoroquinolones. ARGs were detected throughout the system with minimal reduction in abundance during treatment.
full_output.methodology: Shotgun metagenomics and bioinformatic analysis of bacterial and viral communities in hospital wastewater samples.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative Proteomics of Extended-Spectrum Cephalosporin-Resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae Isolates Demonstrates Altered Protein Synthesis, Metabolism, Substance Transport, and Membrane Permeability.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified differential protein expression in extended-spectrum cephalosporin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates, highlighting the role of mtrR in resistance mechanisms through efflux pump regulation.
full_output.methodology: Comparative iTRAQ quantitative proteomics was used to analyze differential protein expression in three ESC-resistant N. gonorrhoeae isolates compared to the reference strain ATCC49226.

full_output.paper_title: Cultivation of Bacteria From Aplysina aerophoba: Effects of Oxygen and Nutrient Gradients.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on cultivating bacteria from the marine sponge Aplysina aerophoba using various media formulations and cultivation methods, highlighting the effects of oxygen and nutrient gradients on microbial diversity.
full_output.methodology: The research involved creating nine media formulations based on genomic predictions, using Liquid-Solid cultivation and Winogradsky columns, along with 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing to analyze microbial diversity.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characterization of Staphylococcus aureus Plasmids Associated With Strains Isolated From Various Retail Meats.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 26 rep families in S. aureus plasmids from retail meats, highlighting the diversity and association of these plasmids with antimicrobial resistance and meat sources.
full_output.methodology: PCR analysis of rep genes and plasmid isolation techniques were used to characterize S. aureus plasmids.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity of berberine chloride (BBR) and vancomycin (VAN) against Clostridioides difficile strains, showing that BBR reduces the MIC of VAN for ten strains and affects biofilm formation and motility.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution to determine MIC and MBC values, evaluated biofilm formation using crystal violet staining, and assessed motility on soft agar plates.

full_output.key_findings: The study presents an automated sputum-to-genotype system for detecting multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It successfully identified drug-resistant mutations in katG (S315T), inhA (-15T), and rpoB (S531W) using PCR and hybridization techniques.
full_output.methodology: The system uses MagVor for sample lysis, TruTip for DNA purification, and Lab-on-a-Film for amplification and hybridization. Mutations were detected via PCR and hybridization.

full_output.paper_title: The Pyrazolo[3,4-d]pyrimidine Derivative, SCO-201, Reverses Multidrug Resistance Mediated by ABCG2/BCRP.
full_output.key_findings: SCO-201 reverses multidrug resistance mediated by ABCG2/BCRP by inhibiting its efflux pump activity.
full_output.methodology: Cell viability assays, dye efflux assays, ATPase assays, molecular docking simulations.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance and virulence patterns of pathogenic Escherichia coli strains associated with acute gastroenteritis among children in Qatar.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M-G1, bla CTX-M-3, bla CTX-M-15, bla TEM, and bla SHV as the main genes responsible for extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) production in EPEC and EAEC strains isolated from children with acute gastroenteritis in Qatar.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect and characterize ESBL genes in EPEC and EAEC isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies phylogenetically informative mutations in 92 genes associated with antibiotic resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, highlighting both neutral and resistance-conferring mutations, including loss-of-function mutations in mmpL5 leading to hyper-susceptibility to bedaquiline and clofazimine, and frameshift mutations in ald and cycA contributing to intrinsic resistance to cycloserine.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) testing were used to analyze mutations in 92 genes implicated in antibiotic resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex.

full_output.paper_title: Insights into the improved macrolide inhibitory activity from the high-resolution cryo-EM structure of dirithromycin bound to the E. coli 70S ribosome.
full_output.key_findings: Dirithromycin (DIR) is a more potent inhibitor of in vitro protein synthesis compared to erythromycin (ERY). The enhanced inhibitory activity of DIR is likely due to its side chain pointing into the lumen of the nascent peptide exit tunnel (NPET), where it can interfere with the normal passage of the growing polypeptide chain.
full_output.methodology: High-resolution cryo-EM structure of DIR bound to the E. coli 70S ribosome, competition-binding assay, and in vitro translation analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Suppression of antibiotic resistance evolution by single-gene deletion.

arcA.mechanism: regulation of aerobic respiration and metabolic shifts

gutM.encodes: DNA-binding transcription factor that regulates genes related to glucitol utilization

full_output.key_findings: Deletion of arcA and gutM significantly suppressed antibiotic resistance evolution in E. coli, suggesting their roles in metabolic regulation and stress resistance.
full_output.methodology: Systematic laboratory evolution of single-gene deletion strains under different antibiotics, followed by IC50 measurements and statistical analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characteristics of the first case of haloxyfop-resistant Poa annua.
