full_output.paper_title: Co-occurrence of antibiotic, biocide, and heavy metal resistance genes in bacteria from metal and radionuclide contaminated soils at the Savannah River Site.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes and metal resistance genes (MRGs) in soil samples from the Savannah River Site, highlighting the co-occurrence of resistance mechanisms against antibiotics, biocides, and heavy metals. Key AMR genes included emrB, cusS, mdtB, vanR, rosA, macB, mfpA, aah (2')-I, bacA, and others, while MRGs such as corR, copR, ricR, pstB, arsT, and others were also detected.
full_output.methodology: The study employed 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing, metagenomic analysis, and bioinformatics tools to identify and characterize AMR and MRG genes in soil samples from different contaminated sites.
geographic_location: Savannah River Site, South Carolina, USA

full_output.paper_title: Exogenous maltose enhances Zebrafish immunity to levofloxacin-resistant Vibrio alginolyticus.

cpxA.evidence_note: The paper mentions that cpxA is one of five genes with point mutations in Lev-R V. alginolyticus, but does not explicitly state that these mutations confer resistance to levofloxacin.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in several genes, including gyrB, which is associated with fluoroquinolone resistance in Levofloxacin-resistant Vibrio alginolyticus. Other genes like AT730_01475, aceF, cpxP, and cpxA also show mutations linked to resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and qPCR were used to analyze mutations and gene expression in Levofloxacin-resistant and sensitive strains of Vibrio alginolyticus.

full_output.paper_title: Simultaneous detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex and resistance to Rifampicin and Isoniazid by MDR/MTB ELITe MGB® Kit for the diagnosis of tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The MDR/MTB ELITe MGB® Kit successfully detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex and resistance to Rifampicin and Isoniazid through analysis of mutations in the rpoB, katG, and inhA genes.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the performance of the MDR/MTB ELITe MGB® Kit using melting temperature analysis for detecting mutations in the rpoB, katG, and inhA genes associated with Rifampicin and Isoniazid resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and Characterization of Two Klebsiella pneumoniae Phages Encoding Divergent Depolymerases.
full_output.key_findings: Two new K. pneumoniae phages, πVLC5 and πVLC6, were isolated and characterized. These phages encode divergent depolymerases that enable them to infect various capsular types of K. pneumoniae. Phage πVLC6 was found to have a second, divergent depolymerase contributing to its extended tropism.
full_output.methodology: Phages were isolated from environmental samples, characterized through genome sequencing, and tested for their host range and depolymerase activity.

full_output.paper_title: Genotyping, Assessment of Virulence and Antibacterial Resistance of the Rostov Strain of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Attributed to the Central Asia Outbreak Clade.

mutations_found.validated_by: genomic analysis and drug susceptibility testing

full_output.paper_title: Fluoroquinolone Metalloantibiotics: A Promising Approach against Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antimicrobial activity of metalloantibiotics formed by fluoroquinolones (FQs) complexed with copper and phenanthroline against multidrug-resistant (MDR) clinical isolates, particularly methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Metalloantibiotics showed improved activity against MRSA compared to pure FQs, with synergistic effects observed when combined with ciprofloxacin and ampicillin. The mechanism of action was found to be similar to that of FQs, involving inhibition of DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity was assessed using broth microdilution, disk diffusion, and checkerboard methods. Enzymatic inhibitory assays and atomic force microscopy (AFM) were employed to investigate the mechanism of action.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the Antibacterial Activity and Efflux Pump Reversal of Thymol and Carvacrol against Staphylococcus aureus and Their Toxicity in Drosophila melanogaster.
full_output.key_findings: Thymol and carvacrol showed antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus IS-58, but did not inhibit the TetK efflux pump. They exhibited toxicity towards Drosophila melanogaster.
full_output.methodology: Broth microdilution method for MIC determination, efflux pump inhibition assays, and Drosophila toxicity tests.

full_output.paper_title: Novel enterocin E20c purified from Enterococcus hirae 20c synergised with ß-lactams and ciprofloxacin against Salmonella enterica.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel bacteriocin, enterocin E20c, which exhibits strong antimicrobial activity against multidrug-resistant Salmonella enterica and enhances the efficacy of antibiotics such as ampicillin, penicillin, ceftriaxone, and ciprofloxacin through synergistic interactions.
full_output.methodology: Purification and characterization of E20c, antimicrobial activity assays, physico-chemical analysis, hemolytic activity assessment, MIC determination, time-kill assays, and checkerboard titrations.

full_output.paper_title: Prospects of Indole derivatives as methyl transfer inhibitors: antimicrobial resistance managers.

organisms_tested_in: Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ZINC04899565 and ZINC49171024 as potential broad-spectrum antimicrobial agents targeting multiple methyl transfer enzymes, including MetK, CobA, Dam, and TrmD, which are crucial for bacterial survival and resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Computational strategies including molecular docking and ADMET screening were used to evaluate the potential of indole derivatives as inhibitors of methyl transfer enzymes.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of fexA in Mediating Resistance to Florfenicols in Campylobacter.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies fexA as a novel mobile florfenicol resistance gene in Campylobacter jejuni, demonstrating that its acquisition increases resistance to florfenicol, while its inactivation reduces resistance.
full_output.methodology: Functional cloning, MIC testing, whole-genome sequencing, and molecular techniques were used to validate the role of fexA in florfenicol resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Clinically Relevant Epithelial Lining Fluid Concentrations of Meropenem with Ciprofloxacin Provide Synergistic Killing and Resistance Suppression of Hypermutable Pseudomonas aeruginosa in a Dynamic Biofilm Model.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that combination therapy with meropenem and ciprofloxacin provides synergistic bacterial killing and suppresses resistance emergence in hypermutable Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains in a dynamic biofilm model.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a dynamic in vitro CDC biofilm reactor (CBR) model to evaluate the antibacterial effects of meropenem and ciprofloxacin, both individually and in combination, against hypermutable P. aeruginosa strains.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro and In Vivo Antibiotic Capacity of Two Host Defense Peptides.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of two host defense peptides, Pin2[G] and FA1, against various bacterial pathogens, including S. aureus, P. aeruginosa, and S. Typhimurium. Pin2[G] showed higher effectiveness in reducing bacterial loads in both in vitro and in vivo models, while FA1 exhibited limited antimicrobial activity.
full_output.methodology: The study assessed antimicrobial activity through MIC testing, in vivo infection models in rabbits and mice, and evaluated immunomodulatory effects using cell cultures.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative Genomic Analysis of Third-Generation-Cephalosporin-Resistant Escherichia coli Harboring the blaCMY-2-Positive IncI1 Group, IncB/O/K/Z, and IncC Plasmids Isolated from Healthy Broilers in Japan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaCMY-2 as the primary gene responsible for third-generation cephalosporin resistance in Escherichia coli isolates from healthy broilers in Japan, highlighting its prevalence and the role of specific plasmid types in its dissemination.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, plasmid analysis, and comparative genomic analysis were used to characterize the AMR genes and plasmids in the E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance genes in raw milk for human consumption.

full_output.key_findings: This study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in raw milk samples, including genes encoding efflux pumps, beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside modifying enzymes, and others. full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis of raw milk samples followed by bioinformatics tools to identify and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Intracellular Staphylococcus aureus persisters upon antibiotic exposure.

full_output.methodology: The study uses RNA-sequencing, fluorescence dilution-based methods, and quantitative RT-PCR to analyze the transcriptomic and phenotypic characteristics of intracellular S. aureus persisters.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypes, antibacterial-resistant profile, and virulence-associated genes of Salmonella serovars isolated from retail chicken meat in Egypt.

full_output.methodology: Uniplex PCR for virulence genes and disk diffusion for antibiotic susceptibility testing.
full_output.sample_size: 200 chicken meat samples and 25 stool specimens

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes and mutations in E. coli isolates from European starlings, including β-lactamases like bla AmpC-CIT, bla CTX-M, and bla TEM, as well as quinolone resistance genes such as emrA, emrB, mdtM, qacH, and qnrB10. Mutations in gyrA and parC were also found to confer quinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR-based characterization, in silico analysis, and whole genome sequencing to identify AMR genes and mutations in E. coli isolates from European starlings.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and statistical analysis of SNPs in 1,170 M. tuberculosis isolates, along with experimental validation of promoter activity.

The resistance level depends on the specific β-lactam, with the highest protection observed against PBP3-targeting β-lactams like cefaclor and cephalexin.

full_output.paper_title: Insights into idarubicin antimicrobial activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: Idarubicin exhibits potent bactericidal activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and persister cells, with synergistic effects when combined with fosfomycin. It disrupts the cell membrane and interacts with DNA topoisomerase IIA subunits GyrA and GyrB, leading to effective biofilm inhibition and eradication.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility tests, time-kill assays, biofilm inhibition and eradication assays, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vivo mouse models were used to evaluate the antimicrobial activity of idarubicin.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of FDA-approved antivirulence drugs targeting the Pseudomonas aeruginosa quorum sensing effector protein PqsE.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies nitrofurazone and erythromycin estolate as inhibitors of the PqsE quorum sensing effector protein in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, reducing virulence traits such as pyocyanin production and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening of FDA-approved drugs using a PqsE-Rep biosensor strain to identify inhibitors of PqsE activity.

full_output.paper_title: Defining the oral microbiome by whole-genome sequencing and resistome analysis: the complexity of the healthy picture.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the resistome of the healthy oral microbiome, identifying several resistance genes including mefA, ermB, tetB, aac1, SHV, QnrD, and msrA, which confer resistance to macrolides, tetracyclines, aminoglycosides, beta-lactams, and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and qPCR microarray analysis were used to characterize the oral microbiome and its resistome.

full_output.paper_title: Repeated disinfectant use in broiler houses and pig nursery units does not affect disinfectant and antibiotic susceptibility in Escherichia coli field isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that repeated disinfectant use in agricultural settings does not lead to increased antibiotic resistance in E. coli isolates. High levels of resistance to certain antibiotics were observed, but no association was found between disinfectant use and antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed E. coli isolates from broiler houses and pig nursery units for susceptibility to disinfectants and antibiotics through microbiological testing and statistical analysis.
full_output.sample_size: 67 E. coli isolates from broiler houses and 183 from pig nursery units

full_output.paper_title: Multi-drug resistant and extended-spectrum β-lactamases producing bacterial uropathogens among pregnant women in Northwest Ethiopia.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that K. aerogenes bloodstream infections were associated with poorer clinical outcomes compared to Ecc BSI. Antibiotic resistance was more prevalent in Ecc lineage 1, which had a higher rate of multidrug-resistant phenotype.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro Antibiotic Susceptibility, Virulence Genes Distribution and Biofilm Production of Staphylococcus aureus Isolates from Bovine Mastitis in the Liaoning Province of China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Staphylococcus aureus isolates from bovine mastitis in the Liaoning Province of China that showed resistance to multiple antibiotics, including sulfamethoxazole, penicillin, daptomycin, oxacillin, and clindamycin. The predominant spa type was t267, which exhibited high antimicrobial resistance and harbored several virulence genes.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, spa typing, and PCR-based detection of virulence genes were performed.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of Resistance Mechanisms in Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several carbapenemase genes (bla OXA-48-like, bla NDM, bla IMP, bla VIM, and bla KPC) and porin genes (ompK35 and ompK36) as key resistance mechanisms in carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence characterization of Klebsiella pneumoniae and its relation with ESBL and AmpC beta-lactamase associated resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Microevolution in the major outer membrane protein OmpA of Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies five major ompA variant groups (V1-V5) in Acinetobacter baumannii, highlighting the microevolutionary divergence of the OmpA protein, which plays a role in virulence, antibiotic resistance, and host-cell interactions. full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and multilocus sequence typing were used to explore the microevolution of the ompA gene in Acinetobacter baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Association of intestinal colonization of ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae in poultry slaughterhouse workers with occupational exposure-A German pilot study.

full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect ESBL genes in E. coli isolates from fecal samples of slaughterhouse workers.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Antimicrobial Evaluation of Novel Schiff Bases Derived from Triazole Derivatives
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis of novel Schiff bases derived from triazole derivatives and evaluates their antibacterial activity against various Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. full_output.paper_title: Potent, specific MEPicides for treatment of zoonotic staphylococci.

full_output.paper_title: Structural and functional evidence of bacterial antiphage protection by Thoeris defense system via NAD(+) degradation.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance patterns in human, animal, food and environmental isolates in Ghana: a review.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights high antibiotic resistance rates in various bacterial isolates in Ghana, particularly in Escherichia coli, Klebsiella spp., and Pseudomonas spp. It identifies significant regional disparities in research and emphasizes the need for improved surveillance and quality research.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review of literature from PubMed and Google Scholar focusing on antibiotic resistance in Ghana.

full_output.paper_title: Whole Genome and Transcriptome Sequencing of Two Multi-Drug Resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis Strains to Facilitate Illustrating Their Virulence in vivo.

full_output.paper_title: An integrated biophysical approach to discovering mechanisms of NDM-1 inhibition for several thiol-containing drugs.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the inhibition mechanisms of thiol-containing compounds against NDM-1, a metallo-beta-lactamase, using various biophysical techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial activity of Xenorhabdus and Photorhabdus isolated from entomopathogenic nematodes against antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: Xenorhabdus and Photorhabdus isolates showed antibacterial activity against antibiotic-resistant bacteria, particularly against S. aureus strains. Some isolates, such as P. luminescens subsp. akhurstii bSBR36.2_TH, exhibited broad-spectrum inhibition.
full_output.methodology: Isolation and identification of Xenorhabdus and Photorhabdus from entomopathogenic nematodes, followed by evaluation of their antibacterial activity through disk diffusion, MIC, MBC, and time-killing assays.

full_output.paper_title: 1,2,3-Triazolylmethaneboronate: A Structure Activity Relationship Study of a Class of β-Lactamase Inhibitors against Acinetobacter baumannii Cephalosporinase.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ADC-7 as a β-lactamase from Acinetobacter baumannii and characterizes a series of α-triazolylmethaneboronic acid inhibitors that effectively inhibit ADC-7, thereby restoring the activity of ceftazidime against bacteria expressing this enzyme.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of inhibitors, determination of binding affinities, and evaluation of MICs against bacterial strains expressing ADC-7.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibitor design to target a unique feature in the folate pocket of Staphylococcus aureus dihydrofolate reductase.
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on designing inhibitors targeting the folate pocket of Staphylococcus aureus dihydrofolate reductase (SaDHFR) to enhance enzyme inhibition and whole-cell growth suppression. Key findings include the identification of optimal modifications at the chiral center and distal positions of the dihydrophthalazine ring that improve inhibitor potency and binding affinity.
full_output.methodology: The research involved chemical synthesis, enzymatic inhibition assays, and structural analysis through X-ray crystallography to evaluate the efficacy of novel inhibitors against SaDHFR.

full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the management of initial colonizations with Burkholderia species in cystic fibrosis patients, focusing on treatment strategies and outcomes. The study highlights the challenges in treating Burkholderia infections due to their multidrug resistance and the need for further research.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of data from five French cystic fibrosis centers, including microbiological and clinical data from patients with initial Burkholderia colonizations.

full_output.paper_title: Association among biofilm formation, virulence gene expression, and antibiotic resistance in Proteus mirabilis isolates from diarrhetic animals in Northeast China.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative Target Analysis of Chlorinated Biphenyl Antimicrobials Highlights MenG as a Molecular Target of Triclocarban.

full_output.paper_title: Mode of action of teixobactins in cellular membranes.

full_output.paper_title: Population genomics of Staphylococcus pseudintermedius in companion animals in the United States.

full_output.paper_title: Therapeutic potential of a designed CSαβ peptide ID13 in Staphylococcus aureus-induced endometritis of mice.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of Microbiota Transplant on Resistome of Gut Microbiota in Gnotobiotic Piglets and Human Subjects.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative Genome Analyses of Wild Type- and Quinolone Resistant Escherichia coli Indicate Dissemination of QREC in the Norwegian Broiler Breeding Pyramid.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation, characterization, and comparative genomic analysis of a phage infecting high-level aminoglycoside-resistant (HLAR) Enterococcus faecalis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the class D β-lactamases from Bacillus, specifically BSU-2 and BAT-2, have low catalytic activity due to an elongated loop1. Deleting three amino acid residues (RLT) in this loop significantly enhances their activity against ampicillin and ticarcillin.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mcr-1 and mcr-2 as genes responsible for colistin resistance by modifying lipid A, and shows that combining colistin with antimicrobial peptides can overcome this resistance.
full_output.methodology: In vitro MIC assays and combinatorial experiments with antimicrobial peptides and colistin.

full_output.paper_title: Haemophilus influenzae HP1 Bacteriophage Encodes a Lytic Cassette with a Pinholin and a Signal-Arrest-Release Endolysin.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the HP1 bacteriophage's lytic cassette, identifying the hol and lys genes as encoding a pinholin and a signal-arrest-release (SAR) endolysin, respectively. The hol gene product was shown to be a transmembrane protein with C-out, N-in topology, and the lys gene product was identified as an SAR-endolysin with lysozyme activity.
full_output.methodology: In silico analysis, molecular cloning, and experimental validation through protein expression and functional assays in E. coli and H. influenzae.

full_output.paper_title: Whole Genome Sequencing Analysis of Porcine Faecal Commensal Escherichia coli Carrying Class 1 Integrons from Sows and Their Offspring.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in porcine faecal commensal E. coli, including blaTEM-1, strA, strB, tetA, dfrA12, aadA1, aadA2, cmlA, aph(3')-Ia, sul2, and sul3, which confer resistance to beta-lactams, streptomycin, tetracyclines, trimethoprim, aminoglycosides, chloramphenicol, neomycin, kanamycin, and sulfonamides.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing of 117 intI1+ E. coli isolates from sows and piglets.

full_output.paper_title: Proteomic Characterization of Antibiotic Resistance, and Production of Antimicrobial and Virulence Factors in Streptococcus Species Associated with Bovine Mastitis. Could Enzybiotics Represent Novel Therapeutic Agents Against These Pathogens?

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various AMR genes and proteins involved in antibiotic resistance in Streptococcus species associated with bovine mastitis, highlighting the importance of proteomic analysis for understanding resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Proteomic analysis using LC–ESI–MS/MS to identify AMR genes and proteins in Streptococcus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genotype distribution of methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus clinical isolates in Iran: high multiresistant clonal complex 8.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various clonal complexes and spa types among MSSA isolates, highlighting the high genetic diversity and the prevalence of CC8-MSSA. It also found that mupirocin-resistant strains belonged to CC8-MSSA, and determined the presence of virulence genes such as pvl and tst.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR for virulence genes, and molecular typing methods including agr and spa typing.

full_output.paper_title: Cetylpyridinium Chloride: Mechanism of Action, Antimicrobial Efficacy in Biofilms, and Potential Risks of Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the potential for resistance development towards cetylpyridinium chloride (CPC) in various bacterial species, highlighting the mechanisms such as cell surface alterations and efflux pumps. It also mentions cross-resistance to other antimicrobials.
full_output.methodology: Review of existing literature on CPC's mechanism of action, antimicrobial efficacy, and resistance development.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Activities of Eravacycline and Other Antimicrobial Agents against Human Mycoplasmas and Ureaplasmas.

M. genitalium.notes: Multiple point mutations in an efflux ABC transporter suggest a potential new mechanism of tetracycline resistance in M. genitalium that also affects eravacycline.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of eravacycline against various Mycoplasma and Ureaplasma species, revealing that eravacycline was highly effective, especially against isolates resistant to other antimicrobials. A unique resistance mechanism involving an efflux ABC transporter was identified in M. genitalium.
full_output.methodology: In vitro susceptibility testing using broth microdilution technique according to CLSI guidelines.
full_output.sample_size: 10 Mycoplasma genitalium, 40 Mycoplasma hominis, 44 Mycoplasma pneumoniae, 20 Ureaplasma parvum, and 20 Ureaplasma urealyticum isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the macrolide resistance gene erm(X), tetracycline resistance genes tet(O) and tet(W), and characterized unique mutations in a nitroreductase gene associated with metronidazole resistance in Mobiluncus isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and Etest for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Activity of Omadacycline, a New Tetracycline Analog, and Comparators against Clostridioides difficile.
full_output.key_findings: Omadacycline showed potent in vitro activity against Clostridioides difficile isolates, with no significant differences in MIC values based on ribotype, disease severity, or vancomycin susceptibility. The study identified the presence of tetA(P) and tetB(P) resistance genes in one isolate, but these did not affect omadacycline MIC.
full_output.methodology: Broth microdilution, whole-genome sequencing, and time-kill assays were used to evaluate the in vitro activity of omadacycline and other antibiotics against C. difficile isolates.

mcr-1.validation_method: expression in E. coli and demonstration of colistin resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the mcr-1 gene, when expressed in Escherichia coli, confers resistance to colistin and modulates the inflammatory response of human macrophages.
full_output.methodology: Cloning and expression of the mcr-1 gene in E. coli, assessment of colistin resistance, and evaluation of inflammatory responses in macrophages.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Profiling Reveals Distinct Routes To Complement Resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies rfaH, lpp, and arnD as shared serum resistance factors in four diverse serum-resistant K. pneumoniae strains. These genes contribute to complement resistance through mechanisms involving capsule production and lipid A modification.
full_output.methodology: Functional genomic profiling using transposon-directed insertion site sequencing (TraDIS) and deletion mutant analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Innate Effector Systems in Primary Human Macrophages Sensitize Multidrug-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae to Antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that activation of innate effector systems, such as antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), reactive oxygen species (ROS), and autophagy, can sensitize multidrug-resistant (MDR) Klebsiella pneumoniae to conventional antibiotics. Compounds like vitamin D3, PBA, and HO53 were shown to enhance the antibacterial effects of antibiotics against MDR K. pneumoniae in a primary human macrophage model.
full_output.methodology: The study used primary human macrophages and tested the effects of vitamin D3, PBA, and HO53 in combination with antibiotics. It included CFU assays, qRT-PCR, and siRNA transfection experiments to investigate the mechanisms involved.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes OXA-23 and OXA-58 carbapenemase-producing Proteus mirabilis isolates from human and animal sources, revealing a single lineage carrying these genes on chromosomes or plasmids, highlighting their potential as a hidden reservoir of carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, sequencing, and bioinformatics tools were used to identify and characterize the AMR genes and mutations in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: A nutrient-limited screen unmasks rifabutin hyperactivity for extensively drug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that the wild-type fhuE gene contributes to rifabutin sensitivity in Acinetobacter baumannii, highlighting its role in the mechanism of action of rifabutin under nutrient-limited conditions.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a nutrient-limited screening approach, along with genetic manipulation and whole-genome sequencing, to investigate the mechanism of rifabutin's enhanced activity against drug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Hospital-environment strains overlapping with patient isolates are globally disseminated and enriched for multidrug resistance
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes and mutations in hospital environmental strains, highlighting their global dissemination and enrichment for multidrug resistance. Key findings include the presence of mecA, qacA, qacC, aac3-IIa, fosA, fosA2, mcr1, arr, ant6-Ia, sat4A, aph3-III, strA, strB, sulII, aadD, aac6-Aph2, far1, and blaZ, which confer resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study uses metagenomic sequencing, plasmid analysis, and comparative genomics to characterize AMR genes and their distribution in hospital environments.

full_output.paper_title: A novel colistin adjuvant identified by virtual screening for ArnT inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies BBN149, a natural diterpenoid, as a potential colistin adjuvant that potentiates colistin activity against colistin-resistant P. aeruginosa and K. pneumoniae by inhibiting the ArnT enzyme involved in lipid A aminoarabinosylation.
full_output.methodology: In silico virtual screening, molecular docking, and in vitro assays including MIC determination, growth inhibition, and lipid A analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanistic Insights Into the Differential Efficacy of Daptomycin Plus β-Lactam Combinations Against Daptomycin-Resistant Enterococcus faecium.

full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro and in vivo models, including BOC-FL labeling of PBPs and gene expression analysis, to investigate the role of pbp5 in daptomycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic diversity, antimicrobial resistance, and virulence genes of thermophilic Campylobacter isolated from broiler production chain.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several virulence genes in thermophilic Campylobacter isolates from broiler production chains, including cadF, ciaB, cdtA, cdtB, cdtC, flaA, dnaJ, flhA, racR, pldA, and wlaN. These genes are associated with adhesion, invasion, toxin production, and other virulence mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Pathogenic spectrum of blood stream infections and resistance pattern in Gram-negative bacteria from Aljouf region of Saudi Arabia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Gram-negative bacteria, particularly Klebsiella pneumoniae and Acinetobacter baumannii, dominate bloodstream infections in the Aljouf region of Saudi Arabia, with high levels of resistance to multiple antibiotics including carbapenems, cephalosporins, and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed culture and susceptibility reports of blood samples from hospitalized patients to determine the pathogenic spectrum and resistance patterns of Gram-negative bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the bacterial ocular surface microbiome in ophthalmologically normal dogs prior to and following treatment with topical neomycin-polymyxin-bacitracin.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized the bacterial ocular surface microbiome of healthy dogs and examined the effects of topical neomycin-polymyxin-bacitracin treatment on microbial communities, finding no significant changes in alpha or beta diversity over time.
full_output.methodology: 16S rRNA gene sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the ocular surface microbiome of dogs before and after antibiotic treatment.

full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the high resistance rates of uropathogens such as Escherichia coli, Klebsiella spp., and Enterococcus spp. to various antibiotics, including levofloxacin, amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, and others, emphasizing the need for targeted antimicrobial strategies.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of urine samples from 7719 patients to determine antimicrobial resistance rates using disk diffusion techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Spill-Over from Public Health? First Detection of an OXA-48-Producing Escherichia coli in a German Pig Farm.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first detection of an OXA-48-producing E. coli isolate in a German pig farm, highlighting the potential for carbapenem resistance to spill over from human to animal reservoirs.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic resistance testing, whole-genome sequencing, and molecular characterization were performed to identify and analyze the OXA-48-producing E. coli isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance Is Associated with Integrative and Conjugative Elements and Genomic Islands in Naturally Circulating Streptococcus pneumoniae Isolates from Adults in Liverpool, UK.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies tetracycline and macrolide resistance genes, including tet(M), erm(B), tet(32), mef(A), and msr(D), located on mobile genetic elements in naturally circulating Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatic analysis were used to characterize resistance genes and mobile genetic elements in S. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of clinical enterococci isolates, focusing on the vancomycin-resistant enterococci in a tertiary hospital in China: based on the data from 2013 to 2018.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified vanA and vanM genes as the primary determinants of vancomycin resistance in vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) isolates from a tertiary hospital in China. vanA was the most prevalent gene, while vanM was also detected, with some isolates carrying both genes.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 3913 enterococci isolates, with 60 VRE isolates further analyzed using PCR, DNA sequencing, and MLST.

full_output.paper_title: Structural analysis of avibactam-mediated activation of the bla and mec divergons in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: Avibactam up-regulates the expression of blaZ and pbp2a in S. aureus SF8300, indicating its role in activating the bla and mec divergons.
full_output.methodology: X-ray crystallography and qRT-PCR analysis of gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: BacEffluxPred: A two-tier system to predict and categorize bacterial efflux mediated antibiotic resistance proteins.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents BacEffluxPred, a computational tool designed to predict and classify bacterial efflux proteins responsible for antibiotic resistance. It uses a two-tier support vector machine (SVM) approach to identify antibiotic resistance efflux (ARE) proteins and predict their families.
full_output.methodology: The study employed a two-tier SVM-based approach, utilizing PSSM profiles from PSI-BLAST searches and cross-validation techniques to develop and evaluate the predictive models.

full_output.paper_title: Host dependent maintenance of a bla(NDM-1)-encoding plasmid in clinical Escherichia coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome sequence analysis of environmental Escherichia coli from the faeces of straw-necked ibis (Threskiornis spinicollis) nesting on inland wetlands.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance of Neisseria Gonorrhoeae in a Newly Implemented Surveillance Program in Uganda: Surveillance Report.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights high levels of antimicrobial resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae in Uganda, with over 90% resistance to ciprofloxacin, tetracycline, and penicillin, and 2.1% reduced azithromycin sensitivity. It underscores the urgent need for improved surveillance and antimicrobial stewardship to combat the rising threat of multidrug-resistant gonorrhea.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted antimicrobial susceptibility testing using disk diffusion and Etest methods on Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates collected from men with urethral discharge syndrome in Uganda.

full_output.paper_title: Frequency of genomic mutations mediating resistance of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates to rifampicin in Northern Morocco.

full_output.paper_title: Dual RNA-seq provides novel insight into the roles of dksA from Pseudomonas plecoglossicida in pathogen-host interactions with large yellow croakers ( Larimichthys crocea).

full_output.key_findings: The study describes the first complete sequence of a multiple drug-resistant IncHI2 ST4 plasmid, pTZ41_1P, from a commensal E. coli in Australia. The plasmid carries genes conferring resistance to heavy metals, beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, and sulfonamides.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and genomic analysis were used to characterize the plasmid and its resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization, antibiotic resistance pattern and capsular types of invasive Streptococcus pneumoniae isolated from clinical samples in Tehran, Iran.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the impact of adjuvant lung resection on nontuberculous mycobacterial pulmonary disease (NTM-PD) and identifies factors associated with refractory and recurrent cases. full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of clinical data, surgical outcomes, and antibody levels in NTM-PD patients undergoing adjuvant lung resection.

full_output.paper_title: A silent outbreak of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium in a neonatal intensive care unit.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a silent outbreak of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VRE-fm) in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). All isolates showed high-level resistance to vancomycin, and the vanA gene was detected in all isolates, while the vanB gene was absent.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and sequencing for detection of vanA and vanB genes, along with molecular genotyping using BOX-PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical and bacteriological profile of diabetic foot infections in a tertiary care.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus, and Bacteroides species as the most common pathogens causing diabetic foot infections, with varying levels of antibiotic resistance. Vancomycin, Imipenem, and Amikacin were found to be effective against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Prospective analysis of DFI samples collected from 2016 to 2018, with microbiological culturing and antibiotic susceptibility testing performed according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: A Physiological Basis for Nonheritable Antibiotic Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study explores the physiological basis for nonheritable antibiotic resistance, focusing on mechanisms such as toxin-antitoxin (TA) modules, ATP levels, and the stringent response. full_output.methodology: The research involved experimental analysis of bacterial growth, gene expression, and antibiotic susceptibility, alongside review of existing literature on antibiotic resistance mechanisms.

full_output.key_findings: The leader peptide peTrpL increases resistance to tetracycline, erythromycin, chloramphenicol, and the flavonoid genistein by forming antibiotic-dependent ribonucleoprotein complexes that regulate the smeR mRNA, which encodes the repressor of the multidrug efflux pump SmeAB.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptome sequencing, coimmunoprecipitation, qRT-PCR, and growth inhibition assays.

full_output.paper_title: Novel Biogenic Silver Nanoparticle-Induced Reactive Oxygen Species Inhibit the Biofilm Formation and Virulence Activities of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) Strain.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that biogenic silver nanoparticles (D-SNPs) and silver nitrate (AgNO3) inhibit the growth of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and other pathogenic bacteria, likely through the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and disruption of cellular functions.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar well diffusion assays, minimum inhibition concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) tests, and TEM microscopy to evaluate the antibacterial effects of D-SNPs and AgNO3 against MRSA and other bacteria.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized 16S rRNA and gyrB gene sequencing, MLSA, WGS, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to characterize Nocardia isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes and mutations associated with drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including katG, inhA, rpoB, embB, pncA, rpsL, rrs, gyrA, thyA, and folC, which are linked to resistance against isoniazid, ethambutol, rifampicin, streptomycin, aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, and para-aminosalicylic acid.

full_output.paper_title: Surface sensing triggers a broad-spectrum antimicrobial response in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies rhamnolipids, pyochelin, pyoverdin, and AQNOs as key antimicrobial agents produced by a Δ wspF mutant of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, contributing to the killing of Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: Metabolomic analysis and genetic manipulation of Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains to evaluate antimicrobial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Influence of analysis conditions for antimicrobial susceptibility test data on susceptibility rates.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates how different parameters in antimicrobial susceptibility testing affect susceptibility rates, focusing on Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli, and Klebsiella pneumoniae. It highlights the impact of duplicate isolate removal periods and data collection periods on susceptibility rates, showing that longer removal periods reduce the number of isolates and alter susceptibility rates, particularly for β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed antimicrobial susceptibility test data from isolates collected over five and a half years, using software to calculate susceptibility rates under varying conditions of duplicate isolate removal and data collection periods.

full_output.paper_title: Development of small-molecule inhibitors of fatty acyl-AMP and fatty acyl-CoA ligases in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 11-phenoxyundecanoyl-AMS (compound 32) as a potent inhibitor of FAAL28 with high biochemical selectivity over FACL19, showing significant antitubercular activity against M. tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and evaluation of acyl-AMS analogs for their inhibitory activity against FAD enzymes and whole-cell antitubercular activity.

full_output.paper_title: The PK/PD Integration and Resistance of Tilmicosin against Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae.

23S rRNA.notes: An acquired A2058G transition in region V was found only in the resistant M. hyopneumoniae strains (M3, M4).

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the A2058G mutation in the 23S rRNA gene of M. hyopneumoniae strains M3 and M4, which conferred resistance to tilmicosin, tylosin, erythromycin, and lincomycin.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro dynamic models, MIC determination, time-killing curves, and sequencing analyses to investigate the PK/PD relationship and resistance mechanisms of tilmicosin against M. hyopneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical Findings and Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Anaerobic Bacteria Isolated in Bloodstream Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports high resistance rates to clindamycin and moxifloxacin among anaerobic bacteria, particularly Bacteroides spp., while resistance to imipenem and amoxicillin-clavulanic acid was low.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the gradient diffusion method (Etest) against several antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic and Phenotypic Resistance to Clarithromycin in Helicobacter pylori Strains.

23S rRNA.notes: Mutations in the 23S rRNA gene are associated with clarithromycin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that all clarithromycin-resistant Helicobacter pylori strains had either the 2146A>G or 2147A>G mutation in the 23S rRNA gene, indicating that testing for these mutations could predict clarithromycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) testing were used to analyze the 23S rRNA gene mutations and their association with clarithromycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Selected Antibiotic Resistance Genes in Two Different Wastewater Treatment Plant Systems in Poland: A Preliminary Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of tetracycline resistance genes (tet(B), tet(K), tet(L), tet(O)) and the sulfonamide resistance gene sulIII in wastewater treatment plant samples. These genes were detected in both raw influent and final effluent samples, indicating their persistence through the treatment process.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative PCR (qPCR) was used to detect and quantify selected antibiotic resistance genes in wastewater samples from two different treatment plants.

full_output.paper_title: Chalcones Isolated from Arrabidaea brachypoda Flowers as Inhibitors of NorA and MepA Multidrug Efflux Pumps of Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: Chalcone 4 was identified as an efflux pump inhibitor (EPI) targeting NorA and MepA efflux pumps in Staphylococcus aureus, enhancing the efficacy of Norfloxacin against strains overexpressing these pumps.
full_output.methodology: Microdilution assays, molecular docking, and MIC testing were used to evaluate the antimicrobial activity and efflux pump inhibition potential of chalcones.

full_output.key_findings: Melectin, an antimicrobial peptide derived from bee venom, exhibits broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against both gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria, including drug-resistant strains, with low cytotoxicity and no hemolytic activity. full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of melectin through MIC measurements, cytotoxicity assays, hemolytic activity tests, time-kill kinetics, liposome aggregation experiments, and mechanisms of action involving membrane permeabilization and depolarization.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the resistance mechanisms of Gram-positive bacteria to various antibiotics, including β-lactams, glycopeptides, fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides, and others. It highlights the importance of understanding these mechanisms to develop new treatments and overcome resistance.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing literature and provides detailed information on the resistance mechanisms of Gram-positive bacteria, focusing on specific genes and mutations associated with resistance.

full_output.paper_title: First report of plasmid-mediated colistin resistance mcr-8.1 gene from a clinical Klebsiella pneumoniae isolate from Lebanon.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first occurrence of the mcr-8.1 gene in a clinical Klebsiella pneumoniae isolate from Lebanon, highlighting the emergence of plasmid-mediated colistin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, plasmid typing, conjugation assays, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Sex dependent effects of post-natal penicillin on brain, behavior and immune regulation are prevented by concurrent probiotic treatment.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that post-natal penicillin exposure leads to long-term changes in social behavior in male mice, along with changes in gene expression related to social behavior and the blood-brain barrier. Probiotic treatment with L. rhamnosus JB-1 prevents these effects.
full_output.methodology: Behavioral tests, qRT-PCR, flow cytometry, and microbiome sequencing were used to analyze the effects of penicillin and probiotic treatment on mice.

full_output.paper_title: Lytic Activity of Polyvalent Staphylococcal Bacteriophage PhiSA012 and Its Endolysin Lys-PhiSA012 Against Antibiotic-Resistant Staphylococcal Clinical Isolates From Canine Skin Infection Sites.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the lytic activity of bacteriophage phiSA012 and its endolysin Lys-phiSA012 against antibiotic-resistant staphylococcal isolates from canine skin infections. It found that Lys-phiSA012 showed significant lytic activity against multidrug-resistant (MDR) S. pseudintermedius and S. schleiferi, while phiSA012 had limited lytic activity against MDR S. pseudintermedius isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, spot testing, and turbidity reduction assays were used to assess the lytic activity of phiSA012 and Lys-phiSA012 against staphylococcal isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial potential of Forsythia suspensa polysaccharide against resistant Enterobacter cloacae with SHV-12 extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL).
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that Forsythia suspensa polysaccharide (FSP) exhibits potent antibacterial activity against Enterobacter cloacae producing SHV-12 ESBL by inhibiting SHV-12 ESBL gene expression.
full_output.methodology: Isolation and purification of polysaccharide, qRT-PCR, and antibacterial assays.

full_output.paper_title: A study of Rose Bengal against a 2-keto-3-deoxy-d-manno-octulosonate cytidylyltransferase as an antibiotic candidate.
full_output.key_findings: Rose Bengal was identified as an inhibitor of three KdsB enzymes (Bp KdsB, Bt KdsB, and Pa KdsB) with promising IC50 values and increased thermostability.
full_output.methodology: Enzymatic assays, malachite green assay, and computational docking were used to evaluate the inhibitory effects of Rose Bengal on KdsB enzymes.

full_output.paper_title: Agricultural Injury-Associated Chromobacterium violaceum Infection in a Bangladeshi Farmer.
full_output.key_findings: The case describes a successful treatment of a Chromobacterium violaceum infection in a Bangladeshi farmer, highlighting the importance of considering C. violaceum in the differential diagnosis of wound infections in tropical regions.
full_output.methodology: Bacteriological investigation, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic characterization of Salmonella Uzaramo for human invasive infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first case of Salmonella Uzaramo causing invasive infection in China, highlighting its potential virulence factors such as typhoid toxin and tcf fimbriae, and notes low antimicrobial resistance potential except for a lake-water isolate.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and Caenorhabditis elegans killing assay were used to analyze the isolates.
full_output.sample_size: Two S. Uzaramo isolates (U301 and U302)

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the performance of PlasmidSPAdes in detecting ESBL-encoding genes and plasmid replicons in Enterobacteriaceae, identifying several beta-lactamase genes and plasmid replicon families.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis using PlasmidSPAdes and other tools.

full_output.paper_title: A 10-year single-center experience on Stenotrophomonas maltophilia resistotyping in Szeged, Hungary.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the resistance profiles of 817 Stenotrophomonas maltophilia isolates, highlighting high resistance rates to amikacin (72.5%) and varying susceptibility to other antibiotics, with sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim being the first-line treatment.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing using E-tests and broth microdilution methods.

full_output.paper_title: Xpert Mycobacterium tuberculosis/Rifampicin-Detected Rifampicin Resistance is a Suboptimal Surrogate for Multidrug-resistant Tuberculosis in Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo: Diagnostic and Clinical Implications.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified rpoB S531L and katG S315T1 mutations as the most frequent causes of rifampicin and isoniazid resistance, respectively, in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized MTBDR plus assay for detection of drug resistance mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Reservoirs of antimicrobial resistance genes in retail raw milk.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in retail raw milk, including bla CMY-2, aph (3')-Ib, aph (6)-Id, bla TEM-1B, mdf(A), catA2, sul2, tet(B), and dfrA14, which confer resistance to various antibiotics. These genes were found in E. coli and other bacteria, and some were transferable between species.
full_output.methodology: The study used 16S rRNA gene sequencing, metagenomic sequencing, and conjugation assays to analyze the microbiome and resistome of retail milk samples.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and susceptibility to antibiotics from Campylobacter jejuni and Campylobacter coli isolated from chicken meat in southern Benin, West Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 32.8% of chicken thigh samples were contaminated with Campylobacter, with 72.7% of the strains resistant to ciprofloxacin, 71.4% to ampicillin and tetracycline, and 55.8% being multidrug-resistant.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted bacteriological culture, PCR-based identification, and antibiotic susceptibility testing of Campylobacter isolates from chicken meat samples.

full_output.paper_title: The Conjugation Window in an Escherichia coli K-12 Strain with an IncFII Plasmid.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the IncFII plasmid pUUH239.2 carrying the bla gene, which confers resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics in E. coli K-12.
full_output.methodology: Experiments involved conjugation studies, cloning, and susceptibility testing of E. coli strains with the IncFII plasmid.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes novel synthetic peptide inhibitors that bind to and inhibit NDM-1, a metallo-beta-lactamase responsible for carbapenem resistance in Enterobacteriaceae. These peptides enhance the effectiveness of meropenem against NDM-1-producing bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a cell-based high-throughput antimicrobial discovery system called SLAY to screen for peptides that potentiate carbapenem-dependent killing of NDM-1-expressing E. coli. Validated peptides were chemically synthesized and tested for their ability to inhibit NDM-1 activity and restore carbapenem susceptibility.

full_output.key_findings: KanJ is a kanamycin B dioxygenase that catalyzes the oxidative deamination of kanamycin B to 2'-oxo-kanamycin B, with structural insights into its substrate recognition and catalytic mechanism.
full_output.methodology: Structural modeling, ITC binding assays, HPLC activity tests, and computational analysis of reaction mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: A novel incompatibility group X3 plasmid carrying bla(NDM-1) encodes a small RNA that regulates host fucose metabolism and biofilm formation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel plasmid-transcribed small RNA, IGR plas2, which regulates fucose metabolism and biofilm formation in E. coli. The plasmid pNDM-HN380 carries the blaNDM-1 gene, which confers resistance to carbapenems and cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: RNA sequencing, Northern blot, and biofilm assays were used to characterize the role of IGR plas2 in fucose metabolism and biofilm formation.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the antibacterial and antifungal properties of Anacardium species, particularly A. occidentale, A. microcarpum, and A. humile, highlighting their potential as sources of natural antimicrobial agents.
full_output.methodology: The study involved in vitro antibacterial and antifungal assays using various extracts and compounds derived from Anacardium species.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance, Virulence Genes, and Biofilm Formation Capacity Among Enterococcus species From Yaks in Aba Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes in Enterococcus species isolated from yaks, including ermA, ermB, tetA, tetB, tetM, tetL, cat, optrA, and poxtA. These genes conferred resistance to various antibiotics such as erythromycin, tetracycline, chloramphenicol, and linezolid. Additionally, a high prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Enterococcus strains was observed.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PCR and sequencing to detect AMR genes, along with antimicrobial sensitivity testing and biofilm formation assays.

full_output.paper_title: Determining the Genetic Characteristics of Resistance and Virulence of the "Epidermidis Cluster Group" Through Pan-Genome Analysis.

aadD2.evidence_note: The aadD2 gene was cloned and functionally evaluated, showing increased MIC levels to tobramycin and kanamycin.

full_output.key_findings: Two resistance genes, aadD2 and blaZ, were identified in S. caprae SY333 and experimentally validated for their roles in conferring resistance to aminoglycosides and beta-lactams, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, molecular cloning, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize resistance genes in the Epidermidis Cluster Group.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamases (ESBL) Producing Enterobacteriaceae from Fish Trapped in the Lagoon Area of Bizerte, Tunisia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several β-lactamase genes (bla CTX-M-1, bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-9, bla OXA-1, and bla TEM-1-a) and other resistance genes (sul1, sul2, tetA, aac(6')-Ib-cr, qnrA, and qnrB) in ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae isolated from fish in the Bizerte lagoon, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant bacteria in aquatic environments.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to characterize antibiotic resistance genes in ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae isolated from fish samples.

full_output.paper_title: Guide-free Cas9 from pathogenic Campylobacter jejuni bacteria causes severe damage to DNA.

CjeCas9.validation_method: Western blot, fluorescence microscopy, BLESS analysis

full_output.key_findings: CjeCas9, a nuclease from Campylobacter jejuni, causes severe DNA damage in human cells through nonspecific DNA cleavage, leading to cell death.
full_output.methodology: Experimental validation through Western blot, fluorescence microscopy, BLESS analysis, and in vitro cleavage assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that ridinilazole treatment preserves secondary bile acids and maintains a bile acid profile associated with a lower risk of Clostridioides difficile infection recurrence compared to vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: The study used a longitudinal design to compare the effects of ridinilazole and vancomycin on intestinal bile acid profiles in patients with C. difficile infection, utilizing targeted and untargeted LC-MS analyses.

full_output.paper_title: Vancomycin C-Terminus Guanidine Modifications and Further Insights into an Added Mechanism of Action Imparted by a Peripheral Structural Modification.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies G3-CBP-vancomycin and CBP-vancomycin as novel glycopeptide antibiotics with enhanced antimicrobial activity against vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium and Staphylococcus aureus. These compounds exhibit two synergistic mechanisms of action, one of which is independent of D-Ala-D-Ala binding and cell wall biosynthesis inhibition.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity was determined via microdilution assays, and the mechanisms of action were analyzed through permeability assays and resistance development studies.

full_output.paper_title: Potential of MurA Enzyme and GBAP in Fsr Quorum Sensing System as Antibacterial Drugs Target: In vitro and In silico Study of Antibacterial Compounds from Myrmecodia pendans.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that compounds from Myrmecodia pendans exhibit antibacterial and anti-quorum sensing (QS) activity by inhibiting the MurA enzyme and GBAP. Specifically, compound 2 showed strong binding affinity towards gelatinase and GBAP, suggesting its potential as an anti-QS agent.
full_output.methodology: In silico molecular docking and in vitro antibacterial assays were used to evaluate the activity of compounds from Myrmecodia pendans against MurA, GBAP, gelatinase, and serine protease.

full_output.paper_title: An emerging role for cyclic dinucleotide phosphodiesterase and nanoRNase activities in Mycoplasma bovis: Securing survival in cell culture.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Mbov_0328, Mbov_0327, and Mbov_0276 as critical genes involved in cyclic dinucleotide and nanoRNA degradation, essential for Mycoplasma bovis survival in cell culture conditions.
full_output.methodology: Random transposon mutagenesis, biochemical assays, and complementation studies were used to characterize the roles of these genes in nucleotide recycling and survival.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and molecular characterization of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus with mupirocin, fusidic acid and/or retapamulin resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mupA as the primary gene responsible for high-level mupirocin resistance, and mutations in ileS (N213D and V588F) for low-level mupirocin resistance. Additionally, lsaE was found to contribute to retapamulin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, DNA sequencing, and MIC testing were used to identify resistance genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Biofilm formation, antimicrobial susceptibility and virulence genes of Uropathogenic Escherichia coli isolated from clinical isolates in Uganda.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 62.5% of Uropathogenic E. coli (UPEC) isolates formed biofilms, and 78% of these were multidrug-resistant (MDR). High resistance rates were observed to trimethoprim-sulphamethoxazole (93%) and amoxicillin (93%), with the lowest resistance to imipenem (0.5%). The most prevalent virulence genes were fimH (53.5%), pap (21%), sfa (13%), afa (8%), and cnf1 (5.5%).
full_output.methodology: The study used the Congo Red Agar method for biofilm detection, Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion for antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and PCR for virulence gene detection.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of tetracycline and streptomycin in beef tissues using Charm II, isolation of relevant resistant bacteria and control their resistance by gamma radiation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several bacterial isolates, including Streptococcus thoraltensis, Escherichia coli, and Proteus mirabilis, that exhibit high resistance to tetracycline and streptomycin. Gamma radiation was found to increase the susceptibility of these resistant strains to the antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study used the Charm II system for detecting antibiotic residues, susceptibility testing via disc diffusion, and determination of minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs). Gamma radiation was applied to assess its effect on bacterial susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Nosocomial infections due to multidrug-resistant bacteria in cancer patients: a six-year retrospective study of an oncology Center in Western China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae (ESBL-PE) as the most prevalent multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens in cancer patients, followed by Acinetobacter baumannii and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia. MDR bacteria showed high sensitivity to meropenem, imipenem, and amikacin.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective observational study analyzing clinical data from cancer patients with nosocomial infections caused by MDR bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiologically characteristics of human brucellosis and antimicrobial susceptibility pattern of Brucella melitensis in Hinggan League of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, China.
full_output.key_findings: All 25 B. melitensis strains were susceptible to doxycycline, tetracycline, gentamicin, ciprofloxacin, ofloxacin, moxifloxacin, and streptomycin. 20% of the strains were resistant to cotrimoxazole, and all 25 strains were resistant to azithromycin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the microdilution method for 25 B. melitensis strains.
geographic_location: Hinggan League, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, China

full_output.key_findings: The study identified Coagulase-negative Staphylococcus (CoNS) as the predominant cause of asymptomatic central line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSI) in children with long-term hemodialysis. It also found that CoNS was significantly associated with right-sided infective endocarditis (IE) in these patients.
full_output.methodology: The study involved analyzing blood cultures, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and echocardiography to identify and characterize CLABSI and its complications in children with long-term hemodialysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a MprF S337L mutation in Staphylococcus argenteus that confers resistance to daptomycin and vancomycin, highlighting the emergence of resistance in this newly recognized staphylococcal species.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify the MprF S337L mutation and its association with resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Prolonged Exposure to β-Lactam Antibiotics Reestablishes Susceptibility of Daptomycin-Nonsusceptible Staphylococcus aureus to Daptomycin.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that prolonged exposure to β-lactam antibiotics can resensitize daptomycin-nonsusceptible Staphylococcus aureus to daptomycin through the accumulation of additional mprF mutations, particularly in the bifunctional domain and synthase domain, and also identifies mutations in the div1b gene associated with increased daptomycin susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, time-kill assays, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to analyze the effects of β-lactam exposure on daptomycin susceptibility in Staphylococcus aureus isolates.
full_output.sample_size: 25 DAP-S/DAP-NS isogenic, clinically derived MRSA bloodstream isolates

full_output.paper_title: Antileishmanial Aminopyrazoles: Studies into Mechanisms and Stability of Experimental Drug Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the development of resistance to aminopyrazoles in Leishmania infantum. While resistance was successfully selected in the promastigote stage, the resistant phenotype was found to be unstable after in vivo passage. Whole-genome sequencing identified several mutations, including a mutation in LinJ.31.1290 (P-glycoprotein e ABCC4) that conferred resistance to DNDI-1044.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, in vitro and in vivo resistance selection, and susceptibility assays were used to investigate resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial and host determinants of cough aerosol culture positivity in patients with drug-resistant versus drug-susceptible tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that drug-resistant tuberculosis patients can still have culturable Mycobacterium tuberculosis in their cough aerosols, and that mycobacterial genomic variants and physiological state were not associated with culturable aerosols.
full_output.methodology: The study used a cross-sectional design with prospective follow-up, involving cough aerosol sampling, sputum microbiology, and whole genome sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Design and synthesis of 4-[4-formyl-3-(2-naphthyl)pyrazol-1-yl]benzoic acid derivatives as potent growth inhibitors of drug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and antimicrobial evaluation of naphthyl-substituted pyrazole-derived hydrazones, which exhibited potent activity against drug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Acinetobacter baumannii, with MIC values as low as 0.78 μg/mL. Some compounds also showed efficacy against biofilm formation and eradication.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of compounds, MIC and MBC assays, time-kill assays, and biofilm inhibition and destruction assays were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Phase-variable capsular polysaccharides and lipoproteins modify bacteriophage susceptibility in Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies phase-variable S-layer proteins, such as BT1927, BT1826, and BT0292, that enhance resistance to multiple bacteriophages in Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron. These proteins are part of a broader mechanism involving capsular polysaccharides (CPS) and other surface structures that help the bacteria evade phage predation.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized bacterial strain engineering, phage isolation, plaque assays, RNA-seq, and mutational analysis to investigate the role of phase-variable features in phage resistance.
full_output.sample_size: 71 phages isolated from two US locations

full_output.key_findings: Zn++ and Cu++ inhibit H. pylori HtrA activity by interacting with specific amino acid residues in the allosteric loop, affecting oligomer stability and proteolytic activity.
full_output.methodology: FRET peptide assay, mutagenesis, thermal shift assay, and Western blot analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Targeted surveillance strategies for efficient detection of novel antibiotic resistance variants.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated targeted sampling strategies for detecting novel antibiotic resistance variants in Neisseria gonorrhoeae, highlighting the importance of genetic diversity and genomic background in improving detection efficiency.
full_output.methodology: The study used computational simulations and analysis of genomic data to assess the effectiveness of different sampling strategies for detecting resistance variants.

full_output.paper_title: Structure-guided design of TrmD inhibitors for mycobacterial infections
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TrmD as an essential target for mycobacterial inhibition and reports the discovery of new inhibitors targeting TrmD, showing activity against various mycobacterial species.
full_output.methodology: Structure-guided fragment-based drug discovery, X-ray crystallography, biochemical assays, and antimicrobial testing.

full_output.paper_title: Neonatal septicemia at intensive care unit, Ayder Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Tigray, North Ethiopia: Bacteriological profile, drug susceptibility pattern, and associated factors.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high rates of antimicrobial resistance among bacterial isolates from neonatal septicemia cases, with Klebsiella pneumoniae showing 100% resistance to several antibiotics, including ampicillin, amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, and ceftazidime. Staphylococcus aureus isolates exhibited 100% resistance to oxacillin, ampicillin, erythromycin, and gentamycin, with 55.6% being methicillin-resistant.
full_output.methodology: The study involved culturing blood samples from neonates with suspected sepsis and performing antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Hybrid Quinoline-Sulfonamide Complexes (M(2+)) Derivatives with Antimicrobial Activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the design, synthesis, and antimicrobial evaluation of hybrid quinoline-sulfonamide complexes (QSC) with potential activity against Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, and Candida albicans. The Cd complex (QBSC 4d) showed the highest antimicrobial activity with notable minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs).
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of QSC compounds via acylation of aminoquinoline and subsequent complexation with metal ions, followed by antimicrobial testing using disk diffusion and broth microdilution methods.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Peptides Display Strong Synergy with Vancomycin Against Vancomycin-Resistant E. faecium, S. aureus, and Wild-Type E. coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that antimicrobial peptides, particularly Bip-P-113, demonstrate strong synergy with vancomycin against vancomycin-resistant E. faecium, S. aureus, and wild-type E. coli. These peptides enhance vancomycin's effectiveness by increasing membrane permeability and reducing LPS release.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized antimicrobial activity assays, checkerboard synergy tests, calcein leakage assays, and LPS neutralization experiments to evaluate the effects of P-113 derivatives.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance of Pasteurella multocida type B isolates associated with acute septicemia in pigs and cattle in Spain.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports high resistance rates to lincomycin in P. multocida type B isolates from pigs and cattle in Spain, with 100% of porcine isolates and 94.4% of bovine isolates resistant. full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility was determined using minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) testing for 10 different antimicrobial agents.

full_output.paper_title: The Neutrally Charged Diarylurea Compound PQ401 Kills Antibiotic-Resistant and Antibiotic-Tolerant Staphylococcus aureus.

full_output.methodology: The study used transduction experiments, PCR, WGS, and an experimental infective endocarditis (IE) model to investigate the role of ϕSA169 in MRSA persistence.

full_output.paper_title: Enhanced Antibacterial Activity of Se Nanoparticles Upon Coating with Recombinant Spider Silk Protein eADF4(κ16).
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that eADF4(κ16)-coated selenium nanoparticles exhibit enhanced antibacterial activity against E. coli compared to PVA-coated nanoparticles, likely due to the positive surface charge provided by eADF4(κ16).
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and characterization of selenium nanoparticles, cytotoxicity tests, and antibacterial activity assays.

full_output.paper_title: The Antimicrobial Activity of Ciprofloxacin-Loaded Niosomes against Ciprofloxacin-Resistant and Biofilm-Forming Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that ciprofloxacin-loaded niosomes can restore ciprofloxacin activity against resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates. Mutations in the quinolone resistance-determining regions of gyrA, grlA, and grlB were detected in some isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect mutations in the quinolone resistance-determining regions of S. aureus isolates.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR and virulence genes in the strains.

full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, conjugation assay, S1-PFGE, and whole-genome sequencing were used to characterize the plasmid and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.methodology: Proteomic profiling, qRT-PCR, and comparative analysis of resistant and susceptible strains.
