full_output.sample_size: Multiple B. pseudomallei strains including Bp1651, MSHR1655, 724644, 1026b, 1631, 6296, and 6788.

full_output.paper_title: Validation of the T86I mutation in the gyrA gene as a highly reliable real time PCR target to detect Fluoroquinolone-resistant Campylobacter jejuni.
full_output.key_findings: The T86I mutation in the gyrA gene was validated as a highly reliable marker for detecting fluoroquinolone resistance in Campylobacter jejuni isolates.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR and sequencing were used to detect the T86I mutation in the gyrA gene and correlate it with fluoroquinolone resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the widespread multidrug resistance in invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella (NTS) infections in sub-Saharan Africa, with resistance to third-generation cephalosporins and fluoroquinolone non-susceptibility also reported. Azithromycin resistance was noted in DR Congo, while no carbapenem resistance was found.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of literature on antimicrobial resistance and treatment in invasive NTS infections.

full_output.paper_title: Increase of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium strain type ST117 CT71 at Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin, 2008 to 2018.

msrC.encodes: Macrolide, Lincosamide and Streptogramin B resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identified an increase in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREfm) strain type ST117 CT71 at Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin from 2008 to 2018. The vanB genotype became predominant in 2018, replacing the earlier vanA genotype. Several resistance genes and virulence factors were detected in ST117 strains, including msrC, erm(B), efmA, dfrF, dfrG, aac(6')-aph(2''), aph(3')-III, ant(6)-Ia, aac(6')-Ii, cat, tet(M), gyrA, parC, pbp5, and vanB.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatic analyses were used to determine MLST, cgMLST, resistance genes, and virulence factors in VREfm isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of indole production increases the activity of quinolone antibiotics against E. coli persisters.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that indole production enhances the formation of E. coli persisters against quinolone antibiotics, particularly ciprofloxacin. Indole pulse signaling, not persistent signaling, is responsible for this effect. Indole interacts with the GyrB subunit of DNA gyrase, inhibiting its ATPase activity and leading to dormancy.
full_output.methodology: The study used persister assays, flow cytometry, and molecular docking to investigate the role of indole in E. coli persister formation and its interaction with DNA gyrase.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of extended-spectrum-β-lactamase producing Klebsiella pneumoniae phage KP1801 and evaluation of therapeutic efficacy in vitro and in vivo.
full_output.key_findings: Phage KP1801 was characterized as having broad lytic activity against ESBL-KP and showed effectiveness in reducing biofilm formation and treating infections in a Galleria mellonella model.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, proteomic analysis, in vitro and in vivo experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of larvicidal potential against larvae of Aedes aegypti (Linnaeus, 1762) and of the antimicrobial activity of essential oil obtained from the leaves of Origanum majorana L.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the larvicidal and antimicrobial activity of Origanum majorana L. essential oil, showing high larvicidal activity against Aedes aegypti larvae and antimicrobial activity against Gram-negative bacteria, but not against Gram-positive bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) for chemical composition analysis, larvicidal activity tests, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Profile of Enterobacteria Resistant to Beta-Lactams.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple beta-lactamase genes, including bla GIM, bla SIM, bla DHA, bla TEM, bla CMY, bla CTX-M, bla NDM, bla OXA, bla IMP, bla SHV, bla SPM, bla KPC, bla VIM, and bla SME, which contribute to resistance against various beta-lactam antibiotics in Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing and real-time PCR were used to identify beta-lactamase genes in Enterobacteriaceae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Indicator Organisms Escherichia coli and Enterococcus spp. Isolated from U.S. Animal Food, 2005-2011.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that E. coli and Enterococcus spp. were commonly present in U.S. animal food products with resistance to several antimicrobials, though at lower rates compared to NARMS retail meat data. No mcr-1 gene was detected in E. coli isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using broth microdilution and PCR screening for the mcr-1 gene.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Activity of Bacteriocinogenic Commensal Escherichia coli against Zoonotic Strains Resistant and Sensitive to Antibiotics.

ColE1.evidence_note: The paper describes ColE1 as a bacteriocin gene, but does not provide evidence that it confers resistance to antibiotics. Instead, it states that ColE1 is involved in bacteriocin production and has antibacterial activity against zoonotic strains.

ColIb.evidence_note: The paper describes ColIb as a colicin gene, part of the bacteriocin production mechanism. The gene was detected in E. coli isolates from humans and tested for bactericidal activity against zoonotic strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various bacteriocin genes, including ColE1, ColE7, ColIa, ColIb, ColK, ColM, MccH47, and MccV, in commensal E. coli strains that exhibit antibacterial activity against zoonotic strains, highlighting their potential in combating antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: PCR and bactericidal activity testing were used to identify and characterize bacteriocin genes in commensal E. coli strains.

full_output.paper_title: The rapid and visual detection of methicillin-susceptible and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus using multiplex loop-mediated isothermal amplification linked to a nanoparticle-based lateral flow biosensor.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a multiplex LAMP-LFB technique targeting the femA and mecA genes for rapid and visual detection of S. aureus and MRSA. The method demonstrated high specificity and sensitivity, capable of detecting 100 fg of genomic DNA within 80 minutes.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) combined with a nanoparticle-based lateral flow biosensor (LFB) was used for detection and identification of S. aureus and MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular analysis of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates from four teaching hospitals in Iran: the emergence of novel MRSA clones.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 24 MRSA isolates with the mecA gene, which confers resistance to methicillin. Various SCC mec types were found, with SCC mec type V being the most prevalent. Additionally, MSCRAMMs genes such as eno, fib, cna, and fnbB were prevalent among the MRSA isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR and MLST were used to identify MRSA strains and their genetic characteristics.

full_output.paper_title: AbGRI4, a novel antibiotic resistance island in multiply antibiotic-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii clinical isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel antibiotic resistance island, AbGRI4, in multiply antibiotic-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii clinical isolates. AbGRI4 contains a class 1 integron with aadB, aadA2, and sul1 genes, conferring resistance to aminoglycosides and sulfonamides.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and BLAST-based analysis were used to identify and characterize the novel resistance island AbGRI4 in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Optimization of 4-Substituted Benzenesulfonamide Scaffold To Reverse Acinetobacter baumannii Serum-Adaptive Efflux Associated Antibiotic Tolerance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and optimizes benzenesulfonamide-based compounds that reverse serum-adaptive efflux-mediated antibiotic tolerance in Acinetobacter baumannii, particularly enhancing the effectiveness of minocycline and tigecycline.
full_output.methodology: Structure-activity relationship (SAR) studies, ethidium bromide efflux assays, and membrane depolarization assays were used to evaluate the compounds' ability to inhibit efflux pumps and enhance antibiotic efficacy.

full_output.paper_title: Enterotoxigenic Bacteroides fragilis induces the stemness in colorectal cancer via upregulating histone demethylase JMJD2B.

full_output.key_findings: The review highlights the increasing resistance of Escherichia coli to levofloxacin (LVX) in Iran, particularly in the western regions, with resistance rates ranging from 0% to 66.7% depending on the study and sample type.
full_output.methodology: Narrative review of published studies on E. coli resistance to LVX in Iran.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence factors analysis and antibiotic resistance of uropathogenic Escherichia coli isolated from patients in northeast of Iran.

full_output.paper_title: Generation of High Dose Inhalable Effervescent Dispersions against Pseudomonas aeruginosa Biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed inhalable effervescent particles combining ciprofloxacin (CFX) and tartaric acid (TA) to enhance efficacy against Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms. The hybrid particles showed improved antimicrobial activity compared to CFX alone.

full_output.paper_title: Escherichia coli ST8196 is a novel, locally evolved, and extensively drug resistant pathogenic lineage within the ST131 clonal complex.

full_output.paper_title: Targeting ESKAPE pathogens with anti-infective medicinal plants from the Greater Mpigi region in Uganda.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified medicinal plant extracts from the Greater Mpigi region in Uganda that exhibit growth inhibition against multidrug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens and quorum-sensing inhibition activity against Staphylococcus aureus. Specific plant extracts showed potent antimicrobial and antivirulence effects, highlighting their potential as sources of novel anti-infective agents.

Adjusting pH and temperature can enhance mecillinam's stability.
full_output.methodology: The study employed a 'delay-time bioassay' and Raman spectroscopy to assess antibiotic degradation in bacterial growth media.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that obligate cross-feeding slowed the rate of antibiotic resistance evolution in both E. coli and S. enterica. The model suggested that interdependency is sufficient to alter the rate and mechanisms of resistance evolution.

mmpL7.encodes: inner membrane protein associated with phthiocerol dimycocerosate (PDIM) transport to the MOM
mmpL7.mechanism: transport of PDIMs to the mycobacterial outer membrane (MOM)
mmpL7.validation_method: mutant analysis in NHP and mouse models

mmpL2.encodes: putative inner membrane transporter protein with unknown substrate

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Mtb genes, particularly mmpL7, involved in regulating the formation of inducible bronchus-associated lymphoid tissue (iBALT) during tuberculosis. The mmpL7 mutant shows reduced inflammation and increased iBALT formation, potentially through altered lipid profiles and cytokine production.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis in NHP and mouse models, lipid profiling, and cytokine analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Susceptibility, Clonality, and Molecular Characterization of Carbapenem-Resistant Clinical Isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii from Washington DC.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla OXA-51-like, bla OXA-23-like, and bla VIM genes as contributors to carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from Washington DC.
full_output.methodology: PCR and PFGE were used to analyze antibiotic resistance genes and clonality.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance Profile and Biofilm Production of Microorganisms Isolated from Oropharynx of Rupornis magnirostris (Gmelin, 1788) and Caracara plancus (Miller, 1777).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antimicrobial resistance profiles and biofilm production in microorganisms isolated from the oropharynx of Rupornis magnirostris and Caracara plancus. It found methicillin-resistant and vancomycin-resistant coagulase-positive staphylococci (MR-CoPS, VR-CoPS), extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae (ESBL), and KPC-producing bacteria. Additionally, certain yeast species showed resistance to antifungals.
full_output.methodology: Microbial isolation, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and biofilm production assessment via Congo red agar and crystal violet staining methods.

full_output.paper_title: Structural definition of polyspecific compensatory ligand recognition by P-glycoprotein.

full_output.paper_title: Lipid A profiling and metabolomics analysis of paired polymyxin-susceptible and -resistant MDR Klebsiella pneumoniae clinical isolates from the same patients before and after colistin treatment.

mgrB.notes: Inactivation of mgrB is a mechanism of polymyxin resistance in K. pneumoniae.

phoQ.notes: Intragenic suppressor mutation in phoQ contributes to polymyxin resistance in K. pneumoniae.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mgrB inactivation and a phoQ intragenic suppressor mutation as mechanisms of polymyxin resistance in MDR K. pneumoniae clinical isolates.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and metabolomics to investigate lipid A modifications and metabolic changes associated with polymyxin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic analysis of methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus clinical isolates: High prevalence of multidrug-resistant ST239 with strong biofilm-production ability.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high prevalence of multidrug-resistant ST239 isolates with strong biofilm-producing ability. Key AMR genes included mupA, fusC, erm(A), erm(C), ant(4')-Ia, aac(6')-Ie/aph(2''), aph(3')-IIIa, tetM, and tetK.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR-based detection of resistance and virulence genes, biofilm formation assessment, and molecular typing methods.

full_output.paper_title: Synthetic-Bioinformatic Natural Product Antibiotics with Diverse Modes of Action.

farR.notes: Mutations in farR contribute to resistance against SyCPA 116

mutations_found.validated_by: Whole genome sequencing of resistant mutants

clpP.notes: Deletion of clpP provides resistance to SyCPA 116

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the discovery of nine new syn-BNP cyclic peptide antibiotics (SyCPAs) with diverse mechanisms of action, including cell lysis, membrane depolarization, inhibition of cell wall biosynthesis, and ClpP protease dysregulation. These antibiotics show activity against ESKAPE pathogens and Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and resistance development was not observed in laboratory experiments.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a synthetic-bioinformatic approach involving bioinformatics, chemical synthesis, and various biochemical assays to evaluate the antimicrobial activity and mechanisms of action of the synthesized peptides.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the genomic diversity of the Saccharibacteria phylum, revealing ultra-small, parasitic bacteria with reduced genomes that are prevalent in human and mammalian hosts. It identifies novel genomic groups (G3, G5, G6) and provides insights into their adaptation to mammalian environments.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of Saccharibacteria strains from human and environmental sources, including metagenomic sequencing and phylogenetic comparisons.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular detection and genetic characteristics of Babesia gibsoni in dogs in Shaanxi Province, China.

cytb.notes: The M121I mutation in the cytb gene was associated with atovaquone resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified Babesia gibsoni as the sole species causing canine babesiosis in Xi'an and Hanzhong, Shaanxi Province, China. A mutation (M121I) in the cytb gene was associated with atovaquone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Molecular detection and genetic analysis of Babesia spp. in dog blood samples and ticks.

full_output.paper_title: Physiological evidence that three known mutations in the para-sodium channel gene confer cypermethrin knockdown resistance in Rhipicephalus microplus.
full_output.key_findings: The study provides physiological evidence that the G184C, C190A, and T2134A mutations in the para-sodium channel gene of Rhipicephalus microplus are associated with cypermethrin knockdown resistance.
full_output.methodology: Videometric analysis of ovary contraction in response to cypermethrin exposure.

full_output.paper_title: A Race against Time: Reduced Azithromycin Susceptibility in Salmonella enterica Serovar Typhi in Pakistan.

acrB.notes: The R717Q mutation in acrB is associated with increased azithromycin MIC.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports an azithromycin resistance-associated mutation in the acrB gene of a Salmonella Typhi isolate from Pakistan, highlighting concerns about the potential spread of azithromycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed to identify the genetic basis of azithromycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Enterobacterales Infection after Intestinal Dominance in Hospitalized Patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed and validated qPCR assays to measure Enterobacterales abundance in rectal swabs and found that higher Enterobacterales abundance was associated with increased risk of bloodstream infections, especially when exceeding 60%.
full_output.methodology: The study developed and validated qPCR assays to measure Enterobacterales abundance in rectal swabs and compared them with 16S rRNA gene sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Recombinant expression, purification and PEGylation of Paneth cell peptide (cryptdin-2) with value added attributes against Staphylococcus aureus.

mutations_found.validated_by: radial diffusion assay, FACS analysis, MIC testing

E18C.notes: The E18C mutation in cryptdin-2 leads to reduced antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes the recombinant expression, purification, and PEGylation of cryptdin-2, a cationic antimicrobial peptide from Paneth cells, and evaluates its antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus. A mutant (E18C) was also generated and tested. PEGylation reduced antimicrobial activity but improved serum stability and reduced toxicity.
full_output.methodology: Recombinant expression in E. coli, purification via chromatography, PEGylation, and in vitro antimicrobial assays including radial diffusion, MIC, flow cytometry, and SEM.

full_output.paper_title: Cyst infection in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: our experience at Toranomon Hospital and future issues.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the high prevalence of fluoroquinolone-resistant microorganisms in cyst infections of ADPKD patients, suggesting the need to reconsider empirical use of fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective review of ADPKD patients with cyst infections, including analysis of microbial susceptibility to antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that all 3494 GBS isolates were susceptible to cefditoren and vancomycin, but resistance to penicillin, ampicillin, levofloxacin, clindamycin, and erythromycin was observed in 0.2%, 0.1%, 4.6%, 31.2%, and 40.1% of the strains, respectively. High levels of resistance to erythromycin and clindamycin were noted, with most erythromycin-resistant GBS displaying the cMLS B phenotype.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility was determined using the disk diffusion method according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Cefiderocol, a New Siderophore Cephalosporin for the Treatment of Complicated Urinary Tract Infections Caused by Multidrug-Resistant Pathogens: Preclinical and Clinical Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics, Efficacy and Safety.
full_output.key_findings: Cefiderocol shows potent activity against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, including carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii, Burkholderia cepacia, and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia. It is approved for treating complicated urinary tract infections caused by these pathogens, particularly in patients with limited treatment options.
full_output.methodology: Preclinical and clinical studies evaluating the pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, efficacy, and safety of cefiderocol against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.sample_size: Various studies included 9,205 clinical isolates, 448 patients in the APEKS-cUTI trial, and others.

full_output.paper_title: Biofilm formation in Acinetobacter baumannii was inhibited by PAβN while it had no association with antibiotic resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that PAβN inhibited biofilm formation in Acinetobacter baumannii, but there was no clear association between biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance. The efflux pump genes adeB, adeJ, adeG, abeM, and amvA were present but did not show significant differences in expression among different biofilm-forming groups.
full_output.methodology: The study used multiplex PCR, ERIC-2 PCR, and qRT-PCR to analyze biofilm formation and efflux pump gene expression in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Title
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the effects of mutations in the dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) gene in E. coli, focusing on how these mutations influence resistance to trimethoprim and other folate pathway inhibitors.
full_output.methodology: The research involved generating plasmid libraries with single-point mutants of DHFR, performing deep mutational scanning, and analyzing growth rates and enzymatic activity.

full_output.paper_title: An efficient ORF selection system for DNA fragment libraries based on split beta-lactamase complementation.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes an efficient ORF selection system for DNA fragment libraries using split beta-lactamase complementation, enabling the selection of in-frame clones for expression in E. coli.
full_output.methodology: Construction of ORF selection vector, model vectors, western blot analysis, and growth analysis on ampicillin-containing media.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic effects of Cinnamomum cassia L. essential oil in combination with polymyxin B against carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae and Serratia marcescens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla KPC-2 and arnB as resistance genes in carbapenemase-producing K. pneumoniae and S. marcescens, demonstrating their roles in carbapenem and polymyxin resistance, respectively.
full_output.methodology: PCR, MIC testing, RT-qPCR, and time-kill assays were used to validate the resistance mechanisms.
full_output.sample_size: 33 KPC-producing K. pneumoniae and 6 KPC-producing S. marcescens

full_output.paper_title: Sublethal concentrations of undissociated acetic acid may not always stimulate acid resistance in Salmonella enterica sub. enterica serovar Enteritidis Phage Type 4: Implications of challenge substrate associated factors.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the effect of undissociated acetic acid (UAA) on acid resistance of Salmonella Enteritidis Phage Type 4, showing that adaptation to certain pH and UAA concentrations can enhance acid resistance, but this effect is not consistently observed in food matrices like tarama salad.
full_output.methodology: The study used acid adaptation experiments, MIC determination, and inactivation kinetics to assess the effects of UAA and pH on Salmonella Enteritidis survival.

full_output.paper_title: Low iron-induced small RNA BrrF regulates central metabolism and oxidative stress responses in Burkholderia cenocepacia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies BrrF, a small RNA that regulates central metabolism and oxidative stress responses in Burkholderia cenocepacia under iron-depleted conditions. BrrF downregulates genes involved in the TCA cycle and oxidative stress response, such as acnA, fumA, sdhA, sdhC, sodB, and katB.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic manipulation, qPCR, and biochemical assays to characterize BrrF's role in regulating gene expression and metabolic processes under iron-depleted conditions.

full_output.paper_title: Flavonoids isolated from the South African weed Chromolaena odorata (Asteraceae) have pharmacological activity against uropathogens.
full_output.key_findings: Four flavonoid compounds were isolated from Chromolaena odorata and showed antimicrobial activity against uropathogens, with compounds 2 and 3 exhibiting promising results comparable to conventional antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Column chromatography, MIC testing, and structural elucidation via NMR and mass spectrometry.

full_output.paper_title: Stochastic bacterial population dynamics restrict the establishment of antibiotic resistance from single cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that sub-MIC concentrations of antibiotics significantly reduce the probability of establishment of resistant bacterial populations, highlighting the role of stochastic processes in the emergence of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Seeding experiments, MIC assays, and flow cytometry were used to analyze the establishment of resistant bacterial populations under varying antibiotic concentrations.

full_output.paper_title: Specific localisation of ions in bacterial membranes unravels physical mechanism of effective bacteria killing by sanitiser.
full_output.key_findings: The study elucidates the physical mechanism by which cationic surfactants (BAC) and aromatic alcohols (BzA) synergistically enhance bacterial killing, highlighting the role of Ca2+ in protecting bacterial membranes.
full_output.methodology: Combined X-ray reflectivity (XRR) and grazing incidence X-ray fluorescence (GIXF) to analyze membrane structures and ion distribution.

full_output.paper_title: Risk for the development of Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) due to feeding of calves with milk containing residues of antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the risk of antimicrobial resistance development in calves due to feeding with milk containing antibiotic residues, highlighting the role of β-lactamases in reducing β-lactam concentrations.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews existing scientific literature, data from national surveillance programs, and information from questionnaires sent to EU member states.

full_output.paper_title: Cross‑validation of genes potentially associated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy and platinum‑based chemoresistance in epithelial ovarian carcinoma.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified four genes (NFATc1, KLF4, NR4A3, and HGF) potentially associated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy and platinum-based chemoresistance in epithelial ovarian carcinoma.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized microarray data from GEO database and performed differential gene expression analysis, GO and KEGG analyses, and RT-qPCR to validate gene expression levels.

full_output.paper_title: Adipocytes induce the resistance of ovarian cancer to carboplatin through ANGPTL4.
full_output.key_findings: Adipocytes induce resistance of ovarian cancer to carboplatin via ANGPTL4, which activates the c-myc/NF-κB pathway and increases expression of ABC transporters and Bcl-xL.
full_output.methodology: In vivo xenograft models, in vitro co-culture experiments, RT-qPCR, western blot, and immunohistochemistry.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome analyses reveal gene content differences between nontypeable Haemophilus influenzae isolates from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease compared to other clinical phenotypes.

pilA.encodes: Type IV pilin subunit protein PilA

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 79 unique accessory genes significantly associated with COPD strains of nontypeable Haemophilus influenzae, highlighting their potential role in virulence and metabolic functions specific to COPD.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and pan-genome analysis were used to identify genes associated with COPD strains of NTHi.

full_output.paper_title: Evolving MRSA: High-level β-lactam resistance in Staphylococcus aureus is associated with RNA Polymerase alterations and fine tuning of gene expression.

rpoB.mechanism: Mutations in rpoB lead to high-level oxacillin resistance
rpoB.validation_method: Whole genome sequencing and restoration to wild-type rpoB

rpoC.mechanism: Mutations in rpoC lead to high-level oxacillin resistance
rpoC.validation_method: Whole genome sequencing and restoration to wild-type rpoC

full_output.key_findings: High-level β-lactam resistance in Staphylococcus aureus is associated with mutations in rpoB and rpoC, which are responsible for the observed resistance phenotype.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, transduction, and MIC testing were used to validate the role of rpoB and rpoC mutations in high-level oxacillin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified 55 genetic events including nonsynonymous mutations and gene disruptions associated with antimicrobial resistance in Mycoplasma bovis. Key mutations were found in genes encoding ribosomal proteins, methyltransferases, and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, which conferred resistance to various antibiotics such as tetracycline, aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, macrolides, lincosamides, phenicols, and multi-drug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and MIC testing were used to identify and validate antimicrobial resistance-associated mutations in Mycoplasma bovis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The Multidrug Resistance-Reversing Activity of a Novel Antimicrobial Peptide.

ABCB1.validation_method: drug accumulation and efflux assays, ATPase activity analysis

full_output.key_findings: Peptide XH-14C reverses ABCB1-mediated multidrug resistance by inhibiting the efflux function of the ABCB1 transporter, enhancing the intracellular accumulation of paclitaxel and doxorubicin.
full_output.methodology: MTT assay, ATPase activity analysis, molecular docking, drug accumulation and efflux assays, Western blotting, immunofluorescence.

full_output.paper_title: Comprehensive Host Cell-Based Screening Assays for Identification of Anti-Virulence Drugs Targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Salmonella Typhimurium.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies novel compounds with anti-virulence activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Salmonella Typhimurium, including G5 193 and E9 423, which demonstrate cytoprotective effects by targeting the type 3 secretion system (T3SS) and reducing virulence factor production.
full_output.methodology: Host cell-based screening assays were employed to evaluate the anti-virulence effects of small molecules on Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Salmonella Typhimurium, utilizing A549 and J774.2 macrophage cell lines.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of Carbapenem-Resistance Genes in Klebsiella Species Recovered from Selected Environmental Niches in the Eastern Cape Province, South Africa.

blaNDM-1.evidence_note: The paper states that 73 isolates harboured bla NDM-1 and that bla NDM-1 is a carbapenem-resistance gene.

full_output.key_findings: The study detected the presence of carbapenem-resistance genes bla OXA-48-like, bla KPC, and bla NDM-1 in Klebsiella species isolated from various environmental samples in the Eastern Cape Province, South Africa.
full_output.methodology: PCR and phenotypic resistance screening were used to identify and characterize carbapenem-resistance genes in Klebsiella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence, Virulence and Antimicrobial Resistance-Associated Markers in Campylobacter Species Isolated from Retail Fresh Milk and Water Samples in Two District Municipalities in the Eastern Cape Province, South Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antimicrobial resistance genes in Campylobacter species isolated from retail fresh milk and water samples, including catII, tetA, tetB, tetM, ermB, gyrA, ampC, and aac(3)-IIa-(aacC2). These genes were associated with resistance to chloramphenicol, tetracycline, erythromycin, gentamicin, and ampicillin.
full_output.methodology: PCR assay and disk diffusion method were used to detect antimicrobial resistance genes and assess phenotypic resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis, Characterization, and Biologic Activity of New Acyl Hydrazides and 1,3,4-Oxadiazole Derivatives.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on synthesizing new isoniazid derivatives and evaluating their biological activity, including antimicrobial and cytotoxic effects. Compound 9 showed the best antibacterial activity against various bacterial strains, while compounds 7, 8, and 9 exhibited antitumor potential.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized and structurally characterized using spectroscopic techniques. Antimicrobial activity was assessed using broth microdilution and agar disk diffusion methods. Cytotoxicity and cell cycle effects were evaluated using flow cytometry and gene expression analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Monitoring Mycoplasma bovis Diversity and Antimicrobial Susceptibility in Calf Feedlots Undergoing a Respiratory Disease Outbreak.
full_output.key_findings: Mycoplasma bovis isolates were found to be multiresistant to several antimicrobials including oxytetracycline, tilmicosin, and florfenicol, but susceptible to enrofloxacin. Additionally, some isolates showed susceptibility to spectinomycin, differing from previous reports.
full_output.methodology: The study involved sampling and analyzing M. bovis isolates from calf feedlots, determining their antimicrobial susceptibility through MIC assays and genetic subtyping.

full_output.paper_title: Marine Organisms from the Yucatan Peninsula (Mexico) as a Potential Natural Source of Antibacterial Compounds.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antibacterial compounds from marine sponges, including (-)-agelasine B, halitoxins, and amphitoxins, which showed activity against multidrug-resistant pathogens such as Acinetobacter baumannii, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: Bioassay-guided fractionation, NMR spectroscopy, and MIC testing were used to isolate and characterize the active compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Functional Identification and Evolutionary Analysis of Two Novel Plasmids Mediating Quinolone Resistance in Proteus vulgaris.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two novel plasmids, p3M-2A and p3M-2B, which mediate quinolone resistance in Proteus vulgaris. p3M-2B carries the qnrD gene, which confers low-level quinolone resistance. p3M-2A regulates the expression of qnrD in p3M-2B, enhancing quinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid isolation, sequencing, transformation, MIC testing, qRT-PCR, and phylogenetic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Mechanisms, Epidemiology, and Clinical Importance of β-Lactam Resistance in Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses various β-lactamases, including TEM, SHV, CTX-M, KPC, NDM, VIM, IMP, SME, GES, and AmpC enzymes, which confer resistance to β-lactam antibiotics in Enterobacteriaceae. It highlights the molecular mechanisms and epidemiology of these resistance determinants.
full_output.methodology: The paper provides a detailed analysis of β-lactamase families, their genetic origins, and their roles in mediating resistance to β-lactam antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-Resistant Streptococcus agalactiae Strains Found in Human and Fish with High Penicillin and Cefotaxime Non-Susceptibilities.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multidrug-resistant Streptococcus agalactiae strains with high penicillin and cefotaxime non-susceptibilities, highlighting the emergence of MDR and PEN-NS GBS in both human and aquatic environments.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and sequence alignment were used to identify AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: High Antibiotic Resistance of Helicobacter pylori and Its Associated Novel Gene Mutations among the Mongolian Population.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antibiotic resistance in Helicobacter pylori isolates from Mongolia, particularly to amoxicillin, clarithromycin, metronidazole, and levofloxacin. Novel mutations in genes such as pbp1A, 23S rRNA, and gyrA were associated with resistance to these antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to identify resistance mechanisms in H. pylori isolates.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Evaluation of Antimicrobial Peptide Tridecaptin M in Combination with Other Antibiotics against Multidrug Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro potential of tridecaptin M in combination with other antibiotics against multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii. Tridecaptin M sensitized the bacteria to rifampicin, vancomycin, and ceftazidime, showing synergistic effects and enhancing the antimicrobial efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study used checkerboard assays, time-kill experiments, and ex vivo blood infection models to evaluate the synergistic effects of tridecaptin M with antibiotics against A. baumannii.
full_output.sample_size: Five different MDR strains of A. baumannii

full_output.key_findings: The study found that conventional chicken samples had the highest resistance rates to ampicillin, cefotaxime, nalidixic acid, ciprofloxacin, and trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, with a higher prevalence of ESBL-producing E. coli compared to organic and antibiotic-free samples.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing and ESBL detection using Kirby-Bauer and microdilution methods.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel bifunctional antibiotic, Evn P, composed of an everninomicin fragment and a macrolide rosamicin, which binds to both the orthosomycin and macrolide binding sites on the ribosome, demonstrating a strategy to combat antibiotic resistance by targeting multiple sites.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, structural analysis, and biochemical assays were used to characterize the novel antibiotic Evn P and its interaction with the ribosome.

full_output.paper_title: Lysin LysMK34 of Acinetobacter baumannii Bacteriophage PMK34 Has a Turgor Pressure-Dependent Intrinsic Antibacterial Activity and Reverts Colistin Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LysMK34, a lysin from Acinetobacter baumannii bacteriophage PMK34, which exhibits intrinsic antibacterial activity against A. baumannii and P. aeruginosa, and can revert colistin resistance in colistin-resistant A. baumannii strains.
full_output.methodology: The study characterizes the antibacterial activity of LysMK34, evaluates its synergy with colistin, and investigates the impact of turgor pressure on its efficacy.

full_output.paper_title: NisI Maturation and Its Influence on Nisin Resistance in Lactococcus lactis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies NisI as a membrane-bound lipoprotein that confers immunity against nisin in Lactococcus lactis. The maturation of NisI, involving cleavage of the signal peptide by Lsp and lipid modification by Lgt, is critical for its immune function.
full_output.methodology: Mutant analysis, SPR analysis, and protein purification were used to investigate the role of NisI in nisin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: The evolutionary trajectories of P. aeruginosa in biofilm and planktonic growth modes exposed to ciprofloxacin: beyond selection of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in genes such as gyrA, mexR, nalC, nalD, parC, nfxB, ftsZ, murG, sdhA, argS, aotQ, rpoN, and rpoS that contribute to ciprofloxacin resistance in P. aeruginosa. These mutations are associated with cross-resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics like ceftazidime and aztreonam.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing of CIP-resistant isolates from biofilm and planktonic populations, along with phenotypic analyses including growth curves, motility assays, and MIC determinations.

full_output.paper_title: A novel therapeutic antibody screening method using bacterial high-content imaging reveals functional antibody binding phenotypes of Escherichia coli ST131.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in O-antigen and LPS core biosynthesis genes that affect KM467 binding and serum resistance in E. coli ST131 isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, ELISA, high-content imaging, and phenotypic analysis.
full_output.sample_size: 86 clinical E. coli ST131 O25:H4 isolates

full_output.paper_title: A high number of multidrug-resistant and predominant genetically related cluster of Shigella flexneri strains isolated over 34 years in Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high frequency of multidrug-resistant Shigella flexneri strains and a predominant genetically related cluster over 34 years in Brazil.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed virulence genes, antimicrobial resistance profiles, and genotypic diversity using PCR, ERIC-PCR, and PFGE.

full_output.paper_title: Correlation of drug resistance with single nucleotide variations through genome analysis and experimental validation in a multi-drug resistant clinical isolate of M. tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Expansion of acquired 16S rRNA methytransferases along with CTX-M-15, NDM and OXA-48 within three sequence types of Escherichia coli from northeast India.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified ten different 16S rRNA methyltransferase genes (rmtA, rmtB, rmtC, rmtD, rmtE, rmtF, rmtG, rmtH, armA, npmA) along with CTX-M-15, NDM, and OXA-48 beta-lactamases in three sequence types of Escherichia coli from northeast India.
full_output.methodology: PCR assay, sequencing, conjugation, and MLST analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Whole genome sequencing of macrolide resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae serotype 19A sequence type 416.

erm(B).validation_method: whole genome sequencing and phenotypic testing

tet(M).validation_method: whole genome sequencing and phenotypic testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of erm(B) and tet(M) genes in macrolide-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae serotype 19A sequence type 416 isolates, contributing to resistance against erythromycin, clindamycin, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing of 58 isolates of Streptococcus pneumoniae serotype 19A sequence type 416 using the Illumina MiSeq platform, along with phenotypic testing for antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: High in vitro activity of DIS-73285, a novel antimicrobial with a new mechanism of action, against MDR and XDR Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
full_output.key_findings: DIS-73285 exhibited high in vitro potency against all tested N. gonorrhoeae isolates, including MDR and XDR strains, with MICs ranging from ≤0.001 to 0.004 mg/L.
full_output.methodology: Agar dilution and Etest methods were used to determine MICs of DIS-73285 and other antimicrobials against N. gonorrhoeae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution and epidemiological relatedness of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolated from companion dogs, owners, and environments.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in 12 out of 72 households, with the predominant clone being ST72-SCC mec IV. The MRSA strains were found in dogs, owners, and residential environments, indicating potential transmission between humans and companion animals.
full_output.methodology: The study involved sampling from dogs, owners, and residential environments, followed by antimicrobial susceptibility testing, SCC mec typing, spa typing, MLST, and PFGE analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Extracellular Vesicles Influence the Growth and Adhesion of Staphylococcus epidermidis Under Antimicrobial Selective Pressure.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the impact of extracellular vesicles (EVs) on the growth and adhesion of Staphylococcus epidermidis under antimicrobial selective pressure, particularly focusing on gentamicin. EVs from a gentamicin-resistant strain influenced the susceptibility and adhesion of a gentamicin-susceptible strain.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized EV isolation, characterization via nanoparticle tracking analysis and scanning electron microscopy, and assessed the effects of EVs on bacterial growth, viability, and adhesion using kinetic optical density measurements and microtiter plate assays.

full_output.paper_title: Conserved G-Quadruplex Motifs in Gene Promoter Region Reveals a Novel Therapeutic Approach to Target Multi-Drug Resistance Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies conserved G-quadruplex (G4) motifs in the promoter regions of essential genes in Klebsiella pneumoniae, demonstrating that stabilization of these G4 structures by BRACO-19 inhibits bacterial growth and gene expression.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics analysis, NMR, CD spectroscopy, EMSA, ITC, PCR, and qRT-PCR were used to analyze G4 structures and their interaction with BRACO-19.

full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, sequencing, molecular docking, and EC50 measurements were used to analyze resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Characterization of mcr-1-carrying Salmonella enterica Serovar 4,[5],12:i:- ST 34 Clone Isolated From Pigs in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mcr-1 gene in four colistin-resistant Salmonella enterica serovar 4,[5],12:i:- isolates from pigs in China, demonstrating its role in colistin resistance and its potential for horizontal transfer via IncHI2 plasmids.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and conjugation assays were used to characterize the mcr-1 gene and its resistance mechanisms.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in rpoB and rpoC genes of Clostridioides difficile that confer resistance to fidaxomicin.
full_output.methodology: Mutational analysis and susceptibility testing.

full_output.methodology: Bacterial adenylate cyclase two hybrid assay, fluorescent reporter assay, and genetic analysis.

It identifies specific genes associated with mercury, silver, copper, and antibiotic resistance, highlighting their association with porcine sources and their role in the monophasic phenotype.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatic analysis of 811 Salmonella 4,[5],12:i:- isolates to identify resistance genes and genetic elements.

full_output.paper_title: Multifunctional antibiotic- and zinc-containing mesoporous bioactive glass scaffolds to fight bone infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial properties of gelatin-coated meso-macroporous scaffolds based on bioactive glass, doped with ZnO and loaded with antibiotics such as levofloxacin, vancomycin, gentamicin, and rifampicin. The scaffolds showed synergistic effects of zinc ions and antibiotics against S. aureus and E. coli, effectively destroying biofilms and reducing the required antibiotic dosage.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the fabrication and characterization of mesoporous bioactive glass scaffolds, antibiotic loading and release studies, molecular modeling, and in vitro antibacterial assays including agar disk-diffusion, planktonic growth inhibition, and biofilm degradation.

full_output.paper_title: 4-(N-Alkyl- and -Acyl-amino)-1,2,4-triazole-3-thione Analogs as Metallo-β-Lactamase Inhibitors: Impact of 4-Linker on Potency and Spectrum of Inhibition.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla_VIM-2 as a gene responsible for metallo-beta-lactamase activity, which confers resistance to carbapenems. The gene was experimentally validated in an isogenic E. coli strain.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, enzymatic inhibition assays, and microbiological assays were conducted to evaluate the impact of compound modifications on MBL inhibition.

full_output.paper_title: Gram-negative Organisms from Patients with Community-Acquired Urinary Tract Infections and Associated Risk Factors for Antimicrobial Resistance: A Single-Center Retrospective Observational Study in Japan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified ESBL-producing E. coli as a major cause of antimicrobial resistance in community-acquired urinary tract infections (UTIs) and highlighted nursing home residency and recent antibiotic use as significant risk factors for resistant Gram-negative rods (GNRs).
full_output.methodology: Retrospective observational study analyzing antimicrobial resistance patterns in GNRs causing UTIs.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and Genotypic Properties of Vibrio cholerae non-O1, non-O139 Isolates Recovered from Domestic Ducks in Germany.

gyrA.notes: Mutation in gyrA gene leads to resistance to nalidixic acid

full_output.paper_title: Polymeric Nanoparticle Associated with Ceftriaxone and Extract of Schinopsis Brasiliensis Engler against Multiresistant Enterobacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a polymeric nanoparticle (PN) combining ceftriaxone and an extract of Schinopsis brasiliensis, showing improved antimicrobial activity against multidrug-resistant Enterobacteria, particularly against strains producing ESBL and KPC.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a Box-Behnken design to optimize nanoparticle formulation, assessed physicochemical properties via DLS, SEM, and FTIR, and evaluated antimicrobial activity using broth microdilution.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-Genome-Based Survey for Polyphyletic Serovars of Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica Provides New Insights into Public Health Surveillance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies antimicrobial resistance (AMR) profiles in specific lineages of Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovars, highlighting the presence of resistance genes such as aac(6')-Ib, aph(3')-Ib, sul2, and tet(A) in host-preferred lineages, indicating that AMR profiles are lineage-specific and associated with niche preference.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and comparative genomics were used to analyze the genetic diversity and AMR profiles of Salmonella serovars.

full_output.paper_title: The antibacterial activity and toxin production control of bee venom in mouse MRSA pneumonia model.
full_output.key_findings: Bee venom (BV) exhibited antibacterial activity against MRSA and reduced toxin production, which decreased the virulence of the bacterium and alleviated pneumonia symptoms in mice.
full_output.methodology: The study assessed the antibacterial activity of BV through MIC determination, qRT-PCR, western blot, ELISA, and in vivo experiments in a mouse pneumonia model.

full_output.paper_title: A Diverse Panel of Clinical Acinetobacter baumannii for Research and Development.

pmrB.notes: Mutation in pmrB leads to colistin resistance

full_output.paper_title: Rapid Increase of CTX-M-Producing Shigella sonnei Isolates in Switzerland Due to Spread of Common Plasmids and International Clones.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple CTX-M-type beta-lactamase genes (bla CTX-M-3, bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-27, bla CTX-M-55, and bla CTX-M-134) in Shigella sonnei isolates in Switzerland, highlighting the rapid increase of extended-spectrum cephalosporin-resistant isolates due to the spread of common plasmids and international clones.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and plasmid analysis were used to characterize the AMR genes and plasmids in the S. sonnei isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Therapeutic Effect and Mechanisms of the Novel Monosulfactam 0073.
full_output.key_findings: The novel monosulfactam 0073 showed potent activity against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, including those producing various beta-lactamases such as KPC-2, NDM-1, TEM-1, OXA-48, SHV-11, CTX-M-1, and CIT. It exhibited lower MICs compared to aztreonam and had reduced resistance development potential.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of 0073 using MIC and time-kill assays, along with in vivo efficacy in mouse infection models.

full_output.paper_title: Case Commentary: Daptomycin Resistance in Staphylococcus argenteus-from Northern Australia to San Francisco.

mprF.notes: mprF mutation (S337L) associated with daptomycin resistance

full_output.paper_title: Activity of Cefiderocol, Ceftazidime-Avibactam, and Eravacycline against Carbapenem-Resistant Escherichia coli Isolates from the United States and International Sites in Relation to Clonal Background, Resistance Genes, Coresistance, and Region.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the activity of cefiderocol, ceftazidime-avibactam, and eravacycline against carbapenem-resistant E. coli isolates, highlighting the effectiveness of these agents against various resistance mechanisms, including beta-lactamases such as KPC, MBL, and CTX-M.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution MICs to assess the susceptibility of 343 carbapenem-resistant E. coli isolates to several antibiotics, including cefiderocol, ceftazidime-avibactam, and eravacycline, along with molecular typing to identify resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Mycoplasma hominis and Ureaplasma Species in Nonpregnant Female Patients in South Korea Indicate an Increasing Trend of Pristinamycin-Resistant Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified an increasing trend of pristinamycin-resistant isolates of Mycoplasma hominis and Ureaplasma species in nonpregnant female patients in South Korea, with decreasing susceptibility rates to pristinamycin over the study period.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Mycoplasma IST2 kit and statistical analysis of clinical and microbiological data.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of Molecular Subtyping and Antimicrobial Resistance Detection Methods Used in a Large Multistate Outbreak of Extensively Drug-Resistant Campylobacter jejuni Infections Linked to Pet Store Puppies.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations in Campylobacter jejuni isolates from a large multistate outbreak linked to pet store puppies, including resistance to tetracycline, aminoglycosides, macrolides, fluoroquinolones, and others.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and in silico resistance determinant detection were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: The unusual structure of Ruminococcin C1 antimicrobial peptide confers clinical properties.
full_output.key_findings: Ruminococcin C1 is a novel antimicrobial peptide with a unique structure that provides stability and effectiveness against multidrug-resistant pathogens. It exhibits potent activity against various gram-positive bacteria, including clinically relevant strains, without toxicity to human cells.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis using NMR, biochemical assays, and antimicrobial activity testing.

full_output.paper_title: Phosphotransferase System Uptake and Metabolism of the β-Glucoside Salicin Impact Group A Streptococcal Bloodstream Survival and Soft Tissue Infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the β-glucoside transporter bglP and phospho-β-glucosidase bglB as critical for Group A Streptococcus (GAS) survival in human blood and soft tissue infection. Mutations in these genes affect biofilm formation, hemolysis, and localized tissue damage.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized defined nonpolar mutants of bglP and bglB in the M1T1 5448 strain, conducted growth assays in various media, and evaluated biofilm formation and hemolysis.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution of carbapenemase genes in clinical isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii & a comparison of MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry-based detection of carbapenemase production with other phenotypic methods.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the distribution of carbapenemase genes in clinical isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii, including blaOXA-51, blaOXA-23, blaVIM, and blaNDM-1. It also compared the effectiveness of MALDI-TOF MS in detecting carbapenemase production.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR and MALDI-TOF MS were used to detect carbapenemase genes and assess their production in clinical isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the tetracycline resistance gene tet(O) encoded on the megaplasmid pCJDM202 in Campylobacter jejuni WP2-202, which was transferred to C. jejuni NCTC11168 via conjugation, resulting in increased tetracycline resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, conjugation experiments, and MIC testing were used to validate the tetracycline resistance conferred by the tet(O) gene.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid antibiotic susceptibility testing of bacteria from patients' blood via assaying bacterial metabolic response with surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a rapid antibiotic susceptibility testing method using surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) for bacteria from blood cultures, demonstrating its effectiveness in determining susceptibility profiles of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli within four hours.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) to analyze bacterial metabolic responses to antibiotics, coupled with a pretreatment protocol to isolate bacteria from blood components.
full_output.sample_size: 75 clinical strains of S. aureus (n = 32) and E. coli (n = 43)

full_output.paper_title: An embedded lipid in the multidrug transporter LmrP suggests a mechanism for polyspecificity.

mutations_found.validated_by: native mass spectrometry and functional assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies an embedded phosphatidylglycerol (PG) lipid in the binding pocket of LmrP, a multidrug transporter, which is crucial for its function and substrate specificity. Mutations disrupting this lipid binding, such as N116Y, significantly impair LmrP's transport activity.
full_output.methodology: Crystallography, molecular dynamics simulations, native mass spectrometry, and functional assays using inside-out vesicles.

full_output.paper_title: Sulfamethoxazole drug stress upregulates antioxidant immunomodulatory metabolites in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies folX and folM as genes involved in the biosynthesis of colipterins, which are antioxidant metabolites upregulated by sulfamethoxazole stress in E. coli.
full_output.methodology: Metabolite analysis, genetic complementation, and mutant analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of the cereulide synthetase gene cesB in 5.1% of B. cereus isolates from aquatic products, indicating potential emetic toxin production. High levels of antibiotic resistance, especially to β-lactams and rifampin, were observed.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of virulence genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing via Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion.

full_output.paper_title: First Genome Sequences of Two Multidrug-Resistant Candida haemulonii var. vulnera Isolates From Pediatric Patients With Candidemia.

ERG11.validation_method: alignment of the Erg11p amino acid sequences

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first draft genomes of two multidrug-resistant Candida haemulonii var. vulnera isolates and identifies amino acid substitutions in the Erg11p protein associated with reduced susceptibility to azole and polyene antifungal agents.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and comparative genomic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Dissemination of Carbapenemases (KPC, NDM, OXA-48, IMP, and VIM) Among Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacteriaceae Isolated From Adult and Children Patients in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla KPC-2, bla NDM, and bla OXA-48-like as the most prevalent carbapenemase genes among carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) in China. bla KPC-2 was dominant in K. pneumoniae from adult patients, while bla NDM was prevalent in E. coli from both children and adults. bla OXA-232 was exclusively found in K. pneumoniae from children.
full_output.methodology: PCR and DNA sequencing were used to detect carbapenemase genes, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the broth microdilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Avian Pathogenic Escherichia coli (APEC) Associated With Turkey Cellulitis in Iowa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antimicrobial resistance genes in E. coli isolates from turkey cellulitis outbreaks, including blaTEM, aac3VI, tetA, tetB, sulI, qacEdelta1, arsC, pcoA, pcoD, pcoE, silP, terX, terF, terY3, and terD, indicating the presence of multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR and statistical analysis were used to detect and analyze antimicrobial resistance genes in E. coli isolates from turkey farms.

full_output.paper_title: Extensive antimicrobial resistance mobilization via multicopy plasmid encapsidation mediated by temperate phages.

armA.validation_method: experimental validation using qPCR and Southern blotting

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the 16S rRNA methyltransferase gene armA as a key factor in antimicrobial resistance, demonstrating its efficient encapsidation in phage particles when carried on multicopy plasmids, highlighting the role of phages in the mobilization of antimicrobial resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized qPCR, Southern blotting, and plasmid sequencing to analyze the mobilization of the armA gene via phage encapsidation.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro activity of eravacycline against common ribotypes of Clostridioides difficile.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that eravacycline showed potent in vitro activity against various ribotypes of Clostridioides difficile, and the presence of tetM or tetW resistance genes did not affect the MIC of eravacycline.
full_output.methodology: Broth microdilution, MBC assays, time-killing kinetic studies, and whole-genome sequencing were used to evaluate the in vitro activity of eravacycline against Clostridioides difficile isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The AO trauma CPP bone infection registry: Epidemiology and outcomes of Staphylococcus aureus bone infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the epidemiology and outcomes of Staphylococcus aureus bone infections, highlighting the prevalence of methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) and its impact on patient recovery and treatment outcomes.
full_output.methodology: The study is a prospective, observational, nonrandomized case-series analyzing clinical data, bacterial isolates, and patient outcomes from a multinational registry of S. aureus infections.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance in Cancer Therapy: Targeting Multidrug Resistance Mechanisms
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the identification and characterization of various compounds that inhibit multidrug resistance (MDR) mechanisms mediated by ABC transporters such as P-gp, BCRP, and MRP1. Several derivatives of chalcones, flavanones, flavonols, and terpenoids were found to effectively reverse MDR by inhibiting these transporters.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro assays to evaluate the inhibitory effects of synthesized compounds on P-gp, BCRP, and MRP1 efflux functions, along with structural analyses and computational modeling.

full_output.paper_title: Biofilm Formation and Antibiotic Resistance Phenotype of Helicobacter pylori Clinical Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that biofilm formation increases the resistance of Helicobacter pylori to antibiotics, particularly clarithromycin, amoxicillin, tetracycline, levofloxacin, and metronidazole. Strong biofilm-forming strains exhibited higher minimum biofilm eradication concentrations (MBEC) compared to weak biofilm-forming strains.
full_output.methodology: The study used Etest for MIC determination and crystal violet staining for biofilm quantification. MBEC was measured to assess antibiotic resistance in biofilm-forming strains.

full_output.paper_title: 16S and 23S rRNA Gene Mutation Independent Multidrug Resistance of Non-Tuberculous Mycobacteria Isolated from South Korean Soil.

rrs.notes: Mutations in the rrs gene were found in multiple NTM species.
rrs.evidence_note: Mutations in the rrs gene were identified through sequencing in multiple NTM species.

rrl.notes: Mutation in the rrl gene was found in M. intracellulare.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug resistance in non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) isolated from South Korean soil, including resistance to streptomycin, amikacin, azithromycin, ethambutol, isoniazid, and imipenem. Mutations in the rrs and rrl genes were associated with resistance to certain antibiotics, and the erm gene was linked to macrolide resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequence analysis were used to detect mutations in the rrs and rrl genes, and the presence of the erm gene was determined.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Clinical MRSA Isolates from Northern Spain and Assessment of Their Susceptibility to Phage-Derived Antimicrobials.

czr.mechanism: efflux pump for cadmium and zinc ions
czr.validation_method: PCR detection of the gene in four isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study characterized MRSA isolates from northern Spain, identifying the mecA gene as responsible for methicillin resistance and the czr gene associated with zinc resistance. All isolates were susceptible to the endolysin LysRODI, though with varying degrees of susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: PCR and RAPD-PCR for gene detection, biofilm formation assays, phage susceptibility tests, and turbidity reduction assays for endolysin activity.

full_output.paper_title: Role of Bacterial and Host DNases on Host-Pathogen Interaction during Streptococcus suis Meningitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the role of the bacterial nuclease SsnA and host DNase 1 during Streptococcus suis meningitis, revealing that SsnA does not significantly contribute to meningitis pathogenesis in piglets, while host DNase 1 plays a role in modulating the innate immune response.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized animal experiments, in vitro models, and various biochemical assays to analyze the roles of SsnA and DNase 1 in host-pathogen interactions during S. suis meningitis.
full_output.sample_size: 18 pigs in the survival experiment and 39 pigs in the early phase experiment

full_output.paper_title: Changes in the vaginal microbiota following antibiotic treatment for Mycoplasma genitalium, Chlamydia trachomatis and bacterial vaginosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated changes in the vaginal microbiota following antibiotic treatment for sexually transmitted infections and bacterial vaginosis, focusing on the effects of metronidazole, azithromycin, tetracyclines, and moxifloxacin on microbial communities.
full_output.methodology: The study used 16S rRNA gene sequencing, quantitative PCR, and microscopy to analyze the vaginal microbiota of patients and controls before and after antibiotic treatment.

full_output.paper_title: Essential role of Salmonella Enteritidis DNA adenine methylase in modulating inflammasome activation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the genes dam, invC, prgH, and spaN as crucial for inflammasome activation in Salmonella Enteritidis. Deletion or overexpression of dam impaired inflammasome activation, highlighting its essential role in modulating the host immune response.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, Western blot, ELISA, and RNA sequencing were used to analyze gene function and inflammasome activation.

full_output.paper_title: The prevalence and mechanism of fluoroquinolone resistance in Escherichia coli isolated from swine farms in China.

qnrS.evidence_note: The qnrS gene was detected in 7 (9.46%) strains and was associated with fluoroquinolone resistance.

oqxAB.evidence_note: The oqxAB gene was found in 29 (39.19%) of the 74 FQ-resistant E. coli isolates.

aac(6')-Ib-cr.evidence_note: aac(6')-Ib-cr was identified as a plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance (PMQR) gene in E. coli isolates from swine farms.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in the QRDR region
gyrA.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that mutations in gyrA (S83L and D87N, D87Y, D87H, D87G) confer resistance to fluoroquinolones. The organisms observed in are swine-derived E. coli. The mutations were validated by PCR and sequencing.

parC.notes: Mutations in the QRDR region

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of fluoroquinolone resistance in E. coli from swine farms in China, highlighting the role of chromosomal mutations in gyrA, parC, parE, marR, and acrR, along with plasmid-mediated resistance genes qnrS, oqxAB, and aac(6')-Ib-cr.
full_output.methodology: The study involved sampling, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, sequencing, and conjugation experiments to identify resistance mechanisms in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and abundance of selected genes conferring macrolide resistance genes in COPD patients during maintenance treatment with azithromycin.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the relative abundance of macrolide resistance genes (ermB, ermF, and mefA) increased over time in COPD patients receiving azithromycin maintenance therapy compared to the placebo group, although the acquisition rate of these genes was limited.

full_output.paper_title: Hepatocytic transcriptional signatures predict comparative drug interaction potential of rifamycin antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline resistance gene tet(M), and combinations of lsa(E) and lnu(B) conferring resistance to lincosamides, pleuromutilins, and streptogramin A in Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae isolates from pigs, but not in wild boar isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Prediction of Mycobacterium tuberculosis pyrazinamidase function based on structural stability, physicochemical and geometrical descriptors.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the pncA gene that impair pyrazinamidase function, leading to pyrazinamide resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. These mutations primarily affect the active site and metal coordination site of the enzyme.
full_output.methodology: The study used kinetic parameters, structural modeling, and computational analyses to assess the impact of pncA mutations on pyrazinamidase function and pyrazinamide resistance.

full_output.paper_title: MazF cleavage sites in Staphylococcus aureus: Implications for growth arrest and antimicrobial resistance
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MazF cleavage sites in various genes involved in protein synthesis, cell wall synthesis, and cell division in Staphylococcus aureus, leading to growth arrest. full_output.methodology: The study utilized nEMOTE and RNA-seq techniques to identify MazF cleavage sites and assess their impact on gene expression and bacterial growth.

full_output.paper_title: Machine learning reveals that Mycobacterium tuberculosis genotypes and anatomic disease site impacts drug resistance and disease transmission among patients with proven extra-pulmonary tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that East Asian lineage (Beijing clade) of Mycobacterium tuberculosis is significantly more likely to be involved in chains of transmission and is associated with higher drug resistance, particularly rifampin resistance, in extra-pulmonary tuberculosis (EPTB) patients. It also highlights the role of sanctuary sites like lymph nodes, meninges, and cutaneous TB in contributing to drug resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized machine learning algorithms, spoligotyping, and drug susceptibility testing to analyze Mtb isolates from EPTB patients in Tshwane, South Africa.

full_output.key_findings: High fecal carriage of extended Beta Lactamase producing Enterobacteriaceae (ESBL-PE) was observed among hospitalized patients in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Previous antibiotic use was associated with ESBL-PE carriage.

full_output.paper_title: Mapping the Efficacy and Mode of Action of Ethylzingerone [4-(3-Ethoxy-4-Hydroxyphenyl) Butan-2-One] as an Active Agent against Burkholderia Bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Exploiting natural chemical photosensitivity of anhydrotetracycline and tetracycline for dynamic and setpoint chemo-optogenetic control.
full_output.key_findings: The study explores the use of anhydrotetracycline (aTc) and tetracycline (Tc) for optogenetic control by exploiting their photosensitivity. full_output.methodology: The study uses E. coli strains expressing TetR or rTetR, along with mCherry as a reporter, to monitor aTc concentration and gene expression. Light exposure is used to inactivate aTc and Tc, enabling dynamic control of transcription and growth.

full_output.paper_title: Methyl-donor supplementation prevents intestinal colonization by Adherent-Invasive E. coli in a mouse model of Crohn's disease.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic epidemiology of animal-derived tigecycline-resistant Escherichia coli across China reveals recent endemic plasmid-encoded tet(X4) gene.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the tet(X4) gene as a plasmid-encoded tigecycline resistance gene prevalent in Escherichia coli isolates from pigs and chickens in northwestern China, highlighting its potential for human transmission.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial action of 1,10-phenanthroline-based compounds on carbapenemase-producing Acinetobacter baumannii clinical strains: efficacy against planktonic- and biofilm-growing cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the intrinsic bla OXA-51 gene and the acquired bla OXA-23 and bla OXA-24 genes as contributors to carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii clinical strains.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of carbapenemase genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and characteristics of a novel cecropin from the armyworm, Mythimna separata.
full_output.key_findings: A novel cecropin named AC-1 was identified from the armyworm, Mythimna separata, showing effective antimicrobial activity against several bacterial species including Salmonella, E. coli, K. pneumonia, and P. aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptome sequencing and multi-sequence alignment analysis were used to identify AC-1, followed by evaluation of its antimicrobial, hemolytic, and cytotoxic activities.

full_output.paper_title: Conjugative plasmidic AmpC detected in Escherichia coli, Proteus mirabilis and Klebsiella pneumoniae human clinical isolates from Portugal.
full_output.key_findings: The study detected plasmidic AmpC genes (blaCIT, blaCMY, and blaDHA) in clinical isolates of Escherichia coli, Proteus mirabilis, and Klebsiella pneumoniae from Portugal, confirming their role in β-lactam resistance through PCR and phenotypic analysis.
full_output.methodology: PCR, phenotypic testing, and conjugation experiments were used to identify and characterize the plasmidic AmpC genes.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of plasmid-encoded carbapenemases in multi-drug resistant Escherichia coli from patients with urinary tract infection in northern Iran.

full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, phenotypic methods, and multiplex PCR were used to detect carbapenemases in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic characterization and genome comparison reveal insights into potential vaccine coverage and genealogy of Neisseria meningitidis in military camps in Vietnam.

full_output.paper_title: High relatedness of invasive multi-drug resistant non-typhoidal Salmonella genotypes among patients and asymptomatic carriers in endemic informal settlements in Kenya.
