Restoring the wild-type AQP1 open reading frame re-sensitized the 2 independent resistant isolates to antimonials. Alternatively, editing the genome of a sensitive isolate by incorporating the 2-nucleotide insertion in its AQP1 gene led to antimony-resistant parasites.

full_output.paper_title: TNFSF15 Promotes Antimicrobial Pathways in Human Macrophages and These Are Modulated by TNFSF15 Disease-Risk Variants.
full_output.key_findings: TNFSF15 promotes antimicrobial pathways in human macrophages, including PDK1-dependent bacterial uptake, ROS, RNS, and autophagy, which are essential for intracellular bacterial clearance. These effects are mediated through DR3 and require autocrine/paracrine TNFSF15 signaling.
full_output.methodology: Flow cytometry, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and gentamicin protection assays were used to analyze protein expression, signaling, bacterial uptake, and intracellular bacterial clearance in human monocyte-derived macrophages.

However, the effect on outcomes is not significant enough to justify systematic baseline drug susceptibility testing, especially when fluoroquinolone susceptibility is preserved.

Drug resistance was determined using phenotypic and genotypic drug susceptibility testing, and whole-genome sequencing was used to identify genetic variations associated with resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance Caused by KPC-2 Encoded by Promiscuous Plasmids of the Klebsiella pneumoniae ST307 Strain.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the blaKPC-2 gene as a key contributor to carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae ST307, highlighting its horizontal transfer capability among Enterobacteriaceae species.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, whole-genome sequencing, and conjugation experiments were used to analyze the resistance mechanisms and genetic characteristics of the isolates.
full_output.sample_size: Three Enterobacteriaceae strains from a single patient.

full_output.paper_title: Characterisation of Bordetella bronchiseptica isolated from rabbits in Fujian, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 219 B. bronchiseptica isolates from rabbits in Fujian, China, with resistance to cefixime, ceftizoxime, cefatriaxone, and ampicillin. All isolates carried five virulence genes (fhaB, prn, cyaA, dnt, bteA).
full_output.methodology: Multi-locus sequence typing, virulence gene detection, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the vprSJ4 gene from Bacillus subtilis SJ4, which encodes a novel fibrinolytic enzyme with unique structural features and enzymatic properties.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, overexpression in E. coli, purification, and biochemical characterization of the recombinant enzyme.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of anti-BCG benz[α]anthraquinones and new siderophores from a Xinjiang desert-isolated rare actinomycete Nocardia sp. XJ31.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two benz[α]anthraquinones, brasiliquinones D (13) and E (14), which showed potent anti-BCG activity with MIC values of around 25 μM. Additionally, twelve new siderophores, including nocardimicins J-R and brasiliquinone E, were isolated from Nocardia sp. XJ31.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the isolation of rare actinobacteria from Xinjiang region, followed by fermentation, extraction, and purification of natural products. Structural elucidation was performed using HR-ESI-MS, 1D NMR, and 2D NMR techniques. Anti-BCG bioassays were conducted to evaluate the activity of the isolated compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical presentations and antimicrobial susceptibilities of Corynebacterium cystitidis associated with renal disease in four beef cattle.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the clinical presentation and antimicrobial susceptibilities of Corynebacterium cystitidis in four beef cattle with renal disease. The isolates showed similar MICs for several antibiotics, including ampicillin, florfenicol, gentamicin, neomycin, sulfadimethoxine, trimethoprim sulfonamide, and tylosin.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective case series with microbiological testing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of Transferable mcr-9 Gene-Carrying Colistin-Resistant Salmonella enterica Dessau ST14 Isolated from Retail Chicken Meat in Korea.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mcr-9 gene in a colistin-resistant Salmonella enterica Dessau ST14 strain isolated from retail chicken meat in Korea, demonstrating its transferability to Escherichia coli. Additionally, the strain carried other resistance genes including aac(6')-Iaa, blaTEM-1B, and qnrS1.
full_output.methodology: The study used antimicrobial susceptibility testing, whole-genome sequencing, and conjugation assays to characterize the resistance profile and transferability of the mcr-9 gene.

full_output.paper_title: A Dual Enzyme-Based Biochemical Test Rapidly Detects Third-Generation Cephalosporin-Resistant CTX-M-Producing Uropathogens in Clinical Urine Samples.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the DETECT assay can rapidly identify CTX-M-producing uropathogens in clinical urine samples, showing high sensitivity and specificity for detecting third-generation cephalosporin-resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study used a dual-enzyme trigger-enabled cascade technology (DETECT) to detect CTX-M beta-lactamase activity in urine samples, validated through clinical isolates and comparative analysis with standard phenotypic and genotypic methods.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes in five poultry-derived Morganella morganii strains, including beta-lactamases, tetracycline resistance genes, and lipid A biosynthesis genes associated with colistin resistance. These strains exhibited multidrug resistance to several antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify AMR genes and virulence factors in the five poultry strains.

full_output.paper_title: Global transcriptomic responses orchestrate difenoconazole resistance in Penicillium spp. causing blue mold of stored apple fruit.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PEX2_044360 (ABC transporter) and PEX2_012910 (MDR gene) as key players in difenoconazole resistance in Penicillium spp. through transcriptomic analysis and inhibition experiments.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis, qRT-PCR, and inhibition experiments with active efflux pump inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Characterisation of Vibrio Species from Surface and Drinking Water Sources and Assessment of Biocontrol Potentials of Their Bacteriophages.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antibiotic-resistant Vibrio species in water samples and evaluated the biocontrol potential of their bacteriophages. High resistance to cephalothin, ampicillin, and streptomycin was observed, along with the presence of virulence genes such as tdh, trh, and zot.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the isolation and characterization of Vibrio species from water samples, detection of virulence genes via PCR, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and evaluation of bacteriophage efficacy.

full_output.paper_title: A new coumarin compound DCH combats methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus biofilm by targeting arginine repressor.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies argR as a target of the coumarin compound DCH, which inhibits MRSA biofilm formation by disrupting the arginine catabolic pathway.
full_output.methodology: The study used SPR, molecular docking, and gene expression analysis to investigate the mechanism of DCH against MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Peptidoglycan editing provides immunity to Acinetobacter baumannii during bacterial warfare.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the racK gene, which encodes a d-amino acid racemase, as responsible for the production of d-Lys in Acinetobacter baumannii. This d-Lys is incorporated into the peptidoglycan, providing immunity against T6SS-mediated attacks.
full_output.methodology: The study used molecular genetics, biochemical assays, and comparative genomics to characterize the role of racK in d-Lys production and peptidoglycan editing.

full_output.paper_title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa Presents Multiple Vital Changes in Its Proteome in the Presence of 3-Hydroxyphenylacetic Acid, a Promising Antimicrobial Agent.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several genes whose expression was altered in P. aeruginosa upon exposure to 3-HPAA, indicating its antimicrobial effects through disruption of DNA repair, transcription, ribosome assembly, and oxidative stress response mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Proteomic analysis using LC-ESI-MS/MS combined with STRING and KEGG pathway analysis.

full_output.key_findings: Lefamulin is a novel pleuromutilin antibiotic with activity against common aerobic Gram-positive organisms, fastidious Gram-negatives, atypicals, and some Gram-positive anaerobes. Resistance to lefamulin is infrequent, and it shows activity against multidrug-resistant organisms such as methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium. However, it lacks activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii, Enterobacterales, most anaerobes, and E. faecalis.
full_output.methodology: Review of clinical trials and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic data for lefamulin.

full_output.paper_title: Accumulation of antibiotic-resistant genes in anaerobic biofilm reactor fed with household chemical products.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the accumulation of ermC genes in anaerobic biofilm reactors fed with household chemical products, suggesting that these compounds exhibit antimicrobial activity similar to erythromycin.
full_output.methodology: qPCR analysis was used to quantify the presence of antibiotic-resistant genes in the reactors.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae, microbial loads, and endotoxin levels in dust from laying hen houses in Egypt.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the presence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacteriaceae in dust from laying hen houses in Egypt, highlighting their potential as a reservoir for these resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Microbial load, ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae, and endotoxin levels were analyzed in dust samples from 28 laying hen farms using culture-based methods and molecular techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance pattern in domestic animal - wildlife - environmental niche via the food chain to humans with a Bangladesh perspective; a systematic review.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the prevalence of tetracycline resistance genes in various sample sources, including enteric pathogens like Escherichia coli. It also notes the significant resistance to amino-penicillins and the concerning acquisition of cephalosporin resistance in wildlife species.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 45 articles published between 2005 and 2019, analyzing antimicrobial resistance patterns in different samples from domestic animals, wildlife, food sources, environmental samples, and insects.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and molecular characterization of ticks and tick-borne pathogens of one-humped camels (Camelus dromedarius) in Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 'Candidatus Anaplasma camelii' in 40.3% of camel blood samples, highlighting its prevalence in Nigerian camels.
full_output.methodology: Molecular detection using PCR and sequencing for tick-borne pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: The Sensor Kinase QseC Regulates the Unlinked PmrA Response Regulator and Downstream Gene Expression in Francisella.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies QseC as an upstream regulator of priM expression and shows that PmrA represses priM, with the regulation being partially dependent on the aspartate phosphorylation site of PmrA (D51).
full_output.methodology: The study used RNA-seq, qRT-PCR, transposon mutagenesis, and genetic complementation to analyze gene regulation and function in Francisella.

full_output.paper_title: Clarithromycin Exerts an Antibiofilm Effect against Salmonella enterica Serovar Typhimurium rdar Biofilm Formation and Transforms the Physiology towards an Apparent Oxygen-Depleted Energy and Carbon Metabolism.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that clarithromycin exhibits antibiofilm activity against Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium rdar biofilm formation, reducing the expression of the biofilm regulator CsgD and altering cellular metabolism towards an oxygen-depleted state.
full_output.methodology: The study used a 96-well biofilm assay, qRT-PCR, Western blotting, and RNA sequencing to evaluate the effects of clarithromycin on biofilm formation and gene expression in Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium.

full_output.paper_title: Animal Model To Study Klebsiella pneumoniae Gastrointestinal Colonization and Host-to-Host Transmission.
full_output.key_findings: The study established a murine model to investigate Klebsiella pneumoniae gastrointestinal colonization, shedding, and host-to-host transmission. It demonstrated that antibiotic treatment can induce a supershedder phenotype, enhancing transmission efficiency. Capsule-deficient mutants showed impaired colonization and shedding, highlighting the importance of the capsular polysaccharide in GI colonization.
full_output.methodology: Murine model, fecal shedding analysis, antibiotic treatment, and genetic mutants.

full_output.paper_title: In Vivo Activity of QPX7728, an Ultrabroad-Spectrum Beta-Lactamase Inhibitor, in Combination with Beta-Lactams against Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: QPX7728, an ultrabroad-spectrum beta-lactamase inhibitor, effectively restored the activity of multiple beta-lactams against carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in a neutropenic mouse thigh infection model.
full_output.methodology: Evaluation of QPX7728 in combination with beta-lactams against carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae isolates in a neutropenic mouse thigh infection model.

full_output.paper_title: A biphasic nanohydroxyapatite/calcium sulphate carrier containing Rifampicin and Isoniazid for local delivery gives sustained and effective antibiotic release and prevents biofilm formation.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the use of a biphasic nanohydroxyapatite/calcium sulphate carrier for the local delivery of Rifampicin (RFP) and Isoniazid (INH), demonstrating sustained and effective antibiotic release and prevention of biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro drug release profiles, FTIR spectroscopy, computational studies, and antibacterial/biofilm assays to evaluate the performance of the nanocement carrier.

full_output.paper_title: Baculovirus Expression and Functional Analysis of Vpa2 Proteins from Bacillus thuringiensis.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes Vpa2Ac1, Vpa2-like1, and Vpa2-like2 proteins from Bacillus thuringiensis, demonstrating that Vpa2Ac1 and Vpa2-like2 exhibit ADP-ribosyltransferase activity that modulates actin polarization, while Vpa2-like1 lacks this activity.

full_output.paper_title: Surfactant phospholipids act as molecular switches for premature induction of quorum sensing-dependent virulence in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: Surfactant phospholipids in mouse bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) induce premature expression of quorum sensing (QS)-regulated virulence factors, such as LasB and RhlA, in exponential phase P. aeruginosa. This suggests that pulmonary surfactant phospholipids act as molecular switches for QS activation.
full_output.methodology: qPCR, Western blot, exoprotease assays, and GC-MS were used to analyze gene expression and virulence factor production in P. aeruginosa under different culture conditions.

full_output.paper_title: Venom peptides in association with standard drugs: a novel strategy for combating antibiotic resistance - an overview.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the potential of venom peptides in combination with standard antibiotics to combat antibiotic resistance, highlighting their ability to enhance the efficacy of existing drugs and overcome resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The paper is a review article summarizing existing research on the use of venom peptides in combination with antibiotics to address antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Novel phenolic antimicrobials enhanced activity of iminodiacetate prodrugs against biofilm and planktonic bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the addition of (acetoxy)methyl iminodiacetate groups enhances the potency of simple phenols against biofilms and planktonic cells of S. epidermidis and P. aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of phenolic iminodiacetate AM conjugates, determination of MIC and MBEC values, and enzyme assays.

full_output.paper_title: Can Selenoenzymes Resist Electrophilic Modification? Evidence from Thioredoxin Reductase and a Mutant Containing α-Methylselenocysteine.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that selenocysteine (Sec) in thioredoxin reductase (TrxR) provides resistance to electrophilic modification, with a mutant containing α-methylselenocysteine (αMe)Sec showing increased resistance compared to wild-type TrxR.
full_output.methodology: Enzyme activity assays, peptide synthesis, and mass spectrometry were used to characterize the resistance properties of Sec and αMe)Sec-containing TrxR mutants.

full_output.paper_title: Clusters of polymorphic transmembrane genes control resistance to schistosomes in snail vectors.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a genomic region PTC2 in Biomphalaria glabrata snails that exhibits a strong correlation with resistance to schistosome infection. PTC2 contains highly polymorphic transmembrane genes, which are associated with differential susceptibility to infection. The study highlights the role of these genes in host-parasite interactions and suggests their potential as targets for controlling schistosomiasis.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide association study, PacBio sequencing, RNA-Seq, and genotyping of snails to analyze genetic variations and their association with resistance to schistosome infection.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the YoeB-YefM complex in Staphylococcus aureus, identifying two distinct oligomeric states: heterotetramer and heterohexamer, which exhibit different DNA-binding affinities and play roles in transcriptional autoregulation.

full_output.paper_title: Mucoidy, a general mechanism for maintaining lytic phage in populations of bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the rcsC137 gain-of-function mutation as a key factor in mucoidy, which provides broad resistance to lytic phage in E. coli MG1655. Mucoidy allows for the maintenance of phage populations through a high rate of transition from mucoid to non-mucoid states.
full_output.methodology: The study used serial transfer experiments, whole-genome sequencing, and single-cell microscopy to investigate the mechanisms of phage maintenance in mucoid E. coli populations.

It identified significant variations in antimicrobial resistance gene (AARG) presence across serotypes and genetic subpopulations, highlighting the importance of WGS for improved subtyping and tracking of resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, bioinformatics analysis, and comparative genomics were used to analyze the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of fluoroquinolone combinations with antimicrobial and non-antimicrobial agents against multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of fluoroquinolone combinations with antimicrobial and non-antimicrobial agents against multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, highlighting the potential of certain combinations to restore susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: The study used checkerboard method to assess antimicrobial combinations and analyzed MICs of fluoroquinolones with various agents.

full_output.paper_title: Copper primes adaptation of uropathogenic Escherichia coli to superoxide stress by activating superoxide dismutases.
full_output.key_findings: Copper exposure enhances the activity of SodA and SodC, leading to increased resistance of UPEC to superoxide stress. SodA is essential for copper-dependent protection against superoxide-mediated killing.
full_output.methodology: Genetic mutants, real-time PCR, zymogram analysis, and survival assays in macrophages.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a novel AraC/XylS-regulated family of N-acyltransferases in pathogens of the order Enterobacterales.
full_output.key_findings: AatD is a novel N-acyltransferase involved in the acylation of Aap, a lipoprotein critical for bacterial virulence. Its absence disrupts Aap trafficking and reduces bacterial colonization in a mouse model.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, metabolomic analysis, Western blotting, and confocal microscopy were used to characterize AatD's role in Aap acylation and translocation.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance Genes in Phage Particles from Antarctic and Mediterranean Seawater Ecosystems.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in phage particles from Antarctic and Mediterranean seawater, highlighting the presence of beta-lactamase genes (bla TEM, bla CTX-M-1, bla CTX-M-9), tetracycline resistance gene (tetW), and sulfonamide resistance gene (sul1). These genes were detected in phage particles from both regions, indicating their potential role in the dissemination of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) to detect and quantify ARGs in phage particles isolated from seawater and fish samples.
full_output.sample_size: 50 samples of shellfish, Mediterranean fish, Atlantic fish, frozen fish, and farmed fish

full_output.paper_title: Activity of Antimicrobial Peptides and Ciprofloxacin against Pseudomonas aeruginosa Biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that Pseudomonas aeruginosa did not develop resistance to the antimicrobial peptides melimine or Mel4, unlike ciprofloxacin, which saw a 64-fold increase in MIC after 30 passages. Combining melimine or Mel4 with ciprofloxacin effectively disrupted pre-formed biofilms.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibiofilm activity of melimine, Mel4, and ciprofloxacin using crystal violet staining, confocal microscopy, and measurements of ATP and nucleic acid release.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Fosfomycin and Nitrofurantoin Resistance Mechanisms in Escherichia coli Isolated in Clinical Urine Samples.

glpT.notes: Multiple substitutions detected in both resistant and susceptible isolates

ptsI.notes: Detected in both resistant and susceptible isolates

cyaA.notes: Detected in both resistant and susceptible isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies fosA3 as a novel plasmid-mediated fosfomycin resistance gene in E. coli isolates in Spain. Fosfomycin resistance is primarily due to defects in the UhpT transporter system, while nitrofurantoin resistance involves mutations in nfsA, nfsB, and ribE genes.
full_output.methodology: Analysis of clinical isolates for genetic mutations and resistance mechanisms through sequencing and functional assays.
full_output.sample_size: 22 fosfomycin-resistant E. coli isolates and 22 nitrofurantoin-resistant E. coli isolates

full_output.paper_title: Fatal respiratory infection due to ST308 VIM-1-producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa in a lung transplant recipient: case report and review of the literature.

blaVIM-1.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and detection of carbapenemase activity

blaVIM-2.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and detection of carbapenemase activity

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first fatal infection caused by VIM-1-producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa in a lung transplant recipient, highlighting the significant threat posed by metallo-beta-lactamase (MBL)-producing strains in cystic fibrosis patients.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and epidemiological investigation were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of viral coinfection and macrolide-resistant mycoplasma infection in children with refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia.

A2063G.mechanism: mutation in 23S rRNA gene leading to macrolide resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the A2063G mutation in the 23S rRNA gene of Mycoplasma pneumoniae, which is associated with macrolide resistance. This mutation was found in 56.07% of patients with refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect the A2063G mutation in the 23S rRNA gene of Mycoplasma pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: Wild-type cutoff for Apramycin against Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the aac(3)-IV gene as the primary resistance mechanism against apramycin in E. coli, with a high prevalence in isolates with MICs ≥64 μg/mL.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of resistance genes in E. coli isolates and broth microdilution testing for susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance in Vibrio cholerae: Mechanistic Insights from IncC Plasmid-Mediated Dissemination of a Novel Family of Genomic Islands Inserted at trmE.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mobI_M as a critical gene for the mobilization of the genomic island MGI Vch Hai6 by IncC plasmids, revealing its role in the transfer process.
full_output.methodology: Mobilization assays, complementation experiments, and genetic analysis were conducted to investigate the role of mobI_M in MGI Vch Hai6 mobilization.

full_output.paper_title: The H-NS Regulator Plays a Role in the Stress Induced by Carbapenemase Expression in Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that H-NS helps alleviate stress caused by carbapenemase expression in A. baumannii, particularly for VIM-2 and SPM-1, which cause growth defects and stress. NDM-1 expression did not trigger significant stress.
full_output.methodology: Growth curves, MIC determinations, and genetic manipulation of A. baumannii strains were used to assess the effects of carbapenemase expression and H-NS deficiency.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic plasticity of pathogenic Escherichia coli mediates d-serine tolerance via multiple adaptive mechanisms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies cycA and sstT as critical genes involved in d-serine transport, and their disruption leads to d-serine tolerance in EHEC. Additionally, genomic rearrangements involving cscR and dsdA contribute to d-serine catabolism and tolerance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, transcriptome analysis, and isogenic mutant construction were used to identify and validate the genetic mechanisms of d-serine tolerance in EHEC.

full_output.paper_title: Making of water soluble curcumin to potentiate conventional antimicrobials by inducing apoptosis-like phenomena among drug-resistant bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that water-soluble curcumin enhances the efficacy of conventional antibiotics like ciprofloxacin, meropenem, and vancomycin against multidrug-resistant bacteria by inducing oxidative stress and membrane permeabilization.
full_output.methodology: The study involved synthesis of water-soluble curcumin, determination of MIC and MBC, biofilm inhibition assays, and evaluation of synergistic effects with antibiotics using confocal microscopy and flow cytometry.

full_output.paper_title: Coagulase-positive methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus circulating in clinical mastitic goats in Bangladesh.

mecA.validation_method: PCR detection of mecA gene in isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in clinical mastitic goats in Bangladesh, with 8.96% of CoPS isolates carrying the mecA gene, which confers resistance to oxacillin and methicillin.
full_output.methodology: PCR for nuc gene and mecA gene detection, antimicrobial susceptibility testing by disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Detection and antibiotic resistance of Mycoplasma gallisepticum and Mycoplasma synoviae among chicken flocks in Egypt.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of mgc2 and gapA virulence genes in Mycoplasma gallisepticum isolates and the vlhA virulence gene in Mycoplasma synoviae isolates. Tiamulin and spiramycin were found to be effective against MG and MS infections, respectively.
full_output.methodology: PCR and MIC testing were used to identify and assess the antibiotic resistance of Mycoplasma isolates.

full_output.paper_title: β-lactam resistance in bacteria associated with subclinical mastitis in goats in Thika Subcounty, Kenya.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of β-lactam resistance in bacteria isolated from goats with subclinical mastitis in Thika Subcounty, Kenya. Key findings include the resistance of various bacterial species such as Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and others to β-lactam antibiotics like penicillin G, cephalexin, cefoxitin, and cefotaxime.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar disk diffusion method for antibiotic susceptibility testing and the California mastitis test for screening subclinical mastitis.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of Raoultella ornithinolytica isolated from chicken products in Alexandria, Egypt.
full_output.key_findings: Three isolates of Raoultella ornithinolytica were identified from chicken products in Egypt, demonstrating resistance to several antibiotics including flucloxacillin, erythromycin, penicillin, amoxicillin-clavulanate, and bacitracin, with intermediate sensitivity to others.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing via disk diffusion and identification using API 20E and MALDI-TOF MS.

full_output.paper_title: Hybrid Hydrogels for Synergistic Periodontal Antibacterial Treatment with Sustained Drug Release and NIR-Responsive Photothermal Effect.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a hybrid hydrogel system combining mesoporous silica-coated gold nanobipyramids (Au NBPs@SiO2) with gelatin methacrylate (GelMA) for periodontal antibacterial treatment. The system provides sustained release of minocycline and exhibits photothermal antibacterial effects, showing high efficacy against Porphyromonas gingivalis.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and characterization of Au NBPs@SiO2 and GelMA-Au NBPs@SiO2 hybrids, evaluation of drug release profiles, photothermal properties, and in vitro antibacterial effects against P. gingivalis.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution and Molecular Characterization of Resistance Gene Cassettes Containing Class 1 Integrons in Multi-Drug Resistant (MDR) Clinical Isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several resistance gene cassettes within class 1 integrons in multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates, including aadB, aacA4, blaOXA-10, aacA5, cmlA5, and VIM-1, which confer resistance to various antibiotics such as aminoglycosides, beta-lactams, and chloramphenicol.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing analysis were used to detect and characterize resistance gene cassettes in class 1 integrons from Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Property of Halogenated Catechols.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that halogenated dopamine methacrylamide (DMA) derivatives exhibit potent antimicrobial activity against multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, including MRSA, VRE, PAER, AB, and CRKP. The antimicrobial mechanism involves the inhibition of bacterial fatty acid synthesis via targeting the FabI enzyme.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of halogenated DMA derivatives, preparation of hydrogels, antimicrobial testing, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Surveillance of Streptococcus pyogenes Strains Causing Invasive Disease, United States, 2016-2017.

pbp2x.notes: Found in two nearly isogenic strains with elevated MICs.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified erythromycin resistance determinants (ermB, ermT, ermTR), tetracycline resistance (tet), and fluoroquinolone resistance (parC and gyrA mutations) in Streptococcus pyogenes isolates from the United States.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis were used to identify antimicrobial resistance determinants and expanded lineages in S. pyogenes isolates.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro Activity of Robenidine Analog NCL195 in Combination With Outer Membrane Permeabilizers Against Gram-Negative Bacterial Pathogens and Impact on Systemic Gram-Positive Bacterial Infection in Mice.
full_output.key_findings: NCL195 showed antimicrobial activity against Neisseria meningitidis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and synergistic activity when combined with EDTA, PMBN, or PMB against various Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, synergy testing, and time-dependent killing assays were performed.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Susceptibility and Virulence of mcr-1-Positive Enterobacteriaceae in China, a Multicenter Longitudinal Epidemiological Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 17 mcr-1-positive Enterobacteriaceae isolates, primarily Escherichia coli, exhibiting low-level colistin resistance. These isolates carried various antimicrobial resistance genes, including blaTEM-1B, blaCTX-M-14, and others.
full_output.methodology: PCR, MIC testing, whole-genome sequencing, and plasmid analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Novel Antimicrobial Cellulose Fleece Inhibits Growth of Human-Derived Biofilm-Forming Staphylococci During the SIRIUS19 Simulated Space Mission.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of antimicrobial coatings AGXX® and GOX in inhibiting the growth of human-derived biofilm-forming Staphylococci during a simulated space mission. AGXX® completely inhibited the growth of these opportunistic pathogens on all tested surface materials, while GOX effectively immobilized bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study used cultivation-based methods and 16S rRNA gene sequencing to analyze bacterial communities on antimicrobial and uncoated surfaces. Antibiotic resistance profiles and biofilm formation were also assessed.
full_output.sample_size: 80 bacterial isolates from SIRIUS module and 103 isolates from control environment

full_output.paper_title: 2,4-Di-Tert-Butylphenol Isolated From an Endophytic Fungus, Daldinia eschscholtzii, Reduces Virulence and Quorum Sensing in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 2,4-DBP as a quorum sensing inhibitor that reduces virulence factors and biofilm formation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, showing synergistic effects with ampicillin.
full_output.methodology: The study uses agar well diffusion, HPLC, and qRT-PCR to identify and characterize 2,4-DBP's anti-quorum sensing and anti-biofilm properties.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical and Microbiological Characterization of Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis Caused by Aspergillus lentulus in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes six cases of invasive pulmonary aspergillosis caused by Aspergillus lentulus in China, highlighting its resistance to multiple antifungal drugs including amphotericin B, itraconazole, voriconazole, and posaconazole, but susceptibility to echinocandins.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular identification techniques, antifungal susceptibility testing, and phylogenetic analysis to characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: ChromID(®) CARBA Agar Fails to Detect Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacteriaceae With Slightly Reduced Susceptibility to Carbapenems.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that ChromID(®) CARBA agar fails to detect carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae with slightly reduced susceptibility to carbapenems, highlighting the need for alternative selective media such as MacConkey agar supplemented with cefotaxime and meropenem for reliable detection.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the effectiveness of different selective media for detecting carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae through growth experiments and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Surveillance of Ceftriaxone-Resistant Escherichia coli in Western New York Suggests the Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase bla (CTX-M-27) Is Emerging on Distinct Plasmids in ST38.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the emergence of the bla CTX-M-27 gene in Escherichia coli ST38, highlighting its association with distinct plasmids and increased resistance to cephalosporins and aztreonam.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatic analysis were used to characterize the genomic epidemiology of ceftriaxone-resistant E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance and Virulence-Associated Markers in Campylobacter Strains From Diarrheic and Non-diarrheic Humans in Poland.

full_output.paper_title: The Impact of Mercury Selection and Conjugative Genetic Elements on Community Structure and Resistance Gene Transfer.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the integration of a 52 kb integrative and conjugative element (ICE6775) encoding mercury resistance into the Pseudomonas fluorescens SBW25 chromosome, which conferred specific mercury resistance.

full_output.sample_size: Six replicate populations were established for each combination of treatments.

full_output.paper_title: Frequency of Antimicrobial Resistance Genes in Salmonella From Brazil by in silico Whole-Genome Sequencing Analysis: An Overview of the Last Four Decades.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified 65 distinct antimicrobial resistance genes in Salmonella isolates from Brazil, with a focus on aminoglycoside, tetracycline, and beta-lactam resistance genes. Key genes included aac(3)-IIa, aac(6')-Ib, tet(A), bla CMY–2, sul2, and fosA7. Mutations in gyrA and parC were linked to fluoroquinolone resistance, while a mutation in pmrA was associated with colistin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and in silico analysis using STARAMR and ResFinder databases.

full_output.paper_title: Analytical Performance Validation of Next-Generation Sequencing Based Clinical Microbiology Assays Using a K-mer Analysis Workflow.
full_output.key_findings: The study validated the analytical performance of a k-mer based workflow for clinical microbiology assays, including AMR marker detection, demonstrating high repeatability, reproducibility, and accuracy compared to alignment-based workflows.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a k-mer based workflow for WGS analysis, validated through comparative assessment with alignment-based methods, focusing on AMR marker detection and other clinical microbiology assays.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of the IncX3 Plasmid Producing bla (NDM-7) From Klebsiella pneumoniae ST34.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first characterization of the blaNDM-7 gene in a Klebsiella pneumoniae ST34 strain, highlighting its location on an IncX3 plasmid and its ability to confer resistance to carbapenems through horizontal transfer.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, conjugation and transformation experiments, PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic Effect between Usnic Acid and Polymyxin B against Resistant Clinical Isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified that all 104 Stenotrophomonas maltophilia strains were susceptible to levofloxacin, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, and minocycline. Mutations in the rmlA and spgM genes were found to be significantly different between strains with strong and weak biofilm formation abilities.
full_output.methodology: The study used MLST, PFGE, PCR, and biofilm formation assays to analyze the molecular epidemiology and resistance mechanisms of S. maltophilia in pediatric patients.

full_output.paper_title: Trends in the Prevalence and Antibiotic Resistance of Non-tuberculous Mycobacteria in Mainland China, 2000-2019: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the increasing prevalence of non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) in mainland China, with Mycobacterium abscessus and Mycobacterium avium complex being the most common species. NTM showed general sensitivity to ethambutol, linezolid, clofazimine, amikacin, tobramycin, and clarithromycin, but resistance was widespread.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on NTM prevalence and antibiotic resistance in mainland China from 2000 to 2019.

full_output.key_findings: The study presents a rapid carbapenemase detection method called CIM B.S, which uses Bacillus stearothermophilus as an indicator strain. It effectively identifies carbapenemase-producing bacteria, showing high sensitivity and specificity for Enterobacteriaceae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the CIM B.S method using 134 clinical isolates, comparing its performance with existing methods like mCIM and Blue-Carba.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations in the TolC Periplasmic Domain Affect Substrate Specificity of the AcrAB-TolC Pump.

full_output.key_findings: Mutations in the TolC periplasmic domain, particularly D371V, affect substrate specificity of the AcrAB-TolC pump, leading to hyper-susceptibility to efflux substrates.
full_output.methodology: Site-directed mutagenesis, MIC assays, growth kinetics, and dye efflux assays were used to analyze the effects of TolC mutations on efflux activity and substrate specificity.

full_output.paper_title: Conjugative Coupling Proteins and the Role of Their Domains in Conjugation, Secondary Structure and in vivo Subcellular Location.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the T4CPs TraJ pKM101 and MobB CloDF13, focusing on the role of their transmembrane domains (TMD) in conjugation and subcellular localization. A chimeric protein combining the TMD of TraJ pKM101 with the cytosolic domain of TrwB R388 was created, and a TMD deletion mutant of MobB CloDF13 was analyzed. The results demonstrate that the TMD of MobB CloDF13 is essential for plasmid mobilization, whereas the TMD of TrwB R388 influences its subcellular localization and activity.
full_output.methodology: Protein cloning, purification, mating assays, infrared spectroscopy, and subcellular localization studies.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Drug Resistance in Salmonella enteritidis Isolated From Edible Snakes With Pneumonia and Its Pathogenicity in Chickens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antimicrobial resistance genes in Salmonella enteritidis isolated from edible snakes, including blaTEM, qnrD, aadA1, catA1, sulI, and sulII. These genes confer resistance to various antibiotics such as beta-lactams, quinolones, aminoglycosides, chloramphenicol, and sulfonamides.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect antimicrobial resistance genes in the isolated Salmonella enteritidis strains.

full_output.paper_title: Self-targeting, zwitterionic micellar dispersants enhance antibiotic killing of infectious biofilms-An intravital imaging study in mice.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents zwitterionic micelles (ZW-MSPMs) as a novel synthetic dispersant that enhances antibiotic efficacy against staphylococcal biofilms by disrupting the extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix, thereby improving antibiotic penetration and bacterial killing.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro and in vivo experiments, including intravital imaging, to evaluate the effectiveness of ZW-MSPMs in dispersing biofilms and enhancing antibiotic efficacy.

full_output.paper_title: Clonal and drug resistance dynamics of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in pediatric populations in China.

full_output.paper_title: Brief Report: Cessation of Long-Term Cotrimoxazole Prophylaxis in HIV-Infected Children Does Not Alter the Carriage of Antimicrobial Resistance Genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that cessation of long-term cotrimoxazole prophylaxis in HIV-infected children did not significantly alter the carriage of antimicrobial resistance genes. full_output.paper_title: In vitro and in vivo growth inhibitory activities of cryptolepine hydrate against several Babesia species and Theileria equi.

full_output.paper_title: Structural insight into the membrane targeting domain of the Legionella deAMPylase SidD.

full_output.paper_title: Dual antibacterial drug-loaded nanoparticles synergistically improve treatment of Streptococcus mutans biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Stewardship Program, COVID-19, and Infection Control: Spread of Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella Pneumoniae Colonization in ICU COVID-19 Patients. What Did Not Work?
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the spread of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CR-Kp) in an ICU during the COVID-19 pandemic, identifying various carbapenemase genes including KPC, OXA-48-like, OXA-163, NDM, and VIM as contributors to resistance.
full_output.methodology: Active surveillance through rectal swabs and clinical cultures, detection of carbapenemase genes via immunochromatography, and analysis of CRE colonization and acquisition rates.

full_output.paper_title: Functional Analysis of P450 Monooxygenase SrrO in the Biosynthesis of Butenolide-Type Signaling Molecules in Streptomycesrochei.

The srrO mutant KA54 produced 6′-deoxo-SRB1 and 6′-deoxo-SRB2, which showed reduced ligand affinity to the SRB receptor SrrA.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiologic, Phenotypic, and Structural Characterization of Aminoglycoside-Resistance Gene aac(3)-IV.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies aac(3)-IV as the primary gene responsible for apramycin resistance, demonstrating its role in conferring resistance to multiple aminoglycosides. full_output.paper_title: Isolation and characterization of a novel bacterial strain from a Tris-Acetate-Phosphate agar medium plate of the green micro-alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii that can utilize common environmental pollutants as a carbon source.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel bacterial strain, LMJ, capable of utilizing various environmental pollutants as a carbon source. LMJ exhibits sensitivity to penicillin and chloramphenicol, and it produces pyomelanin, a brown-black pigment.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation, physiological, and biochemical characterization of LMJ, including antibiotic susceptibility testing and 16S rRNA gene sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Benzalkonium Chloride Resistance in Staphylococcus epidermidis on the Ocular Surface of Glaucoma Patients Under Long-Term Administration of Eye Drops.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies qacA/B and qacC/smr efflux pump genes as contributors to benzalkonium chloride resistance in Staphylococcus epidermidis isolated from glaucoma patients using long-term eye drops.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and MIC testing were used to analyze the presence of qacA/B and qacC/smr genes and their association with benzalkonium chloride resistance.

full_output.paper_title: The Clinical and Molecular Epidemiology of Noncarbapenemase-Producing Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacteriaceae: A Case-Case-Control Matched Analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple beta-lactamase genes (bla OXA-1, bla TEM-1, bla SHV, bla CTX-M-15) and efflux pump genes (acrB, oqxAB) in noncarbapenemase-producing carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (non-CP-CRE) isolates, indicating that these genes contribute to carbapenem resistance through multiple mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing of 13 non-CP-CRE isolates was performed to analyze the resistome and phylogeny.

full_output.paper_title: Eight-year trends in the relative isolation frequency and antimicrobial susceptibility among bloodstream isolates from Greek hospitals: data from the Greek Electronic System for the Surveillance of Antimicrobial Resistance - WHONET-Greece, 2010 to 2017.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified increasing trends in antimicrobial resistance among bloodstream isolates in Greek hospitals from 2010 to 2017, particularly for Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Acinetobacter baumannii. Notably, resistance to carbapenems, fluoroquinolones, and aminoglycosides increased significantly, highlighting the need for improved surveillance and targeted interventions.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed antimicrobial susceptibility data from 50,488 bloodstream isolates collected from 25 tertiary hospitals in Greece between 2010 and 2017 using the WHONET-Greece surveillance system.

full_output.paper_title: RamA, a transcriptional regulator conferring florfenicol resistance in Leclercia adecarboxylata R25.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ramA as a transcriptional regulator that confers resistance to florfenicol and other antibiotics in Leclercia adecarboxylata R25 by regulating RND efflux pump genes.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, gene knockout, complementation, and MIC detection were used to determine the function of the resistance-related gene.

full_output.paper_title: Selection of High-Affinity RNA Aptamers That Distinguish between Doxycycline and Tetracycline.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the selection and characterization of high-affinity RNA aptamers that specifically bind doxycycline (dox) and distinguish it from tetracycline (tet). These aptamers exhibit high specificity and affinity for dox, with dissociation constants as low as 3 nM, and do not bind tet. The aptamers also enhance fluorescence upon binding to dox, making them suitable for biosensing applications.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized SELEX (Systematic Evolution of Ligands by EXponential enrichment) to select RNA aptamers, along with fluorescence titration spectroscopy, in-gel fluorescence assays, and surface plasmon resonance to analyze binding characteristics.

full_output.key_findings: The study presents a rapid phenotypic drug susceptibility test for mycobacteria using magnetic nanoparticle-based concentration and microchannel electrical impedance spectroscopy (m-EIS).

full_output.paper_title: METTL3 potentiates resistance to cisplatin through m(6) A modification of TFAP2C in seminoma.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies METTL3, IGF2BP1, and TFAP2C as critical players in cisplatin resistance in seminoma through m6A modification and mRNA stability mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study employed immunoblotting, qPCR, RNA immunoprecipitation, and cell viability assays to explore the role of METTL3, IGF2BP1, and TFAP2C in cisplatin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Structure of the 70S Ribosome from the Human Pathogen Acinetobacter baumannii in Complex with Clinically Relevant Antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents high-resolution structures of the 70S ribosome from Acinetobacter baumannii in complex with amikacin and tigecycline, revealing unique structural features that could inform the design of new antibiotics against multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Cryo-electron microscopy was used to determine the structures of the ribosome in complex with the antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Predicting β-lactam resistance using whole genome sequencing in Klebsiella pneumoniae: the challenge of β-lactamase inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several β-lactamase genes, including bla NDM-1, bla OXA-48, bla KPC-8, and bla KPC-14, which confer resistance to various β-lactam antibiotics. It also highlights the importance of considering complex β-lactamase backgrounds when predicting antimicrobial resistance using whole-genome sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Quantitative benzimidazole resistance and fitness effects of parasitic nematode beta-tubulin alleles.

full_output.methodology: In silico analysis, PCR, sequencing, and conjugation experiments were used to validate the presence and functionality of the lsa(C) gene.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Activity of Bacillus inaquosorum Strain T1 against pirAB(Vp)-Bearing Vibrio parahaemolyticus: Genetic and Physiological Characterization.

full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR assay was used to detect the mecA gene in S. sciuri isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Polymyxin B(1) and E(2) From Paenibacillus polymyxa Y-1 for Controlling Rice Bacterial Disease.
full_output.key_findings: Polymyxin B1 and E2 from Paenibacillus polymyxa Y-1 exhibit strong antibacterial activity against Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae and Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzicola, showing potential as new microbial pesticides for controlling rice bacterial diseases.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity assays, SEM, conductivity detection, biofilm formation detection, EPS detection, and proteomic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance of Escherichia coli, Enterobacter spp., Klebsiella pneumoniae and Enterococcus spp. isolated from the feces of giant panda.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antimicrobial resistance genes in E. coli, Enterobacter spp., Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Enterococcus spp. isolated from giant panda feces, highlighting the prevalence of multidrug-resistant strains and the potential risk to captive giant pandas.
full_output.methodology: The study involved antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR detection of resistance genes, and whole-genome sequencing of a multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial Contamination and Susceptibility Pattern Among Blood and Blood Components Using Divergent and Non-Divergent Collection Methods at Armed Forces Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that bacterial contamination in blood and blood components was higher with the non-diverging collection method. Staphylococcus epidermidis was the most commonly isolated bacterium, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa showed resistance to gentamicin.
full_output.methodology: The study involved culturing blood and blood components and performing antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antibacterial response of Helicobacter pylori to daphnetin using quantitative proteomics, identifying changes in protein expression related to metabolism, membrane structure, nucleic acid and protein synthesis, ion binding, colonization, and stress responses.
full_output.methodology: Label-free quantitative proteomics and PRM were used to analyze protein expression changes in daphnetin-treated H. pylori.

full_output.key_findings: The study introduces five new destination vectors for Chlamydomonas reinhardtii that confer resistance to various antibiotics, facilitating modular cloning and reducing the time required for construct assembly and transformation.

full_output.paper_title: Ligand-based design and synthesis of N'-Benzylidene-3,4-dimethoxybenzohydrazide derivatives as potential antimicrobial agents; evaluation by in vitro, in vivo, and in silico approaches with SAR studies.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on designing and synthesizing N'-benzylidene-3,4-dimethoxybenzohydrazide derivatives as potential antimicrobial agents targeting the multidrug efflux pump (MATE). Compounds 4h and 4i showed the most promising antibacterial and antifungal activities, with 4h demonstrating significant improvements in renal and liver parameters in infected rats.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of compounds, in vitro and in vivo biological evaluations, molecular docking, and ADMET studies to assess the antimicrobial and pharmacokinetic properties of the synthesized derivatives.

full_output.paper_title: Metagenomic Insights Into the Changes of Antibiotic Resistance and Pathogenicity Factor Pools Upon Thermophilic Composting of Human Excreta.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a decrease in the abundance of various antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) during thermophilic composting of human excreta, including genes conferring resistance to aminoglycosides, macrolides, sulfonamides, and tetracyclines.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing and qPCR analysis were used to assess the abundance of ARGs and pathogenicity factors in compost samples before and after thermophilic composting.

full_output.paper_title: Elevated Levels of Three Reactive Oxygen Species and Fe(II) in the Antibiotic-Surviving Population of Mycobacteria Facilitate De Novo Emergence of Genetic Resisters to Antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the rpoB gene, specifically in the rifampicin resistance determining region (RRDR), which are associated with the de novo emergence of rifampicin-resistant mycobacterial strains. These mutations were found to be caused by elevated levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and Fe(II) in the antibiotic-surviving population.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized whole-genome sequencing and various biochemical assays to analyze the mutations in the rpoB gene and their association with rifampicin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the microbial spectrum and antibiotic resistance patterns in patients with solid malignancies, highlighting significant resistance to various antibiotics among Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, as well as Candida species.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of blood culture data from patients with solid malignancies, including antimicrobial susceptibility testing and statistical analysis of resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: MCR-1-dependent lipid remodelling compromises the viability of Gram-negative bacteria.

mcr-1.validation_method: Expression in E. coli and K. pneumonia, OM permeability assays

full_output.key_findings: MCR-1 increases outer membrane permeability and causes cell shrinkage and death in stationary phase, leading to reduced viability of Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Gene expression, OM permeability assays, microscopy, and genetic manipulation.

full_output.paper_title: Current treatments for biofilm-associated periprosthetic joint infection and new potential strategies.
full_output.key_findings: This review discusses various strategies for combating biofilm-associated periprosthetic joint infections (PJI), including electrochemical methods, small molecule inhibitors, biologics, and targeting biofilm membrane components. It highlights the challenges posed by biofilms and explores potential treatments that could improve implant retention and reduce infection recurrence.
full_output.methodology: Review of existing literature and experimental studies on biofilm-targeting treatments for PJI.

full_output.paper_title: Infectious Diseases Society of America 2022 Guidance on the Treatment of Extended-Spectrum β-lactamase Producing Enterobacterales (ESBL-E), Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales (CRE), and Pseudomonas aeruginosa with Difficult-to-Treat Resistance (DTR-P. aeruginosa).
full_output.key_findings: The paper provides updated guidance on the treatment of infections caused by extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Enterobacterales (ESBL-E), carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE), and Pseudomonas aeruginosa with difficult-to-treat resistance (DTR-P. aeruginosa).
full_output.methodology: The paper is a guideline document based on a comprehensive review of the literature, clinical experience, and expert opinion.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the transtympanic permeation of liposome-encapsulated pneumococcal endolysin MSlys and found that PEGylated liposomes enhanced its permeation across the tympanic membrane, reducing pneumococcal cell load. However, antipneumococcal activity diminished after 4 hours due to endolysin hydrolysis.
full_output.methodology: Ex vivo permeation studies using Franz diffusion cells, protein quantification via spectrofluorimetry, and SDS-PAGE analysis for protein integrity.

full_output.paper_title: Potential cannabidiol (CBD) repurposing as antibacterial and promising therapy of CBD plus polymyxin B (PB) against PB-resistant gram-negative bacilli.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that cannabidiol (CBD) exhibits antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria, certain Gram-negative diplococci, and Mycobacterium tuberculosis, but not against Gram-negative bacilli. However, the combination of CBD and polymyxin B (PB) showed significant antibacterial activity against PB-resistant Gram-negative bacilli, including Klebsiella pneumoniae, Escherichia coli, and Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized broth microdilution, checkerboard assays, and time-kill assays to evaluate the antibacterial activity of CBD and its combination with PB.

full_output.paper_title: Therapeutic stem cell-derived alveolar-like macrophages display bactericidal effects and resolve Pseudomonas aeruginosa-induced lung injury.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that stem cell-derived alveolar-like macrophages (ALMs) exhibit bactericidal effects against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli, and Staphylococcus aureus, both in vitro and in vivo. These ALMs can internalize and kill bacteria, reducing lung injury caused by P. aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro bactericidal assays, flow cytometry, and in vivo models to evaluate the antibacterial properties of ALMs.

full_output.paper_title: The Cationic Antimicrobial Peptide Activity of Lysozyme Reduces Viable Enterococcus faecalis Cells in Biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: Lysozyme exhibits bactericidal activity against E. faecalis biofilms, and the eep gene is involved in lysozyme resistance in E. faecalis.
full_output.methodology: Experimental validation of lysozyme's effect on E. faecalis biofilms and genetic analysis of eep's role in resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Co-Operative Biofilm Interactions between Aspergillus fumigatus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa through Secreted Galactosaminogalactan Exopolysaccharide.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the role of the deacetylase Agd3 in the de-N-acetylation of galactosaminogalactan (GAG) in Aspergillus fumigatus, which is essential for Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm adherence and resistance to colistin.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, confocal microscopy, and biochemical assays were used to investigate the role of GAG and Agd3 in biofilm interactions between A. fumigatus and P. aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: New Insights into the Mechanism of Action of PirAB from Vibrio Parahaemolyticus.

full_output.methodology: Histopathological analysis, molecular detection, and experimental infection studies were used to investigate the role of the PirAB toxin in AHPND.

full_output.paper_title: High level of persister frequency in clinical staphylococcal isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that clinical staphylococcal isolates exhibit high persister frequency, with icaAD genes playing a significant role in persister formation. However, no specific AMR genes or mutations were characterized in this paper.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 375 clinical staphylococcal isolates using techniques such as tissue culture plate method for biofilm detection, disc diffusion for antibiotic susceptibility, and agar dilution for MIC determination.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a novel drug-resistant community-acquired Nocardia spp. in a patient with bronchiectasis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel Nocardia species, Nocardia guangzhouensis GZ2020T, which exhibits resistance to multiple antibiotics, including sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim, amikacin, and imipenem, but is susceptible to linezolid and possibly moxifloxacin.
full_output.methodology: The study involved genome sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and in vivo pathogenicity testing in mice.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several carbapenemase-producing E. coli strains, including OXA-181, NDM-5, OXA-48, and KPC-2, highlighting their global distribution and association with specific sequence types.

full_output.paper_title: Structure-Based Design of α-Substituted Mercaptoacetamides as Inhibitors of the Virulence Factor LasB from Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the design and evaluation of α-benzyl-N-aryl mercaptoacetamide derivatives as inhibitors of the virulence factor LasB from Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Several compounds, including 12, 13, and 23, were identified as potent inhibitors of LasB with good selectivity against human off-targets.
full_output.methodology: The study employed structure-based design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of mercaptoacetamide derivatives to inhibit LasB, a virulence factor of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaOXA-40 and blaOXA-23 genes as the primary contributors to carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii clinical strains, demonstrating the effectiveness of molecular methods for rapid detection.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular biology-based approaches, including conventional and real-time PCR, to detect and characterize blaOXA genes in carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii strains.

full_output.methodology: The study used purified PBP2a variants and whole-cell binding assays with Bocillin-FL, along with flow cytometry to assess binding differences between NaHCO3-responsive and non-responsive MRSA strains.

full_output.paper_title: Bovine Respiratory Disease: Conventional to Culture-Independent Approaches to Studying Antimicrobial Resistance in North America.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes various antimicrobial resistance genes in bovine respiratory disease pathogens, highlighting the role of integrative and conjugative elements in the dissemination of resistance genes. It identifies specific genes such as bla-oxa-2, erm(42), and sul2 associated with resistance to beta-lactams, macrolides, and sulfonamides, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Genome analysis and metagenomic studies were used to identify and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in bovine respiratory disease pathogens.
full_output.sample_size: Various studies involving numerous isolates from different locations in North America.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmid-Mediated Transfer of Antibiotic Resistance Genes in Soil.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the role of plasmids in the transfer of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in soil environments, highlighting the presence of various resistance genes such as blaTEM, blaOXA, tetA, tetB, tetK, qnrS, arr-3, aacA, intI, intII, sulI, sulII, sulIII, and others. It emphasizes the importance of plasmid-mediated transfer in the spread of ARGs under different environmental conditions.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews current scenarios of plasmid-mediated migration and transmission of ARGs, summarizes methods for plasmid extraction and analysis, and discusses the mechanism of plasmid splice transfer using the F factor as an example.
