It also showed that Ag-MET-Ns effectively inhibited biofilm formation and staphyloxanthin production, indicating its potential as an anti-virulence agent against multidrug-resistant S. aureus.
full_output.methodology: The study used qRT-PCR to measure gene expression and in vitro assays to evaluate biofilm and staphyloxanthin inhibition by the tested agents.

full_output.paper_title: Insight into the impacts and mechanisms of ketone stress on the antibiotic resistance in Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that exposure to methylisobutanone (MIBK) affects the antibiotic resistance in Escherichia coli, particularly highlighting the role of the ampR gene in conferring ampicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR, transformation experiments, and MIC determination to assess the impact of MIBK on antibiotic resistance in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Genome-wide analysis of Brucella melitensis genes required throughout intranasal infection in mice.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes essential for Brucella melitensis survival in different environments, highlighting the role of LPS biosynthesis and metabolic pathways in immune evasion and infection dynamics.
full_output.methodology: Transposon sequencing (Tn-seq) was used to identify genes critical for B. melitensis survival in macrophages and lung tissues, along with functional validation through mutant construction and CFU analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid detection of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in positive blood-cultures by recombinase polymerase amplification combined with lateral flow strip.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed an RPA-LF test for the rapid detection of MRSA in positive blood-cultures, targeting the nuc and mecA genes. The test showed high sensitivity and specificity for identifying S. aureus and methicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The RPA-LF test was evaluated using 60 positive blood-culture samples, with results compared to conventional methods.

full_output.paper_title: Sensitivity of different DNA extraction methods and PCR to detect resistance in patients with leprosy stratified by the bacilloscopic index.

full_output.paper_title: Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase inhibition reveals metabolic vulnerability in chronic myeloid leukemia.

full_output.paper_title: Gram-negative multidrug-resistant organisms were dominant in neurorehabilitation ward patients in a general hospital in southwest China.

These organisms exhibited high resistance to various antibiotics, including carbapenems, cephalosporins, and fluoroquinolones.

full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews evidence of antibacterial resistance following mass drug administration with azithromycin, highlighting the emergence of resistance mechanisms such as erm genes, mcr-1, and NDM-1 in various bacterial species.

full_output.sample_size: Multiple studies with varying sample sizes.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic Microbicidal Effect of AUR and PEITC Against Staphylococcus aureus Skin Infection.

full_output.paper_title: Copper Acts Synergistically With Fluconazole in Candida glabrata by Compromising Drug Efflux, Sterol Metabolism, and Zinc Homeostasis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CTX-M-55, bla CTX-M-14, and bla CTX-M-65 as the most prevalent CTX-M variants in S. Typhimurium isolates from diarrhoeal outpatients in Guangdong, China. It also reported the first detection of bla TEM-141 in S. Typhimurium.
full_output.methodology: PCR, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PFGE, WGS, and phylogenetic analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in 3GC-resistant Enterobacteriaceae isolated from yellow-legged gull chicks, including beta-lactamase genes (blaCTX-M, blaSHV, blaTEM, blaCMY) and sulfonamide resistance genes (sul1, sul2, sul3). Trimethoprim-resistant dihydrofolate reductase genes (drf-A1, drf-A5, drf-A17) were also detected.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and resistome analysis using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD) and Resistance Gene Identifier (RGI).

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Activity of Medicinal Plants against Uropathogenic Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews the antibacterial activity of various medicinal plants against uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC), focusing on their mechanisms of action and potential as alternatives to conventional antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Literature review and analysis of in vitro and in vivo studies on the antibacterial effects of medicinal plants against UPEC.

full_output.paper_title: Strong selective environments determine evolutionary outcome in time-dependent fitness seascapes.

rpoB.notes: Mutations in rpoB conferred resistance to nalidixic acid and spectinomycin.

nadR.notes: Mutations in nadR conferred resistance to spectinomycin.

spoT.notes: Mutations in spoT conferred resistance to spectinomycin.

mreC.notes: Mutations in mreC conferred resistance to nalidixic acid and spectinomycin.

mreD.notes: Mutations in mreD conferred resistance to nalidixic acid and spectinomycin.

acrR.notes: Mutations in acrR conferred resistance to nalidixic acid.

ECB_RS03400.notes: Mutations in ECB_RS03400 conferred resistance to nalidixic acid.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several mutations in genes such as rpoB, nadR, spoT, mreC, mreD, acrR, and ECB_RS03400 that confer resistance to nalidixic acid and spectinomycin in E. coli under different selective pressures.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phenotyping of clones from experimental end-point populations to identify mutations associated with antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Characteristics of Virulence Factors and Prevalence of Virulence Markers in Resistant Escherichia coli from Patients with Gut and Urinary Infections in Lafia, Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several virulence genes including fimH, pap, stb, cs31a, vt2, and east1 in multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli isolates from patients with gut and urinary tract infections in Lafia, Nigeria.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted molecular characterization of virulence markers using PCR and evaluated the prevalence of these genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Non-carbapenemase producing carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from the urinary tract of a dog.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a non-carbapenemase-producing carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolate from a dog's urine, with resistance mechanisms involving efflux pumps (acrAB) and porin gene mutations, along with the presence of bla CMY-2, fosA, and oqxAB genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed on the K. pneumoniae isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance Profiles of Bacteria Isolated from Hotspot Environments in Bahir Dar City, Northwestern Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antibiotic resistance in bacteria isolated from various hotspot environments in Bahir Dar City, Ethiopia, with notable resistance to ampicillin, tetracycline, and other antibiotics. Multi-drug resistance was prevalent, especially in Pseudomonas spp., E. coli, and Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: Bacterial isolates were obtained from waste and wastewater samples, and antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative genomics of Nocardia seriolae reveals recent importation and subsequent widespread dissemination in mariculture farms in the South Central Coast region, Vietnam.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed 20 N. seriolae strains from Vietnam and two from Taiwan, revealing a single, unique clade among Vietnamese strains with minimal genetic diversity. It identified several putative virulence factors and antimicrobial resistance genes, providing insights into the pathogenicity and persistence of this aquatic pathogen.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PFGE, SNP genotyping, and bioinformatic analyses were used to compare N. seriolae strains and identify genetic variations.

full_output.paper_title: Engineering probiotics to inhibit Clostridioides difficile infection by dynamic regulation of intestinal metabolism.

cbh.validation_method: recombinant expression in E. coli Nissle 1917 and in vitro assays

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the bile salt hydrolase Cbh, when expressed in probiotics, effectively deconjugates taurocholate into cholate, thereby inhibiting the germination and growth of Clostridioides difficile. This approach significantly reduces C. difficile toxicity and improves outcomes in a murine model of CDI.
full_output.methodology: Recombinant expression of Cbh in E. coli Nissle 1917, in vitro assays, and in vivo experiments in a murine model of CDI.
full_output.sample_size: n=12 for treatment group, n=7 to n=15 for control groups

full_output.paper_title: Neutralization of ionic interactions by dextran-based single-chain nanoparticles improves tobramycin diffusion into a mature biofilm.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that dextran-based single-chain nanoparticles (SCPNs) enhance tobramycin diffusion into P. aeruginosa biofilms by neutralizing ionic interactions, thereby improving antibiotic efficacy. The combination of SCPNs with DNase I further disrupts the biofilm matrix, increasing the effectiveness of tobramycin.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized SCPNs synthesized from dextran, characterized by dynamic light scattering (DLS) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Antibiotic and DNase I loading capacities were assessed, and biofilm permeability was evaluated using Franz diffusion cells and confocal microscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic analysis of Listeria monocytogenes from US food processing environments reveals a high prevalence of QAC efflux genes but limited evidence of their contribution to environmental persistence.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a high prevalence of QAC efflux genes (bcrABC, qacH, emrE) in Listeria monocytogenes isolates from US food processing environments, but finds limited evidence that these genes directly contribute to environmental persistence.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, BLAST screening, GWAS, and statistical analysis of 4969 Lm isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Stable isotope analysis confirms substantial changes in the fatty acid composition of bacteria treated with antimicrobial random peptide mixtures (RPMs).
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the effects of antimicrobial random peptide mixtures (RPMs) on the fatty acid composition of six plant-pathogenic bacteria. It shows that RPMs induce changes in fatty acid profiles, particularly affecting branched-chain fatty acids (BCFAs) and altering the 13C isotope ratios, indicating metabolic responses to the antimicrobial treatment.
full_output.methodology: The study used stable isotope analysis combined with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC/MS) and gas chromatography-combustion-isotope ratio mass spectrometry (GC-C-IRMS) to analyze fatty acid compositions and isotope ratios in bacteria treated with RPMs.

full_output.paper_title: Tigecycline Suppresses the Virulence Factors of Multidrug-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Allowing Human Neutrophils to Act.
full_output.key_findings: Tigecycline suppresses the virulence factors of multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, including catalase activity and capsule expression, allowing human neutrophils to effectively kill the bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative real-time PCR, catalase activity assay, and microscopy were used to assess the impact of tigecycline on virulence factors of MDRAB.

full_output.paper_title: Thermoresponsive Liposomes for Photo-Triggered Release of Hypericin Cyclodextrin Inclusion Complex for Efficient Antimicrobial Photodynamic Therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed thermoresponsive liposomes (DHβCD-TSL) loaded with hypericin cyclodextrin complex (Hyp-βCD) and the NIR dye DiR for antimicrobial photodynamic therapy. The liposomes showed effective release of Hyp-βCD upon NIR irradiation and demonstrated strong antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus saprophyticus.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the preparation and characterization of liposomes, evaluation of their photothermal and photodynamic properties, and assessment of antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus saprophyticus.

full_output.paper_title: Potentiating hypoxic microenvironment for antibiotic activation by photodynamic therapy to combat bacterial biofilm infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that photodynamic therapy (PDT) can potentiate the hypoxic microenvironment in bacterial biofilms, enhancing the antibacterial activity of metronidazole (MNZ) against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PDT combined with metronidazole-loaded nanoparticles to target MRSA biofilms, evaluating their efficacy through in vitro and in vivo experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and virulence factors in Staphylococcus aureus and other Gram-positive bacteria causing neonatal sepsis in low-resource settings
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various antimicrobial resistance genes in Staphylococcus aureus and other Gram-positive bacteria causing neonatal sepsis, including mecA, tet(K), tet(M), tet(L), aadD, aph(3)-III, ermA, ermC, msrA, mphC, and IS256. These genes confer resistance to multiple antibiotics, highlighting the complexity of antimicrobial resistance in low-resource settings.
full_output.methodology: The study uses PCR, MIC testing, and whole-genome sequencing to characterize antimicrobial resistance genes and virulence factors in Staphylococcus aureus and other Gram-positive bacteria.
full_output.sample_size: 100 S. aureus isolates, 44 CoNS and M. sciuri isolates

full_output.paper_title: Minos: variant adjudication and joint genotyping of cohorts of bacterial genomes.

rpoB.notes: Mutations in the rpoB gene's rrdr region are associated with rifampicin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple mutations in the rpoB gene's rifampicin resistance determining region (RRDR) associated with rifampicin resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including both common and rare variants.
full_output.methodology: Joint genotyping of large M. tuberculosis cohorts using Minos, combined with phenotypic resistance data for rifampicin.

full_output.paper_title: 3D printed PCLA scaffold with nano-hydroxyapatite coating doped green tea EGCG promotes bone growth and inhibits multidrug-resistant bacteria colonization.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the PCLA/KH-EGCG scaffold effectively inhibits methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) colonization and promotes osteoblast proliferation and differentiation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized 3D printing technology to fabricate scaffolds coated with nano-hydroxyapatite and green tea extract (EGCG), followed by in vitro testing for antibacterial and osteogenic properties.

full_output.paper_title: High clustering rate and genotypic drug-susceptibility screening for the newly recommended anti-tuberculosis drugs among global extensively drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.

cycA.evidence_note: The paper mentions that mutations in the cycA gene were found in 153/513 isolates (29.8%) associated with cycloserine resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in Rv0678, Rv1979c, mmpL5, fbiB, ddn, pykA, cycA, ald, and alr genes associated with resistance to bedaquiline, clofazimine, delamanid, pretomanid, and cycloserine in extensively drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.
full_output.methodology: Genotypic drug-susceptibility testing using whole-genome sequencing data.

full_output.paper_title: Assessment of multidrug-resistant Listeria monocytogenes in milk and milk product and One Health perspective.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in Listeria monocytogenes isolates from milk and milk products, including beta-lactamase genes (bla TEM, bla SHV, bla Z), tetracycline resistance genes (tet A, tet D, tet G, tet K, tet M), sulfonamide resistance genes (sul 1, sul 2), and an aminoglycoside resistance gene (aph (3)-IIa (aphA2)).
full_output.methodology: PCR and phenotypic resistance testing were used to identify and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in Listeria monocytogenes isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Exposure of embryonating eggs to Enterococcus faecalis and Escherichia coli potentiates E. coli pathogenicity and increases mortality of neonatal chickens.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the interaction between Enterococcus faecalis and Escherichia coli in chicken embryos and their impact on neonatal chicken mortality, highlighting the role of E. faecalis in increasing pathogenicity and mortality when co-infected with E. coli.
full_output.methodology: The study used experimental challenges with E. faecalis and E. coli isolates, bacterial isolation, molecular screening, and histopathological examinations to analyze the effects of co-infection on chicken embryos and neonatal chicks.

full_output.paper_title: Overcoming addition of phosphoethanolamine to lipid A mediated colistin resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii clinical isolates with colistin-sulbactam combination therapy.
Essential oil-mediated biocompatible magnesium nanoparticles with enhanced antibacterial, antifungal, and photocatalytic efficacies.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the antibacterial, antifungal, and photocatalytic properties of magnesium nanoparticles (MgNPs) synthesized using essential oil from Cymbopogon flexuosus. The MgNPs exhibit significant antimicrobial activity against S. aureus and E. coli, as well as antifungal activity against F. oxysporum. Additionally, the MgNPs show high photocatalytic efficiency in degrading methylene blue under sunlight.
full_output.methodology: The study uses UV-visible spectroscopy, FTIR, XRD, TEM, and XPS to analyze the physicochemical properties of the MgNPs. Antimicrobial and antifungal activities were assessed using well diffusion assays, and photocatalytic efficiency was evaluated by measuring the degradation of methylene blue under sunlight.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical impact of and microbiological risk factors for qacA/B positivity in ICU-acquired ST5-methicillin-resistant SCCmec type II Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies qacA/B as a gene associated with chlorhexidine tolerance in ST5-MRSA-II, highlighting its role in clinical outcomes and resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of MRSA isolates from ICU patients, including PCR and MIC testing for resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Vision Defense: Efficient Antibacterial AIEgens Induced Early Immune Response for Bacterial Endophthalmitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a cationic aggregation-induced emission luminogen (TTPy) for the treatment of bacterial endophthalmitis, demonstrating its effectiveness in killing Staphylococcus aureus and inducing an early immune response, thereby reducing inflammation and protecting the retina.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized photodynamic therapy with TTPy, assessing its antibacterial effects through various in vitro and in vivo experiments, including bacterial culture, fluorescence imaging, and histological analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Application of multiplex amplicon deep-sequencing (MAD-seq) to screen for putative drug resistance markers in the Necator americanus isotype-1 β-tubulin gene.

β-tubulin.notes: No samples contained detectable levels of the F167Y resistance allele.

full_output.key_findings: Three single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) corresponding to resistance-associated mutations (F167Y, E198A, F200Y) within the coding region of the isotype-1 β-tubulin gene were characterized using MAD-seq in 30 matched pre- and post-treatment samples from individuals with persistent infection following therapy.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex amplicon deep sequencing (MAD-seq) was used to screen genomic regions encapsulating putative drug-resistance markers in N. americanus isotype-1 β-tubulin gene.

full_output.paper_title: Hik28-dependent and Hik28-independent ABC transporters were revealed by proteome-wide analysis of ΔHik28 under combined stress.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Hik28-dependent and Hik28-independent ABC transporters in Synechocystis sp. PCC6803 under combined stress conditions, highlighting the role of Hik28 in regulating these transporters.
full_output.methodology: Proteome-wide analysis using LC-MS/MS and yeast two-hybrid assays.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and factors associated with faecal carriage of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Enterobacterales among peripartum women in the community in Cambodia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of ESBL-producing Enterobacterales in peripartum women in Cambodia, with bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-55, and bla CTX-M-27 being the most common ESBL genes. Additionally, bla NDM-1, bla NDM-5, and bla NDM-6 carbapenemase genes, as well as mcr-1 and mcr-3 colistin resistance genes, were detected in the isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and whole genome sequencing were used to characterize ESBL and carbapenemase genes in isolates from peripartum women.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus isolates in bloodstream infections among patients with hematologic diseases. It found that ciprofloxacin prophylaxis was associated with increased ESBL production in Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of bloodstream infection episodes in patients with hematologic diseases, including antimicrobial susceptibility testing and statistical analysis of risk factors.

full_output.paper_title: Remdesivir resistance in transplant recipients with persistent COVID-19.

RdRp.notes: mutation in RdRp associated with remdesivir resistance

full_output.key_findings: Two renal transplant recipients developed de novo V792I RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) mutation after remdesivir exposure, which conferred resistance to remdesivir in vitro.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing and bioinformatic analysis of SARS-CoV-2 isolates from transplant recipients.

full_output.paper_title: Effects of LPS Composition in Escherichia coli on Antibacterial Activity and Bacterial Uptake of Antisense Peptide-PNA Conjugates.

arnT.notes: arnT is a regulator, not an AMR gene

eptA.notes: eptA is a regulator, not an AMR gene

surA.notes: surA is a regulator, not an AMR gene

envC.notes: envC is a regulator, not an AMR gene

tolB.notes: tolB is a regulator, not an AMR gene

tolQ.notes: tolQ is a regulator, not an AMR gene

tolR.notes: tolR is a regulator, not an AMR gene

ompT.notes: ompT is a regulator, not an AMR gene

full_output.key_findings: The study investigates how variations in the lipopolysaccharide (LPS) composition of Escherichia coli affect the antibacterial activity and uptake of antisense peptide-PNA conjugates. It identifies that truncation of the LPS inner core significantly increases susceptibility to (KFF)3K-PNA conjugates, while the O-antigen has limited effects on BPP-PNA activity. Additionally, it shows that polymyxin resistance does not lead to resistance against BPP-PNA conjugates.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of MIC assays, time-kill experiments, flow cytometry, and LPS analysis to evaluate the effects of LPS modifications on BPP-PNA activity.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro Susceptibility to β-Lactam Antibiotics and Viability of Neisseria gonorrhoeae Strains Producing Plasmid-Mediated Broad- and Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamases.

blaTEM-1.validation_method: Minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values determined for β-lactam antibiotics

blaTEM-135.mechanism: The Gly238Ser mutation in blaTEM-135 enables hydrolysis of cephalosporins, leading to resistance.
blaTEM-135.validation_method: Minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values determined for β-lactam antibiotics

blaTEM-20.validation_method: Minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values determined for β-lactam antibiotics
blaTEM-20.evidence_note: The study demonstrates that the TEM-20 β-lactamase, encoded by the p bla TEM-20 plasmid, hydrolyzes both penicillins and cephalosporins, leading to resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterized the resistance profiles of Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains carrying plasmid-mediated β-lactamases, including blaTEM-1, blaTEM-135, and blaTEM-20. The TEM-20 β-lactamase was identified as an extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) capable of hydrolyzing both penicillins and cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: Construction of plasmids with different variants of the bla gene, transformation of N. gonorrhoeae strains, and determination of minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) for β-lactam antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Soil Fungi as Biomediator in Silver Nanoparticles Formation and Antimicrobial Efficacy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified three fungal isolates (Phoma sp., Chaetomium globosum, and Chaetomium sp.) capable of synthesizing silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) with antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant bacteria, including Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: The study used 18S rDNA sequencing for fungal identification, extracellular synthesis of AgNPs, and evaluated antibacterial activity via agar well diffusion and MIC/MBC assays.

full_output.paper_title: Predictors of Occurrence and 30-Day Mortality for Co-Infection of Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaKPC, blaNDM, blaOXA-23, and blaOXA-51 as the primary carbapenem resistance genes in CRKP and CRAB isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect carbapenemase genes in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and Evolutionary Analysis of Salmonella enterica Serovar Kentucky Sequence Type 198 Isolated From Livestock In East Africa.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in gyrA and parC confer resistance to ciprofloxacin.

parC.notes: Mutations in gyrA and parC confer resistance to ciprofloxacin.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in Salmonella enterica serovar Kentucky ST198 isolates from East Africa, including aac(3)-Id, aadA7, strA, strB, bla TEM-1B, sul1, and tet(A), which confer resistance to aminoglycosides, streptomycin, ampicillin, sulfamethoxazole, and tetracycline. Mutations in gyrA and parC were associated with ciprofloxacin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations in Salmonella Kentucky isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution of ß-lactams, fluroquinolones and colistin resistance and genetic profiles in Salmonella isolates from pork in northern Italy.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in gyrA at positions 83 and 87 were observed.

parC.notes: Mutations in parC at positions 80 and 84 were observed.

qnr.notes: Plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance (PMQR) genes such as qnr were observed.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports an increase in beta-lactam and fluoroquinolone resistance in Salmonella isolates from pork in northern Italy over two decades, with the detection of bla CTX-M1, bla SHV, bla TEM, gyrA, parC, and qnr genes.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic analysis using PCR, disk diffusion, and MIC testing.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antimicrobial resistance profile in Salmonella spp. isolates from swine food chain.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Salmonella spp. isolates from the swine food chain, including parC, gyrA, catA1, nfsB, nfsA, blaTEM, tetA, and tetB, which conferred resistance to various antibiotics such as fluoroquinolones, chloramphenicol, nitrofurantoin, ampicillin, piperacillin, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic characterization of AMR Salmonella spp. isolates was conducted using automated systems and PCR assays.

full_output.paper_title: A Teleost CXCL10 Is Both an Immunoregulator and an Antimicrobial.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PoCXCL10, a CXC chemokine from Japanese flounder, which exhibits both immunoregulatory and antimicrobial properties. It binds to various bacteria, inhibits their growth, and kills them by damaging the bacterial membrane. A derived peptide, P13, also shows bactericidal activity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular cloning, protein purification, ELISA, qRT-PCR, and microscopic techniques to investigate the properties and functions of PoCXCL10 and its derived peptide P13.

full_output.paper_title: Calves as Main Reservoir of Antibiotic Resistance Genes in Dairy Farms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies calves as the main reservoir of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in dairy farms, highlighting the presence of bla TEM, erm B, sul 2, and tet A, which confer resistance to penicillins, MLS, sulfonamides, and tetracyclines, respectively.
full_output.methodology: The study used end-point PCR and digital droplet PCR (ddPCR) to detect and quantify ARGs in fecal samples from dairy farms.

full_output.paper_title: Green Synthesis of Silver Nanoparticles Using the Tridax procumbens Plant Extract and Screening of Its Antimicrobial and Anticancer Activities.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the green synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using Tridax procumbens leaf extract, which exhibits antimicrobial activity against multidrug-resistant (MDR) clinical isolates and anticancer activity against A549 cells. The capping and reducing agents were identified as fosinopril, clomipramine, paromomycin, tiamulin, peptides (Leu Met, Ser Pro Asn, Gln Gly Ala), terpenoids (lupanyl acid), polyphenol (peucenin), and alkaloids (8′,10′-dihydroxydihydroergotamine, carteolol).
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of silver nanoparticles using plant extract, characterization via TEM, XRD, FTIR, and HRLC-MS, antimicrobial activity testing via agar well diffusion and MIC determination, and anticancer activity via MTT assay.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenemase Production and Detection of Colistin-Resistant Genes in Clinical Isolates of Escherichia Coli from the Ho Teaching Hospital, Ghana.
full_output.key_findings: The study detected mcr-1 and mcr-2_700bp colistin-resistant genes in 3 out of 135 E. coli isolates, representing 2.2% prevalence.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of mcr genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Gold nanocluster adjuvant enables the eradication of persister cells by antibiotics and abolishes the emergence of resistance.

mutations_found.validated_by: MIC testing with efflux pump inhibitor

mutations_found.validated_by: MIC testing with efflux pump inhibitor

parC.notes: Mutation in parC was identified as the resistance mechanism in PA01 after exposure to sub-MIC of OFL.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that AuNC@CPP acts as an adjuvant to enhance the eradication of persister cells by antibiotics and prevents the emergence of resistance. It does not identify any specific AMR genes or mutations.
full_output.methodology: The study uses in vitro and in vivo experiments to evaluate the efficacy of AuNC@CPP in eradicating persister cells and preventing resistance development.

full_output.paper_title: Confirming the presence of selected antibiotics and steroids in Norwegian biogas digestate.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of antibiotics such as amoxicillin, penicillin G, ciprofloxacin, and prednisolone in biogas digestates, highlighting potential risks for soil microorganisms and antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study developed and validated a multi-compound quantitative trace-level analytical method for detecting antibiotics and steroid hormones in biogas digestates.

full_output.paper_title: Transfer dynamics of multi-resistance plasmids in Escherichia coli isolated from meat.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes various beta-lactamase genes including bla CTX-M-1, bla CTX-M-2, bla CTX-M-8, bla CTX-M-32, bla CTX-M-55, bla CMY-2, bla SHV-12, bla TEM-1B, and bla TEM-52c, which confer resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics such as ampicillin and ceftazidime.
full_output.methodology: Plasmid characterization, sequencing, and MIC assays were used to identify and validate the resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: A previously uncharacterized gene, PA2146, contributes to biofilm formation and drug tolerance across the ɣ-Proteobacteria.
full_output.key_findings: PA2146, a previously uncharacterized gene, contributes to biofilm formation and drug tolerance in P. aeruginosa, K. pneumoniae, and E. coli. Its inactivation leads to reduced biofilm biomass and increased susceptibility to antimicrobial agents.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq, qRT-PCR, biofilm assays, heterologous expression, and mutant analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Methoxyisoflavan derivative from Trigonella stellata inhibited quorum sensing and virulence factors of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified TMF, a methoxyisoflavan derivative from Trigonella stellata, as a potent quorum sensing inhibitor (QSI) that reduces virulence factors of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, including biofilm formation, pyocyanin production, hemolysin activity, and protease activity. TMF also downregulates the expression of QS regulatory genes lasI, lasR, rhlI, and rhlR.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of bioassays, molecular docking, and real-time PCR to evaluate the QSI activity of TMF and its impact on P. aeruginosa virulence factors and gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Prior exposure to microcystin alters host gut resistome and is associated with dysregulated immune homeostasis in translatable mouse models.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that prior exposure to microcystin-LR alters the gut resistome, increasing the abundance of antibiotic resistance genes such as mefA, msrD, mel, tet40, and ant6, which are associated with resistance to macrolides, tetracycline, and aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: Next-generation sequencing, qRT-PCR, and ELISA were used to analyze the gut microbiome and resistome, as well as immune responses in mice exposed to microcystin-LR.
full_output.sample_size: 12 WT mice and 8 humanized NSG™ mice

full_output.paper_title: Genomic surveillance for multidrug-resistant or hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae among United States bloodstream isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations in Klebsiella pneumoniae bloodstream isolates, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant and hypervirulent strains in the United States.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Longitudinal study on background lesions in broiler breeder flocks and their progeny, and genomic characterisation of Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in E. coli isolates, including mdfA, sitABCD, blaTEM1B, sul2, dfrA1, tet(A), aadA1, and qnrS1, which conferred resistance to multidrug, beta-lactams, sulfonamides, trimethoprim, tetracycline, aminoglycosides, and quinolones.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing of E. coli isolates from broiler breeder flocks and their progeny.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic surveillance reveals antibiotic resistance gene transmission via phage recombinases within sheep mastitis-associated Streptococcus uberis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a multi-antimicrobial resistance cassette containing lsa(E), lnu(B), ant(6)-Ia, and spw genes in three S. uberis isolates, suggesting horizontal gene transfer mediated by phage recombinases.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and genomic analysis were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes and their association with phenotypic resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence and potential transmission of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing extraintestinal pathogenic and enteropathogenic Escherichia coli in domestic dog faeces from Minnesota.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) genes, including blaCMY-2, blaTEM-1, blaTEM-1B, blaCTX-M-24, blaCTX-M-15, and blaOXA-1, along with other resistance genes such as strA, strB, aadA1, aadA2, aph(3')-Ia, aac(3)-IId, aac(6')-Ib-cr, mph[A], floR, catA1, catB3, sul1, sul2, tetA, tetB, dfrA1, dfrA7, dfrA12, and dfrA17 in ESBL-producing E. coli isolates from dog feces in Minnesota.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation and characterization of cephalosporin-resistant E. coli from dog fecal samples, followed by PCR-based virulence genotyping, antimicrobial susceptibility profiling, and whole-genome sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Biogeographical variation in antimicrobial resistance in rivers is influenced by agriculture and is spread through bacteriophages.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the prevalence of tetracycline resistance genes (tetA and tetM) in both bacterial and phage populations in river water, highlighting the role of agricultural areas in promoting phage-induced resistance.
full_output.methodology: 16S/18S amplicon sequencing, Oxford Nanopore sequencing, ddPCR quantification, and phage induction assays.
full_output.sample_size: 20 L river water samples collected from 12 sites across the Maipo and Maule rivers.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation and Analysis of Infection among Inpatients in a Tertiary Hospital in Shanghai.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified drug-resistant bacteria in nosocomial infections, including carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE), vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (VRE), methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), and carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB).
full_output.methodology: Analysis of medical records and microbiological data from hospitalized patients.

full_output.paper_title: Genome sequencing data of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli INF191/17/A isolates of nosocomial infection.

sitABCD.encodes: Periplasmic binding protein (sitA), ATP-binding component (sitB), inner membrane component (sitC), inner membrane component (sitD)

full_output.paper_title: Outbreak of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus sequence type 1, spa type t1784, in an equine hospital in Japan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified MRSA ST1-t1784 isolates from horses and veterinarians, which exhibited resistance to oxacillin, gentamycin, and levofloxacin due to mutations in gyrA and grlA, along with the presence of resistance genes aac(6')-aph(2''), blaZ, mecA, and qacA.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, MIC testing, and phylogenetic analysis were used to characterize the MRSA isolates.

full_output.paper_title: New Mutations in cls Lead to Daptomycin Resistance in a Clinical Vancomycin- and Daptomycin-Resistant Enterococcus faecium Strain.

cls.notes: Mutation in cls leads to daptomycin resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies new mutations in the cls gene that confer daptomycin resistance in Enterococcus faecium EF332. Additionally, the vanA and vanM genes were found to contribute to vancomycin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, clone construction, MIC testing, and membrane lipid analysis were used to identify and validate AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Activating natural product synthesis using CRISPR interference and activation systems in Streptomyces.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes the development of CRISPRi and CRISPRa systems for programmable transcription repression and activation in Streptomyces venezuelae, demonstrating their utility in activating silent biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) for natural product synthesis.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized CRISPRi and CRISPRa systems to regulate gene expression in Streptomyces venezuelae, employing fluorescence measurements and LC-MS analysis to assess the impact on gene expression and natural product synthesis.

full_output.paper_title: Restoring and Enhancing the Potency of Existing Antibiotics against Drug-Resistant Gram-Negative Bacteria through the Development of Potent Small-Molecule Adjuvants.

mcr-1.validation_method: construction of mcr-1 expressing E. coli strain and testing its response to MD-124

full_output.key_findings: MD-124 is a potent small-molecule adjuvant that enhances the efficacy of existing antibiotics against drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria by permeabilizing their outer membranes.
full_output.methodology: Screening of cationic compounds, synthesis of analogs, checkerboard assays, MIC determinations, lysozyme assays, and molecular dynamics simulations.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotype-Guided Comparative Genomics Identifies the Complete Transport Pathway of the Antimicrobial Lasso Peptide Ubonodin in Burkholderia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PupB as the ubonodin outer membrane receptor and YddA as the inner membrane transporter in Burkholderia, revealing the complete transport pathway for the antimicrobial lasso peptide ubonodin.
full_output.methodology: Phenotype-guided comparative genomics, deletion and complementation experiments, and RNA sequencing were used to identify and validate the transport pathway for ubonodin.

full_output.paper_title: Relationship between mortality and molecular epidemiology of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified molecular epidemiological characteristics of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) strains, highlighting the prevalence of SCCmec type IV and the association of certain clones with mortality. It also noted the emergence of community-acquired MRSA (CA-MRSA) in hospital settings.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of MRSA isolates from blood cultures, including SCCmec typing, MLST, and POT typing to determine molecular characteristics and resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence of Panton-Valentine leukocidin positive, multidrug resistant, Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus strains circulating among clinical setups in Adamawa and Far North regions of Cameroon.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of multidrug-resistant Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) strains in Cameroon, with mecA and lukPV genes being significantly associated with resistance and virulence.
full_output.methodology: PCR-based detection of mecA and lukPV genes, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and SCCmec typing.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genotypic characterisation of thymine auxotrophy in Escherichia coli isolated from a patient with recurrent bloodstream infection.

thyA.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and growth experiments

mutations_found.validated_by: whole genome sequencing and growth experiments

thyA.notes: found in all TMP-SMX resistant isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a G172C mutation in the thyA gene, leading to thymine auxotrophy and resistance to TMP-SMX in E. coli isolates from a patient with recurrent bloodstream infections.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and growth experiments on M9 agar with varying thymine concentrations.

full_output.paper_title: An in vitro comparison of antimicrobial efficacy and cytotoxicity between povidone-iodine and chlorhexidine for treating clinical endometritis in dairy cows.
full_output.key_findings: The study compared the antimicrobial efficacy of chlorhexidine (CHX) and povidone-iodine (PI) against clinical isolates of Escherichia coli and Trueperella pyogenes, and assessed their cytotoxicity on bovine endometrial epithelial cells. CHX showed lower MIC and MBC values compared to PI for both bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution to determine MIC and MBC values, and cell viability assays along with wound scratch healing assays to evaluate cytotoxicity.

full_output.paper_title: Heavy-Metal Trojan Horse: Enterobactin-Directed Delivery of Platinum(IV) Prodrugs to Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that enterobactin-conjugated platinum(IV) prodrugs (l-EP and d-EP) can deliver cisplatin into E. coli cells through the enterobactin transport machinery, leading to antibacterial activity. The d-enantiomer (d-EP) shows enhanced antibacterial activity compared to l-EP and cisplatin.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of l-EP and d-EP, evaluation of their antibacterial activity against E. coli strains, and assessment of their mechanisms of action through various microbiological and biochemical assays.

full_output.paper_title: Biofabrication of ZnO/Malachite nanocomposite and its coating with chitosan to heal infectious wounds.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on the development of ZnO/Malachite nanocomposites coated with chitosan for treating infectious wounds, highlighting their antibacterial and antioxidant properties, along with wound-healing efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of ZnO/Malachite nanocomposites using pennyroyal extract, followed by characterization through various techniques including SEM, XRD, FTIR, and DLS, alongside in vitro and in vivo evaluations of antibacterial and wound-healing properties.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that culturing clinical isolates in the presence of polymyxin B nonapeptide (PMBN) significantly enhances their electroporation efficiency, enabling more effective delivery of large plasmid constructs, improving mutagenesis rates, and increasing the yield of transposon mutants in Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized electroporation protocols with PMBN-treated bacterial cells to assess improvements in transformation efficiency, mutagenesis, and transposon insertion sequencing library construction.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro assessment of 17 antimicrobial agents against clinical Mycobacterium avium complex isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study assessed the in vitro activity of 17 antimicrobial agents against clinical Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) isolates, revealing low resistance rates for drugs like clarithromycin, amikacin, bedaquiline, and clofazimine, while high resistance rates were observed for isoniazid, rifampin, linezolid, doxycycline, and ethionamide.
full_output.methodology: Drug susceptibility testing was performed using the Sensititre Myco susceptibility plate and broth microdilution method for selected antimicrobial agents.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, Antimicrobial Resistance, and Characterization of Staphylococcus aureus Isolated from Subclinical Bovine Mastitis in East Coast Malaysia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of antimicrobial resistance in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from subclinical bovine mastitis in East Coast Malaysia, with resistance to penicillin, ampicillin, oxacillin, tetracycline, and erythromycin. Additionally, the isolates exhibited biofilm formation and intracellular invasion capabilities.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, biofilm formation assays, and intracellular invasion studies were conducted on S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, Virulence Genes, Phylogenetic Analysis, and Antimicrobial Resistance Profile of Helicobacter Species in Chicken Meat and Their Associated Environment at Retail Shops in Egypt.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of Helicobacter pylori and H. pullorum in chicken meat and their environments, highlighting the high prevalence of virulence genes (vacA, cagA, hrgA) and antimicrobial resistance, particularly to clarithromycin, metronidazole, and erythromycin.
full_output.methodology: PCR, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and phylogenetic analysis were used to identify and characterize Helicobacter species and their resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Profile of Bacterial Community and Antibiotic Resistance Genes in Typical Vegetable Greenhouse Soil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified aadA, aadA2, strA, strB, tetL, sul1, and sul2 as the most prevalent antibiotic resistance genes in vegetable greenhouse soils, highlighting their association with manure application and the potential for horizontal gene transfer.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput sequencing of 16S rRNA genes, qPCR for ARGs and intI genes, and statistical analyses were used to characterize bacterial communities and ARGs.
full_output.sample_size: Sixteen soil samples from two counties in Shandong Province.

full_output.paper_title: Bio-Enhanced Degradation Strategies for Fluoroquinolones in the Sewage Sludge Composting Stage: Molecular Modification and Resistance Gene Regulation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes three proteins (1GKQ, 1OB0, and 5M0K) from thermophilic bacteria involved in the biodegradation of fluoroquinolones, providing insights into their molecular mechanisms and potential applications in environmental remediation.
full_output.methodology: Molecular docking, entropy weight method, index normalization method, and 3D-QSAR models were used to evaluate the biodegradability of fluoroquinolones by thermophilic bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Susceptibility of Bacterial Pathogens That Infect Olive Flounder (Paralichthys olivaceus) Cultivated in Korea.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the antibiotic susceptibility of 84 strains of three pathogenic bacteria (Streptococcus spp., Vibrio spp., and Edwardsiella piscicida) isolated from olive flounders in Korea. High MAR indices were observed, indicating a significant risk of antibiotic resistance. Specific resistance patterns were noted for different antibiotics among the bacterial species.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility was tested using MIC panels and disk diffusion methods.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ARR1, ARR2, and ARR3 as essential genes for arsenic resistance in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, highlighting that their genomic location and copy number play critical roles in resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Comparative genomic hybridization, whole-genome sequencing, transcriptomic profiling, and PFGE with Southern blot analysis.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple S. cerevisiae strains from vineyard-related specimens in Tuscany, Italy.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Activity of Silver- and Gallium-Containing Hydroxyapatite Materials
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of hydroxyapatite-based granules containing silver or gallium ions, demonstrating that silver-containing materials exhibited strong antibacterial effects against various bacterial strains, while gallium-containing materials showed moderate activity.
full_output.methodology: The study assessed the antibacterial activity of synthesized granules through various tests including agar diffusion, bacterial adhesion, and direct contact assays.

full_output.paper_title: The Xanthophyll Carotenoid Lutein Reduces the Invasive Potential of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Increases Its Susceptibility to Tobramycin.

vfr.notes: vfr is a global regulator of virulence factors

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and Immunological Characterization of Hypermucoviscous Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae ST25 Isolates from Northwest Argentina.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the virulence factors and genomic features of hypermucoviscous carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae ST25 isolates from Northwest Argentina, highlighting their ability to cause severe respiratory infections and their unique genetic profiles.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and in vivo murine infection model were used to evaluate the virulence and immune response of the isolates.
full_output.sample_size: Two strains (LABACER 01 and LABACER 27) were analyzed.

full_output.paper_title: Injectable Platelet-Rich Fibrin as a Drug Carrier Increases the Antibacterial Susceptibility of Antibiotic-Clindamycin Phosphate.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that incorporating clindamycin phosphate (CLP) into platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) enhances its antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis, reducing minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) values compared to pure CLP.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial properties of CLP and PRF_CLP using microdilution tests, FTIR, SEM, and UPLC to analyze structural changes and drug release kinetics.

full_output.paper_title: Regioselective One-Pot Synthesis, Biological Activity and Molecular Docking Studies of Novel Conjugates N-(p-Aryltriazolyl)-1,5-benzodiazepin-2-ones as Potent Antibacterial and Antifungal Agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents the synthesis and evaluation of novel 1,5-benzodiazepin-2-one derivatives with triazole moieties, demonstrating significant antibacterial and antifungal activities against various microbial strains.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized via Cu(I)-catalyzed 1,3-dipolar alkyne-azide coupling reaction and evaluated for their antimicrobial activities using microdilution assays and molecular docking studies.

full_output.paper_title: Phytochemical Investigation of Cordia africana Lam. Stem Bark: Molecular Simulation Approach.
full_output.key_findings: The study isolated and identified four compounds from Cordia africana Lam. stem bark: alpha-amyrin, beta-sitosterol, rosmarinic acid (RA), and methyl rosmarinate (MR). MR showed the best antibacterial activity against MRSA and H. pylori with MIC values of 7.81 ± 1.7 and 31.25 ± 0.9 μg/mL, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Phytochemical analysis, HPLC, and antibacterial activity testing using broth microdilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Chemical Composition and Antibacterial Activity of Liquid and Volatile Phase of Essential Oils against Planktonic and Biofilm-Forming Cells of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of essential oils (EOs) against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, focusing on their liquid and volatile phases. Rosemary EO (R-EO) showed the highest antimicrobial activity, followed by tea tree EO (TT-EO). The volatile fractions of EOs exhibited significant antibiofilm effects, particularly against P. aeruginosa biofilms.
full_output.methodology: The study used GC-MS analysis, disc diffusion, MIC determination, and biofilm assays to evaluate the antibacterial activity of EOs against P. aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Raw Meat Contaminated with Cephalosporin-Resistant Enterobacterales as a Potential Source of Human Home Exposure to Multidrug-Resistant Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 3GC-R strains in raw meat samples, primarily Serratia fonticola, Escherichia coli, Enterobacter cloacae, and Klebsiella pneumoniae, highlighting the potential for human exposure to multidrug-resistant bacteria through contaminated meat.
full_output.methodology: The study involved collecting raw meat samples, isolating 3GC-R strains, and analyzing their antibiotic resistance profiles and phenotypic traits.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial, Antifungal, Antiviral, and Antiparasitic Activities of Peganum harmala and Its Ingredients: A Review.
full_output.key_findings: The review highlights the antibacterial, antifungal, antiviral, and antiparasitic activities of Peganum harmala and its ingredients, indicating potential applications in developing natural antimicrobial agents.
full_output.methodology: Literature review and analysis of experimental studies on the antimicrobial activities of P. harmala extracts and compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Pseudomonas cannabina pv. alisalensis Virulence Factors Are Involved in Resistance to Plant-Derived Antimicrobials during Infection.
full_output.key_findings: The RND transporter contributes to Pcal virulence on cabbage and other Brassicaceae plants by providing resistance to plant-derived antimicrobials such as brassinin.
full_output.methodology: Inoculation assays, gene expression profiling, and antimicrobial susceptibility tests were used to evaluate the role of the RND transporter in Pcal virulence and resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Leuconostoc mesenteroides LVBH107 Antibacterial Activity against Porphyromonas gingivalis and Anti-Inflammatory Activity against P. gingivalis Lipopolysaccharide-Stimulated RAW 264.7 Cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that Leuconostoc mesenteroides LVBH107 exhibits antibacterial activity against Porphyromonas gingivalis biofilm formation and possesses anti-inflammatory properties by reducing pro-inflammatory cytokines and inflammatory mediators in P. gingivalis LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 cells.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the probiotic properties of L. mesenteroides LVBH107, including its tolerance to acidic and bile environments, auto-aggregation, co-aggregation with P. gingivalis, surface hydrophobicity, adhesion ability, and antibiotic susceptibility. It also assessed the antibacterial and anti-inflammatory effects of LVBH107 on P. gingivalis biofilms and P. gingivalis LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 cells.

full_output.paper_title: Nanoparticle-Enabled Combination Therapy Showed Superior Activity against Multi-Drug Resistant Bacterial Pathogens in Comparison to Free Drugs.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of nanoparticle-encapsulated drugs against multi-drug resistant (MDR) bacterial pathogens, focusing on the inhibition of resistance mechanisms such as efflux pumps, beta-lactamase enzyme activity, and hydrogen sulfide (H2S) production. The combination of chitosan and silica nanoparticles containing tetracycline (TET) and chlorpromazine (CPZ) showed improved antibacterial efficacy by targeting these resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study used a checkerboard assay to evaluate antibiotic combinations, determined MIC values, and assessed the impact of nanoparticles on bacterial resistance mechanisms including beta-lactamase inhibition, H2S production, and efflux pump activity.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of HPr kinase/phosphorylase inhibitors: novel antimicrobials against resistant Enterococcus faecalis.

full_output.paper_title: Discovery of a novel nucleoside immune signaling molecule 2′-deoxyguanosine in microbes and plants.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology and Genomic Characteristics of Bloodstream Infection Caused by Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae With Decreased Susceptibility to Aztreonam/Avibactam in China.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization and drug susceptibility pattern of Salmonella and Shigella in children below five years: a cross-sectional study conducted in Lodwar, Turkana County, in Northern Kenya.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that iron oxide nanoparticles (IONPs) exhibit potent antibacterial activity through a combination of photothermal effects and peroxidase-like catalytic activity, effectively eradicating both planktonic bacteria and biofilms.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies variations in complement sensitivity among clinical Acinetobacter baumannii strains, highlighting the role of capsule size and genetic factors in serum resistance. full_output.paper_title: Induction of Resistance of Antagonistic Bacterium Burkholderia contaminans to Postharvest Botrytis cinerea in Rosa vinifera.

full_output.paper_title: Using Targeted Liquid Chromatography-Tandem Mass Spectrometry to Rapidly Detect β-Lactam, Aminoglycoside, and Fluoroquinolone Resistance Mechanisms in Blood Cultures Growing E. coli or K. pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed and validated a targeted LC-MS/MS assay for the rapid detection of β-lactam, aminoglycoside, and fluoroquinolone resistance mechanisms in blood cultures growing E. coli or K. pneumoniae. The assay successfully detected various resistance genes including β-lactamases (SHV, TEM, CTX-M-1-like, OXA-1, CMY-2-like, cAmpC, KPC, OXA-48, NDM, VIM), aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes (AAC(3)-Ia, AAC(3)-II, AAC(3)-IV, AAC(3)-VI, AAC(6′)-Ib, ANT(2′′)-I, APH(3′)-VI), 16S-RMTases (ArmA, RmtB, RmtC, RmtF), and quinolone resistance mechanisms (QnrA, QnrB, AAC(6′)-Ib-cr, and wildtype QRDR of GyrA).
full_output.methodology: Targeted LC-MS/MS assay was developed and validated for the detection of resistance mechanisms in blood cultures. The assay involved peptide selection, SIL peptide optimization, and detection criteria. The results were compared with WGS and AST results.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization and Functional Studies of a Novel Depolymerase Against K19-Type Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified and characterized a novel depolymerase, K19-Dpo41, which specifically degrades the capsular polysaccharide of K19-type Klebsiella pneumoniae, increasing the susceptibility of the bacteria to serum killing and improving the survival rate of Galleria mellonella larvae infected with K19-type K. pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: The depolymerase K19-Dpo41 was cloned, expressed, and purified. Its activity was assessed using spot tests, SEC-HPLC, serum resistance assays, and a Galleria mellonella infection model.

full_output.paper_title: Highly Synergistic Effects of Melittin With Vancomycin and Rifampin Against Vancomycin and Rifampin Resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the synergistic effects of melittin with vancomycin and rifampin against vancomycin and rifampin resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis, showing that the combination significantly reduces the required concentrations of antibiotics while maintaining efficacy and reducing toxicity.
full_output.methodology: The study used disk diffusion, MIC, MBC, and synergistic effect assessments to evaluate the antimicrobial activity of melittin in combination with vancomycin and rifampin.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bacteriocins and bacteriophages produced by food microbiota that inhibit the growth of Shigella and STEC. These inhibitory compounds pose challenges for the recovery of these pathogens during food enrichment cultures.
full_output.methodology: Cell-free extracts from bacterial strains and food enrichment broths were tested for inhibitory activity against Shigella and STEC strains using agar diffusion assays. Proteolytic enzymes and dilution methods were used to characterize the nature of the inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Antimicrobial Resistance in Select Bacteria From Retail Seafood-United States, 2019.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified carbapenemases (bla IMI-2, bla NDM-1) and extended spectrum beta-lactamase (bla CTX-M-55) in seafood isolates, indicating the presence of antimicrobial resistance genes in retail seafood.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in bacterial isolates from retail seafood.

full_output.paper_title: Broad-Spectrum Antimicrobial Action of Cell-Free Culture Extracts and Volatile Organic Compounds Produced by Endophytic Fungi Curvularia Eragrostidis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the endophytic fungus Curvularia eragrostidis HelS1 as a source of broad-spectrum antimicrobial compounds, including 26 secondary metabolites with significant antibacterial and antifungal activity against various pathogens.
full_output.methodology: The research involved isolation and characterization of endophytic fungi, screening for antibacterial activity, extraction and purification of metabolites, and evaluation of antimicrobial properties through disk diffusion, MIC, and MBC assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the susceptibility of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) to mecillinam, revealing varying levels of susceptibility across different species and carbapenemase types, with notable resistance observed in VIM and KPC producers, as well as in Morganella morganii and Serratia spp.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 8310 clinical CRE isolates using disc diffusion and agar dilution methods to determine mecillinam susceptibility.

full_output.key_findings: The study shows that β-lactamase genes from different Ambler classes can contribute to cefiderocol resistance, and that mutations in these genes can enhance resistance. Specifically, bla OXA-48, bla KPC-2, bla CMY-2, bla CTX-M-15, and bla NDM-1 were found to confer resistance to cefiderocol, and various mutations in these genes were identified that further increased resistance.
full_output.methodology: Expression of β-lactamase genes in E. coli, mutational libraries, and MIC and IC50 determinations.

full_output.paper_title: Global Trends in the Proportion of Macrolide-Resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae Infections: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies A2063G and A2064G mutations in the 23S rRNA gene as major contributors to macrolide resistance in Mycoplasma pneumoniae, with A2063G being the most prevalent variant globally.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies using PCR for detection of macrolide-resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae infections.

full_output.paper_title: A protein-protein interaction map reveals that the Coxiella burnetii effector CirB inhibits host proteasome activity.

cirB.validation_method: proteasome activity assay, co-immunoprecipitation, CRISPRi, qRT-PCR

full_output.key_findings: CirB, a T4SS effector of Coxiella burnetii, inhibits host proteasome activity, which promotes intracellular replication of C. burnetii.
full_output.methodology: AP-MS, co-immunoprecipitation, proteasome activity assay, CRISPRi, qRT-PCR

full_output.paper_title: Three enigmatic BioH isoenzymes are programmed in the early stage of mycobacterial biotin synthesis, an attractive anti-TB drug target.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three BioH isoenzymes (BioH1, BioH2, and BioH3) in Mycobacterium smegmatis that are involved in the early stage of biotin synthesis. These enzymes hydrolyze methyl pimeloyl-ACP to produce pimeloyl-ACP, a precursor for biotin synthesis. The study shows that the deletion of all three bioH genes makes M. smegmatis biotin auxotrophic, highlighting their importance in biotin synthesis.
full_output.methodology: Expression cloning, enzymatic assays, crystal structure analysis, and growth assays were used to characterize the BioH isoenzymes.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the utility of metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) for predicting antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in bacterial lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI). It identifies AMR genes such as mecA, BlaZ, and MsrA/ErmA, which are associated with resistance to methicillin, penicillin, and macrolide/lincosamide antibiotics, respectively.
full_output.methodology: The study uses mNGS to analyze respiratory samples from critically ill patients with LRTI, focusing on the detection of AMR genes and their correlation with phenotypic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance-Guided Therapy for Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

mtrR.encodes: transcriptional repressor of the mtr gene

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the identification of genetic markers associated with resistance to ciprofloxacin, cefixime, and ceftriaxone in Neisseria gonorrhoeae, highlighting the development of molecular assays for resistance-guided therapy.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular assays, genetic analysis, and clinical trials to identify and validate resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Enhancement of Acinetobacter baumannii biofilm growth by cephem antibiotics via enrichment of protein and extracellular DNA in the biofilm matrices.
full_output.key_findings: Ceftriaxone (CTRX) and ceftazidime (CAZ) increased the biomass of pre-established Acinetobacter baumannii biofilms at sub-MIC concentrations. These antibiotics enriched the biofilm matrix with proteins, extracellular DNA, and outer membrane vesicles, enhancing biofilm virulence and reducing the effectiveness of azithromycin.
full_output.methodology: Microtiter plate assays, biofilm constituent analysis, and SDS-PAGE/western blot analysis were used to evaluate the effects of antibiotics on biofilm formation and composition.

full_output.paper_title: The integration host factor regulates multiple virulence pathways in bacterial pathogen Dickeya zeae MS2.

ihfA.notes: IhfA is a regulatory gene involved in multiple virulence-related processes.

ihfB.notes: IhfB is a regulatory gene involved in multiple virulence-related processes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies IHF as a global transcriptional regulator that modulates the expression of over 100 genes in D. zeae MS2, impacting various physiological, stress resistance, and pathogenic phenotypes, including virulence factor-modulating and putrescine QS systems, cell wall-degrading enzymes, secretion systems, and motility.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized RT-qPCR, EMSA, and genetic manipulation techniques to investigate the role of IHF in D. zeae MS2.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology and clinical characteristics of infection/colonization due to carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales in neonatal patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaNDM-1, blaKPC-2, and blaIMP-4 as the primary carbapenemase genes responsible for carbapenem resistance in Enterobacterales isolates from neonatal patients. These genes were predominantly found in Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli, contributing to high rates of rectal colonization and infections.
full_output.methodology: Genotypic characterization of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales isolates from neonatal patients, including PCR and sequencing for detection of resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a broad-spectrum lytic Myoviridae bacteriophage using multidrug resistant Salmonella isolates from pig slaughterhouses as the indicator and its application in combating Salmonella infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a broad-spectrum lytic Myoviridae bacteriophage, ph 2-2, capable of effectively killing multidrug-resistant Salmonella isolates from pig slaughterhouses. The phage demonstrated stability under various adverse conditions and showed promise in controlling Salmonella infections in mouse models.
full_output.methodology: The study involved sample collection, bacterial isolation, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, bacteriophage isolation, and characterization of phage properties including morphology, host range, and lytic activity.

full_output.paper_title: A stable cyclized antimicrobial peptide derived from LL-37 with host immunomodulatory effects and activity against uropathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the synthetic antimicrobial peptide CD4-PP, which shows activity against uropathogens such as Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. CD4-PP induces membrane deformation and leakage, prevents biofilm formation, and dissolves mature biofilm. It also enhances the expression of tight junction proteins in uroepithelial cells.
full_output.methodology: The study involves the synthesis and characterization of CD4-PP, including its structural analysis, antimicrobial activity testing, biofilm prevention and dissolution assays, and evaluation of its effects on uroepithelial cells.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified Riemerella anatipestifer isolates from ducks in Vietnam and determined their antimicrobial susceptibility. All isolates were susceptible to Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid and Imipenem, while most were resistant to Nalidixic acid, Streptomycin, and Norfloxacin.
full_output.methodology: R. anatipestifer was isolated using blood agar and chocolate agar, identified via PCR and 16S rRNA sequencing, and tested for antimicrobial susceptibility using the disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: The transcription factors VaERF16 and VaMYB306 interact to enhance resistance of grapevine to Botrytis cinerea infection.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiological characteristics of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae among children in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified KPC-2, NDM-1, and IPM-4 carbapenemase genes as the primary contributors to carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from children in China. Additionally, qacE and cepA genes were found to confer resistance to disinfectants.

full_output.paper_title: Transcript Profiling of Nitroxoline-Treated Biofilms Shows Rapid Up-regulation of Iron Acquisition Gene Clusters.
full_output.key_findings: Nitroxoline induces rapid up-regulation of iron acquisition gene clusters in MRSA, S. epidermidis, and A. baumannii biofilms, indicating its mode of action involves iron starvation.
full_output.methodology: RNA-seq and RT-qPCR were used to analyze transcript profiles of nitroxoline-treated biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Knockout of mlaA increases Escherichia coli virulence in a silkworm infection model.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the knockout of the mlaA gene in E. coli leads to increased virulence against silkworms, resistance to vancomycin and chlorhexidine, and increased outer membrane vesicle production.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized gene knockout mutants, bacterial growth assays, and silkworm infection experiments to evaluate the impact of mlaA knockout on E. coli virulence and antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic activities of colistin combined with other antimicrobial agents against colistin-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Factors contributing to the high prevalence of multidrug-resistance/Rifampicin-resistance in patients with tuberculosis: an epidemiological cross sectional and qualitative study from Khabarovsk krai region of Russia.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a strong association between incarceration and previous anti-TB treatment history with multidrug-resistant/Rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB) in the Khabarovsk krai region of Russia. Mutations in the rpoB gene were linked to Rifampicin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used a cross-sectional retrospective design, analyzing clinical, demographic, and drug susceptibility testing data on 1440 patients. Logistic regression analysis and in-depth interviews were conducted to identify factors associated with MDR/RR-TB.

full_output.key_findings: TaHAG1 and TaPLATZ5 cooperate to activate TaPAD4 expression, which is crucial for powdery mildew resistance in wheat. TaHAG1 modulates histone acetylation, while TaPLATZ5 binds to the TaPAD4 promoter.
full_output.methodology: Knockout, knockdown, overexpression, ChIP-qPCR, EMSA, and yeast two-hybrid assays were used to validate the roles of TaHAG1, TaPLATZ5, and TaPAD4 in powdery mildew resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution and antimicrobial resistance of enterococci isolated from Pecorino and goat cheese manufactured on-farm in an area facing constraints as per EU Regulation 1305/2013 in Umbria, Italy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance among enterococci isolated from Pecorino and goat cheese, particularly to amikacin, ciprofloxacin, ceftriaxone, kanamycin, tetracycline, and vancomycin. Five percent of the strains were resistant to vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using the disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Dual-sensitive antibacterial peptide nanoparticles prevent dental caries.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents pHly-1 NPs, a dual-sensitive antibacterial peptide nanoparticle that shows effective antibacterial activity against Streptococcus mutans under acidic conditions, demonstrating potential for preventing and treating dental caries without harming oral microbiota.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized peptide design, physicochemical parameter measurements, antimicrobial activity assessments, bacterial membrane disruption analysis, transcriptomics, and in vivo and ex vivo experiments to evaluate the effectiveness of pHly-1 NPs.

full_output.paper_title: Microbiological Profile and Drug Resistance Analysis of Postoperative Infections following Orthopedic Surgery: A 5-Year Retrospective Review.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Staphylococcus aureus as the most common cause of postoperative orthopedic infections, with a high prevalence of methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA). Vancomycin was found to be the most effective antibiotic against S. aureus, while gram-negative bacteria showed resistance to several antibiotics including ceftriaxone, ceftazidime, and ampicillin.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 158 patients with postoperative orthopedic infections, including bacterial culture, identification, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Characterization of Enterococcus hirae From Beef Cattle Feedlots and Associated Environmental Continuum.

full_output.paper_title: Sequence analysis and plasmid mobilization of a 6.6-kb kanamycin resistance plasmid, pSNC3-Kan, from a Salmonella enterica serotype Newport isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Design, characterization and structure-function analysis of novel antimicrobial peptides based on the N-terminal CATH-2 fragment.

full_output.paper_title: Development of a Photothermal Antibacterial Nanocomposite NAV for MRSA Infections
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a photothermal antibacterial nanocomposite NAV composed of NiO NPs and Van-modified AuNPs, which effectively combats MRSA infections through photothermal effects and magnetic enrichment.
