These genes were found to be transferable via plasmids, emphasizing the potential for spread of antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study employed whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and conjugation experiments to identify and characterize AMR genes in E. coli isolates from pigs and chickens.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Extensively Drug-Resistant (XDR) Carbapenemase-Producing Enterobacterales (CPE) in Canada from 2019 to 2020.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized extensively drug-resistant (XDR) carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) in Canada, identifying blaNDM, blaKPC, and blaOXA-48 as major resistance determinants. XDR CPE were significantly associated with international travel, healthcare exposure abroad, and specific sequence types.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, susceptibility testing, and statistical analysis of CPE isolates from Canadian hospitals.

full_output.paper_title: A Lysozyme Murein Hydrolase with Broad-Spectrum Antibacterial Activity from Enterobacter Phage myPSH1140.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes Gp105, a lysozyme murein hydrolase from Enterobacter phage myPSH1140, which exhibits broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against various Gram-negative pathogens.
full_output.methodology: In silico, in vitro, and in vivo characterization of Gp105, including peptidoglycan hydrolysis assays and antibacterial activity testing.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of Plasmid-Mediated Resistance to Metronidazole in Clostridioides difficile from River Water.
full_output.key_findings: The study detected plasmid-mediated resistance to metronidazole in Clostridioides difficile isolates from river water, specifically the plasmid pCD-METRO.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and sequencing were used to identify and characterize the plasmid-mediated resistance.
full_output.sample_size: 16 water samples, 82 fish and gull samples

full_output.paper_title: Boosting Cosmeceutical Peptides: Coupling Imidazolium-Based Ionic Liquids to Pentapeptide-4 Originates New Leads with Antimicrobial and Collagenesis-Inducing Activities.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents novel ionic liquid/PP4 conjugates (IL-KTTKS) with potent antimicrobial and collagenesis-inducing activities against various bacterial and fungal species, including multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study synthesized and evaluated the antimicrobial and antifungal activities of IL-KTTKS conjugates using in vitro assays, including MIC measurements and collagen production tests.

full_output.paper_title: Pathogen-Specific Bactericidal Method Mediated by Conjugative Delivery of CRISPR-Cas13a Targeting Bacterial Endogenous Transcripts.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the effectiveness of a CRISPR-Cas13a system for selectively killing Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium through conjugative delivery. The system targets endogenous transcripts of S. Typhimurium, leading to significant reductions in bacterial populations in both in vitro and in vivo settings.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR-Cas13a system was engineered to target specific genes (dnaA, katG, hilA) in S. Typhimurium. The system was delivered via conjugation using plasmids, and its efficacy was tested through various in vitro and in vivo experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Using Shotgun Sequencing to Describe the Changes Induced by In-Feed Zinc Oxide and Apramycin in the Microbiomes of Pigs One Week Postweaning.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the impact of in-feed zinc oxide and apramycin on the fecal microbiomes of pigs one week postweaning, revealing changes in microbial diversity and composition, with implications for antimicrobial resistance and gut health.
full_output.methodology: Shotgun metagenomics was used to analyze the fecal microbiomes of pigs under different dietary treatments and cleaning protocols.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility profiles of Mycoplasma hyorhinis strains isolated from five European countries between 2019 and 2021.

23S rRNA.mechanism: point mutation

full_output.paper_title: Refining the definition of the avian pathogenic Escherichia coli (APEC) pathotype through inclusion of high-risk clonal groups.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified specific sequence types (STs) and genetic markers associated with high-risk avian pathogenic E. coli (APEC) clones, highlighting the importance of ST23, ST117, ST131, ST355, and ST428 in clinical settings. The research also emphasized the role of the APEC plasmid and specific serogroups like O78 in virulence.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, PCR, and bioinformatics analyses were used to characterize APEC isolates and identify genetic markers associated with virulence.

full_output.paper_title: A newly identified flavoprotein disulfide reductase Har protects Streptococcus pneumoniae against hypothiocyanous acid.

aad.validation_method: PCR and sequencing confirmation of gene replacement

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel flavoprotein disulfide reductase, Har, in Streptococcus pneumoniae that reduces hypothiocyanous acid (HOSCN) using NADPH, contributing to bacterial tolerance against HOSCN.
full_output.methodology: Deletion mutant analysis, NADPH consumption assays, and biochemical characterization of HOSCN reductase activity.

full_output.paper_title: Adenosine triphosphate-activated prodrug system for on-demand bacterial inactivation and wound disinfection.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents an ATP-activated prodrug system (HiZP) that utilizes zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) and polyacrylamide hydrogel microspheres to deliver horseradish peroxidase (HRP) and indole-3-acetic acid (IAA). This system generates reactive oxygen species (ROS) upon activation by bacterial ATP, leading to effective bacterial inactivation and wound disinfection.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized droplet-based microfluidic technology to fabricate HiZP, along with various biochemical and microbiological assays to evaluate its antibacterial efficacy and mechanism of action.

full_output.key_findings: The paper provides guidelines for empirical antibacterial therapy of sepsis in adults, focusing on resistance patterns of common pathogens in the Netherlands. It highlights the importance of considering local resistance trends and risk factors for infections with third-generation cephalosporin-resistant Enterobacterales (3GCR-E) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: The study involved a systematic review of literature and expert consensus to formulate evidence-based guidelines for sepsis treatment.

full_output.paper_title: Metagenomic assembly reveals hosts and mobility of common antibiotic resistome in animal manure and commercial compost.

lnuA.mechanism: macrolide, lincosamide, and streptogramin B resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identified 201 common ARG subtypes in animal manure, including aminoglycoside, tetracycline, beta-lactam, and multidrug resistance genes. Composting reduced the relative abundance of most ARGs, but certain genes like sul1, sul2, and aadA persisted. Mobile genetic elements played a crucial role in ARG mobility.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic assembly and cross-sample mapping were used to identify and quantify ARGs in animal manure and compost samples.

full_output.key_findings: Non-antibiotic pharmaceuticals promote conjugative plasmid transfer, enhancing the spread of antibiotic resistance genes like bla in microbial communities.
full_output.methodology: Fluorescence-based mating assays, ROS production measurements, and 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing were used to assess the impact of non-antibiotic pharmaceuticals on plasmid transfer and microbial community composition.

full_output.paper_title: Short Communication: Low Prevalence of Clinically Important Antibiotic-Resistant Strains among Non-Pathogenic Genera of the Tribe Klebsielleae.
full_output.key_findings: The study found low prevalence of clinically important antibiotic-resistant strains among non-pathogenic genera of the Tribe Klebsielleae, with Hafnia sp. showing resistance to cefalexin and Serratia sp. showing resistance to cefuroxime and nitrofurantoin. Only one strain was AmpC positive.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic antibiotic resistance was determined using the Vitek 2 system, and presence of resistance genes was detected using MIC test strips.

full_output.paper_title: Insights into the Antimicrobial Resistance Profile of a Next Generation Probiotic Akkermansia muciniphila DSM 22959.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized the antimicrobial resistance profile of Akkermansia muciniphila DSM 22959, identifying resistance to gentamicin, kanamycin, streptomycin, and ciprofloxacin, along with genomic evidence of resistance genes for beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, macrolides, fluoroquinolones, and tetracyclines.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing using broth microdilution and E-test methods, alongside in silico analysis of the genome for antimicrobial resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: The Dual Roles of Nano Zero-Valent Iron and Zinc Oxide in Antibiotics Resistance Genes (ARGs) Spread in Sediment.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that nano zero-valent iron (nZVI) and zinc oxide (nZnO) can promote the spread of tetracycline resistance genes (tet-ARGs) and class 1 integron (intI1) in sediment through both vertical and horizontal gene transfer. However, lower concentrations of nZVI and nZnO can reduce the dissemination of tet-ARGs/ intI1 in sediment when tetracycline is present.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative-PCR and high-throughput sequencing were used to analyze the abundance of tet-ARGs and intI1 in sediment samples treated with varying concentrations of nZVI and nZnO.

full_output.paper_title: Chlorhexidine Promotes Psl Expression in Pseudomonas aeruginosa That Enhances Cell Aggregation with Preserved Pathogenicity Demonstrates an Adaptation against Antiseptic.
full_output.key_findings: Chlorhexidine exposure led to increased Psl expression and Psl-predominated biofilms in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, contributing to reduced susceptibility to colistin and enhanced cell aggregation.
full_output.methodology: Proteomic analysis, PCR, Congo red binding assay, and wound infection model in mice.

full_output.paper_title: The γ-Core Motif Peptides of AMPs from Grasses Display Inhibitory Activity against Human and Plant Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various γ-core motif peptides from grasses with antimicrobial activity against human and plant pathogens, highlighting their potential as novel antimicrobial agents.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and antimicrobial activity testing of γ-core motif peptides from plant AMPs.

full_output.paper_title: Large-Scale Identification of Multiple Classes of Host Defense Peptide-Inducing Compounds for Antimicrobial Therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mocetinostat as a potent inducer of host defense peptides (HDPs) in chicken macrophages and jejunal explants, enhancing antibacterial activity without direct antibacterial effects.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening of 5002 compounds using a luciferase reporter cell line, followed by validation via RT-qPCR and antibacterial assays.

full_output.paper_title: Helicobacter pylori, Protected from Antibiotics and Stresses Inside Candida albicans Vacuoles, Cause Gastritis in Mice.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that Helicobacter pylori inside Candida albicans vacuoles are protected from amoxicillin and can cause gastritis in mice.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro co-cultivation of H. pylori and C. albicans, qPCR, and a mouse model to investigate the protection of H. pylori from antibiotics and its role in causing gastritis.

full_output.paper_title: Nanopore Sequencing for De Novo Bacterial Genome Assembly and Search for Single-Nucleotide Polymorphism.

rpsL.notes: Mutation in the promoter region of rpsL gene leading to reduced susceptibility to streptomycin.

rpsD.notes: Missense mutation in rpsD gene leading to reduced susceptibility to streptomycin.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the rpsL and rpsD genes associated with reduced susceptibility to streptomycin in E. coli strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing using nanopore technology and Sanger sequencing for validation.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Insights of First ermB-Positive ST338-SCCmecV(T)/CC59 Taiwan Clone of Community-Associated Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus in Poland.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first Polish isolate of a community-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CA-MRSA) strain carrying the ermB gene, which confers constitutive resistance to macrolides, lincosamides, and streptogramin B antibiotics (cMLS-B).

full_output.paper_title: Novel Antibiofilm Inhibitor Ginkgetin as an Antibacterial Synergist against Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: Ginkgetin (Gin) inhibits biofilm formation, EPS production, and motility in E. coli without affecting bacterial growth. It also shows synergistic effects with antibiotics like gentamicin and colistin.
full_output.methodology: The study used CV staining, CLSM, qRT-PCR, and Alamar Blue assay to evaluate the effects of Gin on E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Promiscuous Lipase-Catalyzed Knoevenagel-Phospha-Michael Reaction for the Synthesis of Antimicrobial β-Phosphono Malonates.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a new enzymatic method for synthesizing β-phosphonomalononitriles and β-phosphononitriles using lipase from Candida cylindracea (CcL). Compounds 5, 6, 7, and 12 exhibited antimicrobial activity comparable to antibiotics like ciprofloxacin, bleomycin, and cloxacillin.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antibacterial effects of chitosan (CS) and chondroitin sulfate (ChS) coatings on plasma-treated polylactic acid (PLA) films. The CS-ChS polyelectrolyte complex (PEC) showed improved antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus compared to individual coatings. Additionally, the PEC coatings enhanced the drug loading and release efficiency of lomefloxacin, demonstrating a dual killing mechanism involving contact and release of the antibiotic.
full_output.methodology: Surface modification of PLA films via plasma treatment and saccharide coating, followed by evaluation of antibacterial activity, biocompatibility, and drug release properties.

full_output.paper_title: Seven Days of Bismuth-Based Quadruple Therapy Is as Effective for the First-Line Treatment of Clarithromycin-Resistant Confirmed Helicobacter pylori Infection as 14 Days of Bismuth-Based Quadruple Therapy.

full_output.methodology: PCR and molecular analysis were used to identify AMR genes in P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiofilm and Anti-Quorum Sensing Potential of Cycloartane-Type Triterpene Acids from Cameroonian Grassland Propolis: Phenolic Profile and Antioxidant Activity of Crude Extract.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies cycloartane-type triterpene acids from Cameroonian propolis, including 27-Hydroxymangiferonic acid, Ambolic acid, and Mangiferonic acid, which demonstrate antibiofilm and anti-quorum sensing activities against various bacterial and fungal strains.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro and In Vivo Antibacterial Activity, Toxicity and Resistance Analysis of Pleuromutilin Derivative Z33 against Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity, toxicity, and resistance potential of Z33, a pleuromutilin derivative, against MRSA. Z33 showed potent in vitro bactericidal activity, a narrow mutant selection window, and lower resistance development potential compared to tiamulin.
full_output.methodology: The study assessed the in vitro and in vivo antibacterial activity, CYP450 inhibition, cytotoxicity, and acute oral toxicity of Z33 against MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Potential of Bacopa monnieri (L.) Wettst. and Its Bioactive Molecules against Uropathogens-An In Silico Study to Identify Potential Lead Molecule(s) for the Development of New Drugs to Treat Urinary Tract Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Oroxindin as a potential inhibitor against Klebsiella pneumoniae and Proteus mirabilis, showing strong interactions with target proteins involved in fosfomycin resistance and fimbrial adhesion.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and Characterization of Galloylglucoses Effective against Multidrug-Resistant Strains of Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study isolates and characterizes four galloylglucoses effective against multidrug-resistant strains of Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae, showing minimum inhibitory concentrations ranging from 2-256 µg/mL.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Activity of Aureonuclemycin Produced by Streptomyces aureus Strain SPRI-371.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies aureonuclemycin (ANM) as a novel antibacterial compound produced by Streptomyces aureus strain SPRI-371, showing significant activity against plant pathogens such as Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae and Xanthomonas citri.

full_output.paper_title: A Mini Review of Antibacterial Properties of Al(2)O(3) Nanoparticles.
full_output.key_findings: This review discusses the antibacterial properties of aluminum oxide nanoparticles (AlOxNPs) against various bacterial and fungal species, highlighting their mechanisms of action, synthesis methods, and effectiveness in inhibiting microbial growth.
full_output.methodology: Literature review and analysis of experimental studies on the antibacterial effects of AlOxNPs.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of Shiga Toxin-Producing Escherichia coli (STEC) in the Endocervix of Asymptomatic Pregnant Women. Can STEC Be a Risk Factor for Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes?
full_output.key_findings: The study detected the presence of Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC) in the endocervix of asymptomatic pregnant women, with seven out of twelve E. coli isolates carrying the stx2 gene. One isolate, designated STEC 123/21, was found to be O113:NT and stx2a positive, demonstrating cytotoxic effects on Vero cells.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence and distribution of extended-spectrum β-lactamase in clinical Escherichia coli isolates at Ho Teaching Hospital in Ghana.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaTEM-1, blaCTXM-1, blaSHV-73, and TOHO-1 as the primary ESBL genes in E. coli isolates, with blaTEM-1 being the most prevalent. Multiple ESBL gene carriage was observed, indicating complex resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of florfenicol and oxazolidinone resistance in Enterococcus isolates from animals in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified four florfenicol and oxazolidinone resistance genes (fexA, fexB, optrA, and poxtA) in Enterococcus isolates from animals in China, highlighting the role of mobile genetic elements in their dissemination.

full_output.paper_title: CipA mediates complement resistance of Acinetobacter baumannii by formation of a factor I-dependent quadripartite assemblage.

full_output.paper_title: High Prevalence of Asymptomatic Nasopharyngeal Carriage Rate and Multidrug Resistance Pattern of Streptococcus pneumoniae Among Pre-School Children in North Showa Ethiopia.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Properties and Mechanisms of Action of Sonoenzymatically Synthesized Lignin-Based Nanoparticles.

full_output.methodology: The study uses a sonoenzymatic approach to synthesize PheLigNPs and evaluates their antibacterial activity through MIC assays, kinetic growth curves, and mechanisms of action involving ROS generation and membrane disruption.

full_output.paper_title: Optimal dose of lactoferrin reduces the resilience of in vitro Staphylococcus aureus colonies.

full_output.methodology: The study used a checkerboard assay to evaluate the synergistic effects of lactoferrin and cefazolin on S. aureus Xen36, along with a mathematical model to predict population dynamics and validate experimental findings.

full_output.paper_title: Drug susceptibility profiling and genetic determinants of drug resistance in Mycobacterium simiae isolates obtained from regional tuberculosis reference laboratories of Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the gyrB gene (codon 389, 444, and 571) and rrl gene (positions 2058 and 2059) associated with resistance to moxifloxacin and clarithromycin in Mycobacterium simiae isolates.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and molecular methods, including PCR-sequencing, were used to analyze drug resistance and genetic mutations in M. simiae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterial resistance to zinc poisoning requires assembly of P-ATPase-containing membrane metal efflux platforms.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and transcriptomic profiling of phoenix colonies.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) in the PA4673 gene, which is predicted to encode a GTP-binding protein, and the disruption of PA3626, encoding a tRNA pseudouridine synthase D (TruD), eliminates phoenix colony emergence.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, RNA sequencing, transposon mutant screening, and complementation experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance of Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolated from patients attending sexually transmitted infection clinics in Urban Hospitals, Lusaka, Zambia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high resistance rates of Neisseria gonorrhoeae to penicillin (85.2%), tetracycline (68.9%), and ciprofloxacin (59.8%). No resistance was detected to ceftriaxone.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using E-test on 122 N. gonorrhoeae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Associations of antimicrobial use with antimicrobial susceptibility at the calf level in bacteria isolated from the respiratory and digestive tracts of veal calves before slaughter.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that antimicrobial use (AMU) in veal calves was associated with increased antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in bacteria isolated from their respiratory and digestive tracts. Specifically, increased AMU was linked to higher resistance rates in E. coli, P. multocida, and M. haemolytica, particularly for tetracyclines and penicillins.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed antimicrobial susceptibility of bacteria isolated from veal calves using microdilution and examined associations between antimicrobial use and resistance through generalized linear models.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic epidemiological analysis of Klebsiella pneumoniae from Portuguese hospitals reveals insights into circulating antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance patterns of Helicobacter pylori strains isolated from the Tibet Autonomous Region, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high resistance rates to clarithromycin, levofloxacin, metronidazole, and rifampicin, moderate resistance to amoxicillin, and negligible resistance to tetracycline and furazolidone in H. pylori isolates from the Tibet Autonomous Region, China.

full_output.paper_title: Polymyxins induce lipid scrambling and disrupt the homeostasis of Gram-negative bacteria membrane.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the mechanism by which polymyxins disrupt the membrane of Gram-negative bacteria, revealing a novel pathway involving lipid scrambling, membrane phase separation, and peptide translocation.
full_output.methodology: Molecular dynamics simulations were used to analyze the interaction of polymyxins with bacterial membranes.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the impact of antibiotic growth promoters (AGPs) on the chicken gut microbiome, revealing that AGPs have limited effects on taxonomic abundances but significantly alter microbial pathways, including antimicrobial resistance, energy metabolism, and amino acid metabolism.
full_output.methodology: The study uses 16S rRNA sequencing, metatranscriptomics, and metabolomics to analyze the chicken gut microbiome under different diets and AGP treatments.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical Characteristics and Drug Resistance Analysis of 90 Cases of Children with Salmonella Enteritis.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the drug resistance profiles of Salmonella isolates from 90 children with Salmonella enteritis, highlighting high resistance rates to penicillin and erythromycin, moderate resistance to cephalosporins, and low resistance to quinolones. Imipenem and meropenem showed the highest susceptibility rates.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of clinical data, bacterial culture, and drug susceptibility testing using automated systems and CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Within-farm dynamics of ESBL-producing Escherichia coli in dairy cattle: Resistance profiles and molecular characterization by long-read whole-genome sequencing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple ESBL-encoding genes, including bla CTX-M-1, bla CTX-M-14, bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-27, bla CTX-M-32, and bla SHV-12, as well as carbapenemase gene bla NDM-1, in ESBL-producing E. coli isolates from dairy cattle farms. These genes were associated with resistance to various beta-lactam antibiotics. Additionally, several other AMR genes such as aadA2, ant(3")-Ia, aph(3')-Ia, dfrA12, sul3, cmlA1, and others were identified, contributing to resistance against aminoglycosides, trimethoprim, sulfamethoxazole, and chloramphenicol. Mutations in gyrA, parC, and parE were linked to fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Long-read whole-genome sequencing (ONT) and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the AMR genes and mutations in E. coli isolates from dairy cattle farms.

full_output.methodology: SMRT sequencing, ANI analysis, conjugation experiments, and MIC testing were used to characterize the strain and its resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: The dynamic transcriptome during maturation of biofilms formed by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

The arginine deiminase (ADI) pathway, including genes arcA, arcB, arcC, and arcD, is upregulated during biofilm formation, suggesting a role in energy metabolism. Disruption of opp3D in USA300-JE2 significantly reduces biofilm formation, indicating its importance in biofilm development.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic analysis using RNA-seq and differential gene expression analysis, along with transposon mutagenesis experiments to assess the role of specific genes in biofilm formation.
full_output.sample_size: Three MRSA strains: UAS391 (USA300), HEMRSA-15 (EMRSA-15), and ST239-16 (Hungarian/Brazilian ST239).

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the antibiotic resistance mechanisms in Gram-positive anaerobic cocci (GPAC), including target site mutations, enzymatic hydrolysis, and efflux pump systems. Key resistance genes identified include ermA, ermB, ermF, ermTR, nimB, tetK, tetL, tetM, and tetO, which confer resistance to macrolides, metronidazole, and tetracyclines.

full_output.paper_title: Biofilm formation and antibiotic sensitivity in Elizabethkingia anophelis.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that all 197 Elizabethkingia anophelis isolates were multidrug-resistant (MDR) and exhibited high resistance to various antibiotics, including β-lactams, aminoglycosides, and fluoroquinolones. However, minocycline, doxycycline, and rifampin showed potent in vitro activity against these isolates. Additionally, all isolates were capable of forming biofilms, with strong or moderate biofilm-forming strains showing higher resistance compared to weak biofilm-formers.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using agar dilution method, and biofilm formation was assessed using a crystal violet assay. Scanning electron microscopy was used to confirm biofilm structures.

full_output.key_findings: MRX-6038 is a novel leucyl-tRNA synthetase inhibitor with strong anti-Mycobacterium abscessus activity in vitro and in vivo. Resistance to MRX-6038 is conferred by missense mutations in the leuS gene encoding leucyl-tRNA synthetase.

full_output.paper_title: Library Screening for Synergistic Combinations of FDA-Approved Drugs and Metabolites with Vancomycin against VanA-Type Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococcus faecium.
full_output.key_findings: This study identified thirteen drugs with minimum MICs that were ≤12.5 μM against VanA-type vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREfm) and confirmed six of them as synergistic with vancomycin. full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes, including beta-lactamases blaADC-10 and blaADC-25, aminoglycoside phosphotransferase aphA-3, and beta-lactamase blaOXA-50, associated with resistance to beta-lactam and aminoglycoside antibiotics in combat wound bioburden.
full_output.methodology: Targeted sequencing and metagenomic analysis were used to detect AMR genes and their associations with wound outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: Faecal carriage of enterococci harbouring oxazolidinone resistance genes among healthy humans in the community in Switzerland.

cfr.genetic_context: poxtA was flanked on both sides by IS 1216E elements located near fexB
cfr.evidence_note: The paper states that cfr was found in combination with poxtA in some isolates, but does not explicitly state that cfr itself confers resistance to linezolid.

optrA.genetic_context: highly variable, but often resembled previously described platforms
optrA.evidence_note: The paper states that optrA was found in Enterococcus isolates and that some of these isolates were resistant to linezolid.

poxtA.genetic_context: poxtA was flanked on both sides by IS 1216E elements and located on medium-sized plasmids
poxtA.evidence_note: WGS analysis identified the WT poxtA gene, corresponding to that from Staphylococcus aureus AOUC-0915

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of oxazolidinone resistance genes cfr, optrA, and poxtA in enterococci isolated from healthy humans in Switzerland, highlighting the potential for community spread of these resistance determinants.
full_output.methodology: PCR, WGS, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and transcriptomic variation in Bordetella spp. following induction of erythromycin resistance.

23S rRNA.mechanism: mutation

23S rRNA.notes: Mutations in the 23S rRNA gene were detected in all resistant B. holmesii strains.

mexAB-oprM.notes: The mexAB-oprM operon was upregulated in resistant B. parapertussis isolates.

full_output.key_findings: B. holmesii developed resistance due to mutations in the 23S rRNA gene, while B. parapertussis resistance was attributed to upregulation of an efflux pump mechanism.
full_output.methodology: Genomic and transcriptomic analysis of Bordetella isolates following erythromycin exposure.

full_output.paper_title: Ultrasensitive and rapid identification of ESRI developer- and piperacillin/tazobactam-resistant Escherichia coli by the MALDIpiptaz test.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed the MALDIpiptaz test for rapid detection of piperacillin/tazobactam (P/T)-resistant and ESRI developer Escherichia coli. The test uses MALDI-TOF MS and machine learning algorithms to classify isolates accurately and quickly.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized MALDI-TOF MS combined with machine learning algorithms (PLS-DA, SVM, and random forest) to analyze protein profiles of E. coli isolates and identify P/T resistance and ESRI development.

full_output.paper_title: A Novel Oral GyrB/ParE Dual Binding Inhibitor Effective against Multidrug-Resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Other High-Threat Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study describes JSF-2414, a novel tricyclic pyrimidoindole that targets the ATP-binding domains of DNA gyrase (GyrB) and topoisomerase IV (ParE), showing potent activity against multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae and other high-threat pathogens.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of JSF-2414 against a collection of N. gonorrhoeae clinical isolates and other high-threat pathogens using agar dilution methods and in vivo models.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of Delafloxacin against a Burkholderia pseudomallei Efflux Mutant Panel.
full_output.key_findings: Delafloxacin shows improved efflux avoidance compared to ciprofloxacin, particularly at acidic pH, suggesting better therapeutic potential against B. pseudomallei strains expressing efflux pumps like BpeEF-OprC.
full_output.methodology: In vitro activities of delafloxacin and ciprofloxacin were evaluated against B. pseudomallei mutants using CLSI methodology at different pH levels.

full_output.paper_title: Engineered Bacteriophages Containing Anti-CRISPR Suppress Infection of Antibiotic-Resistant P. aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that engineered bacteriophages containing anti-CRISPR genes (AcrIF1, AcrIF2, and AcrIF3) effectively suppress P. aeruginosa infection by inhibiting CRISPR-Cas immunity, showing potential as an alternative therapy for antibiotic-resistant infections.
full_output.methodology: Phage engineering, plaque assays, growth kinetics, and inhibitory rate measurements were used to evaluate the effectiveness of anti-CRISPR-containing phages against P. aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Phage Resistance Evolution Induces the Sensitivity of Specific Antibiotics in Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1.

pilQ.notes: Mutations in pilQ gene are linked to phage resistance and altered antibiotic sensitivity.

full_output.key_findings: The phage-resistant P. aeruginosa variant PAO1-R1 exhibits increased sensitivity to gentamicin and polymyxin B. Mutations in the pilQ gene, involved in T4P synthesis, are associated with phage resistance and altered antibiotic sensitivity.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, disk diffusion assays, and adsorption rate assays were used to characterize the phage-resistant variant and its antibiotic sensitivity profile.

full_output.paper_title: 3-Phenylpropan-1-Amine Enhanced Susceptibility of Serratia marcescens to Ofloxacin by Occluding Quorum Sensing.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 3-PPA enhances the susceptibility of Serratia marcescens to ofloxacin by inhibiting quorum sensing, reducing biofilm formation, and downregulating the expression of virulence-related genes.
full_output.methodology: The study used MIC testing, qRT-PCR, and various imaging techniques to analyze the effects of 3-PPA on S. marcescens.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Selective Combinatory Effect of Ciprofloxacin with Nitroxoline, Sanguinarine, and Zinc Pyrithione against Diarrhea-Causing and Gut Beneficial Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the in vitro synergistic and antagonistic effects of ciprofloxacin combined with nitroxoline, sanguinarine, and zinc pyrithione against diarrhea-causing and gut-beneficial bacteria, highlighting the potential of these combinations for targeted antimicrobial therapy.
full_output.methodology: The study used the checkerboard method to determine the fractional inhibitory concentration indices (FICIs) for evaluating the synergistic and antagonistic effects of the antimicrobial combinations.

full_output.paper_title: Development of Resistance to Eravacycline by Klebsiella pneumoniae and Collateral Sensitivity-Guided Design of Combination Therapies.

lon.mechanism: Mutations in the lon gene contribute to bacterial resistance to eravacycline by reducing the intracellular accumulation of the antibiotic and increasing the expression of efflux pumps such as AcrA-AcrB-TolC.
lon.validation_method: Whole-genome sequencing, complementation experiments, and MIC testing

blaNDM-1.validation_method: experimental validation in vivo and in vitro

full_output.key_findings: Mutations in the lon gene contribute to eravacycline resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae. The combination of eravacycline with aztreonam/avibactam or ceftazidime-avibactam suppresses resistance development and displays synergistic antibacterial effects.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, complementation experiments, MIC testing, and in vivo mouse model experiments.

full_output.paper_title: UPEC Colonic-Virulence and Urovirulence Are Blunted by Proanthocyanidins-Rich Cranberry Extract Microbial Metabolites in a Gut Model and a 3D Tissue-Engineered Urothelium.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that PAC-rich cranberry extract microbial metabolites significantly impede the activation of UPEC virulence genes, including those encoding for toxins, adhesins, and invasins, in a donor-dependent manner.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a TWIN-SHIME fermentation system combined with a dialysis cassette device and a 3D tissue-engineered urothelium model to assess the effects of PAC-rich cranberry extract on UPEC virulence gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: The Azithromycin Pro-Drug CSY5669 Boosts Bacterial Killing While Attenuating Lung Inflammation Associated with Pneumonia Caused by Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that CSY5669, a derivative of azithromycin, enhances the intracellular killing of MRSA by human macrophages and blood leukocytes without direct antibacterial effects. It also reduces lung inflammation and tissue damage in a murine model of MRSA pneumonia.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro experiments with human monocyte-derived macrophages and peripheral blood leukocytes, as well as in vivo experiments with a murine model of MRSA pneumonia to evaluate the effects of CSY5669.

full_output.paper_title: Activity of ertapenem/zidebactam (WCK 6777) against problem Enterobacterales.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the activity of ertapenem/zidebactam against various Enterobacterales, showing effectiveness against many carbapenemase producers and isolates with combinations of impermeability and ESBL or AmpC activity.
full_output.methodology: MICs were determined using BSAC agar dilution for 1632 Enterobacterales isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Acinetobacter baumannii, Klebsiella pneumoniae and Elizabethkingia miricola isolated from wastewater have biodegradable activity against fluoroquinolone.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the aac(6')-Ib-cr gene variant in bacterial isolates capable of degrading fluoroquinolones, highlighting its role in ciprofloxacin biodegradation.
full_output.methodology: Molecular screening, sequencing, and biodegradation assays were used to characterize the role of the aac(6')-Ib-cr gene in fluoroquinolone degradation.

full_output.paper_title: Mitigating the toxicity of palmitoylated analogue of α-melanocyte stimulating hormone(11-13) by conjugation with gold nanoparticle: characterisation and antibacterial efficacy against methicillin sensitive and resistant Staphylococccus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial efficacy of Pal-α-MSH(11-13) and its gold nanoparticle conjugate (GNP-Pal-α-MSH(11-13)) against methicillin-sensitive (MSSA) and methicillin-resistant (MRSA) Staphylococcus aureus. Both forms showed effective bactericidal activity, with the conjugate demonstrating reduced toxicity compared to the peptide alone.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized UV-Vis spectroscopy, DLS, TEM, FTIR, and TGA for nanoparticle characterization, and MIC/MBC assays for antibacterial evaluation.

full_output.paper_title: The l,d-Transpeptidase Ldt(Ab) from Acinetobacter baumannii Is Poorly Inhibited by Carbapenems and Has a Unique Structural Architecture.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the l,d-transpeptidase Ldt Ab from Acinetobacter baumannii, highlighting its poor inhibition by carbapenems and unique structural features. Deletion of the Ldt Ab gene increased susceptibility to β-lactam antibiotics, particularly carbapenems, suggesting its potential as a target for novel antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic deletion, MIC testing, and structural analysis to investigate the role of Ldt Ab in β-lactam resistance in A. baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic-induced reactive electrophilic species (RES) and their impact on bacterial viability
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that under anaerobic conditions, bactericidal antibiotics lead to the accumulation of reactive metabolic byproducts (RMBs), particularly reactive electrophilic species (RES), which contribute to antibiotic lethality. RMB scavengers like glutathione, acetylcysteine, and pyridoxamine reduce RES accumulation and mitigate macromolecular damage, thereby decreasing antibiotic lethality.
full_output.methodology: The study used single-cell assays, bulk culture measurements, and biochemical perturbations to examine the effects of antibiotics on cellular metabolism and RMB production under anaerobic conditions.

full_output.paper_title: Copper starvation induces antimicrobial isocyanide integrated into two distinct biosynthetic pathways in fungi.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies crmA as a gene encoding a multidomain ICS-NRPS-like enzyme that generates valine-derived isocyanide, contributing to two distinct biosynthetic pathways under copper-starvation conditions. This isocyanide exhibits antimicrobial activity against various bacteria and fungi.
full_output.methodology: Metabolite profiling using HPLC-HRMS, MS2, and NMR spectroscopy, along with genetic manipulation of crmA in various fungal species.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and whole-genome sequencing analysis of Vibrio vulnificus strains causing pearl gentian grouper disease in China.

blaTEM-1.validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and CARD database annotation
blaTEM-1.evidence_note: The paper states that the EPL 0201 strain contains the TEM-1 gene, which confers resistance to penam, cephalosporin, carbapenem, and monobactam antibiotics.

sul1.validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and CARD database annotation

tet.validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and CARD database annotation
tet.evidence_note: The paper states that the EPL 0201 strain had resistance genes such as tet, which can confer resistance to tetracyclines.

parE.validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and CARD database annotation

APH(6)-Id.validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and CARD database annotation
APH(6)-Id.evidence_note: The CARD database annotation explicitly states that APH(6)-Id confers resistance to aminoglycosides.

arr-3.validation_method: whole-genome sequencing and CARD database annotation

adeF.evidence_note: The paper states that the EPL 0201 strain contains adeF, which is annotated in the CARD database as conferring resistance to tetracycline and fluoroquinolone through antibiotic efflux.

sul2.evidence_note: The paper states that the EPL 0201 strain contains sul2, which confers resistance to sulfonamides, as per the CARD database annotation.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified Vibrio vulnificus EPL 0201 biotype 2 as a multidrug-resistant strain with high pathogenicity, possessing virulence factors vvhA, rtxA, and wza, as well as resistance genes such as H-NS, TEM-1, sul1, tet, floR, parE, mprF, APH(6)-Id, APH(3'')-Ib, aadA16, and arr-3.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the strain.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance, virulence genes, and phylogenetic characteristics of pathogenic Escherichia coli isolated from patients and swine suffering from diarrhea.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that E. coli isolates from swine exhibited significantly higher antimicrobial resistance compared to those from patients, particularly to fluoroquinolones and aminoglycosides. Both swine and human isolates harbored the stx2 gene, which is associated with severe diseases.
full_output.methodology: The study involved antimicrobial susceptibility testing, detection of virulence genes, O-serogroup typing, and multi-locus sequence typing (MLST) of E. coli isolates from pigs and patients.

full_output.paper_title: Production of new antimicrobial palm oil-derived sophorolipids by the yeast Starmerella riodocensis sp. nov. against Candida albicans hyphal and biofilm formation.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the production of novel antimicrobial sophorolipids by Starmerella riodocensis GT-SL1R, demonstrating effective inhibition of Candida albicans hyphal growth and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the isolation and characterization of sophorolipids from Starmerella riodocensis, assessing their antimicrobial activity through various assays including hyphal growth inhibition, biofilm formation, and scanning electron microscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution and Transmission of Cefiderocol-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii During an Outbreak in the Burn Intensive Care Unit.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies disruptions in the piuA and pirA genes as mechanisms of cefiderocol resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii during an outbreak in a burn intensive care unit.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) testing were used to analyze cefiderocol resistance mechanisms in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Optimization and development of high-resolution melting curve analysis (HRMA) assay for detection of New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase (NDM) producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed and optimized a high-resolution melting curve analysis (HRMA) assay for detecting New Delhi metallo-beta-lactamase (NDM)-producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The HRMA method demonstrated high analytical sensitivity and specificity for identifying NDM and MBL genes in P. aeruginosa strains.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized HRMA coupled with real-time PCR to detect and differentiate NDM and MBL genes in P. aeruginosa strains.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence of bla(VEB), bla(GES) and bla(PER) genes in beta-lactam resistant clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

bla(VEB).validation_method: PCR and correlation with antibiotic resistance data

bla(GES).validation_method: PCR and correlation with antibiotic resistance data

bla(PER).validation_method: PCR and correlation with antibiotic resistance data

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the high prevalence of bla(VEB), bla(GES), and bla(PER) genes in beta-lactam-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolates, highlighting their significant role in resistance to various beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: A Novel Triple Combination To Combat Serious Infections with Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii in a Mouse Pneumonia Model.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel triple combination of imipenem, sodium ascorbate, and apo-transferrin that shows synergistic effects against carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, significantly reducing imipenem MIC and demonstrating bactericidal activity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro checkerboard assays, time-kill assays, and a mouse pneumonia model to evaluate the efficacy of the triple combination against carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Omadacycline Pharmacokinetics/Pharmacodynamics in the Hollow Fiber System Model and Potential Combination Regimen for Short Course Treatment of Mycobacterium kansasii Pulmonary Disease.
full_output.key_findings: Omadacycline showed efficacy against Mycobacterium kansasii, with MIC values ranging from 4 to 32 mg/L. The optimal exposure for maximal bacterial kill was an AUC0-24/MIC ratio of 3.05, achievable with a 300 mg/day dose. The combination regimen of omadacycline, moxifloxacin, and tedizolid demonstrated superior efficacy compared to the standard regimen.
full_output.methodology: MIC testing, hollow fiber system model, and pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics studies were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Wearable adjunct ozone and antibiotic therapy system for treatment of Gram-negative dermal bacterial infection.

vancomycin.role_in_paper: used as a proof of concept
vancomycin.validation_method: combination therapy with ozone demonstrating increased antibacterial activity

linezolid.role_in_paper: used as a proof of concept
linezolid.validation_method: combination therapy with ozone demonstrating increased antibacterial activity

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that combining gaseous ozone with antibiotics like vancomycin and linezolid enhances their effectiveness against Gram-negative bacteria, suggesting ozone can sensitize these bacteria to antibiotics typically effective against Gram-positive bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Experimental evaluation of ozone and antibiotic combination therapy on Gram-negative bacteria in vitro.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of antimicrobial resistance and risk factors for recovery of intrauterine Escherichia coli from cows with metritis on California commercial dairy farms.
full_output.key_findings: All intrauterine E. coli isolates were resistant to ampicillin (AMP), with 30.2% and 33.9% resistance to chlortetracycline and oxytetracycline, respectively. Ceftiofur resistance was observed in 8.6% of isolates.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study analyzing antimicrobial resistance in E. coli isolates from post-partum dairy cows with metritis.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of multidrug-resistant ESKAPEE pathogens from clinical samples in Chonburi, Thailand (2017-2018).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes in ESKAPEE pathogens, including bla OXA-23, bla NDM, bla OXA-48-like, bla CTX-M group 1, bla CTX-M group 9, mcr-1, mcr-3, mecA, and vanA. These genes conferred resistance to various antibiotics such as carbapenems, beta-lactams, colistin, methicillin, and vancomycin.
full_output.methodology: PCR, real-time PCR, and whole-genome sequencing were used to identify AMR genes in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing of Staphylococcus aureus isolates from patients at a tertiary hospital in Tehran, Iran, 2018-2019.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 37.5% of S. aureus isolates were methicillin-resistant (MRSA), with high resistance rates to erythromycin, clindamycin, ciprofloxacin, and levofloxacin. No resistance was observed against linezolid, daptomycin, and tigecycline, and vancomycin remained effective against MRSA isolates.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing using Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion and VITEK 2 automated system.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid Detection of Beta-Lactamases Genes among Enterobacterales in Urine Samples by Using Real-Time PCR.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a real-time PCR system to detect beta-lactamase genes (blaSHV-12, blaTEM, blaCTX-M-15, blaCTX-M-9, blaCMY-2, blaOXA-48, and blaNDM-1) in Enterobacterales strains from urine samples, demonstrating high sensitivity and specificity.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR was used to detect beta-lactamase genes in 78 uropathogenic Enterobacterales strains, with validation through phenotypic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Multidrug-Resistant CTX-M Extended Spectrum Beta-Lactamase-Producing Escherichia coli From Different Bovine Faeces in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several CTX-M beta-lactamase genes including CTX-M-15, CTX-M-14, CTX-M-55, CTX-M-79, and TEM-1 as the predominant resistance genes in multidrug-resistant E. coli isolates from bovine feces in China.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibilities and mechanisms of resistance of commensal and invasive Mycoplasma salivarium isolates.

23S rRNA.mechanism: mutation in 23S rRNA gene leading to resistance
23S rRNA.validation_method: sequencing of 23S rRNA gene and ribosomal protein genes

16S rRNA.mechanism: mutation in 16S rRNA gene leading to resistance

tetM.validation_method: PCR and sequencing for detection of tetM gene

gyrA.mechanism: mutation in gyrA gene leading to resistance

parC.mechanism: mutation in parC gene leading to resistance

mutations_found.validated_by: sequencing of 23S rRNA gene and ribosomal protein genes
sequencing of 23S rRNA gene and ribosomal protein genes
sequencing of 23S rRNA gene and ribosomal protein genes

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in 23S rRNA, 16S rRNA, gyrA, parC, and the presence of tetM gene as mechanisms of resistance to erythromycin, clindamycin, tetracycline, and levofloxacin in Mycoplasma salivarium isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and sequencing of relevant genes.

full_output.paper_title: The integrase of genomic island GIsul2 mediates the mobilization of GIsul2 and ISCR-related element CR2-sul2 unit through site-specific recombination.

CR2.validation_method: plasmid construction and restriction enzyme analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the integrase of genomic island GIsul2 mediates the excision and integration of GIsul2 and the CR2-sul2 unit through site-specific recombination. The sul2 gene confers sulfonamide resistance.
full_output.methodology: Site-specific recombination experiments, PCR, sequencing, and restriction enzyme analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Spontaneous Resistance of Erwinia amylovora Against Bacteriophage Y2 Affects Infectivity of Multiple Phages.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a deletion in the gene EAMY_2231, which encodes a glycosyltransferase group 1, as the cause of spontaneous resistance in Erwinia amylovora against bacteriophage Y2. This mutation leads to cross-resistance against other phages and affects amylovoran and LPS production.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and complementation experiments were conducted to validate the role of EAMY_2231 in phage resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of Different Tolerable Levels of Constitutive mcr-1 Expression on Escherichia coli.

mcr-1.validation_method: expression in E. coli and measurement of colistin MICs

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the mcr-1 gene, which confers colistin resistance in Escherichia coli. The expression levels of mcr-1 were shown to correlate with increased colistin MICs, demonstrating the gene's role in mediating resistance.
full_output.methodology: Construction of isogenic E. coli strains with varying mcr-1 expression levels, measurement of colistin MICs, and assessment of growth rates and membrane integrity.
full_output.sample_size: Seven isogenic E. coli strains were constructed.

full_output.paper_title: Proteomic Investigation of the Antibacterial Mechanism of Cefiderocol against Escherichia coli.

nuoJ.notes: Knockout of the NADH-quinone oxidoreductase gene nuoJ in E. coli resulted in a 60-fold increase in MIC to cefiderocol.

full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that cefiderocol induces ROS stress in E. coli through NADH and iron overload, leading to bacterial cell death. Knockout of NADH-quinone oxidoreductase genes, particularly nuoJ, significantly increases resistance to cefiderocol.
full_output.methodology: The study used DIA-based quantitative proteomics, PRM validation, and MIC testing to investigate the antibacterial mechanism of cefiderocol against E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Development of Microfluidic Chip-Based Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Method for Detection of Carbapenemase Producing Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a microfluidic chip-based LAMP method for the detection of carbapenemase-producing organisms (CPO) and evaluated its performance in identifying carbapenemase genes such as bla KPC, bla NDM, bla VIM, bla IMP, bla oprD2, bla OXA-23, bla OXA-48, and bla OXA-58.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a microfluidic chip-based LAMP method combined with PCR and sequencing for the detection and characterization of carbapenemase genes in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Conditional Antimicrobial Peptide Therapeutics.

Tachyplesin I.mechanism: activity masking through anionic block and protease-cleavable linker
Tachyplesin I.validation_method: microdilution assays, SDS-PAGE analysis, and in vivo biodistribution studies

full_output.key_findings: The study presents an ABD-AMP conjugate that enables conditional activation of antimicrobial peptides, enhancing their therapeutic index by reducing off-target toxicity and improving targeted delivery to infected lungs.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of ABD-AMP conjugates, in vitro microdilution assays, SDS-PAGE analysis, in vivo biodistribution studies, and FRET cleavage assays.

full_output.paper_title: Exploration of Streptococcus core genome to reveal druggable targets and novel therapeutics against S. pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified PCS8235_RS04650 as a druggable target for Streptococcus pneumoniae, showing potential for binding with Artenimol through molecular docking and dynamics simulation.
full_output.methodology: Bioinformatics analysis, molecular docking, and dynamics simulation.

full_output.paper_title: Nodule-specific cysteine-rich peptides of all nodulating plants have a common origin
full_output.key_findings: DgDef1, a defensin-like peptide, exhibits antimicrobial activity against Gram-negative bacteria such as Sinorhizobium meliloti 1021 and Escherichia coli K-12 substrain MG1655, but not against Gram-positive Streptomyces coelicolor A3(2) M145.
full_output.methodology: RT-qPCR, subcellular localization, peptide production, and growth inhibition assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study introduces STIMS, a method to infer positive and purifying selection in metagenomic time series of hypermutator microbial populations. It demonstrates STIMS' effectiveness in detecting selection in both nonmutator and hypermutator populations, highlighting the role of regulatory genes in adaptation.
full_output.methodology: The study uses in silico evolution experiments and metagenomic data analysis to validate the STIMS method.

full_output.paper_title: Substandard and falsified antibiotics: neglected drivers of antimicrobial resistance?
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the widespread presence of substandard and falsified (SF) antibiotics, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, with 17.4% of tested samples failing at least one quality test. It emphasizes the need for improved regulatory frameworks to address the issue of SF antibiotics and their potential contribution to antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies assessing the quality of antibiotics, including prevalence surveys, equivalence studies, and case reports.

full_output.paper_title: Metagenomic data from cerebrospinal fluid permits tracing the origin and spread of Neisseria meningitidis CC4821 in China.

farB.mechanism: resistance to antibacterial free fatty acids

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes AMR genes and mutations in Neisseria meningitidis CC4821, highlighting the emergence of quinolone resistance due to gyrA mutations and the presence of efflux pumps and tetracycline resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of N. meningitidis isolates using mNGS and bioinformatics tools.

full_output.paper_title: RNAi-mediated knockdown of gut receptor-like genes prohibitin and α-amylase altered the susceptibility of Galleria mellonella to Cry1AcF toxin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies prohibitin and alpha-amylase as potential receptors for Cry1AcF toxin in Galleria mellonella, as their knockdown reduced insect susceptibility to the toxin.
full_output.methodology: The study used RNAi to knockdown genes and RT-qPCR to analyze gene expression, along with protein docking analysis to understand receptor interactions.

full_output.paper_title: Colistin-degrading proteases confer collective resistance to microbial communities during polymicrobial infections.

cdp.validation_method: growth inhibition experiments, coculture experiments, animal infection model

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a colistin-degrading protease (Cdp) in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia that confers resistance to colistin by inactivating the antibiotic, providing protection to colistin-susceptible pathogens like Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii during polymicrobial infections.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, purification and identification of the colistin-degrading enzyme, construction of knockout and complementation mutants, growth inhibition experiments, colistin inactivation assays, coculture experiments, and animal infection models.

full_output.paper_title: Longitudinal metatranscriptomic sequencing of Southern California wastewater representing 16 million people from August 2020-21 reveals widespread transcription of antibiotic resistance genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a wide diversity of transcribed antibiotic resistance genes in Southern California wastewater, highlighting the presence of resistance mechanisms such as multidrug efflux pumps, ribosomal protection proteins, and aminoglycoside modifying enzymes.
full_output.methodology: Metatranscriptomic sequencing of RNA from wastewater samples to analyze the transcription of antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular detection of fluoroquinolone-resistant Neisseria meningitidis by using mismatched PCR-restriction fragment length polymorphism technique.

gyrA.notes: The T91I mutation in gyrA was associated with high-level ciprofloxacin resistance.
