full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of Bi2O3, Bi2O3/GO, and Bi2O3/CuO/GO nanocomposites against Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria, demonstrating their effectiveness in inhibiting bacterial growth.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of nanocomposites using eco-friendly methods, evaluation of antibacterial activity via disk diffusion assay, and characterization using XRD, FTIR, and SEM.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring phytochemical composition, photocatalytic, antibacterial, and antifungal efficacies of Au NPs supported by Cymbopogon flexuosus essential oil.
full_output.key_findings: The study explores the antimicrobial and photocatalytic properties of gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) synthesized using Cymbopogon flexuosus essential oil. The AuNPs exhibit significant antibacterial and antifungal activities against Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, and Fusarium oxysporum, as well as high photocatalytic efficiency in degrading methylene blue.
full_output.methodology: The study uses GC-MS for compositional analysis, UV-Vis and FTIR spectroscopy for characterizing AuNPs, and well diffusion assays to assess antimicrobial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Evybactin is a DNA gyrase inhibitor that selectively kills Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

bacA.notes: Mutations in bacA lead to evybactin resistance

mutations_found.validated_by: genomic sequencing of resistant mutants and construction of recombinant mutants

gyrA.notes: Mutations in gyrA lead to evybactin resistance

full_output.key_findings: Evybactin is a novel antimicrobial agent that targets mycobacterial DNA gyrase, showing potent activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis and other mycobacteria. Mutations in bacA and gyrA contribute to evybactin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Structural analysis, MIC assays, mutagenesis, and enzymatic assays were used to characterize evybactin's mechanism of action and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome sequencing and analysis of Streptomyces strains producing multiple antinematode drugs.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified secondary metabolite biosynthetic gene clusters in Streptomyces spectabilis KCTC9218 T and Streptomyces sp. AN091965, including those responsible for the production of spectinabilin, streptorubin B, and RED, which exhibit antinematode activity.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing using PacBio and Illumina platforms, along with bioinformatics and mass spectrometry analyses, was employed to characterize the strains and their secondary metabolite production.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation, identification and antimicrobial profile of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus from bovine mastitis in and around Adama, Central Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) isolates from bovine mastitis cases in Adama, Ethiopia, with a prevalence of 32.4%. MRSA isolates exhibited high resistance to amoxicillin (75%) and oxytetracycline (66.7%).
full_output.methodology: The study used the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method to identify MRSA and assess antimicrobial susceptibility.

full_output.key_findings: The study develops the Global One Health Index (GOHI)-AMR to assess global antimicrobial resistance (AMR) status, highlighting disparities in AMR prevalence and control across income groups and regions.
full_output.methodology: The study integrates data from multiple global databases to construct the GOHI-AMR framework, analyzing AMR trends and correlations with socioeconomic and environmental factors.

full_output.paper_title: P22 Phage Shows Promising Antibacterial Activity under Pathophysiological Conditions.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the P22 phage effectively reduces the growth of Salmonella typhimurium under various pathophysiological conditions, including acidic pH and stationary phase. It also shows synergy with antibiotics ampicillin and kanamycin.
full_output.methodology: The study used phage enumeration, bacterial growth kinetics, SEM analysis, and checkerboard assays to evaluate the effectiveness of P22 phage against Salmonella typhimurium.

full_output.paper_title: Pathophysiology of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Superinfection in COVID-19 Patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) superinfections in COVID-19 patients, highlighting their association with increased mortality and complications. The mecA gene was detected in MRSA strains, contributing to methicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study involved screening of 3492 COVID-19 positive samples, bacterial isolation, antibiotic sensitivity testing, and PCR-based detection of the mecA gene.

full_output.paper_title: International Spread of Multidrug-Resistant Rhodococcus equi.

rpoB.evidence_note: The paper states 'carried the rpoB S531F mutation unique to the MDR-RE 2287 clone'.

rpoB.notes: The rpoB S531F mutation is unique to the MDR-RE 2287 clone and contributes to rifampin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the international spread of the multidrug-resistant Rhodococcus equi clone MDR-RE 2287, highlighting the presence of erm(46) and the rpoB S531F mutation as molecular markers for tracking its dissemination.
full_output.methodology: PCR, whole-genome sequencing, and phylogenetic analysis were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms and genetic relatedness of the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Contrasting long-term dynamics of antimicrobial resistance and virulence plasmids in Salmonella Typhimurium from animals.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various antimicrobial resistance genes and plasmid replicons in Salmonella Typhimurium isolates from animals, highlighting the prevalence of multidrug resistance in food production animal-associated clades.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and in silico detection of resistance genes and plasmid replicons.

full_output.paper_title: Detection and molecular characterization of VRE isolates in Slovakia from stool samples positive for Clostridioides difficile toxins.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of vanA and vanB genes in VRE isolates from stool samples positive for C. difficile toxins, highlighting the local dominance of the vanA genotype and its association with high resistance to vancomycin, teicoplanin, and occasionally linezolid.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of vanA and vanB genes in VRE isolates, along with antibiotic susceptibility testing using disk diffusion and E-test methods.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteriological aspects of bacteremia in the intensive care unit of the Mohammed V Military Hospital: 10 months prospective study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, particularly Gram-negative bacilli such as Acinetobacter baumannii and Klebsiella pneumoniae, as significant causes of bacteremia in ICU settings. MDR Acinetobacter baumannii, extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Enterobacterales (ESBL-E), and carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) were the most frequently isolated MDR bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Prospective study involving blood cultures, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and analysis of clinical data from ICU patients.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic surveillance of Salmonella spp. in the Philippines during 2013-2014.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized various AMR genes and mutations in Salmonella isolates from the Philippines, highlighting the presence of ESBL genes, plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance genes, and mutations in gyrA and parC associated with fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in Salmonella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Harmonisation of in-silico next-generation sequencing based methods for diagnostics and surveillance.
full_output.key_findings: This study evaluated the sensitivity and specificity of five in-silico AMR detection software using a panel of 436 E. coli isolates. The study highlighted the importance of harmonizing AMR predictions from sequence data and identified limitations in current in-silico technologies for detecting resistance to certain antimicrobials.
full_output.methodology: The study compared the performance of five AMR detection pipelines using WGS data from 436 E. coli isolates and evaluated their sensitivity and specificity against phenotypic data.

full_output.key_findings: E. coli and Klebsiella spp. were the most common pathogens causing early-onset sepsis (EOS) in very preterm infants, showing high resistance to ampicillin and third-generation cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: Prospective, observational study analyzing pathogen distribution and antibiotic susceptibility patterns in very preterm infants.

full_output.paper_title: Duplicated ribosomal protein paralogs promote alternative translation and drug resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the minor paralog of uL30 (uL30B) enhances resistance to staurosporine by optimizing translation of long open reading frame (ORF) genes, whereas the major paralog (uL30A) is essential for ribosome biogenesis.
full_output.methodology: RNA sequencing, mass spectrometry, and growth experiments were used to analyze the impact of uL30 paralogs on ribosome biogenesis and drug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Mesoporous silica-coated silver nanoparticles as ciprofloxacin/siRNA carriers for accelerated infected wound healing.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a nanoplatform combining silver nanoparticles and mesoporous silica coated with ciprofloxacin and siRNA to treat bacterial-infected wounds. The platform showed effective antibacterial activity against E. coli and reduced inflammation by silencing TNF-α.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized nanoparticle synthesis, in vitro and in vivo antibacterial testing, and gene expression analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of the nanoplatform.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Salmonella endolysin XFII produced by recombinant Escherichia coli and its application combined with chitosan in lysing Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the endolysin XFII, derived from Salmonella phage XFII-1, which exhibits potent bactericidal activity against Gram-negative bacteria, including E. coli and Salmonella. XFII was successfully overexpressed in E. coli BL21 and showed high stability under various conditions. Additionally, XFII demonstrated synergistic bactericidal effects when combined with chitosan.
full_output.methodology: The endolysin XFII was cloned, overexpressed, and purified from E. coli BL21. Its bactericidal activity was assessed using turbidity measurements, colony-forming unit counts, and transmission electron microscopy. The stability and synergistic effects with chitosan were also evaluated.

full_output.paper_title: Machine learning algorithm to characterize antimicrobial resistance associated with the International Space Station surface microbiome.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies beta-lactam resistance genes in Enterobacter bugandensis and Bacillus cereus using a deep learning model and experimental validation through AST.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a deep learning model (DeepARG) combined with experimental validation through AST to identify and confirm AMR genes in ISS microbiome samples.
full_output.sample_size: 226 pure strains, 21 shotgun metagenome sequences, and 24 MAGs

full_output.paper_title: ESBL plasmids in Klebsiella pneumoniae: diversity, transmission and contribution to infection burden in the hospital setting.

blaCTX-M-15.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

blaVEB-1.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

blaOXA-48.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

blaIMP-4.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identified 25 distinct ESBL plasmids, with Plasmid A carrying bla CTX-M-15 being the most prevalent and contributing significantly to the burden of ceftriaxone-resistant and multidrug-resistant infections in the hospital setting.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and phylogenetic analysis were used to investigate ESBL plasmid diversity, transmission, and their contribution to infection burden.
full_output.sample_size: 440 K. pneumoniae, K. variicola, and K. quasipneumoniae isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified OXA-23 as a carbapenem-resistance gene in CRKP and CRAB isolates, highlighting the role of environmental and healthcare worker contamination in CRO transmission.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis were used to trace the transmission routes of carbapenem-resistant organisms in hospital settings.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcus aureus and Enterococcus faecium isolated from pigeon droppings (Columba livia) in the external environment close to hospitals.

Staphylococcus_aureus_norA.encodes: NorA gene cloned from S. aureus

mgrA.encodes: Regulator for norA, norB, and tet38

ANT(4')-Ib.encodes: Kanamycin nucleotidyltransferase sequence from S. aureus plasmid

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Staphylococcus aureus and Enterococcus faecium isolated from pigeon droppings near hospitals, highlighting the potential public health risks posed by these pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were conducted on bacterial isolates from pigeon droppings.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis Utilizes Host Histamine Receptor H1 to Modulate Reactive Oxygen Species Production and Phagosome Maturation via the p38MAPK-NOX2 Axis.
full_output.key_findings: M. tuberculosis uses host HRH1 to suppress NOX2-mediated cROS production and inhibit phagosome maturation and acidification, thereby enhancing its intracellular survival.
full_output.methodology: siRNA knockdown, agonist/antagonist treatment, western blotting, flow cytometry, and confocal microscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Orchestrated Biosynthesis of the Secondary Metabolite Cocktails Enables the Producing Fungus to Combat Diverse Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a supercluster in Metarhizium robertsii that produces four classes of compounds: ustilaginoidin D, indigotides, pseurotins, and mer-f3. The transcription factor UpmR regulates the coordinated production of these compounds, enabling the fungus to combat various bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Genome survey, gene deletion and overexpression experiments, HPLC, GC-MS, and LC-MS analyses were used to characterize the biosynthetic pathways and evaluate the antimicrobial effects of the produced compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic and Biochemical Characterization of Halogenation and Drug Transportation Genes Encoded in the Albofungin Biosynthetic Gene Cluster.

orfA.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + in vivo and in vitro assays

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes the albofungin biosynthetic gene cluster (abf BGC) from Streptomyces tumemacerans JCM5050, focusing on the roles of orfA and orfL. orfA encodes a FAD-dependent halogenase involved in chlorinating albofungin, while orfL encodes a proton-dependent oligopeptide transporter that contributes to drug detoxification and resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic DNA isolation, NGS, BAC cloning, CRISPR-Cas9 editing, LC-MS analysis, and in vivo/in vitro assays were used to characterize the abf BGC and its components.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence and Transmission of Plasmid-Mediated Mobile Colistin Resistance Gene mcr-10 in Humans and Companion Animals.

mcr-10.genetic_context: The colistin resistance gene mcr-10 located in different plasmids of 4 ECC strains was adjacent to a XerC-type tyrosine recombinase-gene, designed as xerC.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the mcr-10 gene in colistin-resistant Enterobacter cloacae complex isolates from humans and companion animals, highlighting its potential for transmission between these sources.
full_output.methodology: PCR, Sanger sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and whole-genome sequencing were used to characterize the mcr-10 gene and its genetic context.
full_output.sample_size: 4 mcr-10-bearing isolates from 294 feces samples and 734 clinical strains

full_output.paper_title: Estimated Roles of the Carrier and the Bacterial Strain When Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Decolonization Fails: a Case-Control Study.

mupA.validation_method: searching the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD) for resistance genes

qacA.validation_method: searching the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD) for resistance genes

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mupA and qacA genes associated with resistance to mupirocin and chlorhexidine, respectively, which could impact decolonization success in MRSA carriers.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and machine learning models were used to analyze genetic features associated with chronic MRSA carriage.

full_output.paper_title: Low Ciprofloxacin Concentrations Select Multidrug-Resistant Mutants Overproducing Efflux Pumps in Clinical Isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

mexS.mechanism: overexpression of MexCD-OprJ and MexEF-OprN efflux pumps
mexS.validation_method: sequencing of genes and expression analysis

nfxB.mechanism: overexpression of MexCD-OprJ and MexEF-OprN efflux pumps
nfxB.validation_method: sequencing of genes and expression analysis

mexS.notes: mutation in mexS leads to overproduction of efflux pumps

nfxB.notes: mutation in nfxB leads to overproduction of efflux pumps

gyrA.notes: mutation in gyrA contributes to ciprofloxacin resistance

parE.notes: mutation in parE contributes to ciprofloxacin resistance

full_output.key_findings: Low ciprofloxacin concentrations select for multidrug-resistant mutants in Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolates, primarily through overproduction of efflux pumps mexCD-oprJ and mexEF-oprN, along with mutations in gyrA, parE, mexS, and nfxB.
full_output.methodology: Short-term adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) assays, MIC testing, sequencing, and efflux pump expression analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmid-Borne AFM Alleles in Pseudomonas aeruginosa Clinical Isolates from China.

blaAFM-2.validation_method: cloning in E. coli and P. aeruginosa PAO1 followed by antimicrobial susceptibility testing

blaAFM-4.validation_method: cloning in E. coli and P. aeruginosa PAO1 followed by antimicrobial susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identified two plasmid-borne AFM alleles, AFM-2 and AFM-4, in Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolates from China. Both alleles conferred resistance to multiple beta-lactam antibiotics, with AFM-4 being a novel variant detected in a strain isolated from a water sink.
full_output.methodology: The study involved screening of P. aeruginosa isolates for AFM alleles, whole-genome sequencing, plasmid analysis, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing after cloning the genes into E. coli and P. aeruginosa PAO1.

full_output.paper_title: Four Novel Leaderless Bacteriocins, Bacin A1, A2, A3, and A4 Exhibit Potent Antimicrobial and Antibiofilm Activities against Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: Four novel leaderless bacteriocins, bacin A1, A2, A3, and A4, were identified in Bacillus sp. TL12, exhibiting potent antimicrobial and antibiofilm activities against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
full_output.methodology: Genome mining, culture-based screening, purification, and identification of antimicrobial substances, followed by antimicrobial activity testing.
full_output.sample_size: 1,056 strains of the B. cereus group

full_output.paper_title: Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification Assay for Identifying Neisseria gonorrhoeae Nonmosaic penA-Targeting Strains Potentially Eradicable by Cefixime.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a LAMP assay to detect nonmosaic penA in Neisseria gonorrhoeae, which is associated with cefixime susceptibility. The assay shows high sensitivity and specificity for identifying strains with a CFM MIC of <=0.064 mg/L.
full_output.methodology: LAMP assay and real-time PCR were used to evaluate penA types and cefixime susceptibility in N. gonorrhoeae strains.
full_output.sample_size: 204 N. gonorrhoeae strains and 95 other Neisseria species strains

full_output.paper_title: Comparative Genomics Analysis and Outer Membrane Vesicle-Mediated Horizontal Antibiotic-Resistance Gene Transfer in Avibacterium paragallinarum.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 11 antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in Avibacterium paragallinarum P4chr1, including bl2d_oxa1, aph33ib, cml_e3, and tetB, which confer resistance to beta-lactam, aminoglycoside, phenicol, and tetracycline antibiotics, respectively. These ARGs were transferred via outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) to a susceptible strain, although the resistance was transient.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and validate the ARGs.

full_output.paper_title: Prior Exposure to Azithromycin and Azithromycin Resistance Among Persons Diagnosed With Neisseria gonorrhoeae Infection at a Sexual Health Clinic: 2012-2019.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that recent exposure to azithromycin (within 30 days) was strongly associated with subsequent azithromycin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae infections. The long half-life and persistence of subtherapeutic levels of azithromycin may contribute to the selection of resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed data from the Public Health–Seattle and King County Sexual Health Clinic, examining the association between azithromycin exposure and azithromycin resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae infections using multivariate logistic regression and linear regression.

full_output.paper_title: The human gut serves as a reservoir of hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (hvKp) in the human gut, highlighting its potential as a reservoir for these strains. While hvKp strains were found to be genetically related to clinical isolates, no antimicrobial resistance genes were detected in the majority of hvKp isolates.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of gut K. pneumoniae isolates from healthy individuals, including whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility and risk factors for resistance among Escherichia coli isolated from canine specimens submitted to a diagnostic laboratory in Indiana, 2010-2019.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed 2,738 E. coli isolates from dogs in Indiana and found that 20.2% were susceptible to 17 of 27 antimicrobials tested. Significant decreases in susceptibility were observed for several beta-lactam antimicrobials, including amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, ampicillin, cefazolin, and ceftazidime. The study also identified risk factors for antimicrobial resistance (AMR) such as age, breed, and sample origin.
full_output.methodology: The study used antimicrobial susceptibility testing via broth microdilution and statistical analysis to evaluate resistance patterns and risk factors in E. coli isolates from dogs.

full_output.paper_title: ESKAPE bacteria characterization reveals the presence of Acinetobacter baumannii and Pseudomonas aeruginosa outbreaks in COVID-19/VAP patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaOXA-23 as a beta-lactam resistance gene in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from COVID-19/VAP patients.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to identify and characterize the blaOXA-23 gene in Acinetobacter baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Hemithioindigo-Based Visible Light-Activated Molecular Machines Kill Bacteria by Oxidative Damage.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that hemithioindigo (HTI)-based molecular machines effectively kill Gram-positive bacteria upon visible light activation, without inducing detectable resistance. HTI also eliminates antibiotic-resistant MRSA, persister cells, and biofilms, primarily through oxidative damage.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized time-kill experiments, MIC determination, and ROS measurement techniques to evaluate the antibacterial activity of HTI-based molecular machines.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and construction of a multi-epitopes vaccine design against Klebsiella aerogenes: molecular modeling study.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on identifying potential vaccine candidates against Klebsiella aerogenes by analyzing its proteome and selecting surface-exposed, non-homologous, and non-toxic proteins. Three virulent proteins were identified, and epitopes were predicted for B-cell and T-cell immunity.
full_output.methodology: The study used bioinformatics tools for proteome analysis, subcellular localization, virulence factor database (VFDB) analysis, and epitope prediction for vaccine design.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology and genomic analysis of Klebsiella oxytoca from a single hospital network in Australia.

mutations_found.validated_by: phenotypic testing and whole genome sequencing
phenotypic testing and whole genome sequencing

bla OXY.notes: Mutations in the promoter region of the chromosomal bla OXY gene lead to overexpression and resistance to third-generation cephalosporins.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes, including bla SHV−12, bla CTX−M−9, bla IMP−4, and aph(3')-Ia, in Klebsiella oxytoca isolates from a single hospital network in Australia. Mutations in the bla OXY promoter were associated with increased resistance to third-generation cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and phenotypic testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in Klebsiella oxytoca isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic characterization of Salmonella Infantis from South Africa, 2004-2016.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified AMR genes such as strA, strB, sul2, tet(A), aadA1, sul1, and dfrA14 in Salmonella Infantis isolates from South Africa, highlighting differences in AMR profiles between eBG31 and eBG297 isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatic analysis were used to characterize AMR determinants in Salmonella Infantis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Automated antimicrobial susceptibility testing and antimicrobial resistance genotyping using Illumina and Oxford Nanopore Technologies sequencing data among Enterobacteriaceae.
full_output.key_findings: The study compared the accuracy of Illumina and Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) sequencing platforms for determining AMR classes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) among 181 clinical Enterobacteriaceae isolates. Both platforms showed high categorical agreement with phenotypic AST, with Illumina showing slightly better performance. The study highlighted the potential of ONT for clinical use when combined with robust bioinformatics.
full_output.methodology: The study used whole-genome sequencing (WGS) with Illumina and ONT platforms, followed by analysis with AREScloud for AMR marker detection and WGS-AST prediction. Phenotypic AST was performed using broth microdilution.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates: A 5-year retrospective study at a Tertiary Hospital in Northern Thailand.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the high prevalence of ESBL-producing E. coli and K. pneumoniae isolates in a tertiary hospital in northern Thailand, emphasizing their resistance to multiple antibiotics except carbapenems and aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of clinical specimens and antibiotic susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of a Salmonella Rissen ST469 clinical isolate carrying bla (NDM-13) in China.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular and clinical characterization of hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from individuals with urinary tract infections.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of NDM-1-producing carbapenem-resistant E. cloacae complex from a tertiary hospital in Chongqing, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first nosocomial outbreak of NDM-1-producing Enterobacter cloacae complex ST177 in China, highlighting the co-existence of bla NDM-1 and mcr-9 genes, which contribute to multidrug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic diversity and antimicrobial resistance of invasive, noninvasive and colonizing group B Streptococcus isolates in southern Brazil.

mef A/E.evidence_note: The paper states that the mef A/E gene was found in 45 isolates and is associated with erythromycin resistance.

erm B.evidence_note: The paper mentions the presence of the erm B gene in 19 isolates and associates it with erythromycin and clindamycin resistance.

The most common genotypes were Ia/MT12 and V/MT18, showing high resistance to macrolides.

full_output.key_findings: Bacteria exposed to antineoplastic agents developed increased resistance to antibiotics, as evidenced by significantly higher MICs for vancomycin, teicoplanin, linezolid, levofloxacin, and ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Determination of MICs after exposure to antineoplastic agents and assessment of bacterial tolerance and resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Toxin-Producing Endosymbionts Shield Pathogenic Fungus against Micropredators.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies rhizoxin, a secondary metabolite produced by the endosymbiotic bacterium Mycetohabitans rhizoxinica, as a key factor in protecting the fungus Rhizopus microsporus from predation by amoebae and nematodes.
full_output.methodology: Culture extracts and purified rhizoxin S2 were tested in survival assays against protostelium, nematodes, and amoebae.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic Characteristics of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus argenteus Isolates Collected in the Dutch National MRSA Surveillance from 2008 to 2021.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus argenteus (MRSArg) isolates from the Dutch national MRSA surveillance, identifying resistance genes such as mecA, dfrG, blaZ, aadD, and tet(L), along with virulence factors like sak and scn.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, wgMLST, and bioinformatic analyses were used to characterize the genetic traits of the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Novel β-Hairpin Peptide from Marine Polychaeta with a High Efficacy against Gram-Negative Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies novel β-hairpin antimicrobial peptides, including abarenicin, UuBRI-21, and their analogs (Ap4, Ap9, Ap11), which show strong antibacterial activity against Gram-negative pathogens, including drug-resistant strains. These peptides disrupt bacterial membranes and demonstrate low toxicity, making them promising candidates for combating antibiotic-resistant infections.
full_output.methodology: The peptides were identified through transcriptome analysis, recombinantly expressed, and tested for antimicrobial activity using microdilution assays, membrane permeability tests, and in vivo models.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial and Anticancer Activities of Pleurocidin-Amide, a Potent Marine Antimicrobial Peptide Derived from Winter Flounder, Pleuronectes americanus.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial and anticancer activities of Pleurocidin (Ple) and its C-terminal-amidated derivative Pleurocidin-amide (Ple-a). Both peptides showed significant antibacterial activity against a broad spectrum of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains. Ple-a also exhibited notable cytotoxicity towards various cancer cell lines, particularly A549 human lung adenocarcinoma cells, through mechanisms involving apoptosis and autophagy.

full_output.methodology: Review of literature on S. aureus intracellular survival mechanisms and antimicrobial therapy approaches.

full_output.paper_title: The Search for Antibacterial Inhibitors Targeting Cell Division Protein FtsZ at Its Nucleotide and Allosteric Binding Sites.
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on identifying small molecule inhibitors targeting the FtsZ protein, a critical component of bacterial cell division. It highlights the development of inhibitors that either replace bound GTP in the nucleotide binding pocket or bind to the allosteric site of FtsZ, providing insights into their mechanisms of action and potential as antibacterial agents.
full_output.methodology: The research involved fluorescence polarization assays, structural studies, and cytological profiling to evaluate the efficacy of FtsZ inhibitors.

full_output.methodology: PCR-RFLP, multiplex PCR, and disk diffusion methods were used to identify staphylococcal species, detect superantigen genes, and assess antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The review discusses various mechanisms of antibiotic resistance in bacteria, including resistance genes such as blaCTX-M, ermB, tet(O), vanA, vanB, and aac(6')-Ie-aph(2")-Ia, as well as mutations in gyrA, gyrB, and 23S rRNA associated with resistance to fluoroquinolones, macrolides, and other antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Literature review and analysis of published studies on antibiotic resistance mechanisms in bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and Antimicrobial Resistance of Virulent Listeria monocytogenes and Cronobacter sakazakii in Dairy Cattle, the Environment, and Dried Milk with the In Vitro Application of Natural Alternative Control.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance in Listeria monocytogenes, particularly to sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim, gentamicin, penicillin, and imipenem. Cronobacter sakazakii showed susceptibility to all tested antibiotics. The study also highlighted the presence of virulence genes (iap, hlyA, and actA) in L. monocytogenes isolates.
full_output.methodology: The study involved sampling from dairy cattle, their environment, and dried milk, followed by bacterial isolation, identification, and antibiotic resistance testing using agar disk diffusion and molecular techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Epidemiology of Antimicrobial Resistance, Virulence and Capsular Serotypes of Carbapenemase-Carrying Klebsiella pneumoniae in China.

mcr-8.mechanism: Modification of lipid A to confer resistance to polymyxins

mcr-9.mechanism: Modification of lipid A to confer resistance to polymyxins

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several carbapenemase genes, including blaKPC-2, blaNDM-5, blaNDM-1, blaOXA-232, blaOXA-48, and blaIMP-4, as well as polymyxin resistance genes mcr-1, mcr-8, and mcr-9. Additionally, mutations in mgrB, pmrB, OmpK35, and OmpK36 were associated with resistance to polymyxins and carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis using Kleborate software on 4643 carbapenemase-carrying Klebsiella pneumoniae strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of ceftolozane/tazobactam (C/T) against clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Enterobacterales from five Latin American countries, showing that C/T had moderate to good activity against these organisms, with varying susceptibility rates depending on the species and country.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using broth microdilution with Sensititre plates following CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Microbial Resistance to Carbapenems in Effluents from Gynaecological, Paediatric and Surgical Hospital Units.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteria (CRE) in hospital effluents, highlighting the association between antibiotic consumption and resistance levels. It reports significant resistance to carbapenems, particularly meropenem, in effluents from two hospital units.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed bacterial isolates from hospital effluents using standard microbiological methods, including antibiotic susceptibility testing and determination of minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC).
full_output.sample_size: 24 effluent samples from ArzH and 12 from MCH

full_output.paper_title: Development of Dicationic Bisguanidine-Arylfuran Derivatives as Potent Agents against Gram-Negative Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies dicationic bisguanidine-arylfuran derivatives as potent antibacterial agents against Gram-negative bacteria, including ESKAPE pathogens, with activity not diminished by existing antibiotic resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and evaluation of antibacterial activity against various Gram-negative bacterial strains, including ESKAPE isolates, and assessment of cytotoxicity.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance towards Critically Important Antimicrobials among Enterococcus faecalis and E. faecium in Poultry Farm Environments in Selangor, Malaysia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high resistance rates among Enterococcus faecalis and E. faecium isolates from poultry farms in Selangor, Malaysia, particularly towards tetracycline, erythromycin, and linezolid. Linezolid-resistant enterococci (LRE) were prevalent and often co-existed with resistance to other antibiotics, highlighting concerns regarding the spread of multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the VITEK 2 system on 80 enterococcal isolates from poultry farm environments.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes and mutations in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from persistent and relapsing prosthetic joint infections, including aac(6')-aph(2"), dfrB, blaZ, grlA, gyrA, and norA. These genes and mutations were experimentally validated and associated with resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic analyses, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, whole genome sequencing, and biofilm formation assays were used to characterize the AMR genes and mutations in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Characteristics of Antibiotic Resistance and Tolerance of Environmentally Endemic Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that environmental Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains had a lower percentage of antibiotic-resistant strains (4%) compared to clinical strains (35.7%). However, a high percentage of both environmental (90%) and clinical (78.8%) strains showed antibiotic-tolerance, indicating a significant risk of treatment difficulty in cases of infection.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of culture methods, PCR-based genotyping, and antibiotic susceptibility testing to isolate and characterize P. aeruginosa strains from environmental and clinical sources.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified chromosomal mutations in mgrB, pmrA, pmrB, eptA, and arnT as the primary mechanisms of polymyxin resistance in Klebsiella aerogenes. Additionally, various beta-lactam, aminoglycoside, tetracycline, quinolone, sulfonamide, trimethoprim, amphenicol, fosfomycin, macrolide, and rifamycin resistance genes were found.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations in polymyxin-resistant K. aerogenes isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Biochemical Characterizations of the Putative Endolysin Ecd09610 Catalytic Domain from Clostridioides difficile.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the biochemical properties of the putative endolysin Ecd09610 and its domain variants, showing their lytic activity against Clostridioides difficile.
full_output.methodology: Cloning, expression, purification, and lytic activity assays of Ecd09610 and its domain variants.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Activity of Sulbactam-Durlobactam against Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Clinical Isolates: A Multicentre Report from Italy.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of sulbactam-durlobactam (SUL-DUR) against 141 carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii isolates. It identified several resistance genes including blaOXA-20, blaOXA-58, blaOXA-66, blaADC-25, aac(6')-Ib3, aac(6')-Ib-cr, and mutations in gyrA (S81L) and parC (V104I, D105E). Additionally, mutations in PBP3 (Q488K and Y528H) were found in SUL-DUR resistant isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were conducted on the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: New RAPMYCOI Sensititre(TM) Antimicrobial Susceptibility Test for Atypical Rapidly Growing Mycobacteria (RGM).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of the erm(41) gene associated with inducible macrolide resistance in M. abscessus subsp. abscessus and the MUT2 mutation in the rrl gene linked to constitutive resistance in M. abscessus subsp. massiliense.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility was tested using broth microdilution and the RAPMYCOI panel, with molecular analysis via GenoType NTM-DR assay.

full_output.paper_title: Queuine Salvaging in the Human Parasite Entamoeba histolytica.
full_output.key_findings: EhDUF2419 is the enzyme that salvages queuine from Q or from E. coli K12 in E. histolytica, contributing to the parasite's resistance to oxidative stress.
full_output.methodology: Used genetic approaches, LC-MS, and APB PAGE analysis to characterize EhDUF2419's role in queuine salvage.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Factors and Mechanisms Driving Multidrug Resistance in Uropathogenic Escherichia coli-An Update.

blaCTX-M.source: BlaTEM, the first group of β-lactamases described in Gram-negative bacteria, along with BlaCTX-M are the most common β-lactamases among E. coli detected worldwide.
blaCTX-M.evidence_note: Genes encoding both these groups are mostly transferred by plasmids, but differ in their spectrum of action. Bla TEM genes mostly encode β-lactamases that are able to decompose penicillin and first-generation cephalosporins, while bla CTX-M encode enzymes which can hydrolyze even third-generation cephalosporins.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the molecular factors and mechanisms driving multidrug resistance in uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC), focusing on beta-lactamases, aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes, quinolone resistance genes, and carbapenemases. It highlights the role of mobile genetic elements in the spread of these resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews and summarizes recent findings on the role of various resistance mechanisms in UPEC, including the analysis of gene sequences, plasmid-mediated transfer, and the impact of mobile genetic elements.

full_output.paper_title: A DNA-Damage Inducible Gene Promotes the Formation of Antibiotic Persisters in Response to the Quorum Sensing Signaling Peptide in Streptococcus mutans.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies pep299 as a gene that promotes the formation of antibiotic persisters in Streptococcus mutans in response to quorum sensing signaling peptides.
full_output.methodology: Gene expression analysis, mutant analysis, and overexpression experiments were used to investigate the role of pep299 in persister formation.

full_output.paper_title: The Sources and Potential Hosts Identification of Antibiotic Resistance Genes in the Yellow River, Revealed by Metagenomic Analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified sul1, sul2, tetG, and ANT(3'')-IIa as dominant antibiotic resistance genes in the Yellow River sediments, highlighting the role of sulfonamides, tetracyclines, and aminoglycosides in resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis, 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, and real-time quantitative PCR were used to characterize the antibiotic resistome and microbial communities in the Yellow River sediments.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial, Multi-Drug and Colistin Resistance in Enterobacteriaceae in Healthy Pigs in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana, 2022: A Cross-Sectional Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mcr-1 gene in Enterobacteriaceae isolates from healthy pigs in Ghana, with 60% of phenotypic colistin-resistant E. coli and 33% of Enterobacter spp. carrying this gene. Over 60% of Enterobacteriaceae were resistant to tetracycline, and 23% of E. coli isolates showed multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Microbial isolation, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and molecular detection of the mcr-1 gene.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic Mining of Newly Isolated Salmophages for Phage Therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes 10 newly isolated Salmonella phages, identifying genes involved in anti-restriction, superinfection exclusion, and host lysis, highlighting their potential for phage therapy against Salmonella.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, de novo assembly, and functional annotation using bioinformatics tools and experimental validations.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Plasmid-Mediated Quinolone Resistance (PMQRs) Determinants and Whole Genome Sequence Screening of PMQR-Producing E. coli Isolated from Men Undergoing a Transrectal Prostate Biopsy.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance (PMQR) genes such as qnrS, qnrB, and aac(6')-Ib-cr in E. coli isolates from men undergoing transrectal prostate biopsy. Additionally, several other AMR genes were detected, including blaTEM-1B, blaOXA-1, blaTEM-CTX-M-15, and others. Mutations in gyrA, parC, and parE were also found to contribute to fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR, WGS, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify PMQR genes and mutations in E. coli isolates.

full_output.methodology: Transgenic expression of Hco-cyp-13A11 in C. elegans and motility assays to assess susceptibility to macrocyclic lactones.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the development of hydroxamic acid compounds (Compounds 4 and 6) that inhibit the metallo-β-lactamase Bla2 from Bacillus anthracis, which is responsible for β-lactam antibiotic resistance. The compounds show competitive inhibition with IC50 values in the micromolar range and bind to the active site zinc ions of Bla2.
full_output.methodology: Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vitro inhibition tests were conducted to evaluate the efficacy of the hydroxamic acid compounds against Bla2.

full_output.methodology: CRISPR-Cas9 system was used to disrupt the fosA3 gene in E. coli, followed by disk diffusion assays to assess resensitization.

full_output.paper_title: Fighting Antibiotic-Resistant Bacterial Infections by Surface Biofunctionalization of 3D-Printed Porous Titanium Implants with Reduced Graphene Oxide and Silver Nanoparticles.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that surface biofunctionalization of 3D-printed porous titanium implants with reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) enhances antibacterial activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). The rGO+Ag surfaces show improved reactive oxygen species generation, higher Ag+ release, and the presence of 'nano-knife' structures, leading to increased antibacterial efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study used plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO) to incorporate rGO and AgNPs onto titanium implants, followed by evaluation of antibacterial activity through agar diffusion assays and assessment of cellular response using metabolic activity and alkaline phosphatase activity tests.

full_output.paper_title: Decoding Genetic Features and Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Strains Isolated from Bloodstream Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various virulence factor genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains isolated from bloodstream infections, highlighting the genetic diversity and the presence of specific genes like lasB and plC_H in all tested strains.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PCR to detect the presence of virulence factor genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to evaluate resistance profiles.

full_output.key_findings: Silver nanoparticles affect the expression of biofilm-related genes (icaADBC operon and icaR) in Staphylococcus epidermidis, reducing biofilm formation and viability at higher concentrations.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR was used to analyze gene expression changes in S. epidermidis strains exposed to silver nanoparticles.

full_output.methodology: The study used a two-week feeding trial with enrofloxacin and florfenicol, followed by biochemical assays, 16S rDNA sequencing, transcriptomic analysis, and qRT-PCR to evaluate the effects on gut microbiota and immune responses in grass carp.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of blaOXA-145, blaOXA-224, blaOXA-539, and blaOXA-675 Genes and Carbapenem-Hydrolyzing Class D β-Lactamases (CHDLs) in Clinical Isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Collected from West of Iran, Hamadan.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance, biofilm formation, and virulence factors of isolates of staphylococcus pseudintermedius from healthy dogs and dogs with keratitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several virulence factors and biofilm-associated genes in Staphylococcus pseudintermedius isolates from dogs with keratitis and healthy dogs. full_output.paper_title: Co-occurrence of antibiotic resistance and virulence Genes in Methicillin Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) Isolates from Pakistan.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of tem-1 and class-1 integrons in multidrug resistant uropathogens from HIV patients with asymptomatic bacteriuria in a Tertiary Care Hospital, SouthWest Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaTEM-1 as a common gene encoding resistance to ampicillin and penicillin in multidrug-resistant uropathogens from HIV patients with asymptomatic bacteriuria.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical features and molecular epidemiology of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales infection in children.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla NDM, bla IMP, and bla KPC as the primary carbapenemase genes in carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) isolates from children, highlighting the prevalence of metallo-beta-lactamases (NDM) and serine-beta-lactamases (IMP and KPC) in CRE strains.

full_output.paper_title: Spatiotemporal Investigation of Antibiotic Resistance in the Urban Water Cycle Influenced by Environmental and Anthropogenic Activity.

full_output.paper_title: Structure-Kinetic Relationship Studies for the Development of Long Residence Time LpxC Inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the development of long residence time LpxC inhibitors, highlighting the correlation between residence time and post-antibiotic effect (PAE) in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. full_output.paper_title: Discovery of substituted benzyloxy-benzylamine inhibitors of acetyltransferase Eis and their anti-mycobacterial activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified substituted benzyloxy-benzylamine inhibitors of the acetyltransferase Eis, which is involved in kanamycin resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. full_output.paper_title: Outcomes in Oxacillinases β-Lactamases (OXA-48) and New Delhi Metallo-β-Lactamase (NDM-1)-Producing, Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella Pneumoniae Isolates Obtained From Bloodstream Infections.

full_output.paper_title: Metagenomic Analysis of Urban Wastewater Treatment Plant Effluents in Tokyo.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and PCR were used to analyze AMR genes and virulence factors in hvKp isolates.

full_output.paper_title: An Easy-to-Use Plasmid Toolset for Efficient Generation and Benchmarking of Synthetic Small RNAs in Bacteria.

bla.role_in_paper: used as a resistance marker in plasmid construction
bla.validation_method: plasmid construction and testing of sRNA targeting acrA

full_output.key_findings: The study presents a plasmid toolset for generating synthetic small RNAs (sRNAs) in bacteria, focusing on the use of sRNAs to target the acrA gene in E. coli, which is part of the AcrAB-TolC multidrug efflux pump. The toolset facilitates the rapid construction and testing of sRNAs for gene regulation.
full_output.methodology: The study uses Golden Gate cloning and plasmid engineering to create synthetic sRNAs targeting the acrA gene in E. coli, assessing their ability to increase susceptibility to the beta-lactam antibiotic oxacillin.

full_output.paper_title: Serotype Distribution and Antimicrobial Resistance of Streptococcus pneumoniae Causing Invasive Pneumococcal Disease in Korea Between 2017 and 2019 After Introduction of the 13-Valent Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the serotype distribution and antimicrobial resistance profiles of Streptococcus pneumoniae causing invasive pneumococcal disease in Korea post-PCV13 introduction, highlighting the emergence of non-PCV13 serotypes and varying resistance rates among different serotypes.
full_output.methodology: Serotyping, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and multilocus sequence typing were conducted on S. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Developing a multiplex PCR-based assay kit for bloodstream infection by analyzing genomic big data.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a multiplex PCR-based assay kit for detecting pathogens in bloodstream infections, focusing on 14 Gram-negative bacteria, 15 Gram-positive bacteria, and 4 fungi. The kit demonstrated high sensitivity and accuracy, with a detection limit of 100 copies/μl and 95.08% consistency with blood culture results.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genomic data from NCBI to construct a local database, designed primers using Primer3 and Oligo7, and optimized PCR conditions to minimize primer-primer and primer-amplicon interactions.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of Klebsiella pneumoniae human gut carriage: a comparison of culture, qPCR, and whole metagenomic sequencing methods.
full_output.key_findings: The study compares culture, qPCR, and whole metagenomic sequencing (WMS) for detecting Klebsiella pneumoniae (Kp) in human fecal samples. The ZKIR-qPCR showed high sensitivity and specificity for Kp detection, with a low limit of detection. WMS was less sensitive but could estimate Kp relative abundance. The study highlights the importance of sample preparation and the potential for false positives in WMS due to closely related Enterobacterales species.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized ZKIR-qPCR, WMS, and culture-based methods to detect and quantify Kp in fecal samples. Taxonomic profiling with Centrifuge and strain-level analysis with StrainGST were also employed.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance Profile of Enterobacteriaceae and Drinking Water Quality Among Households in Bule Hora Town, South Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance among Enterobacteriaceae isolated from household drinking water in Bule Hora Town, South Ethiopia. All isolates showed resistance to amoxicillin plus clavulanic acid and ampicillin. Shigella and Salmonella exhibited significant resistance to cotrimoxazole, chloramphenicol, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: The study used a community-based cross-sectional design, including bacteriological analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing via the Kirby-Bauer disc-diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Quantitative Evaluation of the Economic Impact of Antimicrobial Resistance on the Treatment of Community-Acquired Acute Pyelonephritis in Korea.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that ESBL-producing Enterobacteriales and ciprofloxacin-resistant Enterobacteriales cause higher medical costs and longer hospital stays for treating community-acquired acute pyelonephritis (APN).
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing medical costs and hospitalization duration for APN patients with resistant pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Production of Helvolic Acid in Metarhizium Contributes to Fungal Infection of Insects by Bacteriostatic Inhibition of the Host Cuticular Microbiomes.

MrHelA.validation_method: gene deletion and complementation, HPLC analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MrHelA as a gene responsible for helvolic acid (HA) production in Metarhizium species, which contributes to fungal infection of insects by inhibiting host cuticular bacteria through bacteriostatic mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Gene deletion, complementation, HPLC analysis, and microbiome analysis were used to validate the role of MrHelA in HA production and its impact on insect infection.

full_output.paper_title: Strongly Bactericidal All-Oral β-Lactam Combinations for the Treatment of Mycobacterium abscessus Lung Disease.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies β-lactam combinations with synergistic bactericidal activity against Mycobacterium abscessus, highlighting the importance of the erm41 gene in mediating macrolide resistance.
full_output.methodology: In vitro screening, MIC determination, time-kill experiments, and checkerboard assays were conducted to evaluate the antibacterial activity of β-lactams against M. abscessus.

full_output.paper_title: A pyrF-Based Efficient Genetic Manipulation Platform in Acinetobacter baumannii To Explore the Vital DNA Components of Adaptive Immunity for I-F CRISPR-Cas.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a pyrF-based genetic manipulation platform in Acinetobacter baumannii, enabling efficient gene deletion and manipulation. The pyrF gene was validated as a selectable and counterselectable marker for genetic studies.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation using pyrF-based vectors, PCR, and sequencing.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic Characterization of Antimicrobial-Resistant Salmonella enterica in Duck, Chicken, and Pig Farms and Retail Markets in Eastern China.

blaTEM-1B.evidence_note: The paper states that bla TEM-1B was identified in a range of different serotypes, including 100% (22/22) S. Kentucky, and that the consistency of acquired AMR genes and resistance phenotypes to ampicillin was >90%.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified 44 acquired AMR genes in Salmonella enterica isolates from duck, chicken, and pig farms and retail markets in eastern China, including aac(6')-Iaa, blaTEM-1B, floR, dfrA14, fosA7, mph(A), qnrS1, sul1, tet(A), and ARR-3, which conferred resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify AMR genes and determine their resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of Ceftolozane-Tazobactam vs. Best Alternative Therapy on Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Multidrug-Resistant and Extensively Drug-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa Lower Respiratory Tract Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that ceftolozane-tazobactam (C/T) was associated with a significant reduction in clinical failure compared to best alternative therapy in patients with multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa lower respiratory tract infections.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of adult patients with MDR/XDR P. aeruginosa LRTI treated with C/T or best alternative therapy.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genotypic antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of the emerging human respiratory pathogen Mycoplasma amphoriforme isolated from the UK and Denmark.

ParC.notes: The S89F mutation in ParC was consistently found in all fluoroquinolone-resistant isolates.

full_output.key_findings: This study identified fluoroquinolone resistance mediated by the S89F mutation in the ParC gene and macrolide/lincosamide resistance due to the A2059G mutation in the 23S rRNA gene in Mycoplasma amphoriforme isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing via microbroth dilution, whole-genome sequencing, and PCR for mutation detection.

full_output.paper_title: Mansonone G and its derivatives exhibit membrane permeabilizing activities against bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: Mansonone G and its derivatives exhibit membrane permeabilizing activities against bacteria, particularly against Gram-positive bacteria and an LPS-defected E. coli strain.
full_output.methodology: Screening of antibacterial activity, synthesis of derivatives, and fluorescent microscopy-based bacterial cytological profiling.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteriological quality and antimicrobial susceptibility profiles of isolates of ready-to-eat raw minced meat from hotels and restaurants in Arba Minch, Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 60% of bacterial isolates from ready-to-eat raw minced meat in Arba Minch, Ethiopia, were multi-drug resistant. Specific resistance patterns were observed for Salmonella spp., Campylobacter spp., Shigella spp., S. aureus, and E. coli.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance, Virulence Factor-Encoding Genes, and Biofilm-Forming Ability of Community-Associated Uropathogenic Escherichia coli in Western Saudi Arabia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of virulence factor-encoding genes (kpsMTII, iutA, traT, csgA, sat, vat) and antimicrobial resistance genes (bla CTX-M, bla KPC) in community-associated Uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) isolates in Western Saudi Arabia. High resistance rates to norfloxacin, ampicillin, and trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole were observed, while no resistance to carbapenems was detected.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to detect virulence factor-encoding genes and antimicrobial resistance in UPEC isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization of multi drug resistant Escherichia coli isolates at a tertiary hospital in Abuja, Nigeria.

blaOXA-2.evidence_note: The paper mentions bla OXA-1 and bla OXA-2 genes were detected in 50 (46.7%) and four (3.7%) of the isolates, respectively. However, it does not explicitly state that blaOXA-2 confers resistance to penicillins.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in multi-drug resistant E. coli isolates, including bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-14, bla CTX-M-27, bla CTX-M-65, bla OXA-1, bla OXA-2, bla CMY-2, bla NDM-1, bla NDM-5, aac(3)-IId, aac(3)-IIe, aac(6')-Ib-cr, aad A5, ant(2′′)-Ia, aph(3′′)-Ib, aph(3′′)-VI, aph(6)-Id, ermB, ermD, fosA3, fosA7, mdtM, emrD, sul1, sul2, sul3, tetA, tetB, tetM, dfrA1, dfrA7, dfrA8, dfrA12, dfrA14, dfrA17, dfrA82, dfrB4, qepA, qepA1, qepA2, qepA4, qnrB19, qnrS1, qacE, catA1, catA2, catB3, cmlA1, mphA.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and their resistance profiles in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of MA01 rhamnolipid on cell viability and expression of quorum-sensing (QS) genes involved in biofilm formation by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that rhamnolipid from Pseudomonas aeruginosa MA01 affects the expression of genes involved in biofilm formation in MRSA, including icaA, icaD, agrA, agrC, and srtA, leading to reduced biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The study used real-time PCR to analyze gene expression and biofilm assays to assess the impact of rhamnolipid on MRSA biofilm formation.

full_output.paper_title: Drug resistant bacteria in perianal abscesses are frequent and relevant.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the frequent occurrence of drug-resistant bacteria in perianal abscesses, particularly in patients with complex and severe infections. It emphasizes the importance of microbiological testing for guiding appropriate antibiotic therapy.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing microbiological data from perianal abscess swabs and their resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Novel chemical entities inhibiting Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth identified by phenotypic high-throughput screening.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 4PP and PCB series as targeting MmpL3, with resistant mutants showing mutations in MmpL3.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput phenotypic screening of a chemical library against M. tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of aminoglycoside modifying enzymes, SCCmec, coagulase gene and PCR-RFLP coagulase gene typing of Staphylococcus aureus isolates from hospitals in Shiraz, southwest of Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified aac(6')-Ie-aph(2") as the most prevalent aminoglycoside modifying enzyme gene among MRSA isolates, along with ant(4')-Ia and aph(3')-IIIa. High resistance to gentamicin and streptomycin was observed.
full_output.methodology: PCR and RFLP analysis for gene detection and typing.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Toxin-Antitoxin Systems in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
full_output.key_findings: This study characterizes various toxin-antitoxin (TA) systems in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, including new type I, IV, and VIII TA systems, and identifies their distribution and potential interactions with mobile genetic elements and antibiotic resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: In silico analysis of genomic sequencing data, sequence alignment, structural prediction, and comparative genomics.

full_output.paper_title: Fish as sentinels of antimicrobial resistant bacteria, epidemic carbapenemase genes, and antibiotics in surface water.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of antimicrobial resistant bacteria (ARB) and antimicrobial resistance genes (ARG) in fish from the Scioto River, including bla CMY, bla CTX-M, bla KPC, and bla NDM genes. These genes were found in the intestinal microbiota of fish, indicating their potential as bioindicators of environmental contamination.
full_output.methodology: Culture methods, PCR, droplet digital PCR, and UHPLC-MS/MS were used to screen for ARB, ARG, and antibiotics in fish samples.

full_output.paper_title: Lipocalin-2 is an essential component of the innate immune response to Acinetobacter baumannii infection.

Lcn2.validation_method: transcriptional profiling and in vitro growth inhibition

full_output.key_findings: Lipocalin-2 (Lcn2) is upregulated during Acinetobacter baumannii infection and plays a critical role in the innate immune response by sequestering iron, thereby inhibiting bacterial growth.
full_output.methodology: NanoString technology for gene expression analysis and in vitro bacterial growth assays.

full_output.paper_title: Predicting antibiotic resistance in complex protein targets using alchemical free energy methods.

gyrA.notes: Resistant to moxifloxacin

full_output.key_findings: The study uses alchemical free energy methods to predict antibiotic resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis by analyzing mutations in RNA polymerase and DNA gyrase. It identifies specific mutations that confer resistance to rifampicin and moxifloxacin.
full_output.methodology: Alchemical free energy calculations were used to predict the effects of mutations on antibiotic binding and resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Antidepressants promote the spread of antibiotic resistance via horizontally conjugative gene transfer.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that antidepressants can promote the conjugative transfer of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) between different bacterial genera, highlighting the potential link between antidepressant use and the spread of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used conjugation assays with plasmids RP4 and pMS6198A, along with various analytical techniques to evaluate the impact of antidepressants on gene transfer.

full_output.paper_title: Protein tyrosine kinase 2b inhibition reverts niche-associated resistance to tyrosine kinase inhibitors in AML.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LPXN and PTK2B as critical players in acquired midostaurin resistance in AML, demonstrating that their inhibition can revert resistance-associated phenotypes and enhance the efficacy of tyrosine kinase inhibitors.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized proteome analyses, co-immunoprecipitation, western blotting, and cell viability assays to investigate the role of LPXN and PTK2B in AML resistance.

full_output.paper_title: A visualization reporter system for characterizing antibiotic biosynthetic gene clusters expression with high-sensitivity.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a visualization reporter system (VRS-bAHL) based on Gram-negative bacterial acyl-homoserine lactone quorum-sensing for characterizing gene expression in Streptomyces. The system was used to identify and characterize the oxazolomycin biosynthetic gene cluster (oxa) and to improve the production of oxazolomycin derivatives.
full_output.methodology: The VRS-bAHL system was constructed using the AHL synthase gene cviI as a reporter, driven by target promoters of Streptomyces. AHL production was detected using indicator strains and various methods including double-layer plate, agar plug, and co-cultivation assays.

full_output.paper_title: Resistance to fosfomycin is increasing and is significantly associated with extended-spectrum β-lactamase-production in urinary isolates of Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: Fosfomycin resistance is increasing in Escherichia coli urinary isolates and is significantly associated with extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) production, particularly with CTX-M-type ESBLs.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR for ESBL detection, and statistical analysis of resistance trends.

full_output.paper_title: Patterns of antimicrobial resistance in Salmonella isolates from fattening pigs in Spain.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed antimicrobial resistance patterns in 1,318 Salmonella isolates from pigs in Spain, identifying high resistance rates to tetracycline, sulfamethoxazole, streptomycin, ampicillin, and chloramphenicol. Multidrug-resistant isolates were prevalent, with specific serotypes showing distinct resistance profiles.
full_output.methodology: The study used antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) and statistical analyses to evaluate resistance patterns in Salmonella isolates from pigs in Spain.

full_output.paper_title: VanA-Enterococcus faecalis in Poland: hospital population clonal structure and vanA mobilome.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the epidemiological situation of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecalis of VanA-phenotype in Poland, identifying the prevalence of specific Tn1546 transposon types and plasmid replicons associated with vanA.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic assays, MLST, PFGE, PCR, sequencing, and conjugation experiments were used to analyze the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Burkholderia pseudomallei biofilm phenotypes confined but surviving in neutrophil extracellular traps of varying appearance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the bpsl0618 gene, a sugar-transferase gene, as critical for Burkholderia pseudomallei biofilm formation and survival against neutrophil-mediated killing. The gene's presence was associated with increased extracellular DNA release and resistance to NET-mediated killing.
full_output.methodology: The study involved constructing and comparing biofilm-producing, biofilm-defective, and biofilm-complemented strains of B. pseudomallei, assessing their interactions with neutrophils and NETs through various experimental techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and antibacterial activity evaluation of N (7) position-modified balofloxacins.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of N (7) position-modified balofloxacins, with compound 2-e showing potent activity against MRSA and P. aeruginosa. It exhibited low toxicity and effectively disrupted MRSA cell membranes.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and characterization of fluoroquinolone derivatives, along with in vitro antibacterial activity testing, hemolysis assays, and atomic force microscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Changes in the phenotypic susceptibility of Mannheimia haemolytica isolates to macrolide antimicrobials during the early feeding period following metaphylactic tulathromycin use in western Canadian feedlot calves.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the macrolide resistance genes msrE and mphE in Mannheimia haemolytica isolates following metaphylactic tulathromycin use in feedlot calves, indicating the emergence of macrolide-resistant clones.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR screening of 36 isolates for macrolide resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic insight into the integrative conjugative elements from ICEHpa1 family.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies four novel ICEHpa1 variants (ICE Gpa1818, ICE Gpa1808, ICE Gpa1807, and ICE Gpa1815) carrying diverse resistance genes, including tetracycline, streptomycin, gentamicin, sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim, florfenicol, and amoxicillin resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, MIC testing, and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the resistance genes and mechanisms in the ICEHpa1 family.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified six marine bacterial strains capable of producing bioactive molecules with strong antibacterial activity against E. coli, S. aureus, and L. monocytogenes. These molecules exhibited heat stability and were primarily composed of carbohydrates.
full_output.methodology: Marine bacteria were isolated, cultured under various conditions, and their supernatants were tested for antibacterial activity using agar-well diffusion assays.

full_output.paper_title: Genome Analysis of an Enterococcal Prophage, Entfac.MY.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the genome of an enterococcal prophage, Entfac.MY, and identified 254 prophage genes, including those involved in packaging, structural components, replication, and lysis. Some genes had unknown functions, highlighting the need for further research.
full_output.methodology: Next-generation sequencing was used to analyze the prophage genome, and genes were functionally annotated.

mecA.validation_method: LAMP assay with DNA from tissue samples

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the feasibility of a LAMP assay for detecting methicillin-susceptible (MSSA) and methicillin-resistant (MRSA) Staphylococcus aureus in tissue samples, demonstrating high sensitivity for both types.
full_output.methodology: LAMP assay with DNA extracted from tissue samples and analyzed for the presence of 16S rRNA, femA, and mecA genes.

full_output.paper_title: A truncated peptide Spgillcin(177-189) derived from mud crab Scylla paramamosain exerting multiple antibacterial activities.
full_output.key_findings: A truncated peptide derived from the Spgillcin gene, Spgillcin 177-189, exhibits broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity against various bacterial strains, including multidrug-resistant isolates, without inducing resistance.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, peptide synthesis, antimicrobial assays, and microscopic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Co-occurrence of dual carbapenemases KPC-2 and OXA-48 with the mobile colistin resistance gene mcr-9.1 in Enterobacter xiangfangensis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the co-occurrence of the carbapenemases KPC-2 and OXA-48 along with the mobile colistin resistance gene mcr-9.1 in the extreme drug-resistant Enterobacter xiangfangensis isolate va18651.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes in the isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of whole-genome sequence to predict drug resistance of nine anti-tuberculosis drugs and characterize resistance genes in clinical rifampicin-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Ningbo, China.

rpoB.mechanism: mutation

full_output.key_findings: The study characterized various mutations in genes associated with resistance to nine anti-tuberculosis drugs in rifampicin-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Ningbo, China. Key findings include mutations in katG, fabG1, rpoB, embB, rrs, gyrA, gid, rspL, thyA, folC, ribD, and dfrA, which confer resistance to isoniazid, rifampicin, ethambutol, streptomycin, amikacin, capreomycin, levofloxacin, and para-aminosalicylic acid.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was used to analyze drug resistance in 59 rifampicin-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates. The study compared WGS results with phenotypic drug susceptibility tests (DST) to validate the accuracy of WGS in predicting drug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Evolutionary History and Strength of Selection Determine the Rate of Antibiotic Resistance Adaptation.

full_output.paper_title: Nasal Staphylococcus aureus and S. pseudintermedius carriage in healthy dogs and cats: a systematic review of their antibiotic resistance, virulence and genetic lineages of zoonotic relevance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various AMR genes such as mecA, blaZ, tet(M), erm(B), aac(6')-aph(2"), aadD, ant(6)-Ia, and sat4 in Staphylococcus aureus and S. pseudintermedius isolates from healthy dogs and cats, indicating widespread antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review of studies reporting nasal carriage of S. aureus and S. pseudintermedius in healthy dogs and cats, focusing on AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of ellagic acid and gallic acid as efflux pump inhibitors in strains of Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: Gallic acid showed potential as an adjuvant in antibiotic therapy against multidrug-resistant bacteria by inhibiting the TetK efflux pump in Staphylococcus aureus strains IS-58 and K2068.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LmOBP11 as a gene involved in the immune response and chemical perception of locusts during infection with Metarhizium anisopliae. Knockdown of LmOBP11 increases resistance to fungal infection but suppresses immune responses, highlighting a trade-off between immune activation and chemical perception.
