full_output.paper_title: Novel Coumarins Derivatives for A. baumannii Lung Infection Developed by High-Throughput Screening and Reinforcement Learning.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed novel coumarin derivatives, including S1032, which showed strong antibacterial activity against Acinetobacter baumannii, reducing bacterial growth and biofilm formation, and improving survival rates in a murine lung infection model.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening, molecular docking, and reinforcement learning were used to design and evaluate novel coumarin derivatives for their antibacterial activity against A. baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Organic fertilization co-selects genetically linked antibiotic and metal(loid) resistance genes in global soil microbiome.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes various antibiotic and metal(loid) resistance genes, including mdtA, mdtB, mdtC, acr3, arsC2, arsH, arsR3, Tn6183, Tn6302, sul2, vanS, arsM, macB, and wtpC, which are co-selected in agricultural soils under organic fertilization. These genes are associated with multidrug, arsenic, and sulfonamide resistance, and their co-existence suggests a genetic linkage driven by environmental pressures.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic and metatranscriptomic analyses were conducted on 511 agricultural soil samples to identify and characterize resistance genes and their co-existence under different fertilization practices.

full_output.paper_title: Study of MIC of silver and zinc oxide nanoparticles, strong and cost-effective antibacterial against biofilm-producing Acinetobacter baumannii in Shiraz, Southwest of Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the prevalence of efflux pump genes (adeR, adeC, adeA, abeM, adeK, adeI) in biofilm-producing Acinetobacter baumannii isolates and found a relationship between the frequency of these genes and the MIC of silver and zinc oxide nanoparticles.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR to detect efflux pump genes and determined the MIC of silver and zinc oxide nanoparticles against Acinetobacter baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: In Vivo and in Vitro activity of colistin-conjugated bimetallic silver-copper oxide nanoparticles against Pandrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that colistin-conjugated bimetallic silver-copper oxide nanoparticles (Col-Ag-CuO NPs) effectively reduce the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of colistin against a pandrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolate, indicating potential as an alternative treatment option.
full_output.methodology: The study synthesized and characterized colistin-conjugated silver, copper oxide, and bimetallic silver-copper oxide nanoparticles using gamma radiation and evaluated their antimicrobial activity through agar well diffusion, broth microdilution, and biofilm assays.

full_output.paper_title: Cefiderocol susceptibility of Achromobacter spp.: study of an accurately identified collection of 230 strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that cefiderocol exhibits excellent in vitro activity against a large collection of accurately identified Achromobacter strains, with 99.1% of strains being susceptible to cefiderocol.
full_output.methodology: The study determined cefiderocol minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) using the broth microdilution reference method according to EUCAST guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Gram-negative bacterial infections in surgical intensive care unit patients following abdominal surgery: high mortality associated with Stenotrophomonas maltophilia infection.
full_output.key_findings: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia infections in post-abdominal surgery patients are linked to higher mortality than non-S. maltophilia GNB and P. aeruginosa infections.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective study analyzing patients with GNB infections following abdominal surgery.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence of carbapenem-resistant hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae in oysters in Egypt: a significant public health issue.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified carbapenem-resistant hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (CR-hvKp) in oysters in Egypt, highlighting the presence of carbapenemase genes (bla VIM, bla OXA−48, bla NDM, bla KPC) and hypervirulence genes (peg-344, rmpA, rmpA2, iucA, iroB).
full_output.methodology: PCR and phenotypic testing for carbapenem resistance and hypervirulence genes.

full_output.paper_title: Dissemination of clinical Escherichia coli strains harboring mcr-1, bla(NDM-7) and siderophore-producing plasmids in a Chinese hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of mcr-1 and bla(NDM-7) genes in clinical Escherichia coli strains, highlighting their role in colistin and carbapenem resistance, respectively. The strains also harbor siderophore-producing plasmids, contributing to their virulence and adaptability.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing, conjugation experiments, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze resistance patterns and plasmid transferability.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical differences between Raoultella spp. and Klebsiella oxytoca.
full_output.key_findings: Raoultella spp. showed higher resistance to Trimethoprim/Sulfamethoxazole compared to Klebsiella oxytoca, with no significant differences in other antibiotic resistances.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of clinical data from a tertiary care hospital.
full_output.sample_size: 43 patients with Raoultella infection and 1173 patients with Klebsiella oxytoca infection

full_output.key_findings: The study compared culture-based susceptibility-guided tailored therapy with empirical concomitant therapy for Helicobacter pylori treatment, finding no significant difference in eradication rates. Tailored therapy showed higher eradication rates for dual-resistant strains but did not demonstrate overall superiority.
full_output.methodology: Randomized clinical trial comparing two treatment approaches for H. pylori, involving 312 patients with culture-positive infections.

full_output.paper_title: A new anti-CRISPR gene promotes the spread of drug-resistance plasmids in Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: A new anti-CRISPR gene, acrIE10, was identified in Klebsiella pneumoniae. It interacts with the Cas7* subunit of the I-E* CRISPR-Cas system, preventing its hexamerization and thereby inhibiting the surveillance complex assembly and crRNA loading.
full_output.methodology: Yeast two-hybrid assay, plasmid transformation assay, phage infection assay, co-purification, size-exclusion chromatography, and structural analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the chromosomal integration of the blaNDM-1 gene in a carbapenem-resistant Proteus mirabilis strain, along with multiple other resistance genes, highlighting the complexity of resistance mechanisms in this bacterium.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the resistance genes in the strain.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-Genome Sequence Analysis of Antibiotic Resistance, Virulence, and Plasmid Dynamics in Multidrug-Resistant E. coli Isolates from Imported Shrimp.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance genes in multidrug-resistant E. coli isolates from imported shrimp, including aac(3)-II, aac(3)-IIa, aac(3)-IId, aadA2, aph(3″)-Ib, aph(6)-Id, catA2, cmlA1, dfrA12, qacE, sul1, sul2, tetA, tetC, and vgaC. Mutations in pmrB, gyrA, and parC were also found to contribute to resistance against colistin, ciprofloxacin, and nalidixic acid.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatic analysis were used to identify antibiotic resistance genes and mutations in E. coli isolates from imported shrimp.

full_output.paper_title: Environmentally Relevant Concentrations of Tetracycline Promote Horizontal Transfer of Antimicrobial Resistance Genes via Plasmid-Mediated Conjugation.
full_output.key_findings: Tetracycline at environmentally relevant concentrations enhances the conjugative transfer of antimicrobial resistance genes via plasmid pVP52-1 from Vibrio parahaemolyticus to Escherichia coli. The study identifies tetA and tetR(A) as key tetracycline resistance genes involved in this process.
full_output.methodology: Conjugation experiments, transcriptional analysis, and ROS generation measurements were used to assess the impact of tetracycline on antimicrobial resistance gene transfer.

full_output.paper_title: Use of Aloe Vera Gel as Media to Assess Antimicrobial Activity and Development of Antimicrobial Nanocomposites.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antimicrobial properties of silver nanoparticles (SAE-AgNPs) and cobalt nanoparticles (CoNPs) using various diffusion assays, including a novel Aloe Vera gel diffusion method. It highlights the effectiveness of these nanoparticles against multiple bacterial strains, with SAE-AgNPs showing higher activity against Gram-negative bacteria and CoNPs demonstrating significant antimicrobial effects, especially against resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study employed drop diffusion, well diffusion, disk diffusion, and Aloe Vera gel diffusion assays to evaluate the antimicrobial properties of silver and cobalt nanoparticles against various bacterial and fungal strains.

full_output.paper_title: The ArgR-Regulated ADI Pathway Facilitates the Survival of Vibrio fluvialis under Acidic Conditions.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the ADI gene cluster (arcD, arcA, arcB, arcC) and the transcriptional regulator ArgR as critical for the acid resistance of Vibrio fluvialis. ArgR directly binds to the promoter regions of arcD and arcACB to activate their transcription, enhancing the survival of V. fluvialis under acidic conditions.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized RT-PCR, EMSA, DNase I footprinting, and reporter gene fusion assays to investigate the regulation of the ADI pathway by ArgR in Vibrio fluvialis.

full_output.paper_title: 1,3,5-Triazine as Branching Connector for the Construction of Novel Antimicrobial Peptide Dendrimers: Synthesis and Biological Characterization.
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the synthesis and biological characterization of novel antimicrobial peptide dendrimers incorporating 1,3,5-triazine as a branching unit. These dendrimers demonstrate significant antimicrobial activity against Gram-negative bacteria, including multidrug-resistant isolates, and show potential as efflux pump inhibitors.
full_output.methodology: Solid-phase peptide synthesis, antimicrobial activity testing, time-kill curve analysis, and efflux pump inhibition studies.

full_output.paper_title: Biological Characterization and Genomic Analysis of Three Novel Serratia- and Enterobacter-Specific Virulent Phages.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified three novel virulent phages (KKP_3708, KKP_3709, and KKP_3711) targeting Serratia and Enterobacter species, which show potential for food biocontrol. No antibiotic resistance genes were detected in the phage genomes.
full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, morphological analysis via TEM, host range determination, growth inhibition assays, and genomic sequencing followed by bioinformatic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Optimizing Antimicrobial Peptide Design: Integration of Cell-Penetrating Peptides, Amyloidogenic Fragments, and Amino Acid Residue Modifications.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated peptides R23F S *, V31K S *, and R44K S * engineered with amyloidogenic fragments and cell-penetrating peptides, showing enhanced antimicrobial activity against various bacterial strains, including S. aureus, MRSA, P. aeruginosa, and E. coli, at lower concentrations compared to unmodified peptides.
full_output.methodology: Peptides were synthesized and purified, and their antimicrobial activity was assessed against multiple bacterial strains in liquid medium. Electrophysiological techniques were used to study the effect of R44K S on lipid bilayers, and cytotoxicity was evaluated against human cells.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the accuracy of whole genome sequencing (WGS)-based predictions of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) to first-line drugs for Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) isolates. It identifies specific genes and mutations associated with resistance to isoniazid, rifampin, ethambutol, and pyrazinamide.
full_output.methodology: The study uses WGS and phenotypic susceptibility testing (DST) to compare AMR predictions for MTBC isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Upregulated Palmitoleate and Oleate Production in Escherichia coli Promotes Gentamicin Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that upregulated production of palmitoleate and oleate in gentamicin-resistant E. coli promotes resistance by reducing intracellular gentamicin levels and mitigating reactive oxygen species accumulation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized untargeted metabolomics, growth curve analysis, MIC determination, and ELISA to assess the role of palmitoleate and oleate in gentamicin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: New Triazole-Isoxazole Hybrids as Antibacterial Agents: Design, Synthesis, Characterization, In Vitro, and In Silico Studies.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and evaluation of triazole-isoxazole hybrids, with compound 7b showing strong antibacterial activity against Gram-negative bacteria, including Escherichia coli and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis, spectroscopic characterization, in vitro antibacterial testing, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations.

full_output.paper_title: Total Syntheses and Antibacterial Studies of Natural Isoflavones: Scandenone, Osajin, and 6,8-Diprenylgenistein.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the total synthesis of three natural isoflavones, scandenone (1), osajin (2), and 6,8-diprenylgenistein (3), and evaluates their antibacterial activities against Gram-positive bacteria. Osajin (2) showed the highest antibacterial activity against MRSA with a MIC value of 2 μg/mL. The study also demonstrated that osajin disrupts bacterial cell membranes, as evidenced by SEM analysis.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of isoflavones and their evaluation for antibacterial activity using MIC assays and SEM analysis.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the synergistic effect of combining ceftriaxone and human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells (HUCDMSCs) in treating acute septic arthritis (ASA). The combination therapy was found to be more effective than either treatment alone in reducing inflammation, bacterial load, and joint damage.
full_output.methodology: The study used a murine model of ASA, with animals treated with ceftriaxone, HUCDMSCs, or a combination of both. Various assessments included body weight, cytokine levels, bacterial colony-forming units, and imaging techniques to evaluate joint damage.

full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using CLSI standards, with resistotypes categorized based on susceptibility to four antibiotics.

These mutations include F88L, R464A, D434N, H457L/N/Y, T436I, V90I, P406L, V407F, G451V, G452C/SV, and T385N. full_output.paper_title: Improved Blue Carba test and Carba NP test for detection and classification of major Class A and B carbapenemases, including dual producers, among Gram-negative bacilli.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance in Enterococci and Enterobacteriaceae from Laboratory-Reared Fresh Mealworm Larvae (Tenebrio molitor L.) and Their Frass.
full_output.key_findings: The study found intrinsic resistance in enterococci and Enterobacteriaceae isolated from mealworm larvae and frass, with specific resistance patterns observed for vancomycin, quinupristin-dalfopristin, cefoxitin, ampicillin, and amoxicillin-clavulanic acid. full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic Resistance Profile and Bio-Control of Multidrug-Resistant Escherichia coli Isolated from Raw Milk in Vietnam Using Bacteriophages.

full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, multiplex PCR, and phage efficacy trials were used to identify AMR genes and assess phage effectiveness.

full_output.paper_title: HIV-Negative MSM Infected with Two Different Isolates of Drug-Resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae-Case Report.
full_output.key_findings: Two different isolates of drug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae were identified in a patient, with the oropharyngeal isolate showing resistance to azithromycin and the urethral isolate showing resistance to penicillin, ciprofloxacin, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using Etest on gonococcal isolates, and genomic DNA isolation and molecular typing (NG-MAST) were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Monitoring Changes in the Antimicrobial-Resistance Gene Set (ARG) of Raw Milk and Dairy Products in a Cattle Farm, from Production to Consumption.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 112 antibiotic-resistance genes in raw milk and dairy products, with a significant increase in resistant genes in aged cheese compared to raw milk. Key genes included OXA-662 and OXA-309, which confer resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics, and several efflux pump genes like abaQ, emrA, and acrAB-tolC, which contribute to fluoroquinolone resistance. The findings highlight the dynamic changes in the resistome during food processing and the potential public health risks associated with the spread of antibiotic resistance genes through raw dairy products.
full_output.methodology: Next-generation sequencing was used to analyze the antimicrobial-resistance gene pool in raw milk and cheese samples collected from a cattle farm, tracking changes from production to consumption.
full_output.sample_size: Five replicates at each sampling point.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of genotyping and phenotyping characteristics of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaOXA-48, blaIMP, and blaNDM genes as the primary carbapenem resistance mechanisms in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic methods including PCR, Blue-carba test, and Carbapenem inactivation method were used to detect carbapenemase production.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified beta-lactam resistance genes in clinical isolates of E. coli, demonstrating their reduced susceptibility to antibacterial treatment.
full_output.methodology: Experimental evaluation of bacterial growth and metabolic activity following treatment with S-nitrosoglutathione (GSNO).

full_output.paper_title: Metagenomic airborne resistome from urban hot spots through the One Health lens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a wide variety of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in airborne particles from urban hot spots, including hospitals and wastewater treatment plants. The highest ARG abundance was found in the wastewater treatment plant, with 32 ARG hits per Gb of metagenome, followed by the hospital's main entrance with approximately 5 ARG hits per Gb of metagenome. No ARGs were detected in the viral fractions analyzed.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis of airborne particles collected from urban hot spots, including hospitals and wastewater treatment plants, using sequencing and bioinformatic tools to identify and characterize ARGs.
full_output.sample_size: Five air samples were taken and analyzed: three outdoor samples from a wastewater treatment plant and two samples from a hospital.

full_output.paper_title: Arginine catabolism is essential to polymyxin dependence in Acinetobacter baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: First Characterization of Acinetobacter baumannii-Specific Filamentous Phages.

full_output.methodology: The study employed in silico analysis, PCR, TEM imaging, protein profiling, and functional assays to identify and characterize filamentous phages in A. baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli isolates and virulence gene expression in poultry farms in Jos, Nigeria.

full_output.paper_title: Using tea nanoclusters as β-lactamase inhibitors to cure multidrug-resistant bacterial pneumonia: A promising therapeutic strategy by Chinese materioherbology.

full_output.paper_title: Average nucleotide identity-based Staphylococcus aureus strain grouping allows identification of strain-specific genes in the pangenome.

It found that intermediate frequency genes in the pangenome can be classified into strain-concentrated and strain-diffuse categories, with strain-diffuse genes often associated with prophages and virulence factors, while strain-concentrated genes were linked to the vSaβ genome island. Antibiotic resistance genes were enriched in the strain-diffuse class.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and risk factors of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase producing E. coli causing urinary tract infections in Iceland during 2012-2021.

Key risk factors included male sex, older age, hospitalization, previous antibiotic use (particularly ciprofloxacin), and proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use.
full_output.methodology: The study was a case-control analysis using data from national registries and laboratory information systems, examining risk factors for ESBL-producing E. coli in UTIs.

full_output.paper_title: The Hidden Epidemic of Isoniazid-Resistant Tuberculosis in South Africa.

full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of phenotypic drug susceptibility testing, FluoroType MTBDR, Sanger sequencing, targeted deep sequencing, and whole-genome sequencing to analyze isoniazid resistance in tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and genotypic characterization of commensal staphylococci isolated from young volunteers in Alexandria, Egypt.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of cell lysis treatment before saliva metagenomic DNA extraction on the oral microbiome and the associated resistome.

full_output.paper_title: BMAL2 promotes eCIRP-induced macrophage endotoxin tolerance.

full_output.paper_title: Development of an inhibitor of the mutagenic SOS response that suppresses the evolution of quinolone antibiotic resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies OXF-077 as a potent inhibitor of the mutagenic SOS response, which suppresses the evolution of quinolone resistance in S. aureus. full_output.methodology: The study involved the design, synthesis, and evaluation of analogues of IMP-1700, focusing on structure-activity relationships (SAR) to identify compounds that inhibit the SOS response and potentiate DNA-damaging antibiotics. full_output.paper_title: Nosocomial outbreak caused by disinfectant-resistant Serratia marcescens in an adult intensive care unit, Hungary, February to March 2022.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified disinfectant-resistant Serratia marcescens strains in an ICU outbreak, highlighting the importance of environmental monitoring and proper disinfectant use.

full_output.key_findings: The study develops a machine-learning classifier called MTB++ to predict phenotypic resistance of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to a broad range of antibiotics using whole-genome sequencing data and antibiotic susceptibility testing. The classifier achieves high discrimination for most antibiotics, particularly for first-line drugs.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a machine-learning approach combining LASSO logistic regression and random forests to classify resistance based on 31-mers from whole-genome sequencing data.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring novel microbial metabolites and drugs for inhibiting Clostridioides difficile.

full_output.paper_title: Patient characteristics and antimicrobial susceptibility profiles of Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae infections in international travellers: a GeoSentinel analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies carbapenem resistance mechanisms, including NDM and OXA-48 beta-lactamases, in E. coli and K. pneumoniae isolates from international travelers, highlighting regional variations in antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The review highlights the prevalence and mechanisms of multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) in solid organ transplant (SOT) recipients, focusing on ESBL-producing Enterobacterales, carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE), difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (DTR-Pa), and carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CR-Ab). Key AMR genes identified include blaCTX-M, blaKPC, blaOXA-48, blaNDM, and blaVIM.
full_output.methodology: Narrative review based on a PubMed search of literature published between June 2013 and June 2023.

full_output.paper_title: Anti-Infection of Oral Microorganisms from Herbal Medicine of Piper crocatum Ruiz & Pav.
full_output.key_findings: The study discusses the anti-infective potential of Red Betel leaf (Piper crocatum Ruiz & Pav) against oral pathogens such as S. mutans, S. sanguinis, E. faecalis, and C. albicans. It identifies bioactive compounds with antibacterial, antifungal, and antiviral activities, highlighting their mechanisms of action and potential as natural alternatives to synthetic anti-infectives.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed the phytochemical composition of Red Betel leaf extracts and evaluated their anti-infective activities through in vitro assays, molecular docking, and bioactivity testing against various pathogens.

full_output.methodology: Phenotypic detection methods including Imipenem EDTA synergy test, DDST, and D-test were used to identify β-lactamases and colistin resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of integrons (intI1, intI2, intI3) in clinical E. coli isolates, which are associated with resistance against beta-lactams and fluoroquinolones. Integrons were found in 67.6% of isolates, with intI1 being the most prevalent.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical Findings, Bacterial Agents, and Antibiotic Resistance in Children with Spontaneous Peritonitis in Southern Iran: An Academic Tertiary Referral Center's Experience.
full_output.key_findings: The study found high bacterial resistance to third-generation cephalosporins in children with spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP), highlighting the need for region-specific empirical antibiotic therapy.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of clinical and microbiological data from pediatric patients with ascites and SBP.

full_output.paper_title: Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) Profiling of Extensively Drug-Resistant (XDR) Pathogenic Bacteria in Pulmonary Tuberculosis Patients.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of rpoB, inhA, and katG genes associated with rifampicin and isoniazid resistance in XDR pulmonary TB strains using PCR profiling.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification targeting rpoB, inhA, and katG genes followed by gel electrophoresis for detection of resistance markers.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical Characteristics and Risk Factors for Infection and Death in Critically Ill Patients with Pulmonary Infection with Elizabethkingia Spp.
full_output.key_findings: Elizabethkingia spp. is highly resistant to cephalosporins, carbapenems, macrolides, and aminoglycosides, and is sensitive to fluoroquinolones, minocycline, and co-trimoxazole.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective case-control study analyzing antimicrobial susceptibility testing results of isolated strains.

full_output.paper_title: Sequence diversity of apidaecin-like peptides arresting the terminating ribosome.
full_output.key_findings: The study explores the sequence diversity of apidaecin-like peptides and identifies multiple substituted variants capable of arresting ribosomes at stop codons. Some of these variants exhibit improved antibacterial activity compared to the wild-type prAMP.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a library of synthetic mutant apidaecin genes, deep mutational screening, and next-generation sequencing to identify active peptides.

full_output.paper_title: Extended period of selection for antimicrobial resistance due to recirculation of persistent antimicrobials in broilers.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that stable antimicrobials like doxycycline and enrofloxacin persist in broiler feces for extended periods, leading to prolonged selection pressure for antimicrobial resistance. Amoxicillin, being unstable, did not show significant resistance gene increases. Enrofloxacin treatment resulted in a complete non-WT E. coli population, suggesting resistance mediated by point mutations.
full_output.methodology: The study used shotgun metagenomics and phenotypic susceptibility testing to analyze the resistome and resistance levels in E. coli isolates from broilers treated with different antimicrobials.

full_output.paper_title: Machine learning-based classification reveals distinct clusters of non-coding genomic allelic variations associated with Erm-mediated antibiotic resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies how specific alleles in the upstream regions of the ermB gene influence the formation of RNA hairpin structures, thereby modulating ermB expression and affecting MLS resistance. Experimental validation confirmed the predictive model linking allele combinations to resistance phenotypes.
full_output.methodology: Population-wide genomic analysis, machine learning clustering, RNA secondary structure prediction, and experimental validation in Staphylococcus aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology of Clostridioides difficile infection at one hospital 10 years after an outbreak of the epidemic C. difficile strain BI/027: changing strain prevalence, antimicrobial susceptibilities, and patient antibiotic exposures.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the epidemic C. difficile strain BI/027 decreased in prevalence, while strains Y and DH increased. BI isolates showed high-level resistance to fluoroquinolones and azithromycin, and resistance to ceftriaxone was higher among BI isolates compared to other strains.

These mutations were not observed in strains evolved under Melittin or Cecropin P1 selection, indicating selective pressure from specific antimicrobials.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the antimicrobial peptide 2K4L exhibits antibacterial activity against both multidrug-resistant and susceptible strains of Acinetobacter baumannii, reduces inflammation, and provides protection against LPS-induced septic shock in mice.

full_output.paper_title: Adult acute leukemia patients with gram-negative bacteria bloodstream infection: Risk factors and outcomes of antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies risk factors for multidrug-resistant (MDR) and carbapenem-resistant (CR) gram-negative bacteria bloodstream infections (BSI) in adult acute leukemia patients, highlighting the association of prior antibiotic exposure with increased risk of MDR and CR BSI, and the high mortality rate associated with CR BSI.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of patients with acute leukemia and gram-negative bacteria BSI, including statistical analysis of risk factors and outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: Identifying antibiotic-resistant strains via cell sorting and elastic-light-scatter phenotyping.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces a novel method combining cell sorting and elastic-light-scatter phenotyping to detect and identify antibiotic-resistant strains, focusing on Staphylococcus aureus. full_output.methodology: The method combines a cell sorter for bacterial detection with elastic-light-scattering technology for bacterial classification, utilizing machine learning to identify resistant strains based on unique colony scatter patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Type IV secretion system effector sabotages multiple defense systems in a competing bacterium.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LtaE, a type IV secretion system effector from Lysobacter enzymogenes, which interacts with transcription regulators LuxR1 and PvdS in Pseudomonas protegens, disrupting the biosynthesis of antibacterial compounds orfamide A and pyoverdine.
full_output.methodology: The study used bacterial two-hybrid assays, HPLC, qRT-PCR, and fluorescence microscopy to investigate the interactions and effects of LtaE on Pseudomonas protegens.

full_output.paper_title: A diverse set of Enterococcus-infecting phage provides insight into phage host-range determinants.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified five novel phages (SHEF10, SHEF11, SHEF13, SHEF14, and SHEF16) that target vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (VRE) strains, with particular emphasis on the role of the Enterococcus polysaccharide antigen (EPA) in phage infection. The research highlights the importance of EPA variations in determining phage host range and identifies a conserved carbohydrate-binding module (CBM22) in certain phage genomes that may facilitate bacterial surface interactions.
full_output.methodology: Phages were isolated from wastewater samples, characterized using transmission electron microscopy, and their genomes were sequenced and analyzed. Functional studies included host range assays, plaque assays, and genetic manipulation of EPA loci to determine their role in phage infection.

full_output.paper_title: Geographical migration and fitness dynamics of Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the geographical migration and fitness dynamics of Streptococcus pneumoniae, focusing on the impact of pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCVs) on serotype replacement and antimicrobial resistance (AMR). It found that PCVs led to an increase in non-vaccine type (NVT) strains, which showed higher fitness and increasing penicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used geolocated genome sequences from South Africa, combined with human mobility data and phylogenetic analysis, to model the spread and fitness changes of S. pneumoniae strains.

These compounds, 3,5-di-O-galloylquinic acid, myricetin 3-O-α-l-rhamnopyranoside, and myricetin 3-O-(2"-O-galloyl)-β-d-galactopyranoside, demonstrate significant anti-QS activity by reducing the expression of QS-regulated genes such as lasI, lasR, rhlI, rhlR, and pqsA.
full_output.methodology: The study employed HPLC, NMR, and molecular docking analyses to identify and characterize the active compounds from Myrtus communis leaves. Anti-QS activity was assessed using violacein production inhibition assays and RT-PCR to evaluate gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: In vivo selection of carbapenem resistance during persistent Klebsiella pneumoniae sequence type 395 bloodstream infection due to OmpK36 deletion.

ompK36.mechanism: deletion leads to reduced carbapenem susceptibility

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a large deletion in the ompK36 gene in Klebsiella pneumoniae ST395, leading to carbapenem resistance during persistent bloodstream infection.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phenotypic susceptibility testing were used to analyze the resistance mechanisms in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Crystal structure of the class A extended-spectrum β-lactamase CTX-M-96 in complex with relebactam at 1.03 Angstrom resolution.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the inhibitory efficacy of relebactam against CTX-M-96, a class A extended-spectrum β-lactamase, and determines its crystal structure in complex with relebactam at 1.03 Å resolution.
full_output.methodology: X-ray crystallography and enzyme kinetics

full_output.paper_title: Zafirlukast induces DNA condensation and has bactericidal effect on replicating Mycobacterium abscessus.
full_output.key_findings: Zafirlukast shows bactericidal effects on replicating Mycobacterium abscessus, inducing DNA condensation and morphological changes, with an MIC of 16 µM and a bactericidal concentration of 64 µM.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, CFU measurement, TEM imaging, and fluorescence microscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Bacillus subtilis-derived peptides disrupt quorum sensing and biofilm assembly in multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

surfactin.mechanism: quorum sensing interference and antibiofilm activity

full_output.key_findings: Bacillus subtilis 6D1 produces peptides, including surfactin, that disrupt quorum sensing and biofilm formation in multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening, biofilm inhibition assays, and genomic analysis were used to identify and characterize the antibiofilm activity of B. subtilis 6D1.

full_output.paper_title: A classic antibiotic reimagined: Rationally designed bacitracin variants exhibit potent activity against vancomycin-resistant pathogens.

bacitracin.mechanism: targets C 55 PP, an important lipid carrier involved in cell wall biosynthesis
bacitracin.validation_method: antibacterial activity assays, MIC determination, cell-based assays, ITC, TLC

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the design and evaluation of bacitracin analogues, specifically analogues 9 and 11, which exhibit enhanced antibacterial activity against vancomycin-resistant pathogens by targeting C 55 PP.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and evaluation of bacitracin analogues, MIC determination, cell-based assays, ITC, TLC, and mechanistic studies.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of mechanisms modulating chlorhexidine and octenidine susceptibility in Proteus mirabilis.

smvR.notes: Inactivation of smvR is associated with adaptation to both biocides.

mipA.notes: MipA inactivation alone confers moderate protection against CHD.

rppA.notes: Mutations in rppA were exclusive to one adapted isolate and were linked with reduced polymyxin B susceptibility.

full_output.key_findings: SmvR inactivation is a key mechanism in both CHD and OCT tolerance. MipA inactivation alone confers moderate protection against CHD, and rppA showed no direct role in either CHD or OCT susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Genetic characterization and complementation studies were used to identify mutations associated with biocide adaptation.

full_output.key_findings: The study presents a high-throughput phage screening platform utilizing ATP bioluminescence for rapid identification of phages targeting multidrug-resistant bacterial isolates. The platform uses solid tablets containing phages and ATP detection reagents, enabling quick and reliable phage susceptibility testing.
full_output.methodology: The study developed a high-throughput phage screening platform using ATP bioluminescence detection, involving phage-mediated bacterial lysis and signal measurement.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcus aureus screening and preoperative decolonisation with Mupirocin and Chlorhexidine to reduce the risk of surgical site infections in orthopaedic surgery: a pre-post study.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the impact of preoperative screening and decolonisation with Mupirocin and Chlorhexidine on reducing the risk of Staphylococcus aureus surgical site infections (SSI) in orthopaedic surgery. The intervention group showed a lower rate of S. aureus SSI compared to the historical control group, although the difference was not statistically significant. The study highlights the importance of nasal screening and targeted decolonisation strategies in reducing SSI risk.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective pre-post study comparing surgical site infection rates before and after implementing a screening and decolonisation strategy in orthopaedic surgery patients.

full_output.paper_title: Ligand-Based Virtual Screening for Discovery of Indole Derivatives as Potent DNA Gyrase ATPase Inhibitors Active against Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Hit Validation by Biological Assays.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several indole derivatives, including G24 and G26, as potent inhibitors of M. tuberculosis DNA gyrase ATPase activity, demonstrating significant anti-tubercular activity.
full_output.methodology: Ligand-based virtual screening combined with biological assays and molecular dynamics simulations were used to identify and validate potent DNA gyrase ATPase inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Coordinated regulation of osmotic imbalance by c-di-AMP shapes ß-lactam tolerance in Group B Streptococcus.

gh25.encodes: secreted cell-wall lytic enzyme with predicted lysozyme activity

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies gdpP as a gene that, when inactivated, confers β-lactam tolerance in Group B Streptococcus. Additionally, the transcriptional repressor busR and its downstream targets busAB, amaP, and pepY2 are shown to play roles in β-lactam susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: The study uses genetic deletions, transcriptome analysis, and spot assays to investigate the role of gdpP and its regulatory network in β-lactam tolerance.

full_output.paper_title: First detection of a Mycobacterium tuberculosis XDR clinical isolate harbouring an RpoB I491F mutation in a Ukrainian patient treated in Germany, October 2023.

RpoB.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that the RpoB I491F mutation causes rifampicin resistance and confirms this through targeted sequencing and phenotypic resistance profiling.

rv0678.evidence_note: Mutations in rv0678 can lead to increased efflux of BDQ, resulting in higher MICs and reduced drug efficacy.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first detection of a multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolate carrying the RpoB I491F mutation, which is not detected by current WHO-recommended rapid diagnostics, highlighting the need for improved diagnostic approaches.
full_output.methodology: Targeted sequencing, whole genome sequencing, and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the resistance mechanisms in the isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Nosocomial transmission of tet(x3), bla (NDM-1) and bla (OXA-97)-carrying Acinetobacter baumannii conferring resistance to eravacycline and omadacycline, the Netherlands, March to August 2021.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the presence of tet(x3), bla NDM-1, and bla OXA-97 genes in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from the Netherlands, which confer resistance to eravacycline, omadacycline, and carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) testing were used to identify and characterize the AMR genes and mutations in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Cefiderocol heteroresistance associated with mutations in TonB-dependent receptor genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa of clinical origin.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: disruption of the DNA binding domain of the response regulator

pirR.notes: Mutations in pirR were associated with cefiderocol heteroresistance.
pirR.evidence_note: The paper states that pirR frameshift mutations occurred in a stretch of seven guanine residues from nucleotide positions 389 to 395, resulting in multiple missense mutations with premature termination of the protein at amino acid position 165. This would be predicted to lead to the loss of the DNA binding domain of the response regulator.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in TonB-dependent receptor genes (pirR and piuA) in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates that were associated with cefiderocol heteroresistance. These mutations impaired the function of the receptors, leading to reduced susceptibility to cefiderocol.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze mutations in TonB-dependent receptor genes and their impact on cefiderocol susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: The role of Listeria monocytogenes PstA in β-lactam resistance requires the cytochrome bd oxidase activity.

pstA.notes: PstA's apo form diminishes β-lactam resistance, while c-di-AMP-bound form promotes it.

full_output.key_findings: PstA's apo form decreases β-lactam resistance, whereas its c-di-AMP-bound form enhances it. The function of PstA in β-lactam resistance is dependent on the cytochrome bd oxidase activity.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, antibiotic susceptibility assays, and biochemical analyses were used to investigate PstA's role in β-lactam resistance.

full_output.paper_title: A high-throughput assay identifies molecules with antimicrobial activity against persister cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a high-throughput assay to identify compounds with antimicrobial activity against persister cells of Staphylococcus aureus. Seven compounds from four structural clusters were identified with activity against antibiotic-tolerant S. aureus, though further screening is needed to identify motifs with lower general cytotoxicity.
full_output.methodology: The study used a high-throughput assay to screen 250 molecular fragments for activity against persister cells of S. aureus, employing techniques such as time-kill curves and CFU enumeration.

full_output.paper_title: Pathogen diversity and antimicrobial resistance transmission of Salmonella enterica serovars Typhi and Paratyphi A in Bangladesh, Nepal, and Malawi: a genomic epidemiological study.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and SRST2 for AMR gene detection, alongside phenotypic testing for resistance confirmation.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies thymoquinone and thymol as major bioactive compounds in Nigella sativa extract with antimicrobial and antivirulence properties against various bacteria and fungi.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis of 2-Ethylhexyl 5-Bromothiophene-2-Carboxylates; Antibacterial Activities against Salmonella Typhi, Validation via Docking Studies, Pharmacokinetics, and Structural Features Determination through DFT.
full_output.key_findings: The study synthesized 2-ethylhexyl 5-(p-tolyl)thiophene-2-carboxylate (4F) which showed strong antibacterial activity against XDR Salmonella Typhi with an MIC of 3.125 mg/mL. Molecular docking studies indicated that 4F binds effectively to DNA gyrase, suggesting a potential mechanism of action.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, molecular docking, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to evaluate the antibacterial activity of the synthesized compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Imidazoquinoline Derivatives as Potential Inhibitors of InhA Enzyme and Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on designing and evaluating imidazoquinoline derivatives as inhibitors of the InhA enzyme in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. While some compounds showed moderate inhibition of InhA, none exhibited effective antimycobacterial activity against MTB H37Rv strain, indicating that the imidazoquinoline scaffold may not be suitable for developing effective anti-TB drugs.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, biological activity evaluation, and molecular docking studies were performed to assess the inhibitory effects of imidazoquinoline derivatives on InhA and their antimycobacterial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Potential of Pomegranate and Lemon Extracts Alone or in Combination with Antibiotics against Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial effects of standardized pomegranate extract (PE) and lemon extract (LE) against various bacteria and fungi, revealing that PE exhibited stronger antibacterial and antifungal effects compared to some antibiotics, while LE showed weaker effects. Combinations of extracts with antibiotics sometimes resulted in antagonistic effects.
full_output.methodology: The study used disk diffusion assays to assess the antimicrobial activity of PE and LE against a range of bacterial and fungal strains, comparing their effects to those of commonly used antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Characterization of a Sustained Nitric Oxide-Releasing Orthodontic Elastomeric Chain for Antimicrobial Action.
full_output.key_findings: The study successfully integrated S-nitroso-acetylpenicillamine (SNAP) into orthodontic elastomeric chains, enabling sustained nitric oxide (NO) release over 29 days. The NO-releasing chains inhibited Streptococcus mutans growth and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: SNAP was incorporated into elastomeric chains using a swell-encapsulation-shrink method, followed by polymer coating via electrospinning. NO release was measured using a chemiluminescence analyzer, and antimicrobial activity was assessed against S. mutans.

full_output.paper_title: Elucidation of the Gemcitabine Transporters of Escherichia coli K-12 and Gamma-Proteobacteria Linked to Gemcitabine-Related Chemoresistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies NupC and NupG as high-affinity gemcitabine transporters in Escherichia coli K-12 and characterizes their homologs in Klebsiella pneumoniae and Citrobacter freundii, revealing their role in gemcitabine uptake and potential contribution to chemoresistance.
full_output.methodology: Expression of genes in E. coli, transport assays, and kinetic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Designed De Novo α-Sheet Peptides Destabilize Bacterial Biofilms and Increase the Susceptibility of E. coli and S. aureus to Antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that α-sheet peptides AP90 and AP401 inhibit amyloid formation in E. coli and S. aureus biofilms, increasing their susceptibility to antibiotics. Specifically, the peptides enhance the effectiveness of gentamicin, ciprofloxacin, vancomycin, amoxicillin, and erythromycin against these bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study used biofilm susceptibility assays, Thioflavin T fluorescence, and optical density measurements to assess the effect of α-sheet peptides on biofilm formation and antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Bioactivity of Eugenol: A Potential Antibiotic Adjuvant with Minimal Ecotoxicological Impact.
full_output.key_findings: Eugenol was found to significantly reduce the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of several antibiotics against various pathogenic bacteria, suggesting its potential as an antibiotic adjuvant. It showed minimal ecotoxicity towards soil and water microbiota compared to the tested antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Microdilution methods, checkerboard assays, and kinetic studies were used to determine the MICs of eugenol and its interactions with antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Anti-Persisters Activity of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus Culture Filtrates against Pseudomonas aeruginosa in Artificial Sputum Medium.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus culture filtrates (LRM-CFS) effectively kill Pseudomonas aeruginosa persisters in artificial sputum medium, showing potent bactericidal activity against both planktonic and biofilm-associated persisters.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the anti-persister activity of LRM-CFS against P. aeruginosa in artificial sputum medium using various concentrations and exposure times, assessing bacterial viability through colony counting.
full_output.sample_size: Two P. aeruginosa strains (PaCF1 and PaCF4) were tested.

full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the antibacterial mechanism and applications of McC7, a bacteriocin with potential as an antibiotic alternative. It explores the role of McC7 in inhibiting bacterial growth, its immune mechanisms, and its effectiveness in improving gut health in poultry and pigs.
full_output.methodology: The research involved mutagenesis studies, in vivo experiments, and evaluation of McC7's effects on bacterial growth and intestinal health.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Activity of Positively Charged Oligopeptides with Theoretical High α-Helix Content against Cutibacterium acnes.

full_output.methodology: The study determined the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of CKR-13 and FK-13 against C. acnes using broth microdilution, and analyzed morphological changes using SEM and TEM.

full_output.paper_title: Efficient synthesis of CRISPR-Cas13a-antimicrobial capsids against MRSA facilitated by silent mutation incorporation.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Property and Mechanisms of Au@Ag Core-Shell Nanoparticles with Near-Infrared Absorption Against E. faecalis Infection of Dentin.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that Au@Ag core-shell nanoparticles combined with photothermal therapy (PTT) exhibit enhanced antibacterial and antibiofilm effects against both original and Ag+-resistant E. faecalis. The antibacterial mechanisms involve the release of silver ions, disruption of the cell membrane, production of reactive oxygen species, and inhibition of ATP production. Additionally, hyperthermia generated by Au@AgNPs reduces membrane fluidity and enhances Ag+ sensitivity by downregulating fabF expression.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a combination of nanoparticle synthesis, antimicrobial activity assays, biofilm analysis, and molecular techniques to evaluate the antibacterial properties of Au@AgNPs with PTT against E. faecalis.

full_output.paper_title: A comparison of antibiotic resistance genes and mobile genetic elements in wild and captive Himalayan vultures.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 414 ARG subtypes in Himalayan vultures, including beta-lactam, multidrug, tetracycline, aminoglycoside, MLS, and others. Certain ARGs were found to differ significantly between wild and captive groups.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing was used to analyze the resistome and mobile genetic elements in wild and captive Himalayan vultures.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution and spread of tigecycline resistance gene tet (X4) in Escherichia coli from different sources.

tet(X4).validation_method: whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the tigecycline resistance gene tet(X4) in Escherichia coli isolates from pigs and pork, highlighting its association with specific plasmid types and the potential for horizontal transfer.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the tet(X4) gene and its resistance profile.

full_output.paper_title: Photoresponsive Multirole Nanoweapon Camouflaged by Hybrid Cell Membrane Vesicles for Efficient Antibacterial Therapy of Pseudomonas aeruginosa-Infected Pneumonia and Wound.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a biomimetic nanoplatform (AB@LRM) that combines photothermal therapy, photodynamic therapy, and chemotherapy for the treatment of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections. AB@LRM showed effective antibacterial activity, reduced bacterial load, and improved wound healing.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of in vitro and in vivo experiments, including transmission electron microscopy, zeta potential measurements, photothermal effect evaluations, and animal models of bacterial pneumonia and wound infections.

full_output.paper_title: The IncC and IncX1 resistance plasmids present in multi-drug resistant Escherichia coli strains isolated from poultry manure in Poland.

blaCMY-2.evidence_note: The paper mentions that plasmids pECmdr13.2 and pECmdr14.1 harbor bla CMY-2, which is a beta-lactamase gene conferring resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics.

blaTEM-176.evidence_note: The paper mentions that blaTEM-176 is present on plasmid pECmdr13.3, which is part of the resistance plasmids identified in the study.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three resistance plasmids (pECmdr13.2, pECmdr13.3, pECmdr14.1) in multi-drug resistant E. coli strains from poultry manure in Poland, each carrying various AMR genes including tetracycline, aminoglycoside, beta-lactam, sulfonamide, fluoroquinolone, and phenicol resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing of E. coli strains isolated from poultry manure, followed by bioinformatic analysis to identify resistance plasmids and their associated AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: An inhibitory mechanism of AasS, an exogenous fatty acid scavenger: Implications for re-sensitization of FAS II antimicrobials.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies AasS as a target for reversing FAS II bypass in bacteria, demonstrating that C10-AMS inhibits AasS activity through a mixed-type mechanism, thereby re-sensitizing bacteria to FAS II-targeted antimicrobials.
full_output.methodology: Structural and biochemical analyses, including cryo-EM, ITC, and enzymatic assays, were used to investigate the inhibitory mechanism of C10-AMS against AasS.

full_output.paper_title: Can Porphyrin-Triphenylphosphonium Conjugates Enhance the Photosensitizer Performance Toward Bacterial Strains?
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the enhancement of photosensitizer performance using porphyrin-triphenylphosphonium conjugates for antimicrobial photodynamic treatment (aPDT). The conjugates showed improved photodynamic activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacterial strains, with reduced irradiation time requirements compared to TMPyP.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and characterization of porphyrin-triphenylphosphonium conjugates, evaluation of their photodynamic activity against bacterial strains using aPDT assays.

full_output.paper_title: Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae in the livestock, humans and environmental samples around the globe: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaKPC-2 as the most prevalent carbapenemase gene among Enterobacteriaceae, followed by blaNDM, blaOXA-48, blaIMP, and blaVIM. The prevalence of these genes varies across different bacterial species and geographic regions.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 studies assessing the prevalence of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of ABCB1 most frequent polymorphisms on the accumulation of bictegravir in recombinant HEK293 cell lines.

ABCB1.notes: Mutations in ABCB1 were analyzed for their impact on bictegravir accumulation.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effect of ABCB1 polymorphisms on bictegravir accumulation in HEK293 cell lines and found no significant impact of the c.1199G > A and c.1236C > T-c.2677G > T-c.3435C > T variants on bictegravir transport.
full_output.methodology: The study used recombinant HEK293 cell lines expressing different ABCB1 variants and measured bictegravir accumulation using flow cytometry and functional assays.

full_output.paper_title: The Prevalence of Multidrug-Resistant Escherichia coli in Chennai and Whole Genome Sequence Analysis of Carbapenem-Resistant Escherichia coli ST410.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations in a carbapenem-resistant Escherichia coli ST410 isolate, including blaTEM-1B, blaCTX-M-15, blaNDM-5, armA, aac(3)-IId, and gyrA mutations (p.S83L and p.D87N), which confer resistance to beta-lactams, cephalosporins, carbapenems, aminoglycosides, and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, whole genome sequencing, and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Study of the Genomic Characterization of Antibiotic-Resistant Escherichia Coli Isolated From Iraqi Patients with Urinary Tract Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of blaTEM, blaSHV, and blaCTXM genes in E. coli isolates from Iraqi patients with urinary tract infections, contributing to resistance against beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to detect resistance genes and evaluate antibiotic resistance patterns in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The FinO/ProQ-like protein PA2582 impacts antimicrobial resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

proQ.mechanism: Regulates transcript levels of genes involved in antimicrobial resistance

oprI.mechanism: Involved in susceptibility to cationic antimicrobial peptides
oprI.validation_method: Transcriptome analysis and protein level determination

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PA2582 as a ProQ-like protein that influences antimicrobial resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa by regulating the expression of genes involved in membrane composition and permeability.
full_output.methodology: The study uses transcriptome analysis, RT-qPCR, northern blotting, and co-purification experiments to investigate the role of PA2582 in antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Interplay among manures, vegetable types, and tetracycline resistance genes in rhizosphere microbiome.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified and compared eight tetracycline resistance genes (TRGs) and the intl1 gene in different manure and vegetable treatment groups, revealing significant variations in TRG abundance and distribution influenced by manure types and vegetable species.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PCR, qPCR, and high-throughput sequencing to analyze TRG profiles and bacterial communities in rhizosphere soils amended with different manures and vegetables.

full_output.paper_title: Facile Synthesis of 5-Bromo-N-Alkylthiophene-2-Sulfonamides and Its Activities Against Clinically Isolated New Delhi Metallo-β-Lactamase Producing Klebsiella pneumoniae ST147.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis of 5-bromo-N-alkylthiophene-2-sulfonamides and evaluates their antibacterial activity against NDM-1-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae ST147. Compound 3b showed high potency with a MIC of 0.39 μg/mL and MBC of 0.78 μg/mL. The presence of the blaNDM-1 gene was confirmed in the isolate, which is responsible for carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of compounds, molecular identification of blaNDM-1, agar well diffusion assay, and MIC/MBC determination.

full_output.key_findings: The study established epidemiological cut-off (ECOFF) values for eravacycline against Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Enterobacter cloacae, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: The study determined MICs of eravacycline using broth microdilution and calculated ECOFF values using ECOFFinder and visual estimation.

full_output.paper_title: A comprehensive investigation of the anion inhibition profile of a β-carbonic anhydrase from Acinetobacter baumannii for crafting innovative antimicrobial treatments.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the β-carbonic anhydrase (β-AbauCA) from Acinetobacter baumannii, highlighting its role in the resistance mechanism mediated by AmpC beta-lactamase. The enzyme was cloned, expressed, and purified, revealing its kinetic properties and inhibition profile with inorganic anions.
full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, expression, purification, and kinetic analysis of β-AbauCA.

full_output.paper_title: Biological characterization of the phage lysin AVPL and its efficiency against Aerococcus viridans-induced mastitis in a murine model.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the phage lysin AVPL, which shows efficient bactericidal activity against multidrug-resistant Aerococcus viridans in vitro and in a murine mastitis model.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the expression and characterization of AVPL, assessment of its enzymatic properties, and evaluation of its therapeutic potential in a murine mastitis model.

full_output.paper_title: Citrobacter spp. and Enterobacter spp. as reservoirs of carbapenemase blaNDM and blaKPC resistance genes in hospital wastewater.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Citrobacter spp. and Enterobacter spp. as significant reservoirs of carbapenemase genes blaKPC and blaNDM in hospital wastewater, highlighting their role in the spread of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study involved PCR screening, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of isolates from hospital wastewater.

full_output.paper_title: A newly identified IncY plasmid from multi-drug-resistant Escherichia coli isolated from dairy cattle feces in Poland.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two IncY plasmids from multi-drug-resistant E. coli isolated from dairy cattle feces in Poland, carrying resistance genes against beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, tetracyclines, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing of E. coli strains isolated from dairy cattle feces.

full_output.key_findings: The study found a low incidence of drug-resistant pathogens, specifically methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PsA), among patients with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) at a safety net hospital.

full_output.paper_title: Berberine analog of chloramphenicol exhibits a distinct mode of action and unveils ribosome plasticity.

CAM-BER exhibits a distinct mode of action compared to chloramphenicol, acting as a translation initiation inhibitor rather than an elongation inhibitor. It shows high affinity for the ribosome and interacts uniquely with the P site, leading to ribosome stalling at the start codon.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized biochemical assays, crystallography, and toe-printing experiments to analyze the interaction of CAM-BER with the bacterial ribosome and its effect on protein synthesis.

full_output.paper_title: Prolonged hospitalization signature and early antibiotic effects on the nasopharyngeal resistome in preterm infants.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of chlorogenic acid and carnosol for anti-efflux pump and anti-biofilm activities against extensively drug-resistant strains of Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: Chlorogenic acid (CGA) and carnosol (CL) showed synergistic effects with gentamicin against extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains of Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, reducing the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and inhibiting efflux pump activity.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial susceptibility testing, checkerboard assays, flow cytometry, and biofilm formation assays were used to evaluate the effects of CGA and CL on XDR strains.
full_output.sample_size: 12 multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains of S. aureus and P. aeruginosa

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of a novel FRI-type carbapenemase; blaFRI-12 in Enterobacter asburiae located on an IncR plasmid.

blaFRI-12.validation_method: cloning into E. coli and susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel FRI-type carbapenemase, blaFRI-12, in Enterobacter asburiae, which confers resistance to carbapenems and aztreonam. The gene was found on a 104 Kb IncR plasmid and was functionally validated through cloning and susceptibility testing.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed to identify and validate the blaFRI-12 gene.

full_output.paper_title: Targeting plasmid-encoded proteins that contain immunoglobulin-like domains to combat antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the RSP protein, a plasmid-encoded protein with immunoglobulin-like domains, as a potential target for combating antimicrobial resistance. Immunization with RSP provided protection against infection by an antibiotic-resistant Salmonella strain, and nanobodies targeting RSP interfered with the conjugative transfer of IncHI plasmids.
full_output.methodology: The study used a mouse infection model, immunization with the RSP protein, and generation of nanobodies to assess their effect on Salmonella infection and plasmid conjugation.

full_output.paper_title: Revealing detrimental effects of various DC electrical energy conditions on different multidrug resistant bacteria: a comprehensive study.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effects of different DC electrical energy conditions on multidrug-resistant bacteria, showing that electrical energy can reduce bacterial counts, inhibit metabolic activity, and impair antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used DC electrical energy with varying voltages and exposure times to assess its effects on bacterial viability, metabolic activity, and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Nanoparticles in liposomes: a platform for increased antibiotic selectivity in multidrug resistant bacteria in respiratory tract infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study explores the use of nanoparticle-liposome (NP-Lip) formulations to improve the selectivity of antibiotics and a quorum sensing inhibitor against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, focusing on their efficacy in targeting bacterial biofilms while minimizing toxicity to mammalian cells.
full_output.methodology: The study employed nanoparticle preparation, in vitro cytotoxicity and uptake assessments, and evaluations of drug delivery efficiency in lung models.

full_output.paper_title: Salmonella Typhi genotypic diversity, cluster identification and antimicrobial resistance determinants in Mukuru settlement, Nairobi Kenya.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations in Salmonella Typhi isolates from Mukuru settlement, Nairobi, Kenya, highlighting the prevalence of multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify antimicrobial resistance determinants in 35 S. Typhi isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Postbiotic mediators derived from Lactobacillus species enhance riboflavin-mediated antimicrobial photodynamic therapy for eradication of Streptococcus mutans planktonic and biofilm growth.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the effectiveness of riboflavin-mediated antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT) enhanced by postbiotic mediators from Lactobacillus casei (LC) and Lactobacillus plantarum (LP) in eradicating Streptococcus mutans planktonic and biofilm growth. The results showed that aPDT combined with LC and LP significantly reduced S. mutans biofilms and gtfB gene expression.
full_output.methodology: The study used MIC and MBC assays, qRT-PCR to assess gene expression, and crystal violet staining to evaluate biofilm disruption.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that 17.5% of patients in healthcare facilities in Ibadan, Nigeria, were colonized with carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE), with a significant proportion showing multidrug resistance. Two E. coli isolates were pan-resistant to multiple antibiotic classes.
full_output.methodology: Rectal swabs were collected and tested for CRE using culture, susceptibility testing, and carbapenemase detection methods.

full_output.paper_title: Mutations Affecting Cellular Levels of Cobalamin (Vitamin B(12)) Confer Tolerance to Bactericidal Antibiotics in Burkholderia cenocepacia.

mutations_found.validated_by: genomic DNA sequencing and PCR screening
genomic DNA sequencing and PCR screening

BCAL2923.notes: mutations in BCAL2923 gene confer decreased susceptibility to multiple antibiotics

full_output.key_findings: Mutations in the BCAL2923 gene, which encodes adenosylcobinamide-phosphate synthase, confer decreased susceptibility to tobramycin and other bactericidal antibiotics in B. cenocepacia. These mutations lead to reduced ROS production, contributing to antibiotic tolerance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic DNA sequencing, PCR screening, MIC determination, and ROS quantification were used to analyze the effects of BCAL2923 mutations on antibiotic susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and prevalence of Listeria species from raw milk and dairy products in Burdur, Turkey.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Listeria spp. in dairy products from Burdur, Turkey, with isolates showing resistance to multiple antibiotics. Biofilm-related genes flaA and luxS were detected in some isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR and disc diffusion techniques were used to identify Listeria species and assess antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Different Contributions of embB and ubiA Mutations to Variable Level of Ethambutol Resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies specific mutations in embB and ubiA genes associated with variable levels of ethambutol (EMB) resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates. Notably, mutations such as Met306Val, Gln497Arg, and Ala39Glu were strongly linked to high-level EMB resistance.
full_output.methodology: DNA sequencing and statistical analysis of mutations in embB and ubiA genes in 146 MDR-TB isolates to evaluate their association with EMB resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the prevalence of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA) in hospital and municipal wastewater, highlighting the role of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in the spread of carbapenem resistance. It emphasizes the environmental impact of antibiotic resistance and the need for better management strategies.
full_output.methodology: The paper is a review of literature published in the last decade, focusing on the prevalence and mechanisms of carbapenem resistance in CRAB and CRPA.

full_output.paper_title: Integrated Analysis of Patient Networks and Plasmid Genomes to Investigate a Regional, Multispecies Outbreak of Carbapenemase-Producing Enterobacterales Carrying Both blaIMP and mcr-9 Genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies blaIMP and mcr-9 genes as key drivers of carbapenem and colistin resistance in a regional outbreak of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales, emphasizing the role of IncHI2 plasmids in their dissemination.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, plasmid analysis, and patient network reconstruction were used to investigate the outbreak.

full_output.key_findings: Steroid drugs, particularly quinestrol, inhibit bacterial respiratory oxidases and exhibit bactericidal effects against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
full_output.methodology: In silico docking, oxygen consumption assays, and growth/viability assays were used to evaluate the effects of steroid drugs on bacterial respiratory complexes.

full_output.paper_title: Minimal Impact on the Resistome of Children in Botswana After Azithromycin Treatment for Acute Severe Diarrheal Disease.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that azithromycin treatment for bacterial diarrhea in children in Botswana did not significantly increase the prevalence of macrolide resistance genes compared to the control group, suggesting minimal impact on the gut resistome.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic DNA sequencing and targeted capture of antibiotic resistance genes from stool samples before and after treatment.
